ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Irregularities in Disbursement of Scholarships under NMMSS 
†180. Shri Harish Chandra Meena: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of beneficiaries affected in Rajasthan, particularly in Tonk and Sawai Madhopur 
districts due to delay in National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) distribution; 
 
(b) whether the Government has recovered the undisbursed amount from the State Bank of India 
and ensured payment to the students' accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (PFMS -DBT), if 
so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) the details of the measures being adopted by the Gov ernment to prevent recurrence of such 
errors in future and to ensure timely provision of scholarships to meritorious students from 
economically weaker sections of Rajasthan? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a):  In Rajasthan, during the Academic Year 2025-26, out of total number of 14334 finally verified 
scholarships on NSP , payments were credited into the bank accounts of 13018 beneficiaries 
without delay , including the Tonk and Sawai Madhopur districts . Re-validation of  failed 
transaction accounts in coordination with the State education authorities to ensure flow of payment 
through DBT is a continuous process . Details of the number of beneficiaries of the State of 
Rajasthan including Sawai Madhopur and Tonk Districts for the year 2025 -26 may be seen at 
Annexure. 
 
(b) & (c):  Under NMMSS, State Bank of India has refunded total amount of ₹218,42,64,760/ - to 
the Government of India f or the period  2022-23 to 2025-26.  The bank account of  NMMSS 
maintained with  the S tate Bank of India, New Delhi  was formally closed during 2025 -26 after 
recovery of all the undisbursed amount lying with the bank. The scheme has successfully switched 
from the erstwhile "Agency Mode" (SBI) to the Pay and Accounts Office Direct Benefit Transfer 
(PAO-DBT) mode through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). The scholarship 
payments for the Financial Year 2025 –26 was successfully disbursed directly into the verified 
Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries via PAO-DBT module through the PFMS.  

Measures such as the adoption of the mandatory Aadhaar Based Payment System (ABPS), 
the implementation of strict vali dation protocols on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) to 
verify beneficiary bank accounts through the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) 
mapper before generating the final payment file and the capacity building of Nodal Officers by 
the Depar tment, following the transition to the PAO -DBT mode, expedite the release of 
scholarship amounts to verified meritorious beneficiaries from economically weaker sections.

181. Shri Konda Vishweshwar Reddy: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of sports infrastructure projects sanctioned in the State of 
Telangana by the Government under the Greenfield and Brownfield 
categories during the last five years and the current year, year and 
district-wise; 
 
(b) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised for each such 
project during the said period including the present status of 
implementation, percentage of physical and financial progress and the 
expected date of completion thereof; 
 
(c) the details of projects that have not been completed within the 
stipulated timeline project-wise, indicating the reasons for the delay; 
 
(d) whether the Government has reviewed the delays in execution of 
such projects and if so, the corrective measures taken to ensure their 
early completion; and 
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to sanction any additional 
Greenfield or Brownfield sports infrastructure projects in Telangana 
during the current financial year and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to (e) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sports, including development and strengthening of 
sports infrastructure, rests primarily with the respe ctive State/Unio n 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Territory Governments. The Union Government supplements these 
efforts by bridging critical gaps. The Khelo India Scheme and National 
Sports Development Fund (NSDF), implemented by this Ministry, under 
which financial assistance for develo pment of sports infrastructure is 
provided are demand -driven schemes. The proposals received from the 
State/ Union Territory Governments and other eligible entities are 
considered for financial support, subject to their completeness, 
technical feasibility and availability  of funds under the scheme. The 
details of the sports infrastructure projects approved and their 
sanctioned cost, funds released and their physical and financial 
progress, under the Khelo India Scheme and National Sports 
Development Funds ( NSDF), across th e country, including in State of 
Telangana, are available in public domain on the dashboards of the 
Ministry at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in and 
http://www.nsdf.yas.gov.in/nsdf-glance.html, respectively. 
 
The responsibility of executing t he projects rests with the grantee.  The 
Ministry continuously monitors the implementation of sanctioned 
projects through regular review meetings with grantees and 
implementing agencies, field inspections and visits by Project Monitoring 
Committees to asse ss actual phy sical progress, periodic progress 
reports, continuous interaction with concerned stakeholders, and 
submission of Utilization Certificates (UCs) in respect of funds released. 
Delays, wherever encountered, are generally attributable to factors s uch 
as statutory clearances, land -related issues, tendering and contractual 
processes, revision in project scope, adverse weather conditions and 
other local implementation issues. This Ministry regu larly takes up the 
matter related to delayed projects wi th the g rantees to expeditiously 
ensure timely completion of the projects.

SC Beneficiaries under Samagra Shiksha 
182. Shri Daggumalla Prasada Rao: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of total enrolment of students in Government schools supported under 
Samagra Shiksha since 2019, in the State of Andhra Pradesh, year-wise and district-wise; 
(b) the number of Scheduled Castes (SCs) students enrolled in the State of Andhra Pradesh, 
year and district-wise; 
(c) funds earmarked, released and utilized for SC -focused interventions since 2019, in the  
said State, year-wise; and 
(d) whether the Government has implemented monitoring  mechanisms such as public 
dashboards to assess the effectiveness of Samagra Shiksha in promoting social inclusion 
and educational outcomes for SC students, if so, provide key parameters and findings and if 
not, specify the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) & (b):   The year -wise and district -wise enrolment of students  including 
Scheduled Caste (SC) students  in Government schools in the State of Andhra 
Pradesh since the academic year 2019–20 are provided at Annexure–I.  
(c) Financial assistance is provided to States/UTs based on the proposals 
received in their Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B), appraisal by  the Project 
Approval Board (PAB), programme norms and availability of funds. The approved 
interventions are intended to benefit all eligible children, including SC students, in 
accordance with the principles of equity and inclusion envisaged under NEP 2020. 
 The year-wise details of funds earmarked, released and utilized , as reported 
by the Government of Andhra Pradesh under Samagra Shiksha since 2019 -20 to 
2025-26 are given at Annexure-II. 

(d)  Central Government has established a comprehensive monitoring and review 
framework under Samagra Shiksha to monitor implementation, equity and 
educational outcomes. The key mechanisms include: 
 UDISE+, which provides school -level information on enrolment, infrastru cture, 
teachers, access, equity, retention, transition, gender and social category-wise 
data.  
 PRABANDH Portal , which facilitates online planning, appraisal, approvals, 
financial monitoring and physical progress under Samagra Shiksha. 
 Project Approval Board (PAB) meetings for annual review of State proposals 
and implementation.  
 Periodic review meetings, field visits and monitoring by the Central and State 
authorities. 
 Large scale assessments at national level  conducted by PARAKH/National 
Assessment Centre for measuring learning outcomes. 
 Monitoring of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) relating to access, equity, 
retention, transition, gender and social inclusion.  
 Vidya Samiksha Kendra (VSK), provides centralised, real -time monitoring of 
learning outcomes and scheme interventions. 
 Further, as informed by the State, the State Government of Andhra Pradesh 
has developed Leap App, a consolidated platform covering student profiles, 
attendance, assessments, entitlements and infrastructure status.  In addition, th e 
State maintains separate dashboards and analytics specifically with respect to SC 
students to monitor their academic performance and outcomes over time, enabling 
targeted follow-up and corrective action. 
 These mechanisms enable continu al monitoring of e ducational progress 
across various social groups, including Scheduled Caste students.

entries.t: Status of PMKVY in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 183 
ANSWERED ON – 20.07.2026 
  
STATUS OF PMKVY IN UTTAR PRADESH 
  
†183. SHRI RAMBHUAL NISHAD:  
             
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the present status of the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) in Uttar Pradesh, 
along with the number of training centers  opened, the details of the courses being conducted, and 
the training partners engaged under the scheme; 
 
(b)  the distribution of these training centers in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in Sultanpur district, 
district-wise; 
 
(c)  the details of the funds allocated, released, and utilized for PMKVY in Uttar Pradesh, along 
with the number of beneficiaries imparted training during the last three years and the current year, 
year-wise; 
 
(d)  whether the Government has forged any partnerships with industries, trade organizations or 
private companies in Uttar Pradesh to promote the recruitment of youth trained under PMKVY; 
and      
 
(e)  if so, the details of the steps taken to establish such industry linkages and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)      The current version of the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) i.e. PMKVY 4.0 is 
a demand driven Scheme and training centres under this scheme are affiliated and accredited based 
on the skill requirement of the particular district.Under PM KVY 4.0, 2,664 Training Centers have 
provided project-based skill training in Uttar Pradesh, of which 63 Training Centers have ongoing 
trainings as on 30 June 2026. Further, a total of 5,74,931 and 4,12,151 candidates have been trained 
and certified respectively in Uttar Pradesh. The job -role-wise details of courses and the Training 
Partner-wise details are given at Annexure-I and Annexure-II, respectively. Since the details in 
aforesaid Annexure-II are too lengthy, it is uploaded on Ministry’s website at 
https://www.msde.gov.in/documents?page=1.  
 
(b)       The district-wise distribution of Training Centers under PMKVY 4.0 in Uttar Pradesh is given 
at Annexure-III. Since the details in aforesaid Annexure-III are too lengthy, it is uploaded on 
Ministry’s website at https://www.msde.gov.in/documents?page=1. Under PMKVY 4.0, 2,664 
Training Centers have provided project -based skill training in Uttar Pradesh including 19 Training 
Centers in Sultanpur district. Out of 63 Training Centers with ongoing training across Uttar Pradesh 
as on 30 June 2026, no training is ongoing in Sultanpur district under PMKVY 4.0. 
 
(c)        PMKVY4.0 is a demand driven scheme and there is no provision of fund allocation in the 
scheme to the states/UT. The details of the funds disbursed under PMKVY 4.0 in Uttar Pradesh, 

along with the number of beneficiaries imparted training during the last three years and the current 
year, year-wise is given below:

(d) and (e)        Presently, six Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with industry and private-sector

 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the current status of the scheme to develop Nalanda and Rajgir as 
international tourism centres under the budgetary provisions of the 
Government; 
(b) the details of the amenities being considered by the Government to be 
provided for domestic and international tourists visiting Nalanda; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to connect Nalanda and Rajgir to the 
global tourism circuit; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF TOURISM   (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): Development and promotion of tourism destinations and products 
is primarily undertaken by the concerned State Government (SG)/Union 
Territory Administration (UTA).  
 
The Ministry of Tourism through its central sector schemes of ‘Swadesh 
Darshan (SD) and Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination

‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Herita ge Augmentation Drive

the country by extending financial assistance to the SGs/UTAs in synergy with

Further, Government of India under its ‘Special Assistance to States for 
Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global 
Scale’ sanctioned 40 projects in 23 States for Rs.3295.76 Crore in the country 
including Bihar in Financia l Year 2024 -25, with the primary objective to 
comprehensively develop iconic tourist centres in the country, branding and 
marketing them at global scale.  
 
The details of the projects sanctioned under SD, SD2.0, CBDD, SASCI and 
PRASHAD schemes in the State of Bihar including in Rajgir is annexed. 
 
Further, State Government of Bihar has submitted comprehensive 
destination strategy and development plan for Nalanda-Rajgir.  
 
Receiving of Project Proposal, Master Plan etc. from the State 
Government/UT Administrations is a continuous process. The proposals 
received are examined as per the scheme guidelines and financial assistance 
is extended for such project proposals subject to availability of funds, inter-se 
priority etc.

entries.t: Dilapidated and Unsafe Classrooms of Government Schools
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.185 
ANSWERED ON - 20/07/2026  
 
Dilapidated and Unsafe Classrooms of Government Schools  
  
†185. Shri Omprakash Bhupalsinh Alias Pavan Rajenimbalkar:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has the latest data regarding the number of dilapidated 
and unsafe classrooms in Government and Zilla Parishad schools located in the 
Dharashiv Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the scheme being implemented by the Central Government for demolition of such 
dilapidated and unsafe classrooms and construction of new classrooms in lieu of it 
and the financial alloca tion/funds provided thereunder;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to accord priority approval for construction of 
new classrooms in such schools in the said Constituency and provide the necessary 
financial assistance therefor; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
A N S W E R 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to ( d):  Education is in the Concurrent list of the Constitution and majority of the 
schools are under the a dministrative control of respective State Government and UT 
Administration. Guidelines issued from time to time by Ministry of Education and 
States/UTs are expected to implement them, they may incorporate additions or modify 
them, according to their specific requirements. 
 
Samagra Shiksha Scheme supports creation of infrastructure and basic facilities for 
students in Government Schools including construction of classrooms and repairs . The 
requirement of infrastructural facilities in schools are worked out every year by the 
respective State/Union Territory depending on their need and priority and reflected in 
their Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B). These plans are then appraised and  
approved by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States and Union 
Territories as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme, physical and 

financial progress of works sanctioned earlier and availability of budgetary resources.  
Further, the Samagra Shiksha scheme  is implemented in convergence with various 
Ministries/ developmental agencies  and schemes  of the Centre and State 
Governments.  
 
State has further informed that a fter structures are certified unsafe for use and 
recommended for demolition, construction of new classrooms and the repair of unsafe 
school buildings are being undertaken under Samagra Shiksha as well as various State 
Government schemes. The State of Maharashtra has informed that classrooms in 287 
Government and Zilla Parishad Schools in Dharashiv Lok Sabha Parliamentary 
Constituency which includes Dharashiv District, Ausa and Nilanga block of Latur 
District and Barshi block of Solapur District are dilapidated. Construction of 203 
classrooms with a total financial  allocation of Rs. 2219.11 lakh has been sanctioned in 
the FY: 2025-26 and FY: 2026-27 for Dharashiv constituency under Samagra Shiksha 
and various other State Government’s schemes . Further, the Government of 
Maharashtra, through its Circular dated 16 April 2025, has directed that infrastructure 
gaps in Government schools be addressed by converging resources from State 
Government schemes, Central Government schemes, and Corporate Social 
Responsibility (CSR) funds. 
 
The Ministry of Education has issued a  directive on 26th July 2025 to all States and 
Union Territories to take urgent steps to ensure the student safety and well -being. It 
refers to the "Guidelines on School Safety and Security" (2021) and the National 
Disaster Management Guidelines on School Safety (NDMA, 2016) issued on 
27.02.2017. The directives are available on the link: https://dsel.education.gov.in/ 
sites/default/files/update/ss2607.pdf  
 
Further, the Ministry of Education on 7th August 2025,  has directed all States/UTs to 
ensure the structural safety of school buildings and urgent identification of unsafe and 
dilapidated school buildings through safety audits, followed by demolition, if required or 
repair of structurally unsafe structures, an d prohibition of use, unless certified as safe. 
The directives may be accessed at https://dsel.education.gov.in/sites/default/files 
/update/ss07008.pdf  
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 186 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 20, 2026/ASHADHA 29, 1948 (SAKA) 
CSR FUNDS IN NASHIK 
      QUESTION 
 
186. Shri Rajabhau Parag Prakash Waje: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the total amount of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds generated by 
companies operating in Nashik district during the last five financial years, company -
wise, year-wise and sector-wise;  
 
(b) the details of CSR amount actually spent within Nashik district on local priorities 
such as education, healthcare, drinking water, skill development and rural 
infrastructure and the amount that was diverted outside the district;  
 
(c) whether the Government is aware that despite being a major industrial and agri -
export hub, Nashik continues to face poor school infrastructure, healthcare gaps and 
farmer distress, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to mandate or incentivize local CSR spending in 
the districts where companies generate profits, to ensure fair regional development, if 
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS  AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a) to (d): The legal framework for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is provided 
through Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘the Act’), Schedule VII of the Act and 
Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014.  Under the Companies Act, CSR is a Board driven 
process and the  Board of the company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and 
monitor CSR activities of the company based on the recommendation of its CSR 
Committee. This Committee formulates and recommends the CSR policy, which 
outlines the activities to be undertaken by the company in alignment with the areas or 
subjects specified in Schedule VII of the Act. The first proviso to Section 135 (5) of the 
Act provides that the company shall give preference to the local area and areas around 
it where it operates.   However, the emphasis on local area is only directory and not 
mandatory in nature and companies need to balance local area preference with 
national priorities. The Government does not issue any specific direction to the 
companies to spend in any particular geographical area or for any particular activity. 
Contd…2/ 
 
 
 

 
       
 
-2- 
All data related to CSR filed by companies in MCA21 registry including State -wise, 
District-wise, year -wise, Development Sector -wise, project -wise and company –wise, 
are available in public domain and can be accessed at www.csr.gov.in.  On the basis 
of annual filings made by companies in the MCA 21 registry, the Sector-wise details of 
CSR expenditure in Nashik for the last five Financial Years (FY) i.e. FY 2020 -21 to FY 
2024-25 is attached at Annexure.

entries.t: PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme for Meritorious Students in HEIs
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 187 
ANSWERED ON- 20/07/2026 
PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme for Meritorious Students in HEIs 
  
187. Km. Sudha R: 
  
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
a) whether the much -hyped PM Vidyalaxmi scheme for meritorious students in Higher 
Education Institutes (HEIs) still in force, if so, the list of the beneficiaries since 2024, State -
wise and year-wise; 
b) the eligibility criteria for students studying in State Government -run Higher Educational 
Institutions to apply for PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme; 
c) the number of students from Tamil Nadu who have benefited under the scheme since 2024, 
along with the names of the Higher Educational Institutions; and  
d) the details of funds allocated for the scheme and the funds spent on beneficiaries since 
2024? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
(a) to (d): Education is in the concurr ent list and both the Central Government and State 
Governments work together for its improvement. The Government of India has launched 
the PM-Vidyalaxmi, a new central sector scheme in November 2024. Any student, who get s 
merit-based admission in top Quality Higher Education Institutions (QHEIs) and who desire s 
to avail the education loan can get collateral -free and guarantor-free education loan under the 
scheme. There is no upper limit on number of students getting such loans. Since the launch of 
this scheme on 6th November, 2024 till 12th July, 2026, 108106 PM Vidyalaxmi education 
loans have been sanctioned. The amount sanctioned is ₹ 15042.52 crore. 
  

All the top 100 ranked HEIs in the overall/ category -specific and/or domain specific rankings 
in the list of National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) list; plus all the top 200 
ranked HEIs under the governance of State/UT governments in the list of NIRF; plus all 
remaining HEIs under the governance of Government of India are included in the list of 
QHEIs. A total of 1051 QHEIs, including 138 QHEIs from the state of Tamil Nadu have been 
included under the PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme. 
  
Further, for students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh, the scheme provides 3% 
interest subvention on loans up to ₹10 lakh. Each year up to one lakh fresh students not 
getting any other scholarship or interest subvention on education loan will get this interest 
subvention benefit. An outlay of ₹ 3,600 crore has been made from 2024 -25 to 2030-31, for 
providing 3% interest subvention benefit for up to 7 lakh fresh students during this period. 
  
The State -wise and year -wise number of PM -Vidyalaxmi education loans and amount 
sanctioned along with Institute -wise number of students from the state of Tamil Nadu who 
have benefitted under the scheme since its launch is Annexed.

        Conservation of Ganga Dolphins 
 
189. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that the Ganga Barrage area in Bijnor, Uttar 
Pradesh is emerging as an important centre for the conservation of Ganga Dolphins (Susu) and 
that a nationwide dolphin census campaign has been launched from here in this year; 
(b) the extent of increase or change recorded in the population of Ganga Dolphins in the Ganga 
River, particularly in the Bijnor region during the last five years; 
(c) the amount of funds allocated so far under Project Dolphin for dolphin conservation, habitat 
security, scientific surveys and public awareness programmes; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering the establishment of any special project or centre to 
promote dolphin conservation, research, public awareness and eco-tourism in the Bijnor region? 
 
 
 ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
 
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d): To ascertain reliable population estimates for river dolphins, the Government of India 
undertook the first-ever range-wide river dolphin survey across the Ganga, Brahmaputra and 
Beas river systems, including stretches of the River Ganga in the Bijnor region of Uttar Pradesh 
from 2021 to 2023. The survey established the first comprehensive baseline for assessing river 
dolphin populations in the country. Building upon this baseline and considering the ecological 
importance of the Bijnor stretch, the second range-wide river dolphin population estimation 
was launched from Bijnor in January 2026 to establish trends over time. 
 
For dolphin conservation activities, an amount of Rs. 1.61 crore was released to the State of 
Uttar Pradesh till the last fiscal year. Further, an amount of Rs. 46.03 crore was released to the 
Wildlife Institute of India for dolphin conservation activities in the country, which included an 
amount of Rs. 12.43 crore for the 2nd range wide estimation of riverine and estuarine Dolphins 
in India. In addition, an amount of Rs. 32.97 crore was approved for implementation of the 
Dolphin Conservation Action Plan and Recovery of River Dolphins and their Aquatic Habitats, 
including habitat security, scientific monitoring and public awareness.

19. SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:  
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether restrictions have been imposed on Bhagat Urban Co -operative Bank Ltd. in 
Himachal, including a cap on withdrawals, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor; 
(b) the total number of de positors, total deposits, shareholders affected by these restrictions, 
the current level of non-performing assets of the bank; 
(c) whether any proposal for merger of the bank with a financially stronger cooperative bank 
has been considered, if so, the present status thereof; 
(d) the number of depositors who have received insurance payouts from Deposit Insurance and 
Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) under Section 18A of the DICGC Act, the total amount 
disbursed so far, number of eligible depositors covered, the amount still pending for settlement; 
(e) whether the Government has conducted any inquiry into functioning, governance, loan 
portfolio, asset quality, management of the bank, if so, the findings thereof; and  
(f) the steps being taken by the Governm ent to protect depositors' interests and restore the 
bank's financial stability? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) In order to protect the interest of depositors, t he Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in exercise 
of powers vested under sub section (1) of Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking 
Regulation Act, 1949, has issued Directive to The Bhagat Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd., Solan 
on October 06, 2025. As per the said Directive, from the close of business on October 08, 2025, 
the bank shall not, without prior approval of RBI in writing, grant or renew any loans and 
advances, make any investment, incur any liability including borrowal of funds and acceptance 
of fresh deposits, disburse or agree to disburse any payment whether in discharge of its 
liabilities and obligations or otherwise, enter into any compromise or arrangement and sell, 
transfer or otherwise dispose of any of its properties or assets except as no tified in the RBI 
Directive dated October 06, 2025. The Directive has since been extended twice and is currently 
in force till the close of business on October 08, 2026, subject to review. 
 
Further, the bank has also been directed to permit withdrawal of a sum not exceeding ₹10,000/- 
(Rupees Ten Thousand only) of the total balance held in savings bank or current accounts or 
any other account of a depositor but is allowed to set off loans against deposits subject to the 
conditions stipulated in the aforesaid Directive. 

(b) RBI has informed that The Bhagat Urban Co -operative Bank Ltd., has reported following 
details as on October 08,2025: - 
i. Total number of depositors: 70,849 
ii. Total deposits: ₹467.46 Crore 
iii. The number of shareholders affected by the restrictions: 10,590 
iv. As on 09.07.2026, the level of Gross Non -Performing Assets (GNPAs) : ₹116.19 crore 
(52.45%). 
 
(c) RBI has informed that n o proposal for voluntary amalgamation of The Bhagat Urban Co -
operative Bank Ltd., Solan, with a financially str onger Co-operative bank, has been received 
by RBI. 
 
(d) RBI has informed that a total of 70,849 are eligible depositors covered as per list submitted 
by the Bank to DICGC. So far 12,653 depositors have received insurance pay -outs from 
DICGC and so far a total of Rs. 191.57 crore have been disbursed. Moreover, Rs. 102.28 crores 
are pending for settlement by DICGC. 
 
(e) & (f) RBI has informed that t he Registrar  of Cooperative Societies (RCS), Himachal 
Pradesh had undertaken a careful perusal of successive statutory inspection reports of the bank 
by RBI and noticed grave irregularities, illegalities and lapses committed in the management 
of the affairs of the bank. Accordingly, in view of the poor performance of the bank and the 
consequent restrictions imposed by RBI on the bank’s operational activities, the RCS had 
issued a number of directions to the bank and also convened review meetings with the bank’s 
Board and directed the Board to take immediate corrective measures and to achieve the trigger 
points prescribed by RBI. However, the Board had failed to meet the prescribed targets and 
did not take adequate remedial steps. As a result, the bank remained unable to conduct normal 
financial operations, thereby posing a risk to depositors, creditors and the public interest. 
Therefore, the Board of Directors of the Bhagat Urban Co -operative Bank Ltd. have been 
placed under suspension by RCS, Himachal Pradesh vide its order dated 19.06.2026. Further,  
three officials from the Himachal Pradesh State Government have been appointed as 
Administrators to manage the affairs of the bank.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 194 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
STATUS OF FOUR LABOUR CODES 
 
194. SMT. PRATIMA MONDAL:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)whether the Government has operationalised the four Labour 
Codes across all States and Union Territories and if so, the 
State/UT-wise status thereof and if not, the reasons for the delay in 
implementation in the remaining States and Union Territories;  
(b)the steps being taken by the Government to facilitate their early 
operationalisation while addressing the concerns raised by 
workers, employers and other stakeholders;  
(c)whether the Government has formulated any roadmap or timeline 
for extending comprehensive labour rights and social security 
benefits to gig and platform workers;  
(d)if so, the details thereof including the proposed social security 
measures, eligibility criteria and implementation mechanism; and  
(e)if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e):  The Government of India has implemented four Labour 
Codes, namely, the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations 
Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with 
effect from 21 st November, 2025. The Central Rules under the said 
Labour Codes have been notified on 8th May, 2026. 
  Since ‘Labour’ falls under the concurrent subject, the 
States/UTs are also required to frame Rules under the Labour Codes. 
The Ministry of Labour and Employment is proactively engaged with 
the States/UTs for finalisation of their rules and smooth 
implementation of the Codes. Accordingly, most of the States/UTs 
have already taken measures & have finalised or published/pre -
published the Rules under the Labour Codes and a few States/UTs are 
in the process of pre-publishing/finalising the Rules. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  The four Labour Codes were passed after extensive 
consultations with all stakeholders including States/UTs. The 
comments/concerns raised by the stakeholders were acknowledged 
and examined before the passage of four Labour Codes and 
finalisation of Rules. Further, several National and Regional Labour 
Conferences were held with States/UTs to discuss issues relating to  
four Labour Codes. The Ministry of Labour and Employment is 
pursuing with stakeholders including States/UTs for smooth 
implementation of the Codes. Labour codes will provide universal 
minimum wages and social security benefits for workers.  
  The gig work ers and the platform workers have been 
defined for the first time in the Labour Code for the purpose of 
formulating schemes to provide social security benefits relating to 
life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection etc. 
 
  The four Labour Codes reduce multiplicity of definitions & 
authorities, facilitate use of technology, bring transparency & 
accountability in enforcement.  Simultaneously, it strengthens the 
protection available to workers, including unorganized workers. 
*****

Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) among all States, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the category-wise and district-wise details of Mudra loans sanctioned and disbursed in Tamil Nadu 
during the last three years and the current year, including the number and value of loans sanc tioned 
in Kanchipuram district; 
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the imp act of PMMY loans on employment generation, 
women entrepreneurs and micro-enterprises in the State, if so, the details thereof; 
(f) the steps taken or proposed to improve access to collate ral-free credit and enhance the 
effectiveness of PMMY in Tamil Nadu? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): Tamil Nadu has recorded the second highest cumulative disbursal of loans under the Pradhan 
Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) among all States. The details are placed at Annexure-I. 
 
 
 (b) :   the number of  Mudra loans sanctioned alongwith amount sanctioned and disbursed in Tamil 
Nadu during the last three years and the current year, category -wise and district -wise including 
Kanchipuram district is placed at Annexure-II. 
 
(d) whether the Government is aware of complaints regardi ng inadequate credit flow, high rejection 
rates and delays in processing applications under PMMY in certain districts of Tamil Nadu; 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof; and 
 

(c) : No specific assessment has been carried out to gauge the impact of PMMY loans on employment 
generation, women entrepreneurs and micro -enterprises in the State. However, Ministry of Labour 
and Employment (MoLE) conducted a large sample survey at the national level to esti mate 
employment generation under PMMY. As per the survey results, PMMY helped in generation of 1.12 
crore net additional employment during a period of approximately 3 years (i.e. from 2015 to 2018).  
Further approx. 68% loans have been extended to women bo rrowers under PMMY in the State of 
Tamil Nadu since inception. 
d) to (f) : Citizens can approach banks through online portals and customer care numbers for any 
assistance to directly address  their issues to the concerned bank b ranches. Further, the Bo ard o f 
Directors of individual b anks lay down appropriate grievance redressal mechanisms within the 
organization to resolve customer grievances. If grievances involving deficiency in services rendered 
by entities regulated by RBI are not resolved to the satisfa ction of the customers or not replied to 
within a period of 30 days by the regulated entity, the customer can approach the “Reserve Bank – 
Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021” that provides cost-free redressal of complaints. Government 
of India also hosts a web-based portal i.e. Centralized Public Grievance Redressal and Monitoring 
System (CPGRAM) wherein Citizens can file their grievances relating to Ministries/Departments of 
Government of India of States/UTs. 
Government has taken various steps towards the e ffective implementation of the Mudra Scheme. 
These, inter-alia, include publicity campaigns, simplification of application form, Credit Guarantee 
Scheme, nomination of Mudra Nodal Officer, frequent reviews at v arious level by Government and 
banks. Further, implementation and progress of the Scheme is  reviewed at State Level Bankers 
Meeting (SLBC) & District Level Review Committee (DLRC) levels.

entries.t: Economic impact of the Surge in Tourism in Himalayan Region
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.197 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
ECONOMIC IMPACT OF THE SURGE IN  
TOURISM IN HIMALAYAN REGION 
 
197. Dr. INDRA HANG SUBBA: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:   
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the economic impact of the 
surge in tourism in Himalayan region and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has taken any specific steps to sustain 
and further enhance this growth in the region and if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has any plans to introduce further 
infrastructure improvement and sustainable tourism initiatives 
including eco -friendly projects to accommodate the rising tourist 
numbers in the high altitudes in the State of Sikkim; 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with their expected timelines for 
completion; and  
(e) whether the Government has any ongoing projects in Sikkim to 
promote trekking tourism and if so, the details thereof?                                        
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM      (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a): During 2014 to 2025, the number of tourist visits to the Himalayan 
region has increased from 10.55 crores in 2014 to 40.78 crores in 2025, 
registering a growth of 286%. Improved tourist visits have generated 
higher employment and economic opportunities.  
 
(b): The Ministry of Tourism undertakes several activities to promote 
domestic tourism in a holistic manner. The Ministry annually organizes 
the International Tourism Mart (ITM) in the North Eastern States to 
showcase the tourism potential of the region, to dom estic and 
international buyers, opinion makers, influencers etc. The 13th edition 

of ITM was held in Gangtok, Sikkim to highlight the different tourism 
destinations and products of the State, including adventure tourism, to 
the domestic and international stakeholders. In addition, to sustain and 
further enhance this growth, the Governme nt has formulated the 
National Strategy for Adventure Tourism and the National Strategy for 
Sustainable Tourism.  
 
(c) to (e): Identification, development and promotion of tourism 
destinations and products is primarily undertaken by the concerned 
State Government (SG)/Union Territory Administration (UTA), while the 
Ministry of Tourism complements these efforts by extending financi al 
assistance to all States/ UTs including Sikkim, under its central sector 
schemes, such as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based 
Destination Development (CBDD), and Special Assistance to States for 
Capital Investment (SASCI).  
 
Sanctioned projects for the state of Sikkim under the SASCI 
scheme in the financial year 2024 -25 include the Skywalk, 
Bhaleydhunga, Yangang in Namchi and Border Experience in Nathula. 
These projects are expected to be developed in a period of 2 years. 
Further, under the CBDD sub -scheme, projects for "Kabi Chronicles: A 
journey through Unity and Heritage" and "Echoes of Valor: The Gnathang 
Valley Experience” were also sanctioned in the financial year 2024-25.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 198 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Construction of Kendriya Vidyalaya in North West Delhi  
 
198.  Shri Yogender Chandolia:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that North West Delhi is one of the most 
populous Parliamentary Constituencies in the country with over 40 lakh 
residents and a large number of Central Government employees, defence  
personnel and students but has only limited number of Kendriya Vidyalayas;  
(b)  if so, the details of existing Kendriya Vidyalayas in North West Delhi district 
along with student -teacher ratio and waiting list for admission during the last 
three years;  
(c)  whether the Government has received any proposal/request for opening of 
new Kendriya Vidyalaya in areas like Narela, Bawana, Rohini, Kanjhawala 
or Alipur of North West Delhi;  
(d)  if so, the present status of the said proposal and the criteria for openi ng a 
new Kendriya Vidyalaya;  
(e)  whether the Government is considering to sanction at least four new 
Kendriya Vidyalayas in North West Delhi; and  
(f)  if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
 
(a) to (f) Opening of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) is a continuous process. KVs 
are opened primarily to cater to the educational needs of the wards of transferable 
Central Government Employees including Defence &  Para-Military personnel, 
Central Autonomous Bodies, Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Central 
Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) by providing a common programme of education 
throughout the country. Proposals for opening of new KVs may be spons ored by 

Ministries or Departments of the Government of India/State Governments/ Union 
Territories Administrations, with commitment to provide requisite extent of land, free 
of cost, and suitable rent-free temporary accommodation for setting up a new KV, as  
per Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) norms.  KVs are not opened on the criteria 
of population/ area/ Parliamentary Constituency /District or State/UT. 
As per the information received from KVS, 47 KVs are presently functioning in 
Delhi, out of which, 10 KVs are already functioning in the Parliamentary 
Constituency of North-West Delhi, namely, PM SHRI KV, Sector-3, Rohini; PM SHRI 
KV, Sector-8, Rohini; KV, Sector -22, Rohini; PM SHRI KV, Sector -25, Rohini; PM 
SHRI KV, Sector -28, Rohini; PM SHRI KV, Sainik V ihar; PM SHRI KV, Paschim 
Vihar; PM SHRI KV, Air Force Station (AFS), Bawana; PM SHRI KV, Narela; and PM 
SHRI KV, Shalimar Bagh. 
At present, there are 06 KVs functioning in North West District, Delhi, namely: 
PM SHRI KV Sector -3 Rohini, PM SHRI KV Sector -8 Rohini, KV Sector -22 Rohini, 
PM SHRI KV Sector -25 Rohini, PM SHRI KV Sector -28 Rohini, and PM SHRI KV 
Sainik Vihar. The consolidated Student-Teacher Ratio across these 06 KVs is 29:1. 
Furthermore, as per the available records with KVS, the total number of

entries.t: Allocation of NCAP Funds to Bihar
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 199 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Allocation of NCAP Funds to Bihar 
 
199.  SHRI SUDAMA PRASAD: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of recent scientific studies indicating that parts of Bihar 
have emerged as hotspots of Particulate Matter (PM) pollution in the Indo-Gangetic Plain; 
(b) if so, the findings of the Government's assessment thereof; 
(c) whether any special action plan has been prepared for Bihar under the National Clean Air 
Programme (NCAP) to address biomass burning and rural air pollution; and 
(d) the funds allocated and released to Bihar during the last three years under NCAP and other air 
quality improvement programmes, along with the outcomes achieved? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d):  As reported by the Bihar State Pollution Control Board (BSPCB), no district in Bihar 
has been identified as hotspot districts within the Indo-Gangetic Plain region. Further, BSPCB has 
informed that air quality assessment in the State of Bihar indicates an improving trend in PM₁₀ and 
PM₂.₅ levels over recent years. The State-wide annual average PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅ concentrations are 
provided at Annexure-I  
 
CPCB identified Non-attainment Cities (NACs) across the country that have failed to meet the 
National Ambient Air quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM₁₀ for five consecutive years. 03 NACs 
have been identified in the State of Bihar namely, Patna, Gaya and Muzaffarpur, and have been 
included under National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) for implementing air quality improvement 
measures. These cities have prepared City Clean Air Action Plans to take measures to address soil 
& road dust, vehicular emissions, construction & demolition activities, biomass burning and 
industrial pollution. 
 
District/ City level Implementation and Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of District 
Collector/ Municipal Commissioner monitors the implementation of City clean air action plans. 
 
Further, Bihar State Pollution Control Board has prepared the "Bihar State Action Plan for 
Prevention & Control of Air Pollution" as per the CPCB’s “Guidelines for Formulation of State 
Action Plan”, which includes specific and comprehensive action to address emission from burning 
of waste, burning of agri-residues and household emissions to improve air quality in the State. 
 

State level Steering Committee under the Chairmanship of Chief Secretary and Air Quality 
Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of Additional Chief Secretary/ Principal 
Secretary, Environment Department periodically monitors the implementation of State Action 
Plan prepared under NCAP  
 
During the last three years, air quality performance based incentive grant of Rs. 80.21 crore has 
been released to Patna, Gaya and Muzaffarpur cities of Bihar under NCAP to implement air quality 
improvement measures. The details of funds provided to the Cities of Bihar during the last three 
years (FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26) are enclosed at Annexure-II.  
 
Air quality improvement in terms of reduction in PM₁₀ levels during FY 2025-26 as compared to 
PM₁₀ levels of FY 2017-18 for Muzaffarpur, Gaya and Patna cities under NCAP is enclosed at 
Annexure III.

entries.t: Strengthening of Higher Education Institutions and Implementation of NEP 2020 Reforms
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Strengthening of Higher Education Institutions and Implementation of NEP 2020 Reforms 
 
2. Dr. Hemang Joshi:  
Smt. Mahima Kumari Mewar:  
Shri Jashubhai Bhilubhai Rathva:  
Shri Ramesh Awasthi:  
Shri Shankar Lalwani:  
Shri Dileshwar Kamait:  
Shri Sanjay Haribhau Jadhav:  
Shri Haribhai Patel:  
Shri Madhavaneni Raghunandan Rao:  
Shri Rajpalsinh Mahendrasinh Jadav: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen higher education institutions through 
accreditation, research promotion and establishment of multidisciplinary universities; 
 
(b) the progress made in integrating skill development and vocational courses in higher 
education curriculum as per National Education Policy (NEP), 2020; and 
 
(c) the initiatives taken by the Government to improve the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER), equity 
in access for disadvantaged groups and internationalisation of Indian higher education? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a):  The Government has undertaken several measures to strengthen Higher Education 
Institutions (HEIs) in line  with the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, with inter-alia 
emphasis on quality assurance, research and innovation, and multidisciplinary education. 
To strengthen the quality of higher education, institutions are encouraged to obtain accreditation 
from the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), and reforms are being 
undertaken to expand accreditation coverage and strengthen the accreditation ecosystem.  NAAC 
evaluates institutions on various parameters including teaching-learning, research, infrastructure, 
governance and institutional best practices, and awards accreditation grades based on their 
performance. The accreditation process promotes quality assurance, accountability, research and 
innovation, and serves as an important benchma rk for institutional excellence and continuous 
improvement in higher education.  

 
To boost research and innovation, the Government has established the Anusandhan National 
Research Foundation (ANRF), which seeks to harness the research potential of universi ties and 
colleges, support academic research, and facilitate translational research in emerging 
technologies and national priority areas. The ANRF aims to mobilize ₹50,000 crore during 
2023–28, including ₹14,000 crore from the Central Government, with the remaining sourced 
from public sector enterprises, the private sector, philanthropies, and international bodies, 
through various funds such as the ANRF Fund, Innovation Fund, and Science and Engineering 
Research Fund. 
Other initiatives such as the Prime Min ister's Research Fellowship (PMRF), Scheme for 
Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration (SPARC), IMPRINT, Uchhatar Avishkar 
Yojana (UAY) and Institutions of Eminence (IoE) continue to enhance research capacity, 
innovation and collaboration between academia, industry and international institutions. 
Focus of NEP on research and innovation has propelled India’s ranking in the Global Innovation 
Index (GII) from 48 in 2020 and currently being ranked at 38th place in 2025. 
The Government has taken several measures to promote multidisciplinary and flexible higher 
education in line with the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020. The University Grants 
Commission (UGC) has notified the Guidelines for Multiple Entry and Exit in A cademic 
Programmes offered in Higher Education Institutions, facilitating flexible learning pathways and 
academic mobility through the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC). The Government is also 
implementing the Multidisciplinary Education and Research Improvem ent in Technical 
Education (MERITE) Scheme to strengthen research infrastructure and promote innovation and 
interdisciplinary research in Higher Educational Institutions.  
In alignment with National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the Government has launched the 
third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of 
Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA) for the period 2023 -24 to 2025 -26 
with an outlay of Rs. 12,926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the  earlier phases of 
RUSA, to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/underserved areas. Under the Multi -
Disciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU) component of PM -USHA, 35 
Universities have been approved for a total amount of Rs. 100 crore each.   
(b): The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 envisages integration of skill development and 
vocational education with mainstream higher education to enhance employability, 
entrepreneurship and lifelong learning.  UGC has notified the National Hig her Education 
Qualifications Framework (NHEQF), aligned with the National Credit Framewor

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 200 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
 
Coastal Regulation Zone 
 
200. SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY: 
  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the State Government of Karnataka has submitted any proposal seeking permission 
for removal of sandbars from rivers, lakes, estuaries and other water bodies falling under 
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) areas;   
(b) if so, the details thereof and the present status of the said proposal;   
(c) whether the Government is aware that accumulation of sandbars in rivers and estuaries is 
causing difficulties to movement of boats and fishing vessels and affecting the livelihood of 
local communities in CRZ areas and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to grant approval for removal of sandbars in CRZ areas 
and to hand over the removed sand to District Sand Monitoring and Management Committees 
headed by Deputy Commissioners for proper utilization and if so, the details thereof; and   
(e) the time by which necessary approval is likely to be accorded in public interest? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
 (a) & (b): The Ministry has not received any proposal from the Government of Karnataka 
seeking permission for removal of sandbars from rivers, lakes, estuaries and other water bodies 
falling under Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) areas. 
 
(c) to (e): To address the accumulation of sandbars in rivers and estuaries, which causes 
difficulties in the movement of boats and fishing vessels, the CRZ Notification, 2019 permits 
the removal of sandbars in CRZ-IB, CRZ-II, CRZ-III, and CRZ-IV areas, subject to obtaining 
prior CRZ Clearance. Further, vide Amendment Notification Nos. 5495(E) and 5494(E), dated 
24/11/2022, the Ministry has permitted the removal of sandbars in intertidal areas by traditional 
coastal communities only through non-mechanized manual methods under both the CRZ 
Notification, 2019 and the Island Coastal Regulation Zone (ICRZ) Notification, 2019. The 
State Governments and Union territory Administration may permit such removal of sand in the 
specified time period in a particular area along with a specific quantity subject to conditions 
such as registration of local community persons permitted to remove the sand manually and 
shall be renewed on yearly basis.

Coastal Erosion Mitigation in Kasaragod 
 
201. SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has identified erosion-prone coastal stretches in Kerala, including 
Kasaragod, under the National Coastal Mission; 
(b) the details of projects sanctioned during the last three years for shoreline protection, beach 
restoration and climate resilience; 
(c) whether any proposal from the State Government of Kerala for coastal protection works in 
Kasaragod is pending with the Government; and 
(d) the time-frame for sanctioning and implementing such projects? 
 
                                                           ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
 (a) and (b):  Coastal Protection Works are undertaken by the respective State Governments/UTs. The 
Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change is implementing the “Mangrove Initiative for 
Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI)” to restore, promote and enhance sustainability of 
the coastal habitats including climate resilience capacity. State of Kerala has submitted a plan for 
restoration and conservation of Mangroves in 13 hectares in Kannur district with a budget of ₹ 3.70 
crores for the period 2024-25 to 2028-29 and subsequently an amount of ₹ 1.68 crores has been 
released. 
 
As informed by the Government of Kerala, coastal protection works in Kasargod district are included 
under the Resilient Kerala Development Programme (supported by the World Bank) and Kerala 
Sustainable Coastal Protection and Climate Resilient Planning Project (ADB assisted).  
 
(c) to (d): No proposal pertaining to shoreline protection, beach restoration or climate resilience has 
been received for Kasargod from the State Government of Kerala during the last 3 years seeking 
central assistance or funding, as per the Central Water Commission, Ministry of Jal Shakti.

202. SHRI SURESH KUMAR KASHYAP: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any special action plan for the hilly States, particularly 
for Himachal Pradesh in order to control pollution, rejuvenate the river and strengthen 
environmental governance and if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the details of the projects sanctioned, and funds allocated and incurred for the conservation of 
rivers and streams, sewage treatment, solid waste management and pollution control in the hilly 
States, particularly in Himachal Pradesh during the last three years, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the details of the projects sanctioned for river and stream conservation, pollution control, sewage 
treatment and environment protection in Shimla Parliamentary Constituency, along with the funds 
allocated for the purpose and current progress and achievements made thereby; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to implement any special environment protection programme 
for the hilly States, particularly for Himachal Pradesh including  Shimla Parliamentary Constituency 
in order to address the environmental challenges posed by climate change, natural disasters and 
increasing tourism; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c) The Central Government has taken various regulatory and management measures to 
control pollution, rejuvenate the river and strengthen environmental governance in the hilly States.  
 
 For the control of pollution, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
(MoEFCC) has enacted Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 (SWM Rules, 2026) to ensure 
environmentally sound management of solid waste across the country, including the hilly States. 
These rules specifically delineate the criteria and actions to be taken for solid waste management in 
hilly and island areas and has enlisted the duties and responsibilities of the local authorities therein. 
Further, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has also prepared an advisory for management 
of solid waste in hilly areas and has circulated the same to the Member Secretaries of all the State 
Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/ Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) and Principal Secretaries 
of Urban Development Departments (UDDs)/ Rural Development Departments (RDDs) of all 
States/UTs on 22nd June 2026.  

 The Ministry has also launched the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) in January 2019 
with an aim to improve air quality in 130 cities (non-attainment cities and Million Plus Cities). City 
Action Plans (CAPs) have been prepared by all 130 cities, including those in hilly States. Seven 
(07) Non-Attainment Towns have been identified in Himachal Pradesh by the Central Pollution 
Control Board (CPCB) namely, Baddi, Damtal, Kala Amb, Nalagarh, Paonta Sahib, Parwanoo and 
Sundernagar. The Action plan for control of air pollution in all Non-Attainment Towns have been 
prepared and the implementation is regularly monitored in review meetings under the Chairmanship 
of Chief Secretary to Government of Himachal Pradesh. Air quality performance-based incentive 
grant of Rs. 25.73 Crore was provided to the 07 non-attainment cities of Himachal Pradesh during 
FY 2019-20 till 2025-26 for implementing air quality improvement measures through city action 
plans under NCAP. 
 
 The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) monitors water quality of aquatic resources in 
the country in association with the State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/ Pollution Control 
Committees (PCCs). Under National Water Quality Monitoring Programme (NWMP), 250 
locations [including 156 rivers (and dams)] are monitored in Himachal Pradesh. The State 
Government of Himachal Pradesh has notified the River Rejuvenation Committee (RRC) for the 
State and District Level Special Environment Surveillance Task Forces in the year 2018. Based on 
recommendation of RRC, Action Plans for the then identified seven Polluted River Stretches of 
Himachal Pradesh have been prepared by the SPCB. The review of the implementation of the action 
plans is taken by the Chief Secretary/ Additional Chief Secretary (Environment) / Principal 
Secretary (Urban Development) on regular basis. 
 
 
 A report titled “Environmental Assessment of Tourism in the Indian Himalayan Region” 
by the G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment (GBPNIHE), Almora was prepared 
in pursuance to the directions of the Hon’ble National Green Tribunal (NGT) in Original 
Application No. 178/2022 dated 09.03.2022 and Hon’ble NGT has directed all States and UTs of 
IHR to ensure effective, proper and time-bound implementation of the re

entries.t: Improving the Quality of Education in Government Schools
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-207 
ANSWERED ON –20/07/2026 
  
Improving the Quality of Education in Government Schools 
207. Shri Aashtikar Patil Nagesh Bapurao: 
 
  Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps to improve the quality of education in 
Government schools in the country; 
 
(b) if so, the details of schemes currently being implemented by the Government  to enhance 
learning outcomes and teacher training; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to increase funding for digital education and school 
infrastructure, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to reduce dropout rates, particularly among girls 
and students from economically weaker sections? 
 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing an integrated 
scheme for school education - Samagra Shiksha, which covers the entire gamut from pre -
school to class XII. The scheme treats school education as a continuum and has been aligned 
with the recommendations of NEP 2020 to ensure that all children have access to qual ity 
education with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment which should take care of 
their diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and make them 
active participants in the learning process. 
 
 Samagra Shiksha focuses on  improvement of quality of education by providing 
support for different interventions to all States and UTs, like in -service training of teachers 
and school heads, composite school grant to every school for providing a conducive learning 
environment, support for children with special needs(CwSN),  grants for library, sports and 
physical activities, support for Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, Tinkering Labs, ICT and digital 
initiatives, school leadership development programme, remedial teaching for academically 
weaker students, introduction of new pedagogical and curricular structure, NIPUN Bharat 
Initiative, child friendly and inclusive classrooms including ECCE facilities, Strengthening of 

School Management Committees(SMCs) and community led initiatives  and Experiential and 
Competency based Learning aligned with NCFs etc. 
 
Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) schools are being set up as NEP 
2020 exemplar schools and are expected to become the template for other schools. 
 
The Government of India conducts large -scale assessments to measure learning and 
education outcomes across the country from time to time. The PARAKH Rashtriya 
Sarvekshan 2024 was undertaken in December, 2024 by the N ational Assessment Centre, 
PARAKH, NCERT under the aegis of the Department of School Education & Literacy, 
Ministry of Education to understand the baseline performance under the National Education 
Policy (NEP) 2020 in development of competencies among the students at the end of the 
Foundational, Preparatory, and Middle stages (Grades 3, 6, and 9 respectively). 
 
 The Department has also implemented NISHTHA (National Initiative for School 
Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement) as an integrated teacher tra ining programme on 
DIKSHA, covering modules on digital pedagogy, use of ICT tools and technology -enabled 
learning. Further, NCERT, SCERTs, DIETs, BRCs and CRCs undertake development of 
resource material, digital content, training programmes and workshops t o strengthen teachers’ 
preparedness for digital education. 
 
(c): The Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under the 
Centrally sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha for strengthening of existing government 
schools for creation and augmentation of infrastructure facilities like toilets, clean drink ing 
water, electricity, library, laboratories and for setting up of ICT labs and smart classrooms in 
Government and Government Aided Schools having classes VI to XI , based on Annual Work 
Plan & budget(AWP&B) proposals prepared by them as per their needs an d priority and gaps 
determined from Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) database. These 
plans are then appraised and approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the 
Department in consultation with the State/UT as per the programma tic and financial norms of 
the scheme, physical and financial progress of works sanctioned earlier and availability of 
budgetary resources.  
   
(d):  Under Samagra Shiksha, there is a dedicated Inclusive Education component for 
various interventions such as Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBVs) residential schools 
from class VI to XII, for girls belonging to disadvantaged groups such as SC, ST, OBC,  
Minority and Below Poverty Line (BPL), Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas 
which provide residential facilities for both girls and boys belong

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 208 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Protection and Preservation of Wetlands in Assam 
 
208. SHRI KAMAKHYA PRASAD TASA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) the details of all the existing wetlands across the country, State/UT-wise, particularly in 
Assam; 
(b) the details of such wetlands that need protection and preservation, State/UT-wise, particularly 
in Assam; 
(c) whether any steps have been taken towards the protection and preservation of such wetlands; 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reason therefor; and 
(e) whether the Government has any plan for the wetlands to be converted into ecotourism, while 
allowing controlled recreational activities like birdwatching and nature photography etc. and if 
so, the details thereof? 
   ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b)  As per the National Wetland Atlas, 2021 published by Space Applications Centre (SAC),  
Ahmedabad, a total of 2,31,195 wetlands (area >= 2.25 ha) have been mapped in the Country. The 
State/UT-wise wetland distribution in the country including Assam is at Annexure. MoEF&CC has 
been advising and facilitating the State/UT Wetland Authorities in protection and preservation of 
these wetlands under the existing regulations including their ground truthing and boundary 
demarcation.  
 
(c) to (e)  MoEF&CC has taken several steps for protection and preservation of wetlands across the 
country, which include, implementation of Ramsar Convention on wetlands, centrally sponsored 
scheme of National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA) for conservation and 
management of wetlands in the country, Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 
under the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, a dedicated Wetlands Web Portal 
(https://indianwetlands.in), Mission Sahbhagita and Save Wetlands Campaign for peoples and 
stakeholders’ participation in the wetlands conservation and management,  Amrit Dharohar initiative 
to promote unique conservation values of Ramsar sites. The NPCA scheme and Amrit Dharohar 
promotes eco-tourism in and around the wetlands.  
 
Further, in accordance with “Whole of the Government Approach”, various other 
Ministries/Departments of the Government have been playing important role in restoration and 
conservation of wetlands. Some such crucial Programmes/Schemes are   Repair, Renovation & 
Restoration (RRR) of water bodies under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY), Jal 
Shakti Abhiyan, Mission Amrit Sarovar, Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee 
Scheme (MGNREGS), Atal Bhujal Yojana and Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban 
Transformation (AMRUT).

entries.t: Closure of Primary Schools due to Low Student Enrollment
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 209 
ANSWERED ON- 20/07/2026 
CLOSURE OF PRIMARY SCHOOLS DUE TO LOW STUDENT ENROLLMENT 
†209. Shri Virendra Singh: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government is of the view that the decision to close certain primary schools  on the 
basis of "low student enrollment" does not constitute a violation of the right to education of 
children residing in remote, poo r, tribal and backward areas in the Country, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is aware that a decline in the literacy rate and school attendance of 
girl children has been recorded in several villages following the closure of schools a nd if so, the 
details thereof; 
(c) whether any socio -economic survey has been conducted in the areas where schools have  been 
closed to assess which sections of society have been most adversely affected by the  deprivation of 
education; and 
 
(d) whether the Government is likely to ensure that before closing any school, a decision is  taken 
only after conducting a proper study of the geographical, social, caste and economic  conditions of 
that area, if so, the details of such a procedure? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and the opening, merger/closing of 
schools is within the purview of respective State Government and UT Administration -which are 
the appropriate Government under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) 
Act, 2009.  
As per UDISE +, Enrolment of girls (pre-primary to higher secondary) in the year 2024-25 
and 2025-26 is  11,93,34,162 and 11,96,30,456 , respectively, which reflects that participation of 
girl students has increased during the period. 
 
 The National Education Policy 2020 underscores that although consolidation of schools is 
an option that is often discussed, it must be carried out very judiciously, and only  when it is 
ensured that there is no impact on access (Para 7.4). The aim of the schoo l complex/cluster is to 
ensure greater resource efficiency and more effective functioning, coordination, leadership, 
governance, and management of schools in the cluster.

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of air and water quality under the National 
Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP) and the National Water Quality Monitoring Programme 
(NWMP) in Karnataka, including districts experiencing rapid urbanisation;  
(b) if so, the number of operational monitoring stations in Karnataka, district-wise; 
(c) the latest air and water quality data reported from such districts and whether any areas have been 
identified as polluted or requiring urgent intervention;  
(d) the steps taken under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) and other Central initiatives for 
conservation and rejuvenation of water bodies in the said State; and  
(e) the action plan to improve environmental monitoring coverage in semi-urban districts 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e):  Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB) carries out ambient air quality 
monitoring and water quality monitoring in Karnataka, in line with the criteria/ guidelines of Central 
Pollution Control Board (CPCB) namely, Guidelines for the Measurement of Ambient Air Pollutants 
(Volume-I: Guidelines for Manual Sampling & Analyses, and Volume-II: Guidelines for Real Time 
Sampling & Analyses) and Guidelines on Water Quality Monitoring, 2017. 
 
Karnataka State Pollution Control Board monitors water quality of aquatic resources at 358 locations 
in Karnataka.  Detailed break-up is given below:

The State wise data on water quality and details of parameters monitored are available at CPCB website 
https://cpcb.gov.in/nwmp-data/. 
The water quality data is utilized for identification of Polluted River Stretches (PRS) based on the level 
of organic load which is measured in terms of Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) levels. The PRS 
are classified under Priority Class-I to Priority Class-V , Priority- I being the most polluted with BOD 

value of more than 30 mg/l and Priority-V being least polluted with BOD ranging between 3-6 mg/l. 
This system of classification of the Polluted River Stretches or locations is given below:   
    
Priority Class I Monitoring locations exceeding BOD concentration 30 mg/ L 
Priority Class II Monitoring locations having BOD between 20.1 – 30.0 mg/ L 
Priority Class III Monitoring locations having BOD between 10.1 – 20.0 mg/ L 
Priority Class IV Monitoring locations having BOD between 6.1 – 10.0 mg/ L 
Priority Class V Monitoring locations having BOD between 3.1 – 6.0 mg/ L 
 
Based on exceedance of Bathing Water Quality Criteria parameter of BOD (exceeding 3 mg/L), CPCB 
during the year 2018 identified 17 PRS in 17 Rivers in Karnataka. Similarly, during the year 2025, 
CPCB identified 14 PRS in 14 Rivers in Karnataka. Details of Polluted Rivers Stretches are as below:

For rejuvenation of polluted river stretches identified by CPCB, action plans were prepared by River

Administration, under the overall supervision and coordination of Principal Secretary, Environment of 
the concerned State/ Union Territory for bringing all the polluted river stretches to achieve water quality 
levels fit for bathing purposes.  
 
Progress of implementation of action plans is reviewed by the RRC’s at State Level and by Central 
Monitoring Committee (CMC) constituted under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Jal Shakti 
at Central Level.  
 
Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), four Non-attainment cities in Karnataka have been

pollution mitigation measures as per the City action plans.

compliance with the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM₁₀. Davanagere 
recorded the highest improvement of 41%, followed by Hubballi-Dharwad with 23%, and Bengaluru 
with 17% improvement.

Navodaya Vidyalayas in Andhra Pradesh 
 
211. Dr. C M Ramesh: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether Government envisages to start one Navodaya Vidyalaya (NV) in each 
district of the country, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether it is true that only 13 districts out of 28 have NVs in Andhra Pradesh and 
if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether it is also true that 15 districts including Anakapalli do not have NVs in 
Andhra Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether any proposal has been received from Government of Andhra Pradesh 
for opening NVs in those districts; and  
 
(e) if so, the steps taken by the Government on the above proposals and timelines 
by when NVs are going to be opened in the above have not districts?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs is a continuous 
process which depends on the willingness of the concerned State Government/UT 
administration to make available requisite suitable land, free of cost, for construction 
of the permanent building and making available require d temporary building, free of 
rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent building is constructed. Sanction and 
opening of new NVs depends on approval by the competent authority as per extant 
procedures. As on date, a total of 694 NVs have been sanctione d across the 
country, including 28 additional NVs. 
 
At present, 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh have been covered under 
Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme. Further, two additional NVs, which were sanctioned in 
Prakasam (now Markapuram) and East Godavari (now Polavar am) on basis of
