GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO:- 212 
ANSWERED ON-20/07/2026 
 
Impact of Teacher Eligibility Test 
 
212.  Shri E Tukaram: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Central Government has assessed the impact of the Teacher Eligibility Test  
(TET) requirement on in -service teachers in the country including Karnataka who were 
appointed before the TET was made mandatory; 
(b) if so, the number of such teachers in the country, State/UT-wise including Karnataka; 
(c) whether the Central Government proposes to amend Section 23 of the Right of Children 
to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, to provide appropriate relief to teachers 
appointed before the TET requirement came into force, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken or proposed by the Central Government to help such teachers qualify the  
TET before the prescribed deadline, including ensuring that TET examinations are  conducted 
regularly; and 
(e) whether any transitional relief is under consideration and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (e): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of  the Constitution and the 
recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative 
domain of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. 
Accordingly, the data regarding the number of in -service tea chers, including those in the 
State of Karnataka, who were appointed prior to the introduction of the mandatory Teacher 
Eligibility Test (TET), is maintained by the respective State Governments and Union 
Territory Administrations. 
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated 01.09.2025, inter alia, held that 
the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the minimum qualifications prescribed under 
Section 23 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and 
is mandatory for appointment as a teacher in schools covered under the Act . The order of the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court may be accessed at the following link:  
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63764_Judgement_01- 
Sep-2025 pdf. 

Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide judgment dated 
29.05.2026 the Hon'ble Supreme Court extended the timeline for acquisition of TET  
 
qualification from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028.  The judgment dated 29.05.2026 of the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court may be accessed at the following link: 
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_Judgement_29-
May-2026.pdf 
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the judgment dated 29.05.2026 , has further observed that the 
respective appropriate Governments/authorities should endeavour to conduct the Teacher 
Eligibility Test (TET) periodically, preferably twice every year, with an interval of 
approximately six months between successive examinations, so as to afford eligible teachers  
a reasonable opportunity to comply with the prescribed minimum qualification. 
*****

Opening of Bank Branches in Valmikinagar 
 
†214. SHRI SUNIL KUMAR: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is committed to opening a bank in the West Champaran district of 
the Parliamentary Constituency of Valmikinagar in Bihar; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether a request has been made to the Government through a letter to open banks at several 
prominent places in West Champaran district of the said Constituency; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the time by which the Government is likely to open the bank 
there? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d) To ensure accessibility of banking services in rural and remote areas, the endeavour 
of the Government is to provide a banking outlet (Bank branch / Business Correspondent / 
India Post Payments Bank) within 5 kilometres radius of all inhabited villages in the country. 
Availability of banking outlets is monitored by a Geographic Information System (GIS) based 
application, namely, Jan Dhan Darshak (JDD) App.  Based on the data uploaded by Banks on 
the JDD App., 100% inhabited villages in Bihar are covered with banking outlets (Bank 
Branch/ BC/ IPPB) within a radius of 5 KMs (as on 30.06.2026).

Further, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has permitted Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, 
Payments Banks, Local Area Banks and Regional Rural Banks, to open bank branches 
anywhere in India without prior approval, provided 25% are in unbanked rural areas. 
Moreover, in pursuance of extant RBI guidelines, rolling out of banking outlets in uncovered 
areas is a continuous process looked after by the State Level Ban kers’ Committee (SLBC) / 
Union Territory Level Bankers Committee (UTLBC), in consultation with the concerned 
State/UT Government, member Banks and other stakeholders. Banks, inter -alia, consider 
proposals for opening banking outlets in the light of RBI’s i nstructions, their business plans

entries.t: Forest Conservation and Tribal Livelihood in Kandhamal
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 219 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Forest Conservation and Tribal Livelihood in Kandhamal 
 
219. SHRI SUKANTA KUMAR PANIGRAHI: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  the details of afforestation, forest conservation and biodiversity projects undertaken by the 
Government in Kandhamal district of Odisha during the last five years; 
(b) the details of funds allocated and utilised under Compensatory Afforestation Fund 
Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) and Green India Mission in the said 
district; 
(c)  whether the Government has undertaken any special programme for sustainable livelihood 
generation through Non-Timber Forest Produce, medicinal plants and bamboo-based 
industries in tribal areas of the said district, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  the measures taken by the Government to mitigate human-wildlife conflict in forest fringe 
villages of Kandhamal district of Odisha? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b)   The Government of India extended support for carrying out afforestation, 
reforestation, biodiversity conservation programme. Funds are provided under such 
schemes/programme such as Green India Mission, NCAMPA, Nagar Van Yojana, MISHTI 
etc. During the period 2021-22 to 2025-26, a total of ₹216.66 crore was allocated/received 
under CAMPA and the Green India Mission in Kandhamal district, against which ₹214.99 
crore was utilised. 
 
As per the information furnished by the State Government, Kandhamal district is covered under 
the Balliguda and Phulbani Forest Divisions. During the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26), 
afforestation, assisted natural regeneration, avenue plantation, soil and moisture conservation, 
and other eco-restoration activities have been undertaken under various forestry programmes. 
During this period, afforestation was carried out over 960 ha, assisted natural regeneration over 
18,650 ha, avenue plantations covering 670 road kilometres, and about 23.18 lakh seedlings 
were raised/planted. Soil and moisture conservation works and other restoration measures were 
also undertaken in accordance with the approved Annual Plans of Operation. 
 
(c)  Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) collection, value addition, processing and 
marketing support are being promoted through community-based institutions such as Joint 
Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), Eco-Development Committees (EDCs), Vana 

Surakshya Samitis (VSSs) and Self Help Groups (SHGs) under various forest development 
programmes. These institutions facilitate sustainable harvesting, aggregation, processing and 
livelihood enhancement for forest-dependent communities. In addition, the Ministry of Tribal 
Affairs, through the Van Dhan Vikas Yojana, supports tribal communities by promoting value 
addition, processing and marketing of NTFPs, including herbal and other forest produce-based 
enterprises. Efforts are being continued to strengthen community-based forest livelihoods and 
enhance income opportunities from NTFP resources in the region. 
 
(d)  The management of wildlife including mitigation of human-animal conflicts is 
primarily the responsibility of the concerned State Government/UT Territory Administration. 
The State Government/UT administrations are the first responders to any conflict situation and 
they maintain the details of the conflict along with the species involved. Ministry has issued 
advisories and guidelines to manage human-wildlife negative interactions through 
interdepartmental coordination actions besides adherence to SOPs in this regard. Use of 
technological aids are used to strengthen these interventions. 
 
*****

Development of Sports Infrastructure in Dhanbad 
 
†22. Shri Dulu Mahato: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite the presence of 
exceptional talent in  archery and football in rural and tribal areas of 
Dhanbad (such as Tundi and Topchanchi), there  is not a single SAI 
Training Centre in the district; 
 
(b) the reasons for the inordinate delay in approving a state -of-the-art 
sports complex under  Khelo India scheme for the youth of this major 
industrial cluster; 
 
(c) whether the tribal players of Dhanbad, who have won medals at 
national and State  level, are being provided the benefits of any special 
Central scholarship or financial incentive scheme  for advanced training, 
sports kits and nutritional support; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has any time -bound plan to upgrade the 
dilapidated Digwadih  and Golf Ground stadiums of Dhanbad under the 
infrastructure development fund of 'Khelo India'? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) and (b) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sp orts, including establishment of sports training 
centres and development of sports infrastructure, rests primarily with 
the respective State/Union Territory Governments.  The Union 
Government supplements these efforts by bridging critical gaps.  At 
present, there is no Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Centre (STC) 

Page 2 of 2 
 
in Dhanbad district, Jharkhand. However, SAI is operating two STCs in 
the State of Jharkhand at Hazaribagh and Ranchi, imparting training in 
disciplines such as Archery, Football, Hockey and Athletics. Athletes are 
inducted into these Centres through a transparent selection process 
from across the country, with due representation to eligible athletes 
from the State of Jharkhand. 
 
Further, t he Khelo India Scheme is demand -driven scheme. Propos als 
received from the State/UT Governments and other eligible entities are 
considered for financial support subject to their completeness, technical 
feasibility, infrastructure gaps, sporting potential, readiness for 
implementation and availability of funds under the Scheme.  
 
(c) Sportspersons identified under the schemes implemented by this 
Ministry, including those from rural, tribal and backward areas, are 
provided comprehensive support in accordance with the approved 
scheme norms. The support includes expert coaching, sports equipment, 
sports science and medical support, boarding and lodging, sports kits, 
competition exposure, educational expenses, medical insurance and 
stipend for their training and development. 
 
(d) No such proposal is under consideration in this Ministry.

entries.t: Establishment of Centre of Excellence in AI for Education
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 221 
ANSWERED ON- 20/07/2026 
 
Establishment of Centre of Excellence in AI for Education 
 
221.  Shri Rajiv Pratap Rudy: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of current operational status, organizational roadmap and 
implementation timeline for the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Artificial Intelligence 
(AI) for Education; 
(b) the location and selection criteria for setting up the five designated National 
Centres of Excellence for Skilling in AI, robotics, and cybersecurity; 
(c) the allocation of funds and resources out of the sanctioned corpus to integrate AI-
driven personalized learning platforms and adaptive curricula within Government 
schools, State/UT-wise particularly in Bihar; and 
(d) the measures taken to train educators in AI-assisted pedagogy to align with the 
technology integration objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020? 
 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) The Government of India announced the establishment of a Centre of Excellence 
(CoE) in Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Education as part of the vision to "Make AI in 
India and Make AI work for India" for a period of 5 years from 2025-26 to 2029-30 
with a total budget outlay of Rs. 500 Cr. The Ministry of Education has established 
the AI-CoE for Education at IIT Madras. The AI-CoE for Education is designed to 
offer AI enabled tools for learners across the country in alignment with the vision of 
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to integrate technology in education 
ecosystem. 
(b) The five National Centres of Excellence (NCoEs) for skilling that were announced 
in the Budget 2025-26, have been approved as a part of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling 
and Employability through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme. Under the scheme, 
five National Centres of Excellence for Skilling are envisaged in the National Skill 
Training Institutes (NSTI) located at Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, 
and Ludhiana with an aim to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational 
training in the country. These NSTIs were selected based on the parameters like 

 
 
land area of the institute, trade diversity, existing sitting capacity, scope for 
expansion and availability of faculty. 
(c) Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is a platform for providing 
quality e-content for school education along with QR coded Energised Textbooks 
(ETBs) for all grades. DIKSHA supports AI enabled personalised adaptive learning. 
Overall, 579.41 crore learning sessions for 2.29 crore users have been completed on 
DIKSHA by students, teachers and other stakeholders. Further, the National Council 
of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), in collaboration with Central Board 
of Secondary Education (CBSE), has developed resources for computational 
thinking and AI Curriculum for both teachers and students from grade 3 to 8.    
(d) To develop the capacity of teachers in leveraging technology, focused efforts 
have been made by NCERT in organising training activities on AI, covering more 
than 96,000 beneficiaries though these programs.  
Similarly, CBSE organises capacity building programme to sensitise teachers to the 
application of AI tools in teaching, learning, and assessment, as well as their 
relevance in educational management and administration. In last 03 years 1234 
programmes have been conducted, benefitting 64775 teachers of CBSE affiliated 
schools. 
Additionally, the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme (MMTTP) is a 
capacity-building initiative of the Ministry of Education, aimed at faculty members in 
higher education institutions. Under MMTTP, the Capacity Building Programme on 
Artificial Intelligence (CBAI) has been introduced for faculty members. The 
programme aims to modernise pedagogical practices and support the integration of 
emerging technologies within the higher education ecosystem. In addition to CBAI, 
MMTTP offers a range of Short-Term Programmes (STPs) and Refresher Courses 
(RCs) including on  E-Content Development, AI and Online Pedagogy. More than 
100 such programmes have been conducted benefiting more than 13000 
participants across these two initiatives.

entries.t: Market Study by Competition Commission of India
entries.head:
1 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 222 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, July 20, 2026/ ASHADHA 29, 1948 (SAKA) 
MARKET STUDY BY COMPETITION COMMISSION OF INDIA 
QUESTION 
222 Shri G Kumar Naik: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS                                                
be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Competition Commission of India has conducted any study 
on market concentration or oligopolistic tendencies in the telecom services, 
cement manufacturing, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the concentration indicators, including market shares, 
Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) or any other competition metrics, 
examined by the CCI in the above sectors during the last ten years;  
(c) whether the CCI has identified concerns relating to abuse of dominance, 
collusive conduct, barriers to entry or vertical integration in these sectors, 
if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the number of investigations, merger approvals and enforcement actions 
undertaken by the CCI in these sectors during the last ten years; and 
(e) the policy measures proposed to preserve competition and prevent 
excessive market concentration in these sectors? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGWAYS. 
(SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA)  
             ***** 
(a)& (b) Market studies are undertaken by the Competition Commission 
of India (CCI) to assess market structures, business practices, and 
competition issues across various sectors . In this regard, CCI 
conducted a Market Study on the Telecom Sector in India during 2020–
21 (“Telecom Study”). The objective of the Study was to assess the 

2 
level of concentration and competition in the telecom sector, highlight 
changes in competition strategies, analyse the dynamics of 
competition and cooperation between telecom services and related 
industries such as over -the-top (OTT) services, tower companies and 
infrastructure providers, and finally, examine regulations and policy 
developments from a competition standpoint. 
 No sector-wide market study specifically concerning concentration 
or oligopolistic tendencies in the cement manufacturing sector has 
been conducted by the Commission. However, competition concerns in 
the cement sector have been examined by the Commission under the 
enforcement and combination provisions of the Competition Act, 2002 
(“Act”). 
In assessing combinations involving the telecom and cement sectors, 
the Commission considers the factors specified under Section 20(4) of 
the Act. These include, inter alia, the parties’ market shares and the 
degree of concentration in the relevant market.  The Herfindahl –
Hirschman Index (“HHI”) is also used, wherever appropriate, as one of 
the analytical tools for assessing market concentration. Such 
indicators are considered alongside the specific facts and market 
conditions of each case. 
(c) :   The Market Study  on the Telecom Sector  in India highlights 
competition concerns relating to barriers to entry arising from high 
spectrum costs and data -driven network effects, and observes that 
competition issues arising from digital markets, data leverage, privacy, 
and vertical integration re quire case -by-case assessment under the 
Competition Act, 2002. The  study does not record any specific finding 
of collusive conduct and notes that existing vertical integration was  
generally viewed by stakehol ders as pro -competitive and not posing 
any imminent competition concern. 
(d)     During the last 10 years, the Competition Commission of India 
(CCI) has decided 29 combination cases in the telecom sector and 15 
combination cases in the cement sector. During the same period, the 
CCI directed investigations in 3 cases relating to the telecom sector and 
4 cases relating to the cement sector. CCI has also passed final orders 
in 6 cases each relating to the telecom and cement sectors  during this 
period. 
 

3 
(e)    The Market Study on the Telecom Sector in India  contains 
observations aimed at preserving competition, including promoting 
competition based on both price and non -price parameters such as 
quality of service (QoS), data 0speeds and bundled offerings; upholding 
the principles of net neutrality; facilitating transparent traffic 
management practices; encouraging infrastructure sharing and 
unbundling of infrastructure and services; assessing vertical 
integration and multi -sided markets, and strengthening inter-
regulatory consultation. 
 
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 223 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Restoration of Native Forests 
 
223. SMT. RACHNA BANERJEE: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of recent studies indicating that an increase in tree 
plantations does not necessarily improve natural forest biodiversity; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the steps being taken to promote restoration of native forests instead of monoculture 
plantations; and 
(d) the measures adopted to monitor the ecological quality of forests under various afforestation 
programmes? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c)  Forest areas constitute complex ecological landscapes comprising a mosaic of diverse 
ecosystems, including forests, wetlands, grasslands, scrublands, rivers, and other natural 
habitats. These interconnected ecosystems collectively support rich biodiversity, sustain 
ecological processes, regulate hydrological and climatic functions, and provide a wide range of 
ecosystem services. Accordingly, conservation and management of forest areas are undertaken 
through an integrated landscape approach that recognizes the ecological interdependence of 
these various ecosystems. 
 
Afforestation and eco-restoration activities in forest areas are undertaken with scientific and 
technical approach ensuring heterogeneous mix of native plant species. Apart from plantations 
the same principle is followed in seed sowing of grasses, sedges and seed sowing along soil 
moisture conservation structures. This is done to ensure a stratified, multi species floral 
composition in the forest which in turn supports faunal biodiversity. Such afforestation, forest 
restoration and biodiversity conservation programmes, with due emphasis on conservation of 
natural forests, restoration of degraded forest landscapes with use of locally suitable indigenous 
species, and enhancement of ecosystem functions lead to rich biodiverse forests. 
 
(d) The ecological quality of forest areas created and restored under various afforestation 
programmes is monitored through frameworks prescribed under the respective programme 
guidelines. The implementation and monitoring of afforestation activities are primarily done 
by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, which undertake periodic field 
inspections and assessments to ensure adherence to approved technical standards and the 

achievement of ecological objectives. Monitoring includes evaluation of plantation survival, 
species composition, regeneration, and site conditions, as applicable under the respective 
schemes. In addition, the biennial India State of Forest Report (ISFR), published by the Forest 
Survey of India, provides a comprehensive assessment of the country's forest and tree cover 
using remote sensing and field-based inventory. The report serves as an important national-
level tool for assessing changes in forest and tree cover, growing stock, forest health and other 
related parameters, thereby providing valuable inputs for evaluating the overall ecological 
status of forest landscapes and informing policy, planning and management interventions.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 225 
 ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
  
SKILLING IN TRIBAL DISTRICTS IN MAHARASHTRA 
 
225.  SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE:   
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has identified tribal clusters and Aspirational Districts in Maharashtra 
for implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability through Upgraded ITIs scheme 
and, if so, the details thereof, district-wise; 
 
(b)  the number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) located in tribal -dominated districts of 
Maharashtra selected for upgradation, along with the funds sanctioned, released and the progress 
achieved so far; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has assessed the challenges faced by ITIs in tribal areas, including 
inadequate industry linkages, shortage of modern equipment, faculty vacancies, language barriers and 
limited employment opportunities for tribal youth and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  the number of Scheduled Tribe trainees enrolled, trained, certified, placed and retained in 
employment under the scheme in tribal districts of Maharashtra, along with the placement percentage 
achieved, district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
 
(a) to (d):  The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a network of 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for skilling the youth belonging to all the categories. 
 
The ITIs are  under the administrative and financial control of the respective State Governments. 
However, the DGT has been implementing schemes to support the upgradation of ITIs. The Pradhan 
Mantri Skilling and Employability through Upgraded ITIs (PM -SETU) Scheme is being implemented 
across States/UTs, including Maharashtra, to upgrade the quality and relevance of ITIs. 
 
The selection of ITIs under the PM -SETU scheme is led by the respective State/UT Governments in 
consultation with industry, ensuring alignment with emerging skill needs and local industrial potential. 
Accordingly, the Government of Maharashtra has identified three (03) clusters, comprising 03 Hub ITIs 
and 12 Spoke ITIs, in the districts of Nagpur, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), and 
Pune. The details of the ITIs identified by the State of Maharashtra are placed at Annexure-I. 
 
Furthermore, the State Government and Industry Partner are empowered to propose the required 
investment for holistic upgradation of ITIs. At present, no proposal or Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) 
from the State of Maharashtra is pending for consideration or approval before the National Steering 
Committee (NSC). 
 
As of now, the MSDE has released funds to the Government of Maharashtra amounting to ₹50 lakh for 
engagement of a Project Management Consultant (PMC) and ₹30 lakh for Industry Outreach activities 
during FY 2025–26.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 226 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ECONOMY 
 
          226. Dr. Bachhav Shobha Dinesh: 
                  Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi: 
                  Ms. Praniti Sushilkumar Shinde: 
                  Shri Vishaldada Prakashbapu Patil: 
 
 
          Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated or proposes to formulate a national 
strategy for the promotion and development of the cultural and creative 
economy, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
 
(b) the details of the key sectors identified under the cultural and creative 
activities, including media, design, arts, heritage and creative services, if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether any stakeholder consultations, research studies and institutional 
mechanisms are being undertaken to strengthen policy support and governance, 
if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) the details of steps taken by the Government to promote employment, 
entrepreneurship and global competitiveness in this sector; and 
 
(e) the expected contribution of this sector to economic growth and cultural 
diplomacy particularly in Maharashtra? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) The Ministry of Culture has formulated a Cultural and Creative Economy 
intervention, namely Rachnatmak Bharat, for the promotion and development of 
the cultural and creative economy. The proposed strategy envisages 
interventions for capacity building, market access, innovation, digital 
enablement and institutional strengthening with a view to promoting sustainable 
growth of the creative economy, including support for emerging artists and 
creative practitioners. 
 
(b) The proposed intervention broadly covers sectors such as visual arts, performing 
arts, museums, cultural heritage, architecture, digital creative industries and 
other creative services. 
 

 
(c) The Ministry regularly engages with stakeholders, experts, cultural institutions 
and other Ministries/Departments, as and when required, for policy formulation 
and implementation of its programmes. 
 
(d) The Ministry promotes cultural activities through preservation and promotion of 
cultural heritage, support to artists and cultural institutions, organization of 
cultural events, and international cultural exchanges, which contribute to 
employment and livelihood opportunities in the cultural sector. 
 
(e) The initiatives of the Ministry contribute to the promotion of India's cultural 
heritage, tourism, cultural exchanges and livelihood opportunities across the 
country, including the State of Maharashtra. No State-specific assessment of the 
contribution of the cultural and creative sector to economic growth or cultural 
diplomacy is maintained by the Ministry.

Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:

the National Career Service (NCS) portal more user -friendly, 
accessible and effective and if so, the details thereof;

operational and their role in promoting to the NCS portal uses 
along with MCCs registered job seekers, employers and 
employment opportunities provided in the country, State/UT -
wise particularly Shimla and Jalgaon Lok Sabha constituencies;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to    implement any special 
action plan to enhance employment opportunities and launch a 
single-window digital platform integrating employment, skilling 
and career guidance services in the country and if so, the 
details and the timeline thereof, State/UT -wise, especially in 
Shimla Lok Sabha Constituency;  
(d) whether the NCS Portal is providing AI -powered skill 
assessment, job matching algorithms and forecasting of future 
skill requirements and if so, the details thereof; and

and other advanced technologies to improve job matching and

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The National Career Service (NCS) Portal is a one -stop solution 
for providing career related services including jobs from private and 
government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job search 
& matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill 
development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a digital 
platform [www.ncs.gov.in] to all stakeholders across the country.  
 
NCS has been upgraded to cloud -based, open architecture which 
enables skill providers, other private portals, start -ups, ed -techs, HR -
tech companies, local enterprises, etc. to build their own applications, 
services, and solutions using open APIs, open standards, and 
interoperable protocols of NCS portal. 
The NCS project also inter alia, envisaged setting up of Model 
Career Centres (MCCs) in collaboration with States/Institutions to deliver 
career related services. Till date the Government has approved 407 
Model Career Centres across the country. State/UT -wise details of the 
number of Model Career Centres including in the State of Rajasthan may 
be seen 
https://www.ncs.gov.in/User_Manuals/List_of_Model_Career_Centers.pdf 
The State/UT -wise and district -wise details of jobseeker and 
employer registered, and number of vacancies mobilized on NCS portal 
(including through MCCs) across the country may be seen at 
https://www.ncs.gov.in/_layouts/15/ncsp/ViewStaticReport.aspx  
Further, NCS portal provides AI -enabled features like intelligent job 
matching, AI skill gap analysis, personalized job recommendations, AI 
interview coach, multilingual support through Bhasini, etc.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  23 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Mental Pressure of Examination on Primary School Students 
 
†23. Shri Murari Lal Meena:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether educational experts and parents are expressing the need to reduce the increasing 
mental pressure of examinations on primary school students and to encourage their holistic 
development, if so, the view of the Government in this regard;  
 
(b) whether the Government is considering making Continuous and Comprehensive 
Evaluation (CCE) or any other child -friendly evaluation system more effective instead of 
traditional annual examinations for students of Classes 1 to 5, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to deliberate with the States regarding the 
implementation of a two-day weekly holiday on Saturdays and Sundays, keeping in view the 
physical and mental health, family engagement, and hol istic development of primary school 
students (Classes 1 to 5) and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
 
(a) to (b): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of 
schools fall under the administrative control of the respective State Government/Union 
Territory (UT) administration.  On its part, the Ministry of Education is guided by , the 
National Education Policy (NEP), 2020  in all its efforts and initiatives. The NEP 2020  
formulated through extensive and participatory consultation with various stakeholders, 
including educational experts and parents,  emphasises joyful learning, play, discovery and 
activity- based pedagogy at foundational and preparatory stages (i.e. upto Class 5)  and 
transforming assessments for holistic development of learners. 
 
To this end, several initiatives such as the Jaadui Pitara and e -Jaadui Pitara 
(https://ejaaduipitara.ncert.gov.in), a collection of interactive learning teaching materials 
including toys, games, puzzles and story cards ; a three months play based ‘School 
Preparation Module and Guidelines’ for Grade I named ‘Vidya Pravesh’; and play and 
activity based text book for classes  – 1 and 2  have been launched by th e Department of 
School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education under the NIPUN Bharat Mission.  
 
Further, the NEP 2020  stresses upon  a shift in assessment system from one that is 
summative and primarily tests rote memorization skills to one that is more regular and 

formative, competency-based, and promotes learning and development of the students, and 
tests higher -order skills, such as  analysis, critical thinking, and conceptual clarity. It 
envisages assessment as a tool for continuously revising teaching -learning processes to 
optimize learning and development for all students. 
 
In pursuance of the NEP, 2020, the National Assessment Cen tre, PARAKH, NCERT under 
the aegis of the Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education has 
developed the Holistic Progress Card (HPC) for all stages of school education. The same 
are available in the public domain at the link  https://parakh.ncert.gov.in/hpc. The HPC 
designed for the foundational and preparatory stages, covering upto Class 5, is a holistic 
360-degree, multi -dimensional report that integrates teacher, peer and self -assessment to 
reflect the uniqueness of each learner in the cognitive, affective and psycho-motor domains.  
 
(c): With Education being in the Concurrent List of the Constitution , operational and 
administrative matters such as school holidays in majority of schools fall within the purview 
of the respective State Governments and UT Administrations.

(a) to (e): The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is continuously monitoring the 
evolving monsoon situation and the possible impact of El Niño conditions on agriculture in 
close coordination with the India Meteorological Department (IMD), various Indian Council of 
Agriculture Research (ICAR) institutions, ICAR- Central Research Institute for Dryland 
Agriculture (CRIDA), Central Water Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board 
(CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), the Department of Food and 
Public Distribution (DFPD), the Department of Fertilisers (DoF) and State Governments. 
Further, the Government has undertaken the following measures: 

1. District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) have been updated for 14 States 
covering 342 Districts which are likely to receive below normal rainfall by the ICAR 
Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA) in consultation with the 
States for implementation.  
2. Weekly meeting of the Crop Weather Watch Group (CWWG) is being held with the 
representatives of India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission 
(CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast 
Centre (MNCFC), Indian Council of Agriculture Research - Central Research Institute for 
Dryland Agriculture (ICAR - CRIDA), Department of Fertilizers, Department of Food & 
Public Distribution and the State Governments to review rainfall situation, reservoir 
storage, groundwater levels, crop sowing, input availability, market situation and pest/ 
disease incidence for timely intervention. Meeting with State Agriculture Secretaries 
and Relief Commissioners held under the chairmanship of Secretary (DA&FW) on 
27.04.2026 to review availability of inputs like seeds, fodder, drinking & irrigation water, 
fertilizers and general preparedness. Further, a meeting of the Crisis Management 
Group had been conducted on 17.06.2026 to assess and strengthen preparedness for 
the monsoon. In addition, the National Disaster Management Authority has also 
reviewed the preparedness of below-normal rainfall conditions emanating from the 
likely impact of the El Nino conditions on 19th June 2026. Review of the situation has 
been undertaken by the Agriculture Minister, Government of India with the State 
Agriculture Ministers for Kharif preparedness amid El Nino conditions on 23.06.2026.

Maharashtra, for operationalization of District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs). 
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) have also been issued by ICAR for Krishi 
Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) for mitigation of El Niño-related risks.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 (a) to (d) The Government has undertaken various policy and facilitation measures to 
promote cross-border e-commerce exports, particularly for Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, artisans and other small exporters. Key initiatives 
include: 
(i) The Export Promotion Mission (EPM), with an approved outlay of ₹25,060 crore 
for the period 2025–31, comprises sub-schemes Niryat Protsahan, aimed at 
improving access to trade finance for MSMEs, and Niryat Disha, focused on 
strengthening other export enablers. Interventions under EPM to specifically 
promote e-commerce exports include: 
 Provision of an Export Credit Facility for E-Commerce Exports to improve 
access to trade finance. 
 Facilitating Logistics, Overseas Warehousing and Fulfilment initiative to 
strengthen logistics and fulfilment capabilities of e-commerce exporters in 
overseas markets. 
 Partial reimbursement of mandatory international certifications required for 
exports to help MSMEs meet destination-country standards and technical 
regulations. 
(ii) Implementation of the E-Commerce Export Hub (ECEH) initiative on a pilot 
basis to create an integrated ecosystem for e-commerce exports by facilitating 
logistics, customs clearances and other export-related services. 

2 
 
(iii) Leveraging the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative to promote greater 
participation of district-level producers, MSMEs and startups in global markets 
through digital channels.  
(iv) Enabling exports through courier mode to avail benefits under the Remission 
of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP), Rebate of State and 
Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) and Duty Drawback schemes vide CBIC 
Notification No. 60/2024-Customs (N.T.) and Circular No. 15/2024-Customs, 
both dated 12 September 2024. 
(v) The Government has undertaken the following reforms to facilitate exports 
through courier mode and simplify related procedures: 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has relaxed export reconciliation 
requirements for small-value exports up to ₹10 lakh by permitting closure of 
export transactions in the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System 
(EDPMS) on the basis of declarations furnished by exporters and 
reconciliation undertaken by banks. 
 The per-consignment value limit of ₹10 lakh for exports through courier mode 
has been removed vide DGFT Notification No. 67/2025-26 and CBIC 
Notification No. 34/2026. 
 CBIC Notification No. 33/2026 has been issued to facilitate re-import of 
export rejects and returns, thereby simplifying reverse logistics for cross-
border e-commerce exports. 
The above initiatives are aimed at expanding participation of MSMEs and small 
exporters in cross-border e-commerce by reducing logistics and compliance barriers 
and improving access to export-related services. 
 
The Government is pursuing a multi-pronged strategy to promote cross-border 
ecommerce exports by strengthening export infrastructure, improving access to global 
markets and facilitating the integration of MSMEs and district-level producers into 
international value chains.

(a): The Government of India implements the Mission for Integrated Development 
of Horticulture (MIDH) for the holistic development of the horticulture sector, 
including the creation of post-harvest management and cold-chain infrastructure 
across the country, including Tamil Nadu.  
 
Under the scheme, famers/entrepreneur are allowed to use solar powered 
cold storage, pack house and cold chain infrastructure under MIDH thereby allowing 
farmers to store their vegetables and fruits at farm gate in controlled temperature 
before sending it to market and thus protecting them from distress sales.  
 
Further under the scheme, to strengthen the cold chain infra at primary side of 
the Cold chain which is managed by farmers and FPOs, Integrated Pack house 
(IPH) and Collection Aggregation centres (CAC) have been introduced as 
components which allows farmers, growers and FPOs to  grade, store in small micro 
solar based cold storages and transport their fresh produce to market without getting 
in distress.  These components also allow small 2 MT vehicles which allows farmers 
to collect and send their produce as per the market demand and thereby disallowing 
distress sales.  

 
Under AIF, there is provision for collateral free term loan upto Rs. 2.00 crore 
and interest subvention of 3% on the term loan availed for creation of post-harvest 
infrastructure including establishment of cold storages.  
 
(b): Under MIDH scheme, 10 numbers (9 under NHB and 1 under NHM) of cold 
storage with a total capacity of 0.68 lakh MT and under AIF scheme, 99 cold 
storage/cold chain projects have been sanctioned in Tamil Nadu. However, no 
proposal for establishment of solar based cold storage has been received from the 
State of Tamil Nadu.   
 
(c): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare continuously encourages 
Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), cooperatives, Self Help Groups (SHGs), 
entrepreneurs and agri-startups to establish decentralized post-harvest infrastructure 
by providing financial assistance under MIDH. Assistance is also available for 
integrated post-harvest management infrastructure to improve storage, aggregation, 
value addition and marketing of horticulture produce. Capacity building, convergence 
with institutional credit and project-based support further facilitate adoption of such 
technologies.

246.  SMT. MANJU SHARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान 
कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the potential for horticulture production 
across all States; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the details of the area under horticulture, its productivity yield and potential, 
State/UT-wise, including Rajasthan; 
(d) the details of the funds allocated, released and utilized under the Integrated 
Horticulture Development Mission during the last three years along with State/UT and 
district-wise details thereof in Rajasthan; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for 
their horticulture produce? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): According to the Working Group report on Crop Husbandry, Agriculture 
Inputs, Demand & Supply, 2024 by NITI Aayog, there is a vast potential to improve 
production of major food commodities including fruits and vegetables in the country by 
bridging the yield gaps.  
 
(c): The details of State/ UT-wise area, production and productivity/ yield of 
Horticultural crops in the country, including the State of Rajasthan, for 2025-26 
(Second Advance Estimates) has been given at Annexure-1. 
 
(d): The details of the funds allocated, released and utilized under the Mission for 
Integrated Horticulture Development (MIDH) during the last three years along with the 
details thereof in Rajasthan, State/Union Territory-wise are given in Annexure-2. 
However, district-wise allocation is being done by the States/UTs as per their 
requirement and potential. The District-wise expenditure reported by the State of 
Rajasthan is placed at Annexure-3. 

 
(e): Steps taken by the Government to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their 
horticulture produce are as under: 
 
i. Assistance is provided for development of infrastructure for post-harvest 
management and marketing such as storages, wholesale markets, rural 
primary markets, Kisan Mandies, etc.  
ii. National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) portal serves as a single window for 
creating an integrated national market for agricultural commodities, including 
horticulture commodities, providing better prices to the farmers through 
transparent auction processes and enabling farmers to sell their produce 
beyond local markets and reach buyers across the country. 
iii. Providing market information to farmers on prices and arrivals of agricultural 
commodities in regulated markets on AGMARKNET portal to enable the 
farmers to get better remunerative prices. 
iv. Market Intervention Scheme (MIS): Government is implementing the Market 
Intervention Scheme (MIS), as a part of the integrated scheme PM-AASHA, for 
protecting farmers from the distress sale of perishable agricultural and 
horticultural commodities, which are not covered under the Minimum Support 
Price (MSP). The Scheme has the following three provisions for supporting 
Horticulture Farmers whenever the prices are non-remunerative: 
 
• Procurement under MIS: On the receipt of request from the concerned 
State/UT Administration, Government gives sanction for the procurement of a 
predetermined quantity at the fixed Market Intervention Price (MIP) by the 
agencies designated by the State Government for a fixed period or till the prices 
are stabilized above the MIP whichever is earlier. Under Market Intervention 
Scheme (MIS), Central Share of losses, if any (at 50:50 basis for general States 
and 75: 25 basis for NE States), incurred in implementing MIS is released to 
the State procuring agencies as per the specific proposals received from the 
State Governments. 
 
• MIS-PDPS: This component of the Scheme provides for making Price 
Deficiency Payment for horticulture crops whenever the market prices fall below 
the Market Intervention Price, where the State Government does not have to 
do any physical procurement.  
 
• Transportation and storage subsidy for Tomato, Onion and Potato (TOP) 
crops: This component makes provision for providing transportation and 
storage subsidy to Central Nodal Agencies and State designated agencies for 
procurement of TOP crops from farmers where prices are below MIP and 
transport it to other locations where prevailing prices are high.

(a): The Government is implementing National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), a pan-India 
electronic trading platform, to facilitate transparent and competitive online trading of 
agricultural commodities. Integration of Mandis on e-NAM is done on the basis of proposals 
received from States/Union Territories (UTs).   From January to June, 2026, 134 mandis of

(b):   As on 30th June, 2026, 1656 mandis from 23 States and 4 UTs have been integrated

remunerative markets and reduce their dependence on intermediaries. Mandis integrated 
with the e-NAM platform provide farmers access to a larger pool of buyers, transparent

accounts. The platform also facilitates inter-State trade by enabling buyers across the

discovery and better price realization for farmers.

produce for better bargaining power and economy of scale.

 TO BE ANSWERED ON 21ST JULY, 2026 
  
Meri Samiti Mera Patal 
 
†249. Shri Miteshbhai Rameshbhai Patel: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the objectives of the "Meri Samiti, Mera Patal" initiative; 
(b) the manner in which the recently launched "Meri Samiti, Mera Patal" digital portal will 
transform the functioning and public outreach of cooperative societies in North India;  
(c)  the plan being formulated by the Government to extend this portal to all cooperative 
societies across the country; 
(d) whether any tangible benefits in areas such as identity, transparency and digital adoption 
are expected in Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and Self -Help Groups (SHGs); 
and  
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
  
(a) The “Meri Samiti Mera Patal” is an initiative which has been independently 
conceptualized and launched by Regional Institute of Cooperative Management (RICM), 
Chandigarh under National Council for Cooperative Training (NCCT). The objective of the 
“Meri Sam iti – Mera Patal” is to empower and modernize Primary Agricultural Credit 
Societies (PACS) by addressing their training needs, improving governance, and enhancing 
visibility. 
 
(b) This initiative facilitates creation of digital profiling of PACS and centralized, 
transparent, real-time data system to support informed decision -making. The implementation 
covers the jurisdiction of RICM Chandigarh, covering Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pra desh, 
Jammu & Kashmir, Delhi, Chandigarh, and Leh-Ladakh by RICM Chandigarh. 
 
(c) At present there is no such proposal to expand this portal across the country. 
 
(d) & (e) The following tangible benefits are expected in the implemented areas for PACS / 
Multi-purpose Cooperative Societies (MPCS) under this initiative:  

 
• Identity and Transparency:  Each PACS/MPCS expects to have a digital profile 
showcasing its history, membership, services offered, schemes availed, and governance 
structure. 
• Public Visibility: The initiative expects to enhance the visibility of PACS/MPCS in 
the public domain. 
• Real-time Data Transparency:  The initiative expects to promote transparency by 
enabling access to real-time data.

  250. SHRI BALABHADRA MAJHI: 
         SHRI CHAVDA VINOD LAKHAMSHI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the major initiatives taken by the Government during the financial year 2026–27 to 
promote climate-resilient and climate-smart agriculture, including the current status of their 
implementation in the Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) whether any region-specific crop diversification strategies and climate-resilient seed 
varieties have been promoted, if so, the details thereof, including the benefits extended to 
farmers in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency; and 
(c) the details of the financial and technical assistance provided to farmers for adopting 
Climate-resilient agricultural practices, including the number of beneficiary farmers and the 
assistance provided in the Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government through, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is 
implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) in the 
country including the State of Odisha. The programs include studies on the impact of climate 
change on agriculture, conducting district level risk and vulnerability assessment of 
agriculture to future climate change and integrated simulation modelling studies for 
estimating the future projections of climate change.  Further, ICAR has released 2900 
varieties during last 10 years (2014-2024). Out of these 2661 varieties are tolerant to one or 
more biotic and/or abiotic stresses. 
 
Government is implementing various programmes under the National Mission for 
Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) to ensure long-term sustainability and food security. Per 
Drop More Crop scheme to increase water use efficiency at the farm level through Micro 
Irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. Rainfed Area Development 
scheme is being implemented to promote Integrated Farming System for enhancing 
productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability. The Soil Health and 
Fertility scheme is implemented to assist states in promoting Integrated Nutrient 
Management through judicious use of fertilizers. Organic farming promoting through 
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana and natural farming through National Mission on Natural 
Farming scheme. “Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses”, National Mission on Edible Oils – 
Oilseeds, and National Food Security & Nutrition Mission promotes crop diversification.  
Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, Agroforestry & National Bamboo 
Mission also promote climate resilience in agriculture. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
along with weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme 
provides a comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crops, thereby helping 
compensate farmers for losses caused by natural calamities and climate-related risks.  

 
As reported by the Government of Odisha, during 2026–27, in the Nabarangpur 
Parliamentary Constituency, an area of 1,300 ha has been covered under the Crop 
Diversification Programme–Mega Lift Irrigation Project (CDP-MLIP), under which crop 
diversification strategies are being promoted. Under the Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) 
scheme, an area of 791.36 ha has been covered, benefiting 556 farmers, with a financial 
achievement of ₹243.46 lakh. Under the Special Horticultural Crop-Specific Scheme, an 
area of 93 ha has been covered, with a financial achievement of ₹245.91 lakh. Further, 
under the Development of Potato, Vegetable and Spices scheme, a physical progress of 
272.58 ha has been achieved, covering 2,386 beneficiaries. 
 
Further, under the Odisha Integrated Irrigation Project for Climate Resilient 
Agriculture (OIIPCRA), climate-resilient horticultural interventions such as hybrid vegetable 
cultivation, strawberry cultivation, and Low-Cost/Small-Scale Mushroom Units are being 
implemented to strengthen farmers' livelihood resilience. Climate-resilient hybrid vegetable 
varieties are also being promoted under the project. In addition, training and capacity-
building programmes on climate-resilient agricultural practices are being conducted at the 
Block and Gram Panchayat levels under the technical guidance of departmental 
officials.These interventions are aimed at promoting crop diversification, improving water-
use efficiency, enhancing horticultural production, and strengthening the resilience of 
farmers' livelihoods through sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural practices.

(c) whether the Government has assessed the functioning and financial viability of FPOs in

(d) the challenges reported by FPOs in accessing institutional credit, markets and value

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  As on date, 151 Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) have been formed in State 
of Punjab under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer 
Producer Organisations (FPOs).  District-wise details of FPOs formed under the Scheme 
are at Annexure. 
 
(b): Year-wise details of financial assistance released to FPOs in Punjab during the last 
three years, including Equity Grant and Credit Guarantee are at Annexure. 
 
In addition, FPOs are provided continuous handholding support through Cluster 
Based Business Organizations (CBBOs) and Implementing Agencies (IAs) for business 
planning, market linkages, capacity building and facilitation in availing benefits under 
various Government schemes. 
 
  

(c):   An evaluation of the Scheme has been carried out by the Department in 2025-26 
for all States including Punjab.  The mid-term evaluation indicates that the Central Sector 
Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations has 
created a substantial institutional base for farmer collectivisation. The assessment of 400 
FPOs shows strong progress on formal institutional and compliance-related indicators. 
Around 93.5% of assessed FPOs covered four or more Gram Panchayats; 92% achieved 
full license /registration compliance; 89% completed LMS modules with the CEO and 
accountant trained; and a large majority submitted audited financial statements. These 
findings indicate that the scheme has made visible progress in creating formal FPO 
structures, expanding member outreach and strengthening basic institutional readiness. 
 
(d) & (e):  FPOs formed under the Scheme including the FPOs in State of Punjab, are 
provided both financial and other support through various interventions by the Government, 
to strengthen them, improve farmers' income, enhance market access, facilitate access to 
institutional credit and promote value addition. These include: 
i. Management Cost up to ₹18 lakh per FPO over a period of three years to meet 
managerial and operational expenses. 
ii. Matching Equity Grant of up to ₹15 lakh per FPO, to strengthen the equity base 
of FPOs.  
iii. Credit Guarantee Facility for project loans of up to ₹2 crore per FPO to improve 
access to institutional credit.  
iv. Continuous handholding support for five years through Cluster Based Business 
Organizations (CBBOs) for business planning, governance, market linkages and 
capacity building.  
v. Capacity-building, training and skill development programmes for Chief Executive 
Officers (CEOs), Board of Directors (BoDs) and members of FPOs.  
vi. Facilitation in obtaining input licences and dealerships.  In Punjab, 86 FPOs have 
seed licences, 80 FPOs fertilizer licences and 69 FPOs having pesticide licenses, 
enabling them to supply agricultural inputs to their member farmers and augment 
their revenue. 
vii. Facilitation of market linkages through digital platforms. 22 FPOs from the State 
of Punjab have been onboarded on National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) and 
recorded trade worth Rs.2.83 Crore. In addition, 118 FPOs are onboarded on 
Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC). Further, 63 weekly webinars have 
been conducted to support market access and buyer-seller linkages. 
viii. Seventy-four (74) FPOs have established processing infrastructure in the State of 
Punjab, thereby promoting value addition, reducing post-harvest losses and 
enhancing market competitiveness.

entries.t: Delayed Implementation and Utilisation Gaps under the FAME-II Electric Mobility Scheme
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 256 
ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
 
DELAYED IMPLEMENTATION AND UTILISATION GAPS UNDER THE FAME-II 
ELECTRIC MOBILITY SCHEME 
 
†256. SHRI ARUN KUMAR SAGAR:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the central schemes for the development of electric vehicles in the country;  
 
(b) the details of specific provisions made under these schemes with respect to the Faster Adopti on 
and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles (FAME -II) scheme and the establishment of 
charging stations;  
 
(c) the total number of electric vehicles sold under the aegis of these schemes so far;  
 
(d) the major challenges regarding the reach of these electric vehicle schemes; and  
 
(e) the overall impact of these schemes on enhancing electric mobility across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
 
(a) & (b):  The details of the schemes implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) 
for the development of electric vehicles in the country along with provisions for charging stations 
are as under: 
 
(i) Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME 
India) Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years 
from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme 
provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV 
public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh 
electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,197 electric buses (e -buses) 
have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was 
allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. 
 
(ii) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component 
Industry in India (PLI -Auto): The Government notified this sc heme for Automobile and Auto 
Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for 
Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of 
₹25,938 crore.  
 
(iii) Production Linked Incent ive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced  
Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage :  The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  
Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The 
scheme aims to establis h a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC 
batteries. 
 

 
-2- 
 
(iv) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) 
Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This 
scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e -
2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e -Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public cha rging stations 
(EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation 
of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e -buses out of which 
13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e -buses have been 
approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for 
deployment of EV Public Charging Station on pan India basis.   
 
(v) PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme: This Scheme notified on 
28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 
electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to pr ovide payment security to e -bus operators in 
case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). 
 
(vi) Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India 
(SPMEPCI) was notified on 15 th March, 2024 to promote the manufacturing of elect ric cars in 
India. This scheme requires applicants to invest a minimum of ₹4,150 crore and to achieve a 
minimum DVA of 25% at the end of the third year and DVA of 50% at the end of the fifth year. 
 
 Further, following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to 
increase the use of electric vehicles in the country:– 
i. GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been 
reduced to 5%. 
ii. Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles 
will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. 
iii. MoRTH issued advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce 
the initial cost of EVs.

storage and value addition infrastructure in the country;

Rajasthan and if so, the details thereof, including measures taken by the Government to 
encourage participation of the private sector and dairy cooperatives;   
 
(c) the steps being taken by the Government to enhance milk processing capacity and 
farmer’s remuneration, particularly for small and marginal dairy producers; and   
 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen extension services, capacity 
building, awareness programmes and last -mile delivery mechanisms so as to ensure wider 
adoption of improved technologies and best practices in the livestock sector?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING

packaging facilities  and value-added dairy product manufacturing units, cold storage ,

Dairy Cooperatives and Section 8 companies.

a Credit Guarantee Trust to provide Credit Guarantee up to 25% of term loan to MSME and 
Dairy Cooperatives. The Trust is maintained by NABARD through its subsidiary NAB 
Sanrakshan Trustee Pvt. Ltd.  Eligible Entities can also take benefit of dovetailing with various 
Central and State Government initiatives to ensure holistic growth of the dairy ecosystem.

258. SHRI KARTI P CHIDAMBARAM 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष और िकसान 
कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of MSP implementation and procurement for the year 2026-27 
Kharif season, including the estimated payout of Rs. 2.6 lakh crore across 14 crops; 
(b) whether any disparity exists in procurement infrastructure, Mandi access and 
farmer participation, as compared among the States, if so, the details thereof, State-
wise; 
(c) the steps taken to ensure timely payment to farmers, especially in Tamil Nadu and 
other southern States; 
(d) the details of the status of pulses and oilseeds procurement under the Price 
Support Scheme (PSS) in States of Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Haryana;  
(e) whether any State has reported delayed Central reimbursement affecting 
procurement operations, if so, the details thereof; 
(f) the extent of PM-AASHA scheme utilisation in this season, according to the data 
collected; and 
(g) whether any contingency measures have been prepared in view of monsoon 
variability affecting kharif sowing and procurement targets, if so, the details thereof ? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) undertakes 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) procurement of Paddy, Wheat and coarse grains, 
namely Jowar, Bajra, Maize and Ragi. MSP procurement of notified pulses - Arhar, 
Moong, Urad, Gram and Masur, oilseeds - Groundnut, Soybean, Sunflower, 
Sesamum, Nigerseed, Rapeseed/Mustard Seed and Safflower and copra is 
undertaken in Price Support Scheme (PSS) of PM-AASHA. The procurement is 
undertaken during 3 seasons in a crop year namely Kharif, Rabi and Summer, on the 
request of the respective State/UT Governments. As on date, no proposal has been 

received from any State/UT Government for procurement under PSS for the Kharif 
2026-27 season. The procurement infrastructure and mandi access varies across 
States depending on the production pattern of notified crops and the procurement 
requirements. Farmer participation under the scheme largely depends on the 
prevailing market prices. To facilitate timely payment to farmers across the country, 
including Tamil Nadu under PSS, the MSP is paid directly into the bank accounts of 
the farmers, through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism, thereby eliminating 
intermediaries and ensuring transparency. Government of Tamil Nadu has informed 
that to strengthen procurement operations, procurement centres under regulated 
markets are established. Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority 
(WDRA)-accredited warehouses, Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) 
warehouses and State Warehousing Corporation warehouses are utilised to facilitate 
procurement operations, ensure timely handling of stocks. 
 
(d): The detail of procurement of pulses and oilseeds under PSS in the States of Uttar 
Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Haryana during the year 2025-26 for Kharif, Rabi 
& Summer seasons is placed at Annexure. 
 
(e) to (g): Under the PM AASHA Scheme, no instance of delayed central 
reimbursement affecting procurement operations has been reported by any State. 
Procurement under PM-AASHA is undertaken on the request of the respective 
State/UT Governments. No procurement proposal has been received under the 
scheme for Kharif 2026-27. 
 
In view of the Monsoon variability, the State Governments have been advised 
to take necessary measures including updation of District Agricultural Contingency 
Plans in consultation with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), the 
Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA) and State Agricultural 
Universities to ensure availability of suitable seeds, promote agronomic practises for 
moisture conservation and crop diversification, strengthen irrigation and water 
harvesting infrastructure, review water storage, and establish and activate Drought 
Monitoring Centres at the State level. The Crisis Management Plan (CMP) for 2026 
has been updated and circulated to all States and Stakeholders.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 26 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
SOCIAL SECURITY COVERAGE UNDER E-SHRAM PORTAL 
 
26. SHRI AZAD KIRTI JHA:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the number of gig and platform workers registered on the e-Shram   
portal as of September 2025 in the country, State/UT-wise;  
(b)the number of the said workers covered under any other so cial 
security scheme or insurance benefit;  
(c)whether the Government has fixed any timeline for rolling out 
social protection measures for platform workers; and  
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26th August 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
seeded with Aadhaar. eShram portal is meant to register and support 
the unorganised workers by providing them a Universal Account 
Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. 
  As on 14 th July 2026, over 31.78 crore unorganised 
workers have already been registered on eShram portal. 
  State-wise details of gig and platform workers registered 
on eShram Portal as of September 2025 is at annexure -I.  Details of 
gig and platform workers registered on eShram portal enrolled under 
various social welfare schemes is at annexure-II. 
  In keeping  with the vision of the Budget Announcement 
2024-25 on developing eShram as a One -Stop-Solution for 
unorganized workers to have access to various social security 
schemes, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram– 
Contd..2/- 

 
:: 2 :: 
“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024. eShram – “One-Stop-
Solution” entails integration of different social security/ welfare 
schemes at single portal i.e. eShram. This enables unorganised 
workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and 
see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
  So far, fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ 
Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram 
to enhance social security coverage to unorganised workers, such as 
Pradhan Mantri  Street Vendors Atmanirbhar Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), 
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri 
Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Viksit Bharat -Guarantee for 
Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Pradhan Mantri 
Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri 
Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 
(PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM -KISAN), One Nation One 
Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradh an Mantri Matru Vandna Yojana 
(PMMVY), etc. 
  Apart from the above, eShram has linkages with National 
Career Service (NCS) for Job Opportunities, Skill India Digital Hub 
(SIDH) for Skill Development, Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan -dhan 
(PM-SYM) for Pension and convergence portal of MoHUA. 
  For the first time the definition of 'gig workers and 
'platform workers and provisions related to the same have been 
provided in the Code on Social Security, 2020 which has come into 
force on 21.11.2025.  
  The Code provides for framing of suitable social security 
measures for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating 
to life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection, etc. The Code provides for setting up of 
a Social Security Fund to finance these welfare schemes for which 
one of the sources is contribution from aggregators between 1 to 2% 
of annual turnover of an aggregator subject to the limit of 5% of the 
amount paid or payable by an aggregator to such workers. The Code 
also has provisions to constitute a National Social Security Board for 
the purposes of the welfare of gig workers and platform workers.  
 
Contd..3/-

  Further, the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, notified 
on 08.05.2026, mark a sign ificant step towards extending formal 
social protection to gig and platform workers. The Rules 
operationalize the provisions of the Code by mandating registration 
of gig and platform workers on the Central Government portal, 
requiring aggregators to share worker-related data through API or 
other electronic means, prescribing eligibility criteria for social 
security benefits, and strengthening accountability of aggregators in 
relation to welfare measures for such workers.  
  The Ministry of Labour & Employme nt has conducted 
multiple rounds of deliberations with Aggregators, Knowledge 
Partners, Platform Workers Associations, State Government/Union 
Territories and other organisations for social security framework of 
gig and platform workers to move forward for a comprehensive 
welfare scheme for platform workers across the country, as 
mandated under the Code.

SHRI GODAM NAGESH: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the major initiatives undertaken by the Ministry to strengthen veterinary and animal health 
services up to May 2026 in the country, including Chhattisgarh;  
(b)  the details of capacity -building programmes conducted for veterinarians and para - 
veterinary professionals in the country, including Chhattisgarh;  
(c)  the details of the proposed coverage of veterinary institutions and personnel under these 
initiatives along with the planned financial outlay for strengthening veterinary 
infrastructure and services in the country, including Chhattisgarh; and 
(d)  whether any State -specific projects, financial allocations, or action plans have been 
approved for Chhattisgarh under these initiatives and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) Animal Husbandry is State subject. However, the Department of Animal Husbandry & 
Dairying (DAHD), GOI provides following support to the States/ UTs including Chhattisgarh 
for strengthening veterinary and animal health services: 
i. Under Livestock Health and Disease Control Program (LHDCP) scheme, 100% central 
assistance is provided for vaccination of animals against four major diseases, namely FMD, 
Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF). 
ii. Under Establishment and Strengthening of Veterinary Hospital & Dispensary (ESVHD -
MVU) of LHDCP, assistance is provided to States/UTs for operation of MVUs on sharing 

basis. Total 4019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) have been made operational in the 
Country in 29 States/UTs under the scheme.

on sharing basis for prevention and control of state prioritized livestock diseases, 
strengthening of Disease Diagnostic Laboratories etc. 
iv. ICAR-NIVEDI has developed  National Animal Disease Referral Expert System 
(NADRES_v2) which can predict the possibility of disease outbreaks at district level 2-3 
months in advance supporting better preparedness and response.

sharing basis for training of Veterinarians and Para -veterinarians. During 2025 -26 Rs 
971.65 lakh  has been released for all the States including Rs 7.5 lakh for the state of 
Chhattisgarh for capacity building program . Under Assistance to States for Control of 
Animal Diseases (ASCAD) support is provided on sharing basis for prevention and control 
of state prioritized livestock diseases, strengthening of Disease Diagnostic Laboratories 
etc. 
(c) The strengthening veterinary infrastructure and services is under the domain of the State 
Government. However, DAHD, GoI has formulated Guidelines for minimum Standards of 
Veterinary Infrastructure in India and communicated to States/UT for adoption and 
necessary action. 
(d) Under LHDCP scheme, total budget allocated for the state of Chhattisgarh for FY 2026-27 is 
Rs 3162 lakh.
