disabilities in public recruitment and competitive examinations, including the benefits 
extended to candidates including for Nabarangpur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) whether revised guidelines have been issued regarding scribes, assistive technologies and 
examination accommodations and the status of their implementation, if so, the details thereof,

guidelines dated 10.08.2022 for candidates having less than 40% disability. These guidelines,

(a):  The movement of workers from rural to urban and vice-versa is a common 
phenomenon due to various socio-economic reasons. As per the Periodic Labour Force 
Survey (PLFS) conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation 
(MoSPI), the percentage distribution of workers engaged in the agriculture sector (covering 
both rural and urban areas) during the last three years are 46.1% (in 2023), 44.8% (in 2024) 
and 43% (in 2025).  
 
(b) & (c):    Agriculture is a State Subject. The Government of India supports the efforts 
of States through appropriate policy measures, various schemes/programmes, budgetary 
support and price support through MSP for improving the productivity, profitability and 
sustainability in the agriculture sector. The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
(DA&FW) has been implementing several Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes 
to support farmers, including marginal and small farmers, through improved access to 
institutional credit, training, modern agricultural technology and agricultural infrastructure. 
 
       Sustainable agricultural practices, including natural farming, micro-irrigation, organic 
farming and crop diversification, are being promoted through various Central Sector and 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes. The National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) promotes 
chemical-free and low-cost farming practices for improving soil health and reducing input 
costs.  Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) component under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PM-RKVY) promotes efficient use of water through drip and sprinkler irrigation. It 
supports judicious use of water resources and optimize water availability during lean periods.  
Organic farming is supported through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) and 
Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER), while 
crop diversification is encouraged under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY). 
Additionally, schemes such as Soil Health & Fertility (SH&F), National Mission on Edible Oils 
(NMEO)-Oil Palm, National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO)-Oilseeds, Mission for 
Atmanirbharta in Pulses are being implemented to encourage farmers to adopt climate-
resilient, high-value and diversified crops.  
  

 
       To improve access to institutional credit, the Government has taken several measures, 
including annual fixation of Ground Level Agricultural Credit (GLAC) targets for banks, 
prescription of Priority Sector Lending (PSL) targets, and provision of affordable short-term 
crop loans through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme and the Modified Interest 
Subvention Scheme (MISS). Capacity building and skill development of farmers are 
undertaken through Agricultural Universities (AUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). 
Structured training programmes are integral part of various schemes such as the Agriculture 
Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization 
(SMAM), and other flagship programmes like, National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), 
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), National Food Security & Nutrition

DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 267 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
IRRIGATION FACILITIES 
 
 267. SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M.: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed that 315 districts are vulnerable to El Nino and 111 
districts in 12 States are of primary concern due to poor irrigation facilities, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that 111 districts with irrigation coverage below 25% have been 
considered as high priority areas, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) Whether the Government has initiated contingency plans to face the challenge, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d) Whether the deficit in rain could directly affect kharif crops; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government through, Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC) has 
carried out a spatial analysis to assess the possible impact of El Niño on Indian agriculture. Based 
on the analysis, 262 districts have been identified as vulnerable districts based on the following 
criteria: 
 Low Surface Irrigation Coverage (< 50%): Districts where less than 50% of the agricultural 
area is covered by surface irrigation projects, leaving them majorly dependent on monsoon rain 
 High Probability of Low Rainfall (> 30%): Districts that have a greater than 30% probability of 
receiving below-normal rainfall during the monsoon.  
 Districts having more than 20000 Hectares sown area during Kharif season 2024-25.  
 
(c):  District-level contingency plans have been prepared for the identified vulnerable 
districts by Indian Council of Agricultural Research-Central Research Institute for Dryland 
Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA) in consultation with the States. Review meetings have already been 
held with States on the operationalization of district-level contingency measures. The Department 
is also monitoring the availability of quality seeds, maintaining National Seed Reserve of climate-
resilient and short-duration varieties, ensuring adequate availability of fertilizers, and regularly 
reviewing the implementation of contingency plans. 
 
(d) & (e): Deficit or below normal rainfall during the South-West Monsoon may affect the sowing, 
growth and productivity of Kharif crops, particularly in rainfed areas where agriculture is largely 
dependent on monsoon rainfall. The Government is monitoring the monsoon situation and crop 
progress on a continuous basis. Advisory has been issued to the States on El Nino preparedness, 
which includes seed planning, KCC and PMFBY coverage drives etc. Advisory has been issued 
to Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation for judicious 
use of water for irrigation. Further, States have been advised to make intensive use of Viksit 
Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB-G RAM G) funds for 
rejuvenating water conservation structures, such as farm ponds, check dams, canal desilting, and 
bori bandhans, to maximize rainwater harvesting by trapping every drop of early or residual rainfall 
and enhancing water availability for agricultural purposes.

(a) to (c) No such information has been received from the Government of Madhya Pradesh. Further, no proposal for the

received by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying from the Government of Madhya Pradesh. 
 
  Animal Husbandry and management of stray cattle including making availability of fodder for stray animals is a 
state subject. However, the Central Government is providing financial assistance to supplement the efforts of the State 
Governments through various ongoing schemes such as: 
 
(i) Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM):  This flagship scheme focuses on breed improvement, conservation  and 
development of indigenous breeds, and enhancing milk productivity. Under RGM, financial assistance is provided 
for setting up Gokul Grams (Integrated Cattle Development Centres) and Breed Multiplication Farms, which 
directly help to reduce the economic burden of maintaining cattle. 
 
(ii) National Livestock Mission (NLM): NLM provides subsidies for entrepreneurship development in the feed 
and fodder sector, aimed at addressing fodder scarcity across the country  and provides assistance for fodder

Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and Gaushalas for the construction of shelter houses, veterinary treatment, 
and providing food and water to stray/destitute animals.

Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details and the total number of training, leadership development and governance capacity-
building programmes for Women Elected Representatives in Panchayati Raj Institutions during 
the last five years, State-wise; 
  
(b) whether the Government has assessed the prevalence of proxy representation in Panchayati 
Raj Institutions and its impact on the effective participation of women representatives, if so, the 
details thereof; 
  
(c) whether the Government maintains data on Gram Panchayats and Panchayat-level digital 
governance systems in Maharashtra, including Jalgaon that have adopted Theme-9 (Women 
Friendly Village) under the Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDGs) and 
operationalised Mahila Sabhas, if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(d) whether the Government proposes to establish Panchayat Leadership and Governance 
Resource Centres for women representatives in Maharashtra, particularly in Jalgaon, if so, the 
details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a) Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. However, the Ministry has 
been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA) w.e.f. the financial year 2022-23 with the major objective of Capacity Building 
& Training (CB&T) of Elected Representatives, Functionaries and other stakeholders of 
Panchayats across all States/UTs for improving Panchayat Governance. Under the scheme of 
RGSA, the Ministry provides support for Capacity Building & Training of elected 
representatives, functionaries, and other stakeholders of Panchayats in different categories, viz. 
basic orientation and refresher training, thematic training, specialized training, panchayat 
development plan training, and leadership training, etc. A total of 34,14,342 Women Elected 

2 
 
Representatives were trained from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27 (as on 10th July 2026) under the 
scheme, including the State of Maharashtra. The State-wise details is at Annexure-I. 
In addition, on 11th March 2025, the Ministry launched a comprehensive specialised training 
module as part of “Sashakta Panchayat Netri Abhiyan” for building the capacity of Women 
Elected Representatives (WERs) of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to develop their 
leadership, communication, managerial & decision-making skills for effective women-led 
governance. A total of 1,53,616 WERs have been trained on this module as on 10.07.2026. The 
state-wise detail is at Annexure-II.  
(b) Yes, Sir. On the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj 
constituted an Advisory Committee in September 2023 to examine the issue of Women Pradhans 
being represented by the male members of their families and also to examine other issues related 
to proxy representation. The Committee submitted its Report with recommendations to the 
Ministry in February 2025, and the same has been accepted by the Ministry. 
The Advisory Committee recommended that the State Governments take necessary measures, 
including legal safeguards, capacity-building, social audits, and penal provisions, to eliminate 
proxy leadership in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and ensure real empowerment, autonomy 
and accountability of elected women representatives. Owing to the importance of this matter and 
its impact on women's leadership in PRIs, this Ministry has also constituted a Task Force on 17th 
April 2025 to provide an implementation roadmap for the States/UTs to practically execute the 
recommendations put forth by the Advisory Committee on the issues of Women Pradhans. 
(c) Yes, Sir. The Ministry has conceptualized the localization of sustainable development goals 
(LSDGs) through a thematic approach to comprehend global goals into local actions through 
planning. Out of 9 themes of LSDGs, Theme 9: Women-Friendly Panchayat aims to focus on 
gender equality and women's empowerment. Panchayats are mandated to prepare a plan for 
economic development and social justice. During the preparation of the Gram Panchayat

‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the States and Union Territories (UTs) 
are primarily responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation, and 
prosecution of cybercrime. The Central Government, through the Ministry of 
Home Affairs (MHA), supplements the efforts of States and UTs by providing 
policy guidance, technological support, capacity -building assistance, and 
financial resources to strengthen cybercrime management and enforcement 
capabilities.  
 
To strengthen the mechanism to deal with cyber crimes in a 
comprehensive and coordinated manner, the Central Government has taken 
steps which, inter-alia, include the following:

i. The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime 
Coordination Centre’ (I4C) as an attached office to deal with all types of 
cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.

(https://cybercrime.gov.in) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to 
enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, 
with special focus on cyber crimes against women and childre n. Cyber 
crime incidents reported on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, their 
conversion into FIRs and subsequent action i.e. filing of chargesheets, 
arrest and resolution of complaints, thereon are handled by the State/UT

iii. The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ 
(CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate 
reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the

ROLE OF AGROFORESTRY IN GENERATING RURAL EMPLOYMENT 
 
277. Thiru Dr. S Jagathratchakan: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the role envisaged by the Government for agroforestry in 
generating rural employment, strengthening climate resilience, 
promoting sustainable land-use practices and supporting 
livelihood diversification and the factors that have constrained 
its full utilisation despite its recognised potential; 
(b)  the programmes implemented by the Government for linking 
agroforestry with rural development initiatives, livelihood 
schemes, natural resource management activities and 
community-based development interventions; 
(c)  the achievements recorded under initiatives designed to 
encourage the adoption of agroforestry practices while 
enhancing income opportunities and environmental 
sustainability in rural areas; and 
(d)  the measures proposed by the Government for expanding 
agroforestry-based livelihood opportunities, strengthening 
community engagement and improving long-term socio-
economic outcomes in rural areas in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN)  
(a) to (d): As per the information furnished by Ministry of Agriculture 
& Farmers Welfare, Government of India introduced National 
Agroforestry Policy (NAP), 2014 to promote tree planting in 
agricultural landscapes, recommending establishment of a Mission 
for the organized development of agroforestry sector. In pursuance 
of the Policy, Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) under National 
Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) was implemented by 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare from 2016-17 to 2021-
22 to integrate tree planting with agricultural crops under the motto 

Page 2 of 3 
 
"Har Medh Par Ped", thereby providing farmers with an additional 
source of income and enhancing the resilience of farming systems. 
The scheme helped in generating on-farm employment, strengthening 
climate resilience and promoting sustainable land-use practices 
through integration of trees with crops/fruit trees, thus, contributed 
to improve soil health, efficient use of natural resources, carbon 
sequestration, biodiversity conservation and diversification of farm 
income through production of timber, fuelwood, fodder, fruits and 
other tree-based products.  
  Subsequently, from 2023-24, SMAF has been restructured as 
Agroforestry Component under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas 
Yojana (PM- RKVY). The scheme aims to ensure the availability of 
Quality Planting Material (QPM), including seeds, seedlings, clones, 
hybrids and improved varieties, to promote tree-based farming and 
increase tree cover on agricultural lands. Under this component, 
assistance is being provided for establishment of nurseries, raising 
Quality Planting Material (QPM) in existing nurseries, capacity 
building, and technical support through institutions such as ICAR-
CAFRI for effective implementation of agroforestry programmes. 
  Since the start of the agroforestry scheme, a total of 1725 
agroforestry nurseries have been established, around 1,594 lakh of 
quality planting materials (QPM) (saplings) have been raised and 403 
agroforestry nurseries have been accredited under the National 
Nursery Accreditation Protocol. 
In addition, under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS) of the 
Ministry of Rural Development, plantation-based activities such as 
Farm Forestry on individual and community lands were permissible 
works and contributed towards natural resource management, 
climate resilience, and livelihood enhancement.

†279. Shri Patel Umeshbhai Babubhai: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state:

Fisheries Cooperative Society (Diu), and Mahasagar Fish Farming Cooperative Society (Diu) 
cooperative institutions; 
(b)   the details regarding date of last election, present management status, reason and legal 
basis for administration by an administrator/Government official, reasons for postponement of 
elections and the probable time-frame for holding the next election in these institutions; 
(c)  whether any time-bound action plan is being prepared to ensure timely democratic elections 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  the maximum period within which re -elections must be conducted after a society is 
dissolved or an administrator is appointed? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH)  
 
 (a)  As per the information provided by the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and 
Daman & Diu , the Daman & Diu  State Cooperative Bank Limited, Daman; Mahakaleshwar 
Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Saudwadi and Shri Mahasagar Fisheries Cooperative 
Society Ltd. , Vanakbara were registered on 17.11.2015, 27.12.2010 and 10.12.1987, 
respectively. The Cooperative institutions are presently functional.   
 
(b) & (c)   The Daman & Diu State Cooperative Bank Limited, Daman has not held elections 
after its bifurcation from the Goa State Cooperative Bank Ltd. The Registrar of Cooperative 
Societies has intimated that the governing body of the bank constituted for day -to-day 
functioning of the bank, failed to hold election to elect new managing committee, was taking 
major decisions on important matters including advancement of loans and failed to quantify 
and transfer assets and liabilities from the Goa State Cooperative Bank Ltd. 
 
  Accordingly, in exercise of powers under Section 77A(1)(e)(ii) of the Maharashtra 
Cooperative Societies Act, 1960 as extended to the erstwhile Union Territory of Daman & Diu, 
the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS), UT Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and 

Daman & Diu (DNH&DD) appointed an Administrator in the bank vide Order dated 
03.06.2022 until further orders or till the finalization of the new managing committee 
whichever is earlier.   
  
Last elections in Mahakaleshwar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Saudwadi and in 
Shri Mahasagar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Vanakbara were held on 30.08.2019. RCS, 
DNH&DD found the Managing Committee of these societies negligent in the performance of 
its duties, as it failed to submit statutory books of accounts, did not properly maintain trading 
stock and cash book, and did not conduct meetings of the Managing Committee. Accordingly, 
RCS, in exercise of powers under Section 78 of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 
1960 as extended to the erstwhile Union Territory of Daman & Diu, appointed an Administrator 
in these societies vide Order dated 14.10.2022 until further orders or till the finalization of the 
new managing committee whichever is earlier.   
 
(d)  In respect of the Daman & Diu State Cooperative Bank Limited, Daman, there is no 
period prescribed for the tenure of the Administrator, appointed under the provisions of Section 
77A of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, as extended to the er stwhile Union 
Territory of Daman & Diu. 
 
In respect of Mahakaleshwar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Saudwadi and Shri 
Mahasagar Fisheries Cooperative Society Ltd., Vanakbara , as per Section 78 of the 
Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, as extended to the erstwhile Union Territory of 
Daman & Diu, the Registrar is empowered to appoint an Administrator for a period of four 
years in aggregate.

proposals amounting to Rs 2,797 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana

(a) the steps being taken by the Government to strengthen India's position in the 
global seed sector; 
(b) whether the Government has details on the initiatives taken to promote public-
private partnerships in the seed sector, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to address challenges posed by climate 
change and food insecurity through innovations in seed technologies and partnerships; 
and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
                                                      ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): Government has taken several measures to strengthen India’s seed sector and 
enhance its global competitiveness, which include the following: 
(i) The Government, through the National Agricultural Research and Education 
System (NARES), comprising 56 ICAR Institutes, 48 State Agricultural Universities 
(SAUs), 03 Central Agricultural Universities (CAUs) and 39 centres under the All India 
Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Seed (Crops), is undertaking research and 
development of improved crop varieties. During the period from 2014 to 2025, a total 
of 3,236 field crop varieties have been released and notified, of which 2,996 are 
climate-resilient varieties, including 587 extreme climate-tolerant varieties 
comprising 341 drought tolerant, 89 flood tolerant, 80 salinity tolerant, 59 heat stress 
tolerant and 18 cold tolerant varieties.

(ii) The Government promotes the production and multiplication of breeder, foundation 
and certified seeds of high-yielding and climate-resilient varieties, including varieties 
tolerant to drought, heat, flood, salinity and waterlogging, to ensure timely availability 
of quality seeds suited to diverse agro-climatic conditions across the country. 
(iii) During the past three years, the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights 
(PPV&FR) Authority has expedited registration of plant varieties, thereby enabling 
farmers, ICAR Institutes, State Agricultural Universities and private seed companies 
to protect the varieties developed by them. So far, 10,802 varieties of 219 crop 
species have been registered under the PPV&FR Act, out of which 5,689 varieties 
were registered during 2023–26. 
(iv) The Government has established an extensive institutional framework for 
production and distribution of quality seeds. At present, 229 Seed Hubs and 384 
Breeder Seed Production Centres are engaged in seed production. Further, 17 
State Seed Corporations and National Seeds Corporation Limited, along with national 
public sector organizations such as Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), 
Hindustan Insecticides Limited (HIL), National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing 
Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED), National Fertilizers Limited (NFL), Krishak Bharati 
Cooperative Limited (KRIBHCO), Indian Farm Forestry Development Cooperative 
Limited (IFFDC) and private seed companies contribute significantly to the production 
and distribution of quality seeds across the country. 
  

 
(v) To strengthen quality assurance, 178 notified Seed Testing Laboratories (STLs) 
are engaged in seed testing across the country. The Government also provides 
financial assistance for strengthening Seed Testing Laboratories, including support for 
International Seed Testing Association (ISTA) membership and technical audits for 
ISTA accreditation. 
(vi) Seed quality is regulated under the Seeds Act, 1966, the Seeds Rules, 1968 and 
the Seeds (Control) Order, 1983, as amended from time to time. These statutory 
provisions empower the State Governments to regulate seed quality, undertake 
inspections, testing and enforcement, and curb the sale of sub-standard and spurious 
seeds. To support the regulatory framework, a Seed Authentication, Traceability 
and Holistic Inventory (SATHI) Portal has been deployed in phased manner to 
facilitate end-to-end digital traceability in seed production, certification, inventory 
management and distribution, thereby enhancing transparency and quality assurance 
across the seed value chain.

PACS as PM Kisan Samriddhi Kendras  
†288. Dr. Sambit Patra:  
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state:  
(a) the total number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) in the country have been 
granted permission to function as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samridhi Kendra;  
(b) the actual number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) that are currently functioning 
as PMKSK;  
(c) the States where the pilot project for PACS training was conducted by the Government including 
the number of PACS provided training under the said pilot project;  
(d) in which States the pilot project of PACS training was conducted by the Government and how 
many PACS were trained under the 'Pilot Project'; and  
(e) the key learnings from the pilot project on Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) 
training? 
 
ANSWER  
MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) & (b)    The Government aims to operationalise PMKSKs in a phased manner, in all functional 
PACS.  PACS functioning as PMKSKs enables them to provide various quality agri -inputs like 
fertilizers, seeds, farm implements, pesticides, soil/  seed testing facilities, etc., to the farmers at 
Panchayat/village level itself, thus helping in improving the agricultural productivity. 
As per the data provided by States/ UTs, 38,974 PACS are currently operating as Pradhan Mantri 
Kisan Samriddhi Kendras (PMKSKs) in the country. 

(c) & (d)    The pilot project for PACS training was conducted in the year 2024-25 in 4 districts of 
4 states i.e. Himachal Pradesh (Una), Rajasthan (Jodhpur), Tamil Nadu (Theni) and Odisha 
(Sambalpur) in which 284 PACS were provided training by conducting 295 training programmes in 
which 85 ,219 participants were trained. Apart from the pilot project, the NCCT is conducting 
awareness programmes for PACS every year. Since inception of Ministry of Cooperation, the NCCT 
has conducted a total of 7 ,320 awareness programmes in the country for PACS through its 20 
institutes in which 6 ,00,602 participants were trained from the year 2022 -23 to June, 2026. The 
institute-wise position of number of programmes conducted and number of participants trained is 
given in Annexure.  
(e)    Key learnings from the pilot project on PACS training are as follows- 
• Training interventions have significantly reduced performance gaps and strengthened 
functional capabilities. 
• Participants have acquired new skills, particularly in DPR preparation, and gained a better 
understanding of government schemes.  
• Members are now more aware of their roles, responsibilities, and powers within 
cooperatives.  
• PACS have developed a clear understanding of converging schemes of different ministries 
to strengthen cooperative activities.  
• Members have gained a stronger sense of ownership and participation in cooperative 
institutions.  
•  Several PACS have shown interest in diversifying activities, including Common Service 
Centres, Jan Aushadhi Kendras, LPG agencies, obtaining license for providing high quality 
seeds, pesticides, etc., to farmers.

of Prime Minister-Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) across India, especially in 
Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details regarding the status of implementation of its components pertaining 
to agricultural mechanisation, agri-based entrepreneurship and rain-fed areas development 
across Andhra Pradesh, district-wise and in Prakasam District; 
 
(c) the details regarding the total number of beneficiaries (male, female and others) of 
PM-RKVY over the last five years, year-wise, component-wise, district-wise across Andhra 
Pradesh and in Prakasam District; and 
 
(d) Whether the Government has undertaken any steps to raise awareness regarding 
the benefits of PM RKVY amongst farmers, especially the new/upgraded components, if so 
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Evaluation study of all Centrally Sponsored Schemes, including Pradhan 
Mantri- Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) was conducted by Development 
Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), Niti Aayog. The Study covered 14 States across 
diverse agro climatic regions and the study was not district specific.  
 
For agricultural mechanization, the study mentioned that mechanization support 
through Customs Hiring Centres (CHCs) and machinery provisioning has shown alignment 
with smallholder needs, but not as standalone interventions. In regions where 
mechanization was integrated with input distribution and demonstration based activities, 
uptake and service utilization improved significantly. Further, it broadly recommended 
combining Custom Hiring Centres, seed delivery and farmer trainings, use of CHCs as 
integrated hubs and institutionalization of local technical facilitation teams to manage CHCs, 
monitor usage and ensure cross component coverage. With regard to Agri-entrepreneurship 
and Innovation, the study mentioned rationalizing it into value chain incubator platforms 
integrating agri processing, youth skilling, FPO support and innovating labs;, developing 

phased enterprise support frameworks that include infrastructure, branding, certification and 
market on-boarding; and suggested facilitating convergence with financial institutions and 
start up missions to ensure working capital access, book keeping support and mentorship. 
Apart from this, the study also recommended livestock development under integrated 
framing systems, bundling it with extension and backyard framing interventions.   
 
(c): The data regarding beneficiaries are maintained by the respective State 
implementing agencies. The State Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed the total

292. DR. SHASHI THAROOR: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that during the Puncha paddy cultivation season 
(December 2025-Early 2026), farmers in Kuttanad and other parts of Alappuzha and 
Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala faced a severe shortage of fertilizers, particularly urea, 
potash, and phosphate at the critical stage of crop growth, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether an allocation of about 43,000 tonnes of urea for the October-December 2025 
quarter, only around 20,000 tonnes was supplied to Kerala, resulting in a substantial 
shortfall, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of this shortage on paddy productivity, 
acreage and farmer incomes in the affected districts, if so, details thereof; and 
(d) the corrective measures taken by the Government since then and the steps being 
implemented to ensure adequate and timely supply of all essential fertilizers to Kerala for 
the ongoing and forthcoming agricultural seasons? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
 (a) to (d): State Government of Kerala has informed that farmers in Kuttanad and other 
parts of Alappuzha and Thiruvananthapuram Districts in Kerala did not experience any 
shortage of fertilizers particularly urea, potash and phosphate at the critical stage of crop 
growth during Puncha paddy cultivation season (December 2025 to Early 2026) in Kerala.  
As per Integrated Fertilizer Monitoring System (IFMS) report, against the cumulative 
requirement of 39090 MT of urea during October- December 2025 in Kerala, the availability 
(opening stock + supply) of urea was 44680 MT.  State Government of Kerala has further 
informed that since required quantity of Urea and other fertilizers were received during Rabi 
2025 cropping season, paddy productivity, acreage and farmers income were not affected. 
  
          The Government of India in order to ensure the adequate availability of quality fertilizers 
to the farmers, assess the requirement of major fertilizers, namely urea, Di-ammonium 
Phosphate (DAP), Muriate of Potash (MOP), Complexes and Single Super Phosphate (SSP) 
fertilizers, before each cropping season (viz. Rabi and Kharif) in consultations with States. 
Assessment is made based on agronomical requirement, soil health, cropping pattern, 
cropping area, previous sale etc.  Based on assessed requirement of fertilizers, Department 
of Fertilizers, Government of India supplies fertilizers to states by preparing monthly supply 
plan and ensure seamless availability of fertilizers. The movement of all major subsidized 
fertilizers is monitored through IFMS. Regular monitoring is conducted with States including 
Kerala to monitor the supply position and corrective measure is taken as per requirement.

or more rounds of selection. 
The  mandatory  eligibility  criteria  include  minimum  contiguous  land  
area requirement of 100 acres in non -hilly States and 25 acres in hilly States, 
North Eastern Region, Union Territories and States having population below 

one crore as well as availability of 90 percent encumbrance -free land at the 
time of submission of application. 
The selection of projects is based on Challenge mode with evaluation on 
parameters such as connectivity and site suitability, quality of DPR, the demand 
for industrial land, provision of services at site, policy enablers for ensuring 
investments in the developed park, being provided by the State/UT 
Governments. 
Applications meeting the mandatory eligibility criteria would be taken up for 
evaluation and scoring in accordance with the prescribed evaluation criteria as 
prescribed under the Scheme guidelines issued on 23.05.2026. 
The scheme does not propose to develop parks in any specific sector, however, 
weightage is allowed for proposals with sector-specific thrust and infrastructure 
requirements. No proposal has been received on the portal till date. 
Financial assistance upto Rs. 1 crore per acre is provided for eligible 
components listed in the scheme guidelines. This contribution is in the form of 
equity from the Centre, with land contributed by the State/UT Government. 
The Scheme design is flexible for creation of sector specific infrastructure,  
including for encouragement of MSMEs, wherever Stat e/UT Government 
proposes for such infrastructure provision, as part of its Detailed Project Report. 
Guidelines are available on www.dpiit.gov.in .

In order to safeguard  and promote local business interests, the FDI Policy on 

SBRT mandates that in case of foreign investment beyond 51%, 30% of the 
value of goods purchased should be sourced from India, preferably from 
MSMEs, village and cottage industries, artisans and craf tsmen, in all sectors. 
Similarly, the FDI Policy on MBRT mandates that at least 30% of the value of 
procurement of manufactured/processed products purchased shall be sourced 
from Indian MSMEs, which have a total investment in plant & machinery not 
exceeding US $ 2.00 million. The sourcing from agricultural co-operatives and 
farmers co-operatives would also be considered in this category. 
As per the FDI Policy, the quantum of domestic sourcing will be self-certified by 
the company, to be subsequently checked  by statutory auditors from the duly 
certified accounts, which the company is required to maintain. Furthermore, the 
onus of compliance with the provisions of the FDI Policy is on the investee 
company. 
The reporting requirements in respect of investments in India under the Foreign 
Exchange Management (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 are prescribed by 
the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the Foreign Exchange Management 
(Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-Debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019. 
Further, FDI is a capital account transaction and any violation of FDI regulations 
is covered by the penal provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act 
(FEMA). The RBI administers the FEMA, and the Directorate of Enforcement 
under the Ministry of Finance is the authority for the enforcement of FEMA. The 
Directorate takes up an investigation into any contravention of FEMA.

(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that the benefits of the "Yuva Sahakar scheme 
and 'Swayam Shakti Sahakar  scheme are not reaching to all eligible youth and women's 
cooperative societies in the Hisar Lok Sabha constituency in Haryana; 
 
(b) if so, the major shortcomings and challenges noticed in the implementation of these schemes 
along with reasons therefor; 
 
(c) the number of cooperative societies, youth and women's groups that have been provided 
financial assistance or other benefits under these schemes in Hisar Lok Sabha constituency so far; 
 
(d) whether the government has formulated any special action plan to address these shortcomings, 
enhance awareness, simplify credit availability, and ensure the effective implementation of these 
schemes; and

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
(सहकारिता मंत्री) (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (c) National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory organization 
under the Ministry of Cooperation, is implementing Yuva Sahakar and Swayam Shakti Shakar 
Scheme. Both the schemes are fully funded and supported by NCDC.  
Yuva Sahakar Scheme is being implemented with the aim to encourage newly formed cooperative 
societies with new and/or innovative ideas.  

The objective of Swayamshakti Sahakar Scheme is to facilitate access to affordable, cost-effective 
and reliable financial services to the poor including women Self Help Groups (SHGs) to undertake 
the common/collective socio-economic activities in order to promote sustainable livelihood.  
 
NCDC extends funding on a project basis. Under the Yuva Sahakar and Swayam Shakti Sahakar 
schemes, no cooperative from the Hisar Lok Sabha constituency in Haryana has submitted any 
proposal to NCDC. 
 
(d) & (e) NCDC through its 19 Regional Offices and 9 sub offices actively monitors the 
implementation of schemes and ensures access to timely credit flow to women cooperatives. Field 
visits/inspections are done periodically for proper monitoring of loan disbursement under the 
schemes.

(b) to (e) The Government is implementing a number of schemes to support farmers to 
access credit, inputs, training and marketing linkages. The benefits under the scheme 
can be availed by women farmers.  
 
 Under Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) concessional interest rates on 
short-term agricultural loans are provided to farmers through Kisan Credit Cards (KCC). 
Farmers (including women farmers) can avail Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans at a 
subsidized interest rate of 7% for their working capital requirement. Additionally, farmers 
who repay their loans promptly receive a 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI),

who have benefited from Agricultural credit subsidy under the Kisan Credit Card linked

are around 22% of 5.4 crores beneficiaries in financial year 2024-25.

for storage infrastructure, and marketing infrastructure other than storage, to the eligible 
beneficiaries including individuals, Group of farmers/growers, Self Help Group (SHG), 
Cooperative Marketing Federation etc. In order to promote women farmers and 
entrepreneurs including women Self Help Groups (SHGs), assistance in the form of 
subsidy is provided to all the women beneficiaries at a higher rate i.e. @33.33% instead

make farm machinery more accessible and affordable to farmers, financial assistance @ 
40-50% of the cost of machinery depending on the category of farmers is provided for

of the cost of machinery. The Farm Machinery Training and Testing Institutes (FMTTIs) 
imparts training to women farmers/ Technicians/ Engineers/ Unemployed youths/ 
Machinery manufacturers, etc. on latest technology of farm mechanization. 
 
Agriculture Technology Management Agency (ATMA) Scheme supports State 
Government's efforts and introduces latest agricultural technologies and good agricultural 
practices in different thematic areas of agriculture and allied sectors to farmers including 
women farmers through different extension activities viz; farmers training, 
demonstrations, exposure visits, kisan mela, mobilization of famers groups and 
organizing Farm Schools. As per ATMA Guidelines, minimum 30% of resources meant 
for programs and activities are required to be allocated to women farmers and women 
extension functionaries. 
 
The PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year to all eligible farmers through direct 
benefit transfer without gender discrimination, and has significantly benefited women 
farmers as   ensuring transparent and direct financial support to strengthen their income 
and participation in agriculture. A total of 2,18,66,774 women beneficiaries received 
benefits under the 23rd instalment of PM-KISAN Scheme.

EXPANSION OF SAIL BHILAI STEEL PLANT 
  
 
300. SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the expansion of the SAIL Bhilai Steel Plant from 6.8 MTPA to 10.2 
MTPA, including the estimated investment, implementation schedule and expected 
date of completion; 
 
(b) the estimated direct and indirect employment likely to be generated in Chhattisgarh 
as a result of the expansion project; 
 
(c) whether the Government has formulated any strategy to strengthen raw material 
linkages for the expanded capacity, including planning supply from the Satna-Singrauli 
coal belt and other domestic sources; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
 
(a)to(d): Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) has accorded in-principle approval for 
capacity expansion of Bhilai Steel Plant from 6.8 MTPA to 10.2 MTPA at an estimated 
cost of approximately ₹ 31,000 crore. The project completion timeline is 42 months. 
The project has a potential to generate direct and indirect employment during the 
construction and operational phases. All major raw materials will be sourced from 
SAIL's captive mines and domestic and imported sources.

NATIONAL DIGITAL LIVESTOCK MISSION 
 
301.  SMT. BHARTI PARDHI: 
SHRI NARESH GANPAT MHASKE: 
DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE: 
SHRI SHRIRANG APPA CHANDU BARNE: 
SHRI RAVINDRA DATTARAM WAIKAR:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) Whether the Government has operationalised the integrated National Digital Livestock 
Mission digital infrastructure across all states to enforce centralized health mapping and digital 
tracking for dairy herds, if so, the details thereof; 
 (b) the details of the advanced data encryption standards and blockchain -backed protocols 
deployed to protect livestock identity data from unauthorized database manipulation; 
(c)  the structural checks established within the unified portal to ensure seamless, real-time data 
synchronization across remote block-level mobile veterinary units; 
(d)  the criteria used to grant Application Programming Interfaces  (API) integration rights to 
scheduled commercial banks to automate collateral-free working capital loans for smallholder 
farmers; 
(e) the measures taken by the Gov ernment to host localized outbreak prediction models 
directly on the interface to assist field veterinary officers in active monitoring; and  
(f) the projected reduction in processing timelines for formal micro -credit applications 
following the nationwide deployment of this infrastructure? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) The Government has operationalized the Integrated National Digital Livestock Mission 
(NDLM) digital infrastructure across all States and Union Territories (UTs). Under this system, 

every registered animal is assigned a unique 12 -digit Tag ID, which serves as a permanent 
identifier for recording and tracking all animal -related activities, including vaccination, 
artificial insemination, deworming, treatment, and other veterinary interventions. The Tag ID, 
along with the complete history of activities undertaken on the animal, is maintained in the 
NDLM database and is accessible to authorized stakeholders for reference, monitoring, 
planning, and service delivery. 
(b) To protect livestock identity data AES-256 (Advanced Encryption Standard, 256-bit key) 
is used for ‘data at rest’  and ‘data in transit’ is secured using Transport Layer Security  (TLS) 
with RSA 2048 -bit certificates. This ensures end -to-end encryption using industry -standard, 
government-grade security. 
 
(c) Currently, Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) are not integrated with NDLM - Bharat 
Pashudhan Portal. 
 
(d) Department has received no request from any bank for Application Programme Interface 
(API) integration till date. 
 
(e) The National Animal Disease Referral Expert System (NADRES_v2) of Indian Council 
of Agricultural Research  - National Institute of Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease 
Informatics (ICAR-NIVEDI) can be accessed on the designated portal from anywhere anytime 
for advance preparedness and response. However, this module has not been integrated with 
NDLM – Bharat Pashudhan Portal. 
 
(f) As of now, there is no micro-credit provision under any scheme of this Department.

MECHANISM TO TRACK FIR REGISTRATION 
 
308.      SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Andhra Pradesh police officers who received dedicated 
training from the Bureau of Police Research and Development on sensitive 
handling of SC/ST atrocity cases,  including FIR registration, victim 
protection, and witness support, during 2024-25 and 2025-26; 
 
(b) whether the Government maintains a real-time monitoring mechanism to 
track FIR registration, charge-sheeting, and trial progress in SC/ST atrocity 
cases State-wise, including Andhra Pradesh's during the said period; and 
 
(c) whether the Central Government proposes to deploy Special Central 
Monitoring Teams or issue specific advisories to Andhra Pradesh given the 
persistent concerns regarding trial pendency and low conviction rates under 
the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BANDI SANJAY KUMAR) 
 
(a) to (c): Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are ‘State’ subjects under the Seventh Schedule 
of the Constitution of India. State Governments/ UT Administrations are primarily 
responsible for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of crimes 
through their Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs).  
 
 
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 308 FOR 21.07.2026  
Bureau of Police Research & Development (BPR&D) conducted a total of 118 
training courses on various topics in which 1120 police personnel of Andhra Pradesh 
were trained during the years 2024-25 to 2026-27. 
 
The Ministry of Home Affairs has taken a number of steps on issues relating 
to FIR registration, victim protection, witn ess support, charge -sheeting and trial. 
Steps taken are briefly mentioned as under:- 
(i) The Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) application is 
used by State/UTs police to track FIR registration, chargesheeting and trial 
progress of cas es including SC/ST atrocity cases. This system is implemented in 
Andhra Pradesh also. Digital platforms under CCTNS and State Police systems 
facilitate monitoring and tracking of FIR registration, charge -sheeting and trial 
progress of cases by the respective states including Andhra Pradesh.  
(ii) Under Section 173 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 e-FIR 
and Zero FIR provisions enable timely and accessible registration of cases.  
 (iii)  The Ministry of Home Affairs issue advisories to State s/UTs, from time to 
time, for effective implementation of the provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of

farm-sector suicides; 
(b) whether the State Government is required to update the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
Samman Nidhi (PM-PM KISAN) beneficiary database, and if so, the total number of 
eligible beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh as of May 2026; and 
(c) the market intervention mechanisms being deployed to prevent price crashes that 
trigger suicides among farmers in Andhra Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) :    Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) being implemented since 2016 is 
demand driven and voluntary for States/UTs as well as farmers. After implementing the 
scheme initially from Kharif 2016, Andhra Pradesh Government did not implement the 
scheme from Kharif 2020 till Rabi 2021-22.  Andhra Pradesh re-joined the scheme from 
Kharif 2022 season as a free crop insurance scheme, wherein farmers share of premium 
was also borne by the State Government.  However, after implementing the free crop 
insurance scheme till Kharif 2024, State Government decided to transit to voluntary model 
from Rabi 2024-25 wherein farmer has to enrol in the scheme by paying his/ her share of 
premium.  The participation of farmers under the scheme has decreased in Andhra Pradesh 
as compared to the original implementation by the State.   
 Further, the State Government has informed that no study has been brought to the 
notice of the Government establishing any relationship between the decline in enrollment 
and climate vulnerability or farmer suicides. 
 
(b): As per the PM-KISAN scheme guidelines, farmers who acquired land as of 01.02.2019 
(except for succession due to death) are eligible to get the scheme benefit.  The total number 
of beneficiaries in the Andhra Pradesh State under the scheme as of May, 2026 is 41.26 
lakhs. 
 

(c):  Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated agriculture crops 
on the basis of the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices 
(CACP), after considering the views of concerned State Governments and Central 
Ministries/Departments. While recommending MSPs, CACP considers important factors like 
cost of production, overall demand-supply conditions; domestic and international prices, 
inter-crop price parity, terms of trade between agricultural and non-agricultural sectors, the 
likely effect on the rest of the economy, besides ensuring rational utilization of land, water 
and other production resources and a minimum of 50 percent as the margin over cost of 
production. 
 The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of one and half times of the cost of production.  Accordingly, Government 
had increased MSP for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other Commercial crops with a 
minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from year 
2018-19 onwards. 
To realize the objective of MSP policy, Government procures cereals and coarse 
cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other designated state agencies to 
provide price support to farmers. Cotton and Jute are procured by Govt. at MSP through 
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively.  
Further, Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) under the integrated Scheme of Pradhan 
Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) for the procurement of agricultural 
and horticultural commodities which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the 
MSP regime is also implemented by the Government. The objective of intervention is to 
protect the growers of these commodities from making distress sale in the event of a bumper 
crop during the peak arrival period when the prices tend to fall below economic levels and 
the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 percent decrease in the ruling market 
prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request of a 
State/UT government, which is ready to bear 50 percent of the loss (25 percent in case of 
North-Eastern States), if any, incurred on its implementation. The extent of total amount of 
loss to be shared on a 50:50 basis between the Central Government and the State 
Government is restricted up to 25 percent of the total procurement value based on Market

entries.t: Income Generation by Farmers through Carbon Credit
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 312 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st JULY, 2026 
 
INCOME GENERATION BY FARMERS THROUGH CARBON CREDIT 
 
 312. SHRI UMMEDA RAM BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण 
मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) Whether any policy, framework or scheme exists to facilitate participation of farmers in 
carbon credit and carbon trading mechanisms and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) Whether any assessment has been conducted regarding the potential for income 
generation by farmers through carbon credit mechanisms and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) Whether any pilot projects or programmes relating to carbon credit generation in the 
agriculture sector are being implemented in the country and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to facilitate participation of small and marginal 
farmers in carbon credit initiatives? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी                                       (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) The Government has notified the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), 2023, 
under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, which provides the overarching framework for 
the development of the domestic carbon market. As reported by the Bureau of Energy 
Efficiency, Ministry of Power, under the Offset Mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading 
Scheme (CCTS), two methodologies have been approved for the agriculture sector, 
namely: (i) Methane Recovery from Livestock and Manure Management at Households 
and Small Farms; and (ii) Emission Reduction through Improved Management Practices 
in Rice Cultivation. These methodologies, along with the 'Detailed Procedure for Offset 
Mechanism', provide a framework for participation in the generation of carbon credits. The 
detailed procedure and approved methodologies are available on the Indian Carbon 
Market Portal (https://indiancarbonmarket.gov.in/offset-mechanism/MzI=). However, no 
such assessment has been conducted so far regarding the potential for income generation 
by farmers through carbon credit mechanisms. 

(c) & (d) The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is supporting 11 pilot 
projects on the Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) for carbon credit generation in the 
agriculture sector through seven Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) institutes 
and four State Agricultural Universities (SAUs). These projects aim to facilitate technical 
support and capacity building of the participating institutions, including the development of 
methodologies for carbon credit generation from various regenerative agriculture 
practices. 
Government has published the draft Detailed Procedure for Programme of Activities (PoA) 
under the Offset Mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS). The PoA 
framework is to facilitate the participation of small and marginal farmers by enabling 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and 
project developers to aggregate multiple small-scale farm-level activities under a common 
framework for carbon credit generation based on approved methodologies.

(a) the progress made in implementing the "National Strategy and 
Roadmap for Development of Rural Tourism in India", particularly 
concerning the creation of homestay guidelines and the involvement 
of local tribal communities;  
(b) the details of the measures taken/being taken to promote "Green and 
Eco-Tourism" in ecologically sensitive areas, including the 
development of wildlife environmental impact; and  
(c) the manner in which the Government is ensuring that new tourism 
projects under the Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD) 
scheme adhere to strict sustainability criteria, such as waste 
management, waste water recovery and the use of renewable energ y 
sources? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM                 (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (c): Development and promotion of tourist destinations and 
products, including rural tourism and eco -tourism is undertaken by the 
respective State Government/Union Territory (UT) Administration. 
 
With the aim to promote tourism in tribal areas, the Ministry of 
Tourism has issued guidelines along with template for formulation of 
proposal by State Governments and UT Administrations for 'Development of 
Homestays in Tribal Areas' (A sub -scheme of Swade sh Darshan Scheme) 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya  Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM -JUGA). The 
objective of the initiative is to develop homestays in tribal areas to promote 
responsible tourism and enhance livelihood opportunities for tribal 
communities. The guidelines also focus on technical upskilling and training 

of the Homestay owners. The said initiative includes development of 1000 
homestays with support of Up to ₹5 lakh for village community requirement, 
Up to ₹5 lakh for construction of two new rooms for each household and Up 
to ₹3 lakh for renovation of existing rooms for each household. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism promotes India in a holistic manner, through 
various initiatives. As part of on -going activities; promotion of Rural 
homestays and Rural Tourism is also taken up. In order to provide impetus 
for development of Green and Eco Tourism in the country, Ministry of 
Tourism formulated National Strategies for Eco Tourism and Sustainable 
Tourism and initiated Travel for LiFE  programme to promote sustainable 
tourism in the country and to encourage the tourists and tourism 
businesses to adopt sustainable tourism practices. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism under its infrastructure related schemes 
such as SD, SD2.0, CBDD etc. considers sanctioning a range of components 
which may enhance tourism facilitation at the destinations, as per project 
requirement including those related to tour ism core products, tourism 
activities, safety, sanitation, last mile connectivity, parking, general site 
development, soft interventions etc.  It’s implementation is the 
responsibility of the concerned State Government.

MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government of Tamil Nadu/ Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) has 
undertaken several research studies to address the major production constraints affecting 
maize, cotton, paddy and other crops in Perambalur constituency. 
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that 
maize hybrids [VGIH(M) 2, COH(M) 11 & COH(M) 12] suitable for drought-affected rainfed 
cultivation and improved new rice varieties (CO 58 & CO 59) have also been developed 
and released for cultivation in Perambalur constituency. Further, drought tolerant rainfed 
cotton varieties (VPT 2 & VPT 3) have been developed and released. Improved agronomic 
practices, including broad bed and furrow, mulching, moisture conservation, protective 
irrigation, foliar nutrient application, Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), System of Rice 
Intensification (SRI), and Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), etc. have been validated for 
enhancing drought resilience. Crop-specific nutrient formulations, namely “Cotton Plus" 
nutrient and growth regulator technology has been developed to reduce square and flower 
shedding and improve drought tolerance. "Maize Maxim" nutrient formulation has been 
developed to improve crop performance under moisture stress. 
(c): The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that 
the Perambalur constituency has 10 Integrated Agricultural Extension Centres at block 
level and 8 Sub Agricultural Extension Centres at firka level operated by the Government 
of Tamil Nadu promoting various Centre-State shared schemes. Uzhavar mobile 
application provides farmers with real time information and access to Government 
Services through single platform. The application provides information on agricultural 
schemes, benefit registration, seed stock, pest and disease diagnosis, e-market etc. 
Further, trainings are conducted on various Good Agricultural Practices from land 
preparation to marketing for the predominant crops cultivated in the constituency. 
The Department of Agriculture, State Government of Tamil Nadu has also informed 
that during 2025-26, 579 Metric Tonnes of seeds were distributed in the Perambalur 
Constituency comprising 363 Metric Tonnes of Paddy, 41 Metric Tonnes of Millets, 52 
Metric Tonnes of Pulses, 48 Metric Tonnes of Oilseeds & 75 Metric Tonnes of Green 
Manure Seeds. In addition, inputs like 32 Metric Tonnes of Biofertilzers, 49 Metric Tonnes 
of Fertilizers, 1546 Numbers of Machineries & Implements, 92 Metric Tonnes of 
Micronutrient mixtures, 6 Metric Tonnes of Organic Fertilizers, 27 Metric Tonnes Organic 

Inputs, 27 Metric Tonnes of Bio-Pesticides and 3 Metric Tonnes of Traditional Seeds have 
been distributed during 2025-26. Further, seeds, fertilizers and other agriculture inputs are 
distributed through 287 Primary Agricultural Co-operative Credit Societies (PACCS) at 
village level. 
The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Government of 
India is implementing the National Food Security & Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in 28 States 
(including Tamil Nadu) and 2 Union Territories with the objective to increase production of 
Shree Anna, Coarse Cereals (Maize & Barley), Rice, Wheat and Commercial Crops (Jute 
& Sugarcane) through area expansion and productivity enhancement. An amount of 
Rs.9422.155 lakh has been approved in the Annual Action Plan for the state of Tamil Nadu 
under NFSNM during 2026-27. Flexibility has been given to States / UTs to identify districts 
for implementation of different components of the Mission prioritizing districts with low 
productivity but high potential.

and Closer Spacing (CS), Promoting Extra Long Staple (ELS) cotton &good management 
practices and Capacity building of farmers through trainings. During 2026-27, an allocation

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a): The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) was launched to enable financial 
assistance for eligible early-stage startups through incubators across India. As 
on 30th June 2026, 219 operational incubators have been selected under the 
Scheme with a total approved funding of Rs. 945 crore, of which Rs. 650 crore 
has been disbursed to the incubators. 
(b): Under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), funds are released  by 
selected incubators to startups in milestone -based instalments in accordance  
with the guidelines for the Scheme. To ensure timely implementation of the 
Scheme and disbursement of funds, an institutional mechanism comprising the 
Experts Advisory Committ ee (EAC) and Incubator Seed Management 
Committees (ISMCs) has been established. 

The EAC oversees the implementation and monitoring of the Scheme including 
selection of incubators for allocation of funds, while the ISMCs evaluate eligible 
startups and determine the nature and quantum of seed support in accordance 
with the Scheme Guidelines. 
Regular review meetings and webinars are also conducted with incubators to 
review the progress of fund disbursement, identify implementation bottlenecks 
and facilitate th eir timely resolution. Further, advisories and training modules  
have been shared with incubators to facilitate timely processing of funds. 
Further, given the milestone -based nature of disbursement and the time 
required by incubators and startups to utilize  sanctioned funds eﬀectively, the 
Scheme has recently been provided an extension to facilitate disbursement of 
committed funds and to enable incubators and startups to complete approved 
activities.

State/Union Territories (UTs), cities, towns, rural areas, and aspirational 
districts. The State/UT -wise details of funds approved and disbursed to 
incubators selected under the SISFS as on 30th June 2026 are placed as  
Annexure-I. Th e State/UT -wise details of funds approved and disbursed to 
startups by selected incubators under the SISFS as on 30th June 2026 are 
placed as  Annexure-II. The district -wise details of funds approved and 
disbursed to startups in the State of Chhattisgarh by selected incubators under 
the SISFS as on 30th June 2026 are placed as Annexure-III. 
Under SISFS, eligible startups can receive up to Rs. 20 lakh as grant for 
validation of Proof of Concept, or prototype development, or product trials and 
up to Rs. 50 Lakhs of investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling 
up through convertible debentures or debt or debt -linked instruments. As per 
the Chhattisgarh Innovation and Startup Promotion Policy 2025 -2030, under 
Chhattisgarh Seed Fund Assistance (CGSF), eligible startups shall be provided 
seed funding of up to Rs. 10 lakh for the development of a Minimum Viable 
Product (MVP). 
Further, under SISFS, the startup should not have received more than Rs 10 
lakh of monetary support under any other Central or St ate Government 
scheme, and under the CGSF, the startup should not have received seed 
funding for the development of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) under any 
other Scheme of the State or Central Government.

and facilitate timely disbursement of funds across regions, the Government has 
undertaken several measures.

      To provide remunerative price to the farmers for agricultural and horticultural 
commodities including onion which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the 
Minimum Support Price regime, the Government under Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay 
Sanrakshan Abhiyan implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) across the

levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10% decrease in the ruling 
market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request 
of a State/UT Government, which is ready to bear 50% of the loss (25% in case of North-
Eastern States), if any, incurred on its implementation. The maximum quantity of 
procurement is allowed upto 25% of estimated production of the State for particular crop in 
a particular season. Total amount of loss is shared on a 50:50 basis between the Central 
Government and the State Government (75:25 for North East States). 
       A new component of Price Differential Payment (PDP) with an option to make direct 
payment of the price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the selling 
price to the farmers for the crops traded in the Agricultural Produce Market Committee 
(APMC) Mandis has also been added. Additionally, reimbursement for transportation and 
storage cost of TOP crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to Central Nodal Agencies & State 
Designated Agencies for storing and transporting TOP crops from producing state to 
consuming state is allowed.  
      To control extreme volatility of prices in essential commodities, under Price Stabilisation 
Fund (PSF) scheme, the Government creates an annual buffer stock of onions, with the 
buffer target decided each year. Onions are procured from producing States through 
Implementing Agencies (NAFED and NCCF) at market price linked, Minimum Assured 
Procurement Price (MAPP) on the basis of Maximum and Modal prices prevailing during 
previous 3 trading days. The quantity procured in 2025-26 was 2.87 Lakh MT. Under the 
Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF) scheme, Department of Consumer Affairs has approved the 
procurement target of 2 Lakh MT for the year 2026-27, out of which 0.37 LMT procured.

communities and other stakeholders about the schemes, programmes, missions and new

including in rural areas, social media platforms such as Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), 
Instagram, YouTube and WhatsApp Channels are also being utilised for disseminating

DA&FW.

villages, Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands through respective State Horticulture 
Missions. Under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), awareness 
is generated through capacity-building programmes, workshops, seminars, exhibitions, and 
exposure visits aimed at farmers, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholders.

Investment Subsidy for Construction/Expansion /Modernization of Cold Storages and 
Storages for Horticulture Products”. Under the scheme, credit linked back-ended subsidy at 
the rate of 35% of the capital cost of the project in general areas and 50% in case of North 
East, hilly & scheduled areas for construction/expansion/modernization of cold storage and 
Controlled Atmosphere (CA) storage of capacity above 5000 MT and up to 20000 MT is 
available. 
 
As per the records, Rs.175.89 crore and Rs. 37.63 crore have been approved for

Board and Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture respectively during 2025-26.

OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a) to (e):     The legal framework for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is 
established under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, along with Schedule 
VII of the Act and the Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014. The items enlisted in 
the Schedule VII are broad-based and intended to cover a wide range of activities. 
Under the Companies Act, CSR is a Board driven process and the Board of the 
company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR activities of 
the company based on the recommendation of its CSR Co mmittee. This 
Committee formulates and recommends the CSR policy, which outlines the 
activities to be undertaken by the company in alignment with the areas or 
subjects specified in Schedule VII of the Act. The first proviso to Section 135 (5) 
Contd…2/ 
 
 

 
-2- 
 
of the Act provides that the company shall give preference to the local area and 
areas around it where it operates.   However, the emphasis on local area is only 
directory and not mandatory in nature and companies need to balance local area 
preference with national priorities. The Government does not issue any specific 
direction to the companies to spend in any particular geographical area or for any 
particular activity.   
All data related to CSR filed by companies in MCA21 registry is available in public 
domain and can be accessed at www.csr.gov.in. The District -wise  and

मंũी be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that in the first one to two years of 
switching over to natural/organic farming, the yield of many farmers temporarily 
reduced, due to which they become dependent on chemical fertilizers again; 
(b) whether the Government has made any assessment of the impact on the income 
and production of farmers adopting natural farming in the initial years; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide special incentives, direct financial 
assistance or any other support to such farmers during the first two years of the 
transition period; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी                                        (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) : Indian Council of Agricultural Research has initiated study from 2020-21 
through All India Network Programme on Natural Farming (previously AINP-Organic 
Farming) with 20 cooperating centres covering 16 States to evaluate 8 major cropping 
systems and develop package of practices under Natural farming besides evaluation 
of cropping systems under organic farming. The scheme involves 11 State Agricultural 
Universities, 8 ICAR institutes/centres and 1 deemed to be university. 

Studies on the benefits of natural farming have shown that if natural farming is adopted 
with the right techniques and in a balanced manner, yields improve. The experiences 
of many farmers have also proven that improving soil health in the initial years 
improves crop quality, taste, and long-term yield. Furthermore, reducing chemical 
costs increases farmers' net profits. Mulching in natural farming helps maintain soil 
moisture, control weeds, and increase organic matter in the soil. This also increases 
the activity of soil microorganisms and improves soil health. Multi-cropping increases 
biodiversity in the field, reduces the incidence of pests and diseases, and improves 
nutrient utilization. The finding is as below; 
(i) Under the network research, crop system-based natural farming packages 
have been developed for various states, such as groundnut + sesame – fennel 
+ cabbage (Rajasthan and Gujarat), soybean + maize – wheat + mustard 
(Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh), and cassava (Kerala).  
(ii) In Bajaura (Himachal Pradesh), Almora (Uttarakhand) and Gangtok (Sikkim), 
the average system productivity (soybean equivalent) of 6475 kg/ha/year was 
recorded in the soybean + maize – vegetable pea + coriander (green leaf) crop 
system (in 5 years) under completely natural farming, which was about 5 
percent higher than organic farming/integrated crop management.  
(iii)  In Bhopal and Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) and Raipur (Chhattisgarh), the 
average system productivity (soybean equivalent) of 3346 kg/ha/year was 
recorded in the soybean + maize – wheat + mustard crop system (in 5 years), 
which was found to be equivalent to integrated crop management and organic 
farming. 
(iv) S.K. In Nagar (Gujarat), Ajmer, and Udaipur (Rajasthan), the average system 
productivity (cowpea equivalent) of 9209 kg/ha/year was recorded in the 
cowpea + maize/peanut + sesame – fennel + cauliflower/cabbage cropping 
system (in 5 years) under complete natural farming. This was found to be 
comparable to integrated crop management. 
(v) Natural farming (NF) management has shown a clear improvement in soil 
health indicators. Soil organic carbon (SOC) levels increased in natural farming 
fields over a period of 2–3 years. For example, in trials conducted in the 
Himalayan regions, SOC increased from approximately 0.90% to 1.15%. The 
number and diversity index of microorganisms in natural farming soils was 
found to be higher than in soils cultivated with chemical fertilizers. The 
abundance and balanced distribution of beneficial bacteria, fungi, and 

actinomycetes were observed, indicating the development of a healthy soil 
ecosystem over time. This increase in organic matter and microorganisms in 
the soil under natural farming improves nutrient cycling and soil structure, laying 
a strong foundation for long-term soil fertility and crop production sustainability. 
           Further, NITI Aayog Assessment Report states that approximately 91.2% of 
farmers adopting natural farming experience, increased crop productivity and 
significantly improved soil health. 90.1% of farmers reported that adopting natural 
farming has reduced input costs (production costs).

THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH

The Government of India from the financial year 2018-19, has extended the Kisan Credit Card
