ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
Registered Fishermen Families 
345. Shri Murasoli S:  
Will the Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying  be pleased to 
state: 
(a)  the number of registered fishermen families in Thanjavur district in Tamil Nadu 
and the assistance disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) during the last three years; 
(b)  whether the Government is aware of the fact that inland fishermen dependent on 
the Cauvery river system have reported declining catch due to reduced water flow and 
also the steps taken by the Government to rectify the same; and 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to promote inland aquaculture as an 
alternative livelihood in delta districts? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) As per the information received from Go vernment of Tamil Nadu, a total number of 
1,480 inland fish farmers are registered with the District Fish Farmers Development 
Agency (DFFDA) and a total number of 1,234 inland fishermen  are registered in inland 
fishermen cooperative societies in Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. Funds to the tune of  
Rs. 196.30 Lakhs have been disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY), during the last three years (2021 -22 to 20 23-24) for the 
implementation of the projects namely construction of fresh water finfish hatchery (2 
units), construction of seed rearing ponds (07 ha), construction of new grow out ponds 
and input assistance (25 ha), input subsidy assistance for grow out ponds (25 ha), 
establishment of small Biofloc  units (09 units)  and establishment of re -circulatory 
aquaculture system (01 unit). 
(b) As informed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) the Central Inland 
Fisheries Research Institute (CIFRI) has conducted a study in the Cauvery River stretch 
in Thanjavur Dis trict, Tamil Nadu. The study revealed that extensive diversion of  river 
water for agricultural purposes through a well -developed canal network has resulted in 
reduced flow in this stretch for most of the year. The river stretch receives water mainly 
during the monsoon season and through regulated releases from upstream reservoirs. 
Consequently, riverine capture fisheries in the Thanjavur stretch remain seasonal,  with 
limited intensity.  

Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)  implemented by the 
Department of Fisheries , Government of India  (DoF, GoI) , the River Ranching 
Programme was implemented in Tamil Nadu, under which 176 lakh advanced fingerlings 
were released in river stretches across the State (including 59.76 lakh in Cauvery riverine 
system) to enhance fishery resources and conserve native fish biodiversity, enhance fish 
catches and protect the livelihood of inland fishers . This stocking is anticipated to 
increase the fish production to 220 tonnes in the Cauvery river system thereby enhancing 
inland fish production and supporting the livelihood of inland fishers.  
(c) The DoF, GoI since 2015, has substantially stepped-up investment in fisheries sector 
through various schemes for holistic development of fisheries, inland aquaculture and 
welfare of fishermen in the country including delta districts of Tamil Nadu (Thanjavur, 
Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Cuddalore). The Government of Tamil 
Nadu has implemented several activities under the PMMSY and the state schemes to 
enhance the fish production, area expansion  under aquaculture, promotion of 
sustainable livelihoods and intensive aquaculture  by adopting  technologies such as 
Biofloc Systems and Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS). In addition, subsidy 
assistance is provided under the PMMSY for fishing gear to reduce the operational costs 
of inland fishers. 
The Government of Tamil Nadu  has informed that subsidy assistance under PMMSY 
has been provided to 355 beneficiaries from Delta districts for activities su ch as input 
assistance and construction of freshwater finfish hatcheries, new seed rearing ponds, 
grow out ponds, establishment of Biofloc units, RAS, ornamental units, and purchase of 
fishing gear. The State has also facilitated the stocking of 9.00 lakh fingerlings in 
Panchayat tanks covering an area of 450 hectares across the Delta districts during 
2024–25 and 2025–26.

PRODUCTIVITY 
 
346. Md. RAKIBUL HUSSAIN: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of recurrent floods and river erosion 
on agricultural productivity in Assam; 
(b) the estimated area of cultivable land lost during the last five years; 
(c) whether compensation has been provided to affected farmers; and 
(d) the long-term mitigation measures proposed to safeguard agricultural livelihoods? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground 
level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake relief measures 
in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of India approved items and 
norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the 
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of 
disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-
Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). The financial assistance provided under SDRF and 
NDRF is by way of relief and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed. 
Net sown area for Assam during Last 5 years is as under (in thousand hect.): 
Agri Year Net Sown Area 
2020-21 2724 
2021-22 2749 
2022-23 2744 
2023-24 2756 
2024-25  2759 
The net sown area in Assam had shown rising trend during last 05 years.  
(c): The State of Assam was allocated Rs.3793.60 crore from SDRF during the last five 
years from 2021-22 to 2025-26. Rs.3414.40 crore was released as central share. 
Rs.1001.377 crore was released to Assam from NDRF during the last five years from 
2021-22 to 2025-26. 
 

 
(d):  As informed by Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga 
Rejuvenation, Flood management and anti-erosion schemes are formulated and 
implemented by the concerned State Governments as per their priorities. The Union 
Government supplements the efforts of the States by providing technical guidance as well 
as promotional financial assistance for the management of floods in critical areas. The 
Union Government is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely, the Flood 
Management and Border Areas Programme (FMBAP), to provide central assistance to 
States for works related to flood control, anti-erosion, drainage development, etc. during 
the period 2021-26. 
       As per the report of the Central Water Commission (CWC) on “Assessment of Area 
Affected Due to Floods in India”, based on satellite imageries data from 1986 to 2022, the 
total flood-affected areas in India has been assessed as 21.213 million hectares (Mha), 
and area protected through various flood management measures taken by the Central 
and the State Governments is 20.538 Mha. The total flood-affected areas in the state of 
Assam is 2.477 Mha. 
Assam Govt  has undertaken several long-term measures to enhance the resilience of 
agriculture against floods, which include: 
 Distribution of flood-submergence-tolerant crop varieties under various 
Government schemes to improve climate resilience. 
 Promotion of climate-resilient agricultural practices through District Contingency 
Plans, timely advisories and appropriate crop management practices. 
 Implementation of Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) interventions, including 
construction of water harvesting structures and other water conservation 
measures to improve water availability during dry spells. 
 Promotion of efficient water management practices, including micro-irrigation 
systems, to ensure judicious use of available water resources during Rabi Season. 
 Promotion of crop diversification by encouraging farmers to cultivate Rabi crops 
such as pulses, oilseeds and vegetables, supported by modern farm 
mechanization and improved production technologies. 
      National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) project implemented 
by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed and promoted 
climate resilient technologies in agriculture for vulnerable areas of the country. Location-
specific climate resilient technologies are demonstrated under NICRA. climate resilient 
agricultural technologies that enhances the crop yields in the face of climate change is 
promoted in Darrang, Dhemaji, Dhubri and Nalbari districts of Assam.

349. SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has conducted any audit or review in the last five years to 
examine the feasibility of enacting a law guaranteeing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 
farmers, and if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(b) whether the Government considers the need for a legal guarantee of MSP important for 
ensuring farmer welfare and protection from distress sales;  
(c) whether the Government can provide data on the estimated monetary loss suffered by 
farmers due to the absence of a legal MSP framework in the last ten financial years including 
the current financial year, State/UT-wise and year-wise;  
(d) if so, the details thereof, and if not, the reasons therefor; and  
(e) whether the Government has drawn up any time-bound roadmap for implementing a law 
on MSP, and if so, the milestones and timelines and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated 
agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of the 
Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the State 
Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned. 
     The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep 
MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, 
Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops 
with a minimum return of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from 
year 2018-19 onwards. 
Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India 
(FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the 
farmers.Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme 
under Umbrella Scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-
AASHA), on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and 
when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-
AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd 
(NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton 
and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India 
(CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 

Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component under 
PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which are 
perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS). The 
objective of intervention is to protect the growers of these commodities from making distress 
sale in the event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices tend to fall 
below economic levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 percent 
decrease in the ruling market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is 
implemented at the request of a State/UT government. 
Government has introduced a new component of Price Differential Payment (PDP) 
under Market intervention scheme (MIS) from 2024-25 season for direct payment of the 
price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the selling price to the 
farmers of perishable crops. States/UTs have an option to choose either to do physical 
procurement of the crop or to make the differential payment between the MIP & Sale Price 
to the farmers. 
Further, from 2024-25 season, Government added another component under Market 
intervention scheme (MIS) for reimbursing the Storage and Transportation cost of TOP 
crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to central nodal agencies & State designated agencies 
for transporting them from the producing State to consuming states in the interest of the 
farmers. 
Adequate number of Procurement centres are opened by respective State 
Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, convenience 
of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage and 
transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing Mandis and 
depots/godowns are also established at key points. 
The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process and during the last 
few years, procurement processes under Minimum Support Price (MSP) have improved to 
ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and Land 
records with

PRADESH 
 
35.      SHRI P V MIDHUN REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh during the 
last two years and the current year, year-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the specific causes of 
youth unemployment and the measures taken or proposed to 
improve employment opportunities for young job -seekers in the 
said State during the last two years and the current year; 
(c) if so, the details thereof, year-wise; 
(d) the details of unemployment in rural -urban areas of the said State 
during the last two years and the current year, year and gender -
wise; 
(e) whether the Government has assessed the impact of industrial 
and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) closures on 
employment trends in the said State during the last two years and 
current year; and 
(f) if so, the findings thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (f): The official data on Employment and Unemployment is 
collected through Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), which is 
conducted by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation 
(MoSPI) since 2017-18. 
 
As per Annual PLFS reports, the estimated Unemployment Rate 
(UR) on usual status for persons of age 15 years and above has 
decreased from 4.2% in 2021 -22 to 4.1% in 2023 -24 in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh and 3.5% to 3.4% in rural areas and 6.0% to 5.9% in 
urban areas of Andhra Pradesh during the same period.  
 

Also, MoSPI has revamped PLFS from January 2025. The latest 
PLFS report 2025 is the first in the series of Annual report conducted 
during the calendar year (January 2025 -December 2025). As per the 
report, the estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) on usual status for 
persons of age 15 years and above was 4.2% in Andhra Pradesh and 
3.4% in rural areas and 6.2% in urban areas during the year 2025. Also, 
the UR for youth of age 15 -29 years was 16.2% in Andhra Pradesh during 
the same period.  
 
Udyam Registration Portal (URP) was launched on 01.07.2020, The 
number of registered Enterprises, including IMEs, as of 15.07.2026 is 
more than 9.0 Crore. Enterprises de -register on the Portal due to a 
number of reasons such as certificate not required anymore, shutting 
down, duplicate registration, change in the company owner and other 
reasons. As per data on Udyam Registration Portal about, 0.17 % MSMEs 
have been de -registered due to shut down since inception of Udyam 
Registration Portal. 
 
However, as per the latest Annual PLFS reports, the estimated 
Worker Population Ratio (WPR) indicating employment on usual status 
for persons of age 15 years and above has increased from 54.1% in 2022 
to 57.4% in 2025 in the country. 
 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability 
(including youth of Andhra Pradesh) is a priority of the Government. 
Accordingly, Government is implementing various employment 
generation schemes/ programmes in the country. The details of various 
employment generation schemes/ programmes being implemented by the 
Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
 
The Government of India, through the Ministry of Micro, Small & 
Medium Enterprises (MSME), implements various schemes for the 
promotion and development of MSMEs across the country. These 
schemes/programmes include Prime Minister’s Employment Generation 
Programme (PMEGP), Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small 
Enterprises (CGTMSE), Micro and Small Enterprises -Cluster Development 
Programme (MSE-CDP), Entrepreneurship Skill Development Programme 
(ESDP), Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme (PMSS), Raising 
and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP), International Cooperation 
scheme, Tool Rooms, Technology Centre System Programme (TCSP), 
National SC/ST Hub (NSSH), MSME Champions, PM Vishwakarma etc. 

 
Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) to 
deliver skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of 
skill development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. under 
various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), 
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion 
Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial 
Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth 
of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of 
IT Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies 
including Artificial Intelligence. 
 
Government is implementing Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) 
Scheme named as the Pradhan Ma

SCHEMES TO ENHANCE FARMERS’ INCOME 
 
350. DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी

ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b):  Government of India is implementing a comprehensive range of Central 
Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes and programmes aimed at increasing farmers’ 
income across all States/UTs, encompassing  entire spectrum of agriculture, including 
credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops (including horticulture), seeds, 
mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, 
extension, procurement of crops and digital agriculture. The list of agriculture related 
schemes implemented by Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare (DA&FW) in the 
country including the State of Bihar is placed at Annexure-I. The details of the funds 
released to the State of Bihar under major agricultural schemes during the last three years 
is placed at Annexure II. 
(c):  Government is promoting climate-resilient agriculture through various schemes and 
programmes. Under the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY), 
interventions such as Rainfed Area Development (RAD), Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), 
Soil Health & Fertility (SH&F), Crop Diversification Programme (CDP), Paramparagat 
Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) and the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) are 
being implemented to promote efficient water use, improve soil health, crop diversification, 
promote natural/organic farming and support sustainable farming practices. The Pradhan 
Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides financial support to farmers against crop 
losses due to natural calamities. The Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) 
promotes resource conservation technologies. Further, ICAR, through the National 
Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) conducts research & development 
activities on the development of climate resilient technologies and drought resistant 
varieties. 
(d):  In 2026-27, an allocation of Rs 6.69 cr. has been approved for Bihar under PM-
RKVY for strengthening agricultural research through the establishment of a Pulse 
Production Park, varietal development of hybrid maize, propagation of the Dudhia Maldah 
mango variety, development of climate-resilient cropping systems, and establishment of 
an Advanced Centre for Medicinal and Aromatic Plants to produce quality planting material 
for farmers. 

 (e): The Government of India supports the development of agricultural value addition, 
post-harvest management, storage and marketing infrastructure through various schemes 
and programmes. The Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM), including 
the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) component, supports the establishment 
and modernization of agricultural marketing infrastructure. The National Agriculture Market 
(e-NAM) facilitates transparent, efficient and competitive marketing by providing farmers 
with access to a unified online trading platform across regulated markets. Under 
the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), assistance is provided for 
the creation of post-harvest management infrastructure, including pack houses, ripening 
chambers, cold storage and refrigerated transport for horticultural produce. 
Under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), financial assistance is provided for the 
creation of post-harvest management infrastructure such as warehouses, cold storage 
facilities, grading and sorting units, assaying laboratories, primary processing centres, 
pack houses and other community farming assets. In addition, under the Pradhan Mantri 
-Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY), financial assistance is available to States for 
undertaking State-specific projects aimed at strengthening agricultural value chains, post-
harvest management, processing, storage and market linkages, based on local priorities 
and requirements. Under PM-RKVY for the year 2026–27, a total outlay of ₹688.75 crore 
has been approved for the State, comprising a Central Share of ₹413.25 crore and a State 
Share of ₹275.50 crore. The approved outlay includes ₹215.47 crore for the PM-RKVY 
DPR,

CONSTRUCTION AND UPGRADATION OF RURAL ROADS IN BIHAR 
 
351.  Shri Arun Bharti: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the systematic implementation of the Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) has successfully ensured all-
weather road connectivity for remote habitations in Bihar; 
(b)  if so, the total kilometers of new rural roads constructed and 
older roads upgraded using central financial assistance in the 
State during the last two financial years; 
(c)  whether this enhanced connectivity has effectively allowed 
rural farmers to transport perishable agricultural produce to 
urban markets quickly, thereby increasing their daily incomes; 
(d)  if so, the details of the stringent quality control inspections 
conducted to ensure the durability and safety of the newly 
constructed pavement infrastructure; and 
(e)  the future initiatives planned to incorporate sustainable, locally 
available green materials and plastic waste in the construction 
of rural roads to reduce environmental impact? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) has been 
instrumental in establishing systematic, all-weather road 
connectivity across the rural areas of the country including the State 
of Bihar. The phase-wise details of new road length constructed and 
older roads upgraded in the State of Bihar during the last two 
financial years (FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26) are placed at Annexure. 
  
(c): Independent evaluation studies commissioned by organizations 
such as NITI Aayog and the World Bank confirm that the expansion 
of the rural road network under PMGSY significantly enhances farm-
to-market logistics. The consolidation of "Through Routes" and 

Page 2 of 3 
 
"Major Rural Links" has reduced transit times and transportation 
costs, facilitating faster integration of rural agricultural hubs with 
urban wholesale markets and Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs). 
(d): To ensure the structural durability and long-term performance 
of rural roads, a robust Three-Tier Quality Control Mechanism is 
implemented under the scheme: 
i. First Tier: Continuous quality control and field testing managed 
directly by the Program Implementation Units (PIUs) of the state 
executing agency. 
ii. Second Tier: Independent quality monitoring coordinated by the 
State Quality Monitors (SQMs) to conduct structured 
inspections of ongoing and completed works. 
iii. Third Tier: Independent, high-level quality audits executed by 
empanelled National Quality Monitors (NQMs) under the aegis 
of the National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency 
(NRIDA) to enforce strict adherence to standard engineering 
specifications. 
(e): The Ministry actively promotes sustainable construction 
practices through the guidelines established in the "Vision Document 
on New Technology Initiatives & Guidelines". Under this framework, 
the adoption of green technologies is being mainstreamed across all 
rural road projects, utilizing alternative materials to lower 
environmental footprints: 
i. Waste Plastic: The guidelines mandate the compulsory use of 
waste plastic in at least 70% of the eligible length proposed for 
bituminous road works using the Hot Mix process. 
ii. Alternative Green Technologies: New and alternative green 
technologies include cold-mix technology, cell-filled concrete, 
roller compacted concrete pavements, and industrial/agro-
wastes (like fly-ash and slag), along with the application of 
stabilized sub-bases using locally available marginal materials 
to preserve natural resources and reduce carbon emissions.

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a)      the specific schemes being run by the Government to promote natural farming in the

(c)      whether there is any plan to provide any cash incentive or financial assistance to 
farmers practicing natural farming on the lines of the subsidy given on fertilizers; and

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी                                            (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a): The Union Cabinet approved the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) on

the country. 
 
(b) :  During the financial year 2024-25 and 2025-26, expenditure of Rs. 600.51 crore has

(c) : The Mission envisages Output Based Incentive of ₹4000/- per acre, per year to a

FFPOs under PMMSY 
 
353.  Shri G M Harish Balayogi: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be 
pleased to state: 
(a)  the number of Fish Farmers Producer Organisations (FFPOs) approved, 
formed and operational under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) 
during the last five years, State/UT and district -wise in Andhra Pradesh, especially in 
Konaseema district; 
(b)  the number of fishers and fish farmers associated with such FFPOs during the 
said period, in Andhra Pradesh, especially in Konaseema district; year and district -
wise. 
(c)  the amount of funds sanct ioned, released and utilised for formation and 
strengthening of FFPOs under PMMSY during the said period, implementing agency-
wise and district-wise; 
(d)  the details of financial, technical, capacity -building, marketing and 
infrastructure support provided to FFPOs in Andhra Pradesh, district -wise, especially 
in Konaseema district; 
(e)  the current status and performance of FFPOs formed in Andhra Pradesh, 
including number functional and non -functional, FFPOs district -wise, specially in 
Konaseema district; and 
(f)  whether the Government has any proposals to form any new FFPOs in 
Konaseema district, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (f) : The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented 
by the Department  of Fisheries, Government of India inter-alia provides financial 
assistance for  setting up of Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to 
economically empower the fishers, fish farmers and enhance their bargaining power. 
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying 
during the last five years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26) has approved projects worth of 
Rs.544.86 crore for formation of 2195 FFPOs including formation of 195 new FFPOs 

and formation of 2000 existing Primary Fisheries Cooperative S ocieties(PFCSs) as 
FFPOs in the country.  This project is implemented through four central agencies 
namely National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), Small Farmers Agri-business 
Consortium (SFAC), National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India 
(NAFED) and National Cooperative D evelopment Corporation (NCDC). It is reported 
that so far a total 2104 Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) have been 
formed in the country including 192 FFPOs in the State of Andhra Pradesh. The State-
wise details of the Fish Farmers Producer Organ izations (FFPOs) formed in the 
country under PMMSY as on date are furnished at Annexure-I.  
It is reported that 10 new Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs)  have been 
formed and registered in Andhra Pradesh with a Government support of Rs 328.20 
lakh under the PMMSY. The supports extended to such newly formed FFPOs include 
incubation, management cost and equity grant. The district-wise details of the newly 
formed FFPOs  in Andhra Pradesh are furnished at Annexure-II. In addition , 182 
existing Primary Fisheries Cooperative Societies(PFCSs) have been formed as Fish 
Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs)  at a total investment of Rs 963.73 lakh 
covering management cost and equity grant  in the State of Andhra Pradesh. This 
includes formation of 34 primary fisheries cooperatives as FFPO at a cost of Rs. 
165.82 lakh in K onaseema District of Andhra Pradesh. The District-wise details of 
these 182 existing primary fisheries cooperatives formed as FFPO in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh under PMMSY are furnis hed at Annexure-III.  It is reported that a 
total 39,022 members are associated with aforementioned 192 functional  FFPOs 
including 6136 members in new FFPOs and remaining  32,886 members of existing 
PFCSs formed as FFPOs in the State of Andhra Pradesh.

IMPLEMENTATION OF ABC RULES 
 
354. DR. BYREDDY SHABARI:  
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any guidelines or advisories have been issued by the Government to States/Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs) for implementation of the Animal Birth Control (ABC) Rules and compliance with 
directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court regarding management of rabid and aggressive stray dogs, 
if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether financial assistance has been provided to States/ULBs for establishment or upgradation 
of dog shelters, sterilisation and vaccination facilities, and procurement of dog catching equipment 
and vehicles and if so, the details thereof, State-wise;  
(c) whether any training programmes have been conducted for municipal staff, veterinary officers, 
animal handlers and shelter personnel, particularly in rural areas, if so, the details thereof, State -
wise;  
(d) whether Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) or certification protocols have been issued for 
identification and long term sheltering of aggressive or rabid dogs and if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) the details of monitoring mechanism followed by the Government to ensure compliance by 
ULBs with the ABC Rules and Supreme Court directions? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
 
(a) The Government of India has notified Animal Birth Control  (ABC) Rules, 2023 on 
10.03.2023. After notification, The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government 
of India (GoI ) had issued advisory to all the States and UTs to implement ABC Rules, 2023 on 
27.03.2023. Again on 11.11.2024, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, GoI had 
issued advisory to all the States/UTs for Implementation of the Animal Birth Control P rogramme 
as per the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023.  
On 16.07.2025, the Secretaries of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Ministry 
of Panchayati Raj (MoPR), and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) have 
also issued a joint advisory to all the States/UTs, urging the implementation of the ABC Programme 
and the development of requisite infrastructure.  

(b) The dog population management is the mandate of the local bodies. The local bodies are 
implementing the ABC Programme. However, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
GoI is implementing Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) during 2026-27. 
The State Government can avail incentives under the scheme after taking various reform measures. 
Sterilisation and vaccination of dogs are included as an important  reform measures under SASCI. 
The State Governments can establish dog shelter, animal shelter and animal birth control centres 
under the scheme.  
(c) The Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI), in collaboration with the U.P. Pandit Deen 
Dayal Upadhyaya Pashu Chikitsa Vigyan Vishwavidyalaya Evam Go Anusandhan Sansthan 
(DUV ASU), Mathura, organised two National Training Programmes on "Animal Birth Control 
(Awareness on Dog Welfare and Public Health)" in which 49 participants (25 veterinarians and 24 
para-veterinary professionals) from 13 States were trained on scientific dog population 
management, sterilisation, anti-rabies vaccination and implementation of the Animal Birth Control 
Rules, 2023. 
Further, AWBI has signed Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Lucknow Nagar 
Nigam and Uttar Pradesh Urban Development Department to conduct training in the facility 
developed by the Lucknow Nagar Nigam. Three training programmes have been conducted and 35 
participants trained on scientific sterilisation procedures, anti -rabies vaccination and 
implementation of the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023. 
(d) In compliance with the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Suo Motu Writ 
Petition (Civil) No. 5 of 2025, AWBI has issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on 
27.11.2025 prescribing procedures for identification, capture, veterinary exami nation, treatment, 
rehabilitation and long -term sheltering of rabid, suspected rabid and aggressive dogs for the 
Institutions and public places.  
(e) Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of Suo -moto W.P. 05 of 2025 has upheld 
Animal Birth Control Rules and issued detailed direction and guidelines to the State Government 
vide order dated 19.05.2026. A ll the High Courts have been directed to register a suo moto writ 
petition, in the name and style of: “In Re: Compliance with the directions issued by the Supreme 
Court of India in Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No(s). 5 of 2025”, as a continuing mandamus, for 
monitoring compliance with the directions issued

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

COMMISSION FOR AGRICULTURAL COSTS AND PRICES 
 
355. SHRI K E PRAKASH: 
  
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state:
 (a) the factors considered by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices 
(CACP) while recommending Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for agricultural crops 
for the 2026–27 marketing season;  
(b) Whether the Union Government has received any representations from farmers' 
organisations and other stakeholders regarding the MSPs announced for the 2026–
27 season and, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to strengthen consultation with farmers and 
State Governments in the MSP recommendation process;  
(d) whether any measures have been taken to improve awareness and procurement 
under the MSP regime; and  
(e) the steps taken by the Government to support agricultural production during the 
current cropping season? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛमंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the 
recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after 
considering the views of the State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments 

concerned. While recommending MSPs, CACP considers important factors like cost 
of production, overall demand-supply conditions, domestic and international prices, 
inter-crop price parity, terms of trade between agricultural and non-agricultural 
sectors, the likely effect on the rest of the economy, besides ensuring rational 
utilization of land, water and other production resources. Before recommending 
MSP, CACP also consults stakeholders (including Central and State Governments, 
procurement agencies, industry associations, farmers' representatives, research 
institutions etc.) and inputs received were also utilized for finalizing the 
recommendations by the Commission. 
Time to time, suggestions/representations from many farmers’ organizations 
and other stakeholders are also received regarding the MSPs announcement. 
(d): The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process and during the 
last few years, procurement processes under Minimum Support Price (MSP) have 
improved to ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of 
Aadhaar and Land records with the central and State’s procurement portals ensuring 
the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase. Other important initiatives 
to strengthen procurement process by FCI include deployment of biometric based 
procurement system, Integration of Digitized Mandi/Procurement centre operation.  
NAFED has End-to-End Digitization from Procurement to Disposal. 
Procurement is conducted through the e-Samriddhi portal. Inventory is managed via 
the Drishti portal. Stock disposal is facilitated through the NAFED portal. Deployment 
of PoS machines for registration and improved transparency. Opening of model 
procurement centres has ensured seamless operations, Improved transparency and 
created a more farmer-friendly procurement system. 
The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is 
implementing a Central Sector Scheme "Mass Media Support to Agriculture 
Extension" through DD Regional Kendra, DD Kisan and All India Radio to create 
awareness and dissemination of scheme benefits including announcement and 
implementation of MSP among the farming community across the Country. 
  

NAFED’s Farmer Outreach Program include pre-season awareness 
campaigns on MSP and procurement processes, Use of SMS alerts for real-time 
communication with registered farmers, Increased outreach through local 
newspapers and WhatsApp farmer groups, Simplification of registration and 
documentation requirements to encourage participation and Publicity of procurement 
through loudspeakers in APMC mandis and villages.   
(e):  Government supports agriculture production during the cropping season 
through various schemes which include National Food Security and Nutrition Mission 
(NFSNM),  National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO)-Oil Palm, National Mission on 
Edible Oils (NMEO)-Oilseeds, Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture 
(MIDH), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)/ Restructured Weather Based 
Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) Mission for Aatmanirbharata in Pulses and Kisan 
Credit Card (KCC).

356.   SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA: 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether the Government has defined a separate and clearly earmarked share of “Home State” 
or “State Quota” seats at NIFT Srinagar for students domiciled in the Union Territory of Ladakh 
after its bifurcation from the erstwhile State of Jammu & Kashmir;  
(b) if so, the details thereof;  
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and  
(d) whether the Government acknowledges that such a measure would help promote design, 
fashion, and textile management education among youth from Leh  and Kargil and contribute to  
regional value addition and skill development? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्रराज्‍ यमंत्री(श्री‍पबित्र‍मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
 
(a) to (d)   The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Srinagar reserves a 35% 
Special Preferential Quota of its total seats for domicile candidates from the Union Territories of 
Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, as well as registered Kashmiri Migrants. Accordingly, there is 
no separate or exclusive "home State" or "State quota" earmarked solely for candidates 
domiciled in the Union Territory of Ladakh. The existing Special Preferential Quota provides 
reservation to eligible domicile candidates from both the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir 
and Ladakh. This reservation is aimed at facil itating access to quality education in design, 
fashion and textile-related disciplines for eligible candidates from these regions.

REVISION OF AMOUNT UNDER NSAP 
 
357.  Shri Shyamkumar Daulat Barve: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that there has been no 
revision in the amount paid by the center under the National 
Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), including the Indira 
Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, Indira Gandhi 
National Widow Pension Scheme and Indira Gandhi National 
Disability Pension Scheme, since 2012 despite substantial 
inflation and increase in cost of living, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government has conducted any assessments to 
determine whether the present central assistance is sufficient 
to meet the basic needs of the beneficiaries, if so, the details 
thereof and the reasons for not increasing the amount paid; 
(c)  the details of the contribution made by States and the year-wise 
revision of amount paid by the States, if any; and 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to revise and increase the 
amount provided as central assistance under NSAP, if so, the 
details and timeline for implementation, if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is being 
implemented across the country as a social security programme, for 
vulnerable sections of the society such as old aged, widows and 
disabled persons belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL). The rate of 
Central assistance under NSAP pension schemes including National 
Old Age Pension Scheme, National Widow Pension Scheme and 
National Disability Pension Scheme was last revised in 2012.  
  

Page 2 of 3 
 
NSAP caters to more than 3 crore BPL beneficiaries and as per the 
information collected from States/UTs, about 5.9 crore additional 
pensioners are supported by state-funded social pension schemes. 
Therefore, around 9 crore beneficiaries are receiving pension 
benefits either under Central pension schemes and/or under State-
specific social security pension schemes, many of which have 
expanded coverage and higher assistance levels tailored to local 
needs. At present, States are giving top up amount to the 
beneficiaries ranging from ₹50/- to ₹5700/- per month. As a result, 
NSAP pensioners are getting monthly pension on an average of Rs. 
1100/- in several States/ UTs. State/UT-wise details of top-up paid by 
the States/UTs are at Annexure.  
From time to time, various impact assessment and evaluation 
studies have been carried out to assess the impact of NSAP schemes 
by the Ministry and NITI Aayog. The assessments indicate 
satisfactory implementation at the grassroots level, with most 
beneficiaries expressing overall satisfaction with the processes of 
selection, sanction, and disbursement of pensions. The studies also 
find that pension support has helped beneficiaries meet essential 
expenses such as food, healthcare, etc., thereby reducing their 
dependence on family members for these needs. At the same time, 
they have recommended further strengthening of the programme 
through measures such as improving adequacy of assistance, 
ensuring timely and regular payments, enhancing beneficiary 
verification and monitoring systems etc.  
At present, there is no proposal under consideration to revise 
the rate of assistance under NSAP.

EXPORTS OF ALPHONSO MANGOES  
  
358.    SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE:  
PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD:  
DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE:  
SMT. SUPRIYA SULE:  
SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH:  
SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL:  
SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE:  
  
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्री) be pleased 
to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government is aware that exports of Maharashtra’s renowned Alphonso 
mangoes have been severely affected during 2026 due to extreme weather 
conditions, regulatory restrictions in key importing countries, and rising logistics 
costs, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether unseasonal heatwaves and erratic climatic conditions in the Konkan region, 
particularly Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg districts, have caused substantial crop losses 
and reduced exportable surplus, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether countries such as Japan and Nepal have imposed restrictions on Indian 
mango imports citing quarantine, treatment protocol and pesticide residue concerns 
and if so, the details thereof;  
(d) whether escalating air freight and shipping charges, coupled with disruptions in West 
Asian trade routes, have adversely affected Maharashtra exporters, if so, the details 
thereof; and  
(e) the steps taken by the Government to restore market access, strengthen export 
compliance infrastructure, provide financial assistance to affect ed growers and 
exporters, and promote new export destinations for Alphonso mangoes from 
Maharashtra? 
ANSWER 
  
वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्यमंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
  
(a), (b), (d) & (e) The Government of Maharashtra has reported damage to the Alphonso 
Mango crop in the Konkan region, particularly Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg districts, due to 

2 
 
unseasonal heatwaves and erratic climatic conditions, impacting mango product ion and 
availability of quality produce for exports. 
  
Further, exporters have reported disruptions in terms of increased freight rates, imposition 
of war-risk surcharges, container shortages, delays in shipment schedules, and congestion 
at ports due to the Geo-political situation in West Asia and Middle East. 
To support the exporters, including exporters from Maharashtra, Government has 
implemented RELIEF – Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation under the 
Export Promotion Mission (EPM), through the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India 
(ECGC)  and includes support for insured exporters, facilitation of insurance cover for 
upcoming shipments, and reimbursement assistance for eligible MSME exporters facing 
extraordinary freight and insurance surcharge burdens on shipments to the affected West 
Asia region. 
The Department of Commerce through the Agricultural and Processed Food Products 
Export Development Authority (APEDA) provides financial assistance to exporters, for 
export promotion of its Scheduled products, including of Mangoes , through its Financial 
Assistance Scheme (FAS). The scheme through its components viz., Development of 
Export Infrastructure, Quality Development and Market Development enables market 
access, strengthens export compliance infrastructure, and facilitates expansion of exports 
to new destinations. 
The Government has been working towards expanding the footprint of Indian Mangoes, 
including Alphonso mangoes and as a result the number of countries to which Alphonso 
mangoes are being exported has increased from 2 4 in 2020 -21 to 34 countries in the 
current financial year (2026-27). Promotion events for Mangoes, have be en conducted in 
more than 15 countries such as USA, Belgium, UAE, Germany, Iceland, Czech Republic, 
Switzerland, Saudi Arabia, Australia, France, Bru nei, Qatar, Italy, Russia etc so as to 
expand the footprint of Mangoes produced in India, including from Maharashtra. 
(c) There are no restrictions on Mango exports to Nepal. Government of Nepal has clarified 
that imports of mangoes are permitted subject t o the prescribed phytosanitary 
requirements. With respect to Japan, in the 2026 pre-season inspection of Indian facilities 
by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Japan, certain issues were 
raised by Japan, which have been addressed by the National Plant Protection Organization 
(NPPO) India. The National Plant Protection Organization (NPPO), remains engaged with 
the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Japan to resolve the issues 
flagged by the Japanese side for the  resumption of exports of Mangoes to the Japanese 
market.

36.     SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE: 
 SMT. SUPRIYA SULE:

 PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD: 
 SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL: 
 DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE: 
 SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of reports regarding cash shortages and non-functional 
Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) in several cities and districts of Maharashtra during 
recent months, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of complaints received from the public, banks and banking correspondents 
regarding inadequate cash availability in ATMs across the State; 
(c) the details of ATMs that remained without cash or were non-operational during the last six 
months, city-wise and bank-wise; 
(d) the reasons for the reported cash shortages, including currency distribution constraints, 
logistical issues, increased cash withdrawals or shortage of lower denomination notes; 
(e) the measures taken by the Government and the Rese rve Bank of India to ensure 
uninterrupted cash supply and timely replenishment of ATMs in Maharashtra; and 
(f) whether the Government proposes to establish a real-time monitoring mechanism and 
accountability framework to prevent recurring ATM cash shortages an d if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (f): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has informed that the banks are provided with adequate 
cash to meet state’s cash requirements at all times.   
During FY 2025-26, 14 complaints pertaining to 'Cash not available for long time' under the 
category 'ATM/CDM/Debit card' were received at the Offices of the RBI Ombudsman from the 
complainants in the state of 'Maharashtra'. 

The Bank-wise and District- wise instances of cash out at an ATM for more than 10 hours in a 
month reported for the period December 2025 to May 2026 is at Annexure. 
Further, regarding accountability, there is a penalty framework put in place by RBI to penalise 
banks for instances of cash out at an ATM for more than 10 hours in a month. 
RBI has informed that it engages with banks regularly for their cash requirements in the State 
and arranges for the same, as required, through supply from Minting Presses and/or 
arrangement of cash from other Curren cy Chests. Its Offices proactively monitor the stock at 
Currency Chests of the banks and supply currency to banks for their cash requirements, and it 
engages periodically with banks and other stakeholders involved in the ecosystem to identify 
and act on the challenges identified in currency management and holds periodic meetings with 
banks advising them to ensure adequate cash availability in ATMs.

360. SHRI B Y RAGHAVENDRA:  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state? 
(a) the salient features and major achievements of the Soil Health Card Scheme and the 
progress made since its inception;  
(b) the State-wise details of soil samples analysed and Soil Health Cards issued, including 
district-wise details for Karnataka, along with the funds released to the Karnataka State;  
(c) the details of soil testing laboratories and Village Level Soil Testing Labs established and 
operationalised, State-wise including district-wise details for Karnataka;  
(d) the initiatives taken to promote balanced fertilizer use through Soil Health Card 
recommendations, including farmer awareness, digital advisories and extension services; 
and  
(e) the steps taken to expand soil testing infrastructure and promote Soil Health Card-based 
nutrient management, particularly in rain-fed, hilly and Malnad regions, including digital and 
mobile soil testing facilities? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) The Government is implementing Soil Health and Fertility Scheme to assist State 
Governments to issue Soil Health Cards (SHCs) to farmers across the country. SHCs assist 
in promoting Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) through judicious use of chemical 
fertilizers including secondary and micro-nutrients along with organic manures & bio-
fertilizers, for improving soil health and fertility. Soil samples are processed as per standard 
procedures and analyzed for parameters such as pH, Electrical Conductivity, Organic 
Carbon, available Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Sulphur, and micronutrients (Zinc, 
Copper, Iron, Manganese & Boron). The diagnostic soil health assessment of farmer fields is 
taken up periodically so as to issue SHCs at least once in 3 years. Since 2014-15, 26.09 
crore Soil Health Cards have been generated/ distributed as on date across the country. Total 
8313 Soil Testing Labs (1267 Static Soil Testing Labs, 168 Mobile Soil Testing Labs, 6197 
Mini Soil Testing Labs and 681 Village Level Soil Testing Labs) have been established across 
the country. Under the scheme, Rs. 2153.04 crore fund has been released so far since 
inception.  
(b): The State-wise details of soil samples analysed and Soil Health Cards issued under the 
scheme since inception i.e. from 2014-15 till date are at Annexure-I. District-wise details of 
soil samples analysed and Soil Health Cards issued along with the funds released to the 
Karnataka State from 2014-15 till date are at Annexure-II. 

(c): The State-wise details of soil testing laboratories established and operationalised, are at 
Annexure-III and District-wise details of soil testing laboratories established and 
operationalised are at Annexure-IV 
(d) & (e): Under Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, 130627 farmer’s trainings, 7.17 lakh 
demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s Melas/ campaigns on soil health card recommendations have 
been organized across the country to promote balanced use of fertilizer.  Advisories are also 
issued to farmers through Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA) and Krishi 
Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). School Soil Health Programme is implemented to inculcate 
awareness among students about importance of soil. Farmers can access digital SHCs 
through portal. Financial assistance under the scheme is provided to states to set up and 
strengthen soil testing labs. Benefits of scheme can be taken by farmers in Karnataka 
including rain-fed, hilly and Malnad regions

361.  Shri Chintamani Maharaj: 
Shri Arun Govil: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of plan for implementation of the Padhan Mantri Gram 
Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) for the upgradation, consolidation and 
maintenance of rural roads, specifically for the financial year 
2026-27; 
(b) the targets set for construction and widening of roads under this 
scheme for various States, State-wise including Uttar Pradesh; 
and 
(c)  the details of the investment proposed by the Union Government 
to connect agricultural mandis and rural habitations in densely 
populated areas, State-wise such as western Uttar Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
(a) & (b): Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was 
launched by the Government of India aimed at providing rural 
connectivity by way of all-weather roads to eligible unconnected 
habitations and consolidating the existing rural road network across 
the country. Over the years, the scheme has been expanded through 
various verticals, including PMGSY-II for upgradation of through 
Routes and Major Rural Links (MRLs), the Road Connectivity Project 
for Left Wing Extremism Affected Areas (RCPLWEA), and PMGSY-III 
for the consolidation of 1,25,000 Km of rural road network connecting 
key socio-economic growth centers like Gramin Agricultural Markets 
(GrAMs), schools, and hospitals.  
Further, PMGSY-IV was launched in September 2024 to extend 
all-weather connectivity to eligible unconnected habitations based 

Page 2 of 4 
 
on Census 2011 data during its implementation period from Financial 
Year 2024-25 to 2028-29.  
The implementation plan for the Financial Year 2026-27 is 
focused on the execution of already sanctioned projects and the 
consideration of new proposals under PMGSY-IV based on 
compliance with programme guidelines.  
The routine and periodic maintenance of completed PMGSY 
roads is the responsibility of the respective State Governments/UTs. 
Under the programme guidelines, states are required to 
institutionalize a 5-year routine maintenance contract with the same 
contractor upon completion of construction, funded entirely from the 
State budget. Post the initial 5-year period, the roads are expected to 
be maintained by the states/UTs through subsequent maintenance 
and renewal contracts.  
PMGSY guidelines do not prescribe or monitor separate targets 
for the widening of rural roads. Widening works, wherever technically 
required and justified, are considered an integral part of approved 
upgradation projects in accordance with the applicable Indian Roads 
Congress (IRC) and Ministry’s Rural road Manual/Hill road 
Manual specifications. Accordingly, separate state-wise targets for 
widening are not maintained.  
The physical targets fixed for the construction and upgradation of 
roads under PMGSY for the Financial Year 2026-27, including for the 
State of Uttar Pradesh, are placed at Annexure-I.  
(c): Under the scheme verticals, including the recently launched 
PMGSY-IV, priority is given to connecting eligible habitations and 
enhancing access to economic hubs, including agricultural markets 
(GrAMs), healthcare centers, and educational facilities.  
The allocation and release of Central funds to the State Governments 
are regulated based on parameters such as the submission of eligible 
project proposals, the execution capacity of the states, balance 
works in hand, unspent balances available, and compliance with the 
financial criteria stipulated under the program guidelines. The 
Ministry does not make separate, region-specific, or constituency-
specific financial allocations exclusively for connecting agricultural 
mandis or for specific geographical areas such as western Uttar 
Pradesh.  
The State-wise allocation of the budget under PMGSY for the 
Financial Year 2026-27 is placed at Annexure-II.

(a) to (f) :  Pradhan Manti Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) is an umbrella scheme, 
consisting of three components -  Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP) and 
Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) being implemented by the Department of Water Resources, 
River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR,RD&GR), Ministry of Jal Shakti,  and 
Watershed Development Component (WDC) being implemented by Department of Land 
Resources, Ministry of Rural Development.  Central Assistance is provided to the States

development activities. Projects under the Scheme are generally implemented by State 
Governments through competitive tendering processes, in which private contractors and

norms. The scheme does not contain any specific provision for private sector investments.

(i) Component ''A'' of NPDD focuses on creating/strengthening of infrastructure for quality

institutions.

activities (SDCFPO): To assist the State Dairy Cooperative Federations by providing 
interest subvention (regular 2% and additional 2% on prompt repayment) with respect to 

soft working capital loan to tide over the crisis on account of severely adverse market 
conditions or natural calamities.

subvention at the rate 3% per annum for creation/ strengthening of dairy processing and 
diversification infrastructure thereby providing greater access for unorganized producer 
members to organized market.

CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEMES 
  
369:   SHRI KHALILUR RAHAMAN: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
a. the details of funds allocated, utilized and remaining unutilised under Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes for the development of Panchayats in West Bengal during the last 
five years; and 
b. whether any specific funds have been earmarked for Panchayats to support the 
development of various social groups, deprived sections and for promoting employment, 
if so, the details thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) & (b) Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject. Therefore, all matters 
including the development of Panchayats come within the purview of States. Ministry of 
Panchayati Raj (MoPR) supplements and complements the efforts of State Governments, 
including fund support under the schemes towards strengthening and efficient functioning of the 
Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) on a continuous basis. 
MoPR is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan 
(RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/UTs, including the State of West Bengal. The 
main objective of the scheme is to build the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by 
creating a learning ecosystem, especially through the impartment of training to the Elected 
Representatives (ERs), functionaries, and other stakeholders to develop their governance 
capabilities for leadership roles to enable the Panchayats to function effectively and also by 
supporting for exposure visits, development of training modules and materials, etc. 
 
Revamped RGSA is demand-driven in nature. Funds are released to States/UTs based on the 
Annual Action Plans approved by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and the pace of 
expenditure. The funds are to be utilized only for the approved components as prioritized by the 
States/UTs. The Ministry releases the funds under the scheme to States/UTs only.  

2 
 
During the last five years FY (2021-22 to 2025-26), an amount of Rs.145.79 crore was released 
to the State of West Bengal as Central Share. Out of which, Rs.182.02 crore has been utilized 
(which also includes the previous year's unspent balance) on the approved activities under the 
RGSA and Revamped RGSA, and Rs.25.00 lakh has been surrendered during FY 2025-26. 
The funds are released under RGSA for capacity building of the elected representatives and 
functionaries of the PRIs from all socio-economic groups. Funds for the Scheduled Castes (SC) 
and Scheduled Tribes (ST) under the scheme are earmarked in proportion to their population in 
the country.

entries.t: Volatility and Pressure in the Textile Industry
entries.head:
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 371 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 
 
 
VOLATILITY AND PRESSURE IN THE TEXTILE INDUSTRY 
 
371.   SMT. SHAMBHAVI:  
          DR. LATA WANKHEDE: 
 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of recent volatility and pressure in the textile sector 
affecting domestic textile manufacturers and exporters particularly in Bihar and Madhya 
Pradesh, if so, details thereof;  
(b) whether global demand fluctuations, in put cost variations, and trade -related factors have 
impacted the performance and competitiveness of India’s textile industry, if so, the details 
thereof, if not, the reasons therefor;  
(c) the details regarding measures taken to strengthen the resilience, competitiveness, and export 
potential of the textile sector particularly in Khagaria and Samastipur Parliamentary 
constituency, if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor;  
(d) whether initiatives have been undertaken to support domestic text ile companies, promote 
value addition and enhance supply chain stability; and  
(e) the details regarding steps taken to ensure sustainable growth, employment generation and 
global competitiveness of India’s textile industry? 
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्रराज्‍ यमंत्री(श्री‍पबित्र‍मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
(a) to (e):  India’s exports of textiles and apparel, including handicrafts, stood at ₹3,25,339.0 
crore in 2025–26, registering a growth of 1.8 per cent over ₹3,19,573.2 crore in 2024 –25, despite 
fluctuations in global demand, variations in input costs and other trade-related challenges. India’s 
exports of textiles and apparel, including handicrafts, recorded growth in more than 100 export 
destinations during 2025–26 compared with the previous year. 
Exports of textiles and apparel, including handicrafts, from Madhya Pr adesh stood at ₹11,751.7 
crore in 2025 –26, compared with ₹11,748.9 crore in 2024 –25. Exports from Bihar stood at 
₹409.0 crore in 2025–26, compared with ₹375.6 crore in 2024–25. 
The Government has implemented various schemes and initiatives to promote the g rowth of the 
Indian textile and apparel sector. The major schemes and initiatives include the PM Mega 
Integrated Textile Regions and Apparel (PM MITRA) Parks Scheme; Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) Scheme; National Technical Textiles Mission; SAMARTH —Scheme for 
Capacity Building in the Textile Sector; Silk Samagra -2; National Handloom Development 

Programme; National Handicrafts Development Programme; Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster 
Development Scheme; Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL ) Scheme; 
Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme; Export Promotion 
Mission (EPM), comprising Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha; and the Credit Guarantee 
Scheme for Exporters (CGSE). 
The Government of India also launched RELIEF ( Resilience and Logistics Intervention for 
Export Facilitation) on 19 March 2026 under the Export Promotion Mission to support exporters 
affected by disruptions arising from the conflict in West Asia/Middle East and maritime 
challenges in the Gulf r egion. T he Government has also exempted  import of Cotton falling 
under Customs Tariff Heading 5201 from 1 June to 31 October 2026 to augment the domestic 
availability of cotton. 
India's sixteen Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), including the India –United Kingdom 
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), are already in force. In addition, 
negotiations for an FTA with the European Union was successfully concluded, while India has 
signed an FTA with New Zealand. These agreements provide opportunities for the Ind ian textile 
and apparel sector to expand exports and diversify into new markets. 
The Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) Scheme, operational since March 
2019, provides for the rebate of embedded State and Central taxes and levies on the e xport of 
garments and made -ups, with a view to enhancing the competitiveness of these sectors. The 
Scheme has been extended for a further period of six months, up to 30 September 2026, to 
ensure policy predictability and stability for exporters in these se ctors. The Remission of Duties 
and Taxes on Export Products (RoDTEP) Scheme has also been extended for a further period of 
six months, up to 30 September 2026.  
These initiatives are aimed at ensuring sustainable growth, generating employment across the 
textile value chain, promoting value addition, strengthening supply -chain resilience and 
enhancing the global competitiveness of the Indian textile industry. The textile and apparel 
industry in Bihar, including in the Khagaria and Samastipur parliamentary constituencies, as well 
as in Madhya Pradesh, also benefit from these schemes and initiatives..

373. SHRI MALAIYARASAN D: 
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  the present status and objectives of the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project under the 
Digital India programme; 
(b)  the total funds allocated, released and utilised during the last five years, State/UT-wise, 
particularly in Kallakurichi constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
(c)  the number of Gram Panchayats covered under the project and the extent of digitization 
achieved in core Panchayat functions such as planning, accounting, monitoring and service 
delivery; 
(d)  whether issues such as inadequate internet connectivity, capacity building gaps and 
interoperability with other e-governance platforms have been reported;  
(e)  if so, the steps taken to ensure data security, transparency, and time-bound completion of 
pending components of the project along with the timeline for full implementation in the 
country; and 
(f)  whether the Government proposes to strengthen the scheme further by integrating AI 
based monitoring and citizen grievance redressal systems and if so, the details thereof? 
  
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a) & (c)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode 
Project (MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of 
strengthening transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj 
Institutions (PRIs) through digital enablement across all States and Union Territories. The 
Ministry has developed various applications under the project, including eGramSwaraj, and 
AuditOnline, which are being implemented across all States to enhance transparency, 
accountability and efficiency in Panchayat governance. 
The e-Gram Swaraj and AuditOnline applications, developed under e-Panchayat Mission 
Mode Project (MMP), have significantly contributed to strengthening Panchayati Raj Institutions 
(PRIs) by enabling end-to-end digital governance. e-GramSwaraj facilitates planning, budgeting, 
accounting and monitoring of Panchayat activities on a unified digital platform, thereby 
improving transparency, efficiency and real-time tracking of works and fund utilization.

audit processes, improved financial discipline and enhanced accountability. Together, these 
platforms have helped PRIs transition towards data-driven decision-making, improved record 
keeping, better financial management and increased transparency in rural local governance. 
Further, the Ministry has also developed several other applications under the e-Panchayat MMP. 
The Meri Panchayat application provides citizens access to information on Panchayat planning, 
activities and progress of works. Panchayat NIRNAY facilitates transparent conduct and 
management of Gram Sabha meetings. In addition, the Ministry has introduced SabhaSaar, an 
AI-enabled platform for voice-to-text transcription and summarisation of Gram Sabha and 
Panchayat meetings to ensure accurate documentation of proceedings.  
As on date, during the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,730 Gram Panchayats and equivalent

(a): The Government approved the Digital Agriculture Mission in September 2024. The 
Mission envisages the creation of a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture, such 
as AgriStack, Krishi Decision Support System, a Comprehensive Soil Fertility & Profile Map 
and other IT initiatives undertaken by the Central Government/State Government to enable 
a robust digital agriculture ecosystem in the country as a single source of truth for information 
on farmers, crops, livestock and fisheries and farmer centric digital solutions. The main 
features and their outcomes of the above initiatives are as follows: 
  

 
I. The AgriStack DPI consists of three foundational registries or databases 
associated with the agriculture sector, i.e., Farmer Registry, Geo-Reference 
Village Maps and the Crop Sown Registry, all created and maintained by the 
State Governments/ Union Territories. As of 16th July, 2026, more than 10.15 
Crore Farmer IDs have been created. Out of these, 2,20,602 Farmers' IDs have 
been created in Tiruvannamalai district of Tamil Nadu, which includes 
Arani Constituency. During Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was 
conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the 
country, including Tiruvannamalai district. The current status of Farmer IDs 
and year-wise DCS data (since inception) across the nation is given in 
Annexures I, IIA, IIB, IIC and IID. 
II. Krishi Decision Support System DPI has been developed, which is a geo-spatial 
platform that integrates satellite imagery, weather, soil, and crop data using 
Geographic Information System (GIS) to support agricultural planning and 
decision-making.  
III. A Nationwide Soil Resource Mapping project has been initiated by the Soil and 
Land Use Survey of India (SLUSI), for reserve inventory soils at a village level 
on a 1:10,000 scale using high-resolution satellite and ground data. As of June, 
2026, a soil survey of 52.38 million hectares has been carried out across the 
country.  
IV. Digital General Crop Estimation System (DGCES) is a robust crop production 
estimation system that requires truthful and reliable data on area and yield. 
While the Digital Crop Survey provides crop sown area in near real-time, the 
new Digital General Crop Estimation System (DGCES) provides accurate and 
timely crop yield data for evidence-based crop production estimates. Across the 
country, Digitized Crop Cutting Experiments have been conducted in 43,105 
villages during 2025-26.  
  

 
(b) The yearly funds released under the Digital Agriculture Mission (since inception) for 
various components, including the Farmer Registry, Digital Crop Survey (DCS), Digital

(c) The government consistently evaluates the outcomes of the mission. States are using

Samman Nidhi Yojna (PM Kisan), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY), Minimum 
Support Price (MSP) based procurement, access to credit delivery, input distribution, 
and disaster relief.

be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated or is in the process of formulating any comprehensive 
strategy to make Gaushalas self-reliant through activities such as compost fertilizer production, milk 
and ghee processing, and bio -gas/based power generation u nder the Cow/Progeny Development 
Scheme and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the steps taken by the Government to enhance public –private partnerships in the management 
and operation of Gaushalas and to promote the production of medicines and other useful products 
derived from cow-based resources; and  
 
(c) whether any financial or technical assistance is being provided by the Government to such 
Gaushalas for capacity building and value addition and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
 
(a) Animal Husbandry and management of stray cattle including making availability of fodder 
for stray animals is a state subject.  
 
However, t he Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying , Government of India  is 
implementing the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) to incentivize 
establishment of dairy processing and value addition infrastructure. This scheme also provides 
assistance for establishment of infrastructure for animal waste to wealth management (agri -waste 
management). Under this component the eligible e ntities can establish bio -gas/based power 
generation and compost fertilizer  (Phosphate Rich Organic Manure). The eligible e ntities are 
Individuals, MSME, Private Companies, FPO, Dairy Cooperatives and Section 8 companies.  
 
The scheme envisages 3% interest subvention for eight years with a two-year moratorium on term 
loan up to 90% of the project cost borrowed from scheduled banks and institutions such as 
NABARD, NCDC, NDDB, and SIDBI. In addition, the Central Government has established a 
Credit Guarantee Trust to provide Credit Guarantee up to 25% of term loan to MSME and Dairy 
Cooperatives. Eligible entities can also take benefit of dovetailing with various central and state 
government initiatives to ensure holistic development of the dairy ecosystem. 
 

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is promoting the installation of small biogas, medium 
size biogas plants. Under GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) scheme 
implemented by Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, assistance is provided for setting up of 
community/ cluster-based bio-gas plant. 
 
(b) & (c) Since the establishment of gaushala is State subject, the policy of running of gaushala is 
determined by the respective state government. States, if required, can frame policy for running of 
gaushala through Public P rivate Partnership model. The Animal Welfare Board of India promotes 
scientific Gaushala management through awareness and capacity-building programmes. The Board 
has developed a Gaushala Management Training Module and organizes training programmes, 
workshops and seminars on scientific management of Gaushalas, Panchgavya, utilization of cattle 
bio-resources (cow dung and cow urine), and production of Panchgavya and other value -added 
products, with the objective of promoting sustainable and self-reliant Gaushalas
