(a) to (f): Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA) is a Central Sector Scheme notified 
on 10.04.2026 for development of investment -ready industrial parks to enable 
investors to ground investment with ease, thereby adding to the manufacturing 
capacity in the country. 
The total financial outlay for the Scheme is ₹ 33,660 crore and the duration of 
the Scheme is for a period of 6 years. 

Under the Scheme, financial assistance is to be provided for development of 
100 industrial parks. In the first phase, 50 projects are to be taken up, with one 
or more rounds of selection. 
The mandatory eligibility criteria include minimum contiguous land area of 100 
acres in non -hilly States and 25 acres in hilly States, North Eastern Region, 
Union Territories and States having population below one crore as well as 
availability of 90 percent encumbrance -free land at the time of submission of 
application. 
The selection of projects is based on Challenge mode with evaluation on 
parameters such as  connectivity and site suitability, quality of DPR, the 
demand for industrial land provision of services at site, and policy enablers for 
ensuring investments in the developed park, being provided by the State/UT 
Governments. 
Applications meeting the mandatory eligibility criteria would be evaluated and 
scored in accordance with the evaluation criteria prescribed under the Scheme 
guidelines issued on 23.05.2026. No proposal has been received on the portal 
till date. 
Financial assistance upto Rs. 1 crore per acre is allowed for eligible 
components listed in the scheme guidelines. This contribution is in the form of 
equity from the Centre, with land contributed by the State/UT Government. 
The Scheme is designed to further the objective of transforming the country into 
a globally competitive manufacturing hub by providing supportive indus trial 
ecosystem with proximity to cities, connectivity to multi-modal logistics facilities 
and industrial hubs.

380.    Shri Balashowry Vallabhaneni: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: be 
pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government is providing support to development of integrated 
modern coastal fishing villages in the country, including Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) whether it is also true that Sorlag ondhi and Gullalamodha villages in Krishna 
district of Andhra Pradesh has been identified for development; 
(c) if so, the details of initiatives such as fish drying yards, processing centers, fish 
markets, fishing jetty, ice plant, cold storage and emergen cy rescue facilities, etc. 
undertaken to make this village a model and economically vibrant fishermen village; 
and 
(d) whether it is also true that the scheme has been extended till March, 2026 and if 
so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
 
 
(a) to (c): The PMMSY, implemented from 2020-21, provides for developing Integrated 
Modern Coastal Villages at a unit cost of ₹750 lakh to enhance economic and social 
gains for coastal fishers through sustainable practices. The initiative strengthens 
livelihoods and parti cipation across the fisheries value chain by supporting modern 
infrastructure, disaster -resilient housing, cyclone and tsunami shelters, and post -
harvest amenities tailored to local needs. It is a non -beneficiary-oriented intervention 
implemented jointly w ith coastal State Governments on a 60:40 cost -sharing basis. 
The scheme leverages the inherent strengths of coastal communities to promote 
sustainable economic growth. The Government of Andhra Pradesh has not availed 
this activity under the PMMSY.  

 
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
recognizing the importance of developing the coastal communities, has also taken up 
another transformative initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Matya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY) to develop the existing 100 fishermen villages situated close to the coastline 
in various States and Union Territories (UTs), including Andhra Pradesh, into Climate 
Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV), to make them economically vibrant 
fishermen villages. The development of CRCFV has been taken up under the Central 
Sector scheme component of the PMMSY with a unit cost of Rs 200 lakh per fishing 
village, and the entire cost (100%) is borne by the Government of India.  
The Department of Fisheries, Ministr y of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
in consultation with the Government of Andhra Pradesh, has identified 15 villages in 
the state  for development as CRCFV , including Sorlagondhi and Gullalamodha in 
Krishna district  of Andhra Pradesh . The propos als of the Government of Andhra 
Pradesh to develop the identified 15 villages as CRCFV at a total cost of Rs. 30 crore 
have been approved based on the Detailed Project Report ( DPR) submitted by the 
State, and so far, Rs. 15.0 Crore has been released to the  Government of Andhra 
Pradesh for implementation of the approved projects of CRCFV based on the 
utilisation. The approved interventions for Sorlagondhi and Gullalamodha villages 
include fish -drying platforms, solar fish -drying units, multipurpose fisheries  center, 
common fish market, high-mast solar lights, and jetty extension for safe boat mooring. 
Livelihood and climate-resilient activities comprise seaweed culture farms, sea -cage 
culture, colour GPS units, life -saving appliances, iceboxes, and other prod uctivity-
enhancing assets. The details of the interventions in both villages are provided in 
Annexure I.  
(d): The PMMSY scheme is extended up to 30 September 2026.

Barefoot technicians across six districts in the State of Kerala

AGRICULTURAL CENSUS (2021-22) 
 
384. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the present status of the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22), including the stages of 
work completed and the progress made since its commencement in 2022; 
(b) the reasons, if any, for the delay in completing the Census and publishing its 
findings, along with the revised timeline for its completion and release; 
(c) the number of villages and agricultural households selected or covered under the 
Census, indicating the sampling methodology adopted, wherever applicable, State/UT-
wise; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to use the findings of the census for formulating 
polices relating to agricultural production, land holdings, crop diversification and farmers’ 
welfare, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (d):  Agriculture Census in India is conducted after every five years in collaboration 
with the States and Union Territories. The field work of Agriculture Census is carried out 
in three distinct phases. The ongoing 11th Agriculture Census with the reference year 
2021-22 has been commenced in 2022 and so far, field work & data collection for three 
phases have been completed within time frame.         
  

 
 
Further, in phase-I, data on primary characteristics of agricultural holdings and area 
operated are collected on complete enumeration basis. In Phase-II, data on characteristics 
of holdings like cropping pattern, irrigation status etc. are collected from randomly selected 
20% of sample villages in each Tehsil. In phase III, data on input use pattern of operational 
holdings are collected from randomly selected 7% of sample villages in each Tehsil.  
Agriculture Census provides reliable data base on socio-economic aspects of 
operational holders in the country which is used for making agricultural policies. It provides 
information on the number, size and distribution of operational holdings by classes 
(marginal, small, semi-medium, medium and large), tenancy, consolidation of holdings, 
land distribution etc. which is used for efficient planning for utilization of land, irrigation 
facilities, crop diversification, mechanization and other agricultural inputs. It provides data 
on woman-operated land holdings to support gender-based agricultural interventions. 
Census data also enables Government in efficient allocation of subsidies, credit facilities, 
targeting rural development programs, and establishing national and regional agricultural 
priorities. Further, it serves as a key data source in agriculture sector for researchers, 
planners, and other stakeholders.

क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
                        
(a), (b) & (d): States have submitted single consolidated Annual Action Plans 
(AAPs) covering all relevant schemes of the Department of Agriculture & Farmers 
Welfare (DA&FW), including the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization 
(SMAM).  
  

       The State-wise and year-wise number of beneficiaries during last five years

(c) & (e): Impact evaluation study of schemes is a standard, systematic 
process used to determine the long-term, direct, and indirect effects of policies, 
programs, or projects. The impact evaluation of SMAM was carried out as a part of 
study ‘Evaluation of CSS Schemes in Package 1 – Agriculture & Allied Sector’ 
under the aegis of the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI 
Aayog.   
 
        The study report released in 2025, provides an integrated assessment of 
various schemes including SMAM based on primary fieldwork across diverse agro-
climatic zones, quantitative surveys with beneficiaries, extensive stakeholder 
consultations at the central, state, district, and block levels, and secondary data 
analysis from official records and scheme Management Information System (MIS). 
The study report indicated that the SMAM has showed enhanced alignment with 
smallholder needs, particularly through the availability of rental machinery. 
Agricultural mechanization has been viewed as a critical intervention for improving 
farm productivity and reducing labour constraints.  As informed by Indian Council 
of Agricultural Research (ICAR), the farm power availability of India increased from 
0.372 kW/ha in 1971-72 to 3.045 kW/ha in 2021-22.

ACTION PLAN FOR DROUGHT MITIGATION 
393.  SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA:  
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government propose to formulate concrete plan to tackle the drought 
situation in the country in the near future; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Government is primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground 
level in the wake of notified calamities including drought. The State Governments 
undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the 
form of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of 
India approved items and norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, 
is considered from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down 
procedure, in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes an assessment based on 
the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) and a memorandum for assistance 
under NDRF submitted by the State/ UT Government.  
The details of the fund allocated and released under SDRF/NDRF to the States are 
available on Disaster Management, MHA's website i.e. https://ndmindia.mha.gov.in . 
 
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is mandated to monitor and 
coordinate relief measures in the wake of drought in the country. Monitoring and 
management of drought is carried out as per the Manual for drought management which 
clearly delineates the roles and responsibilities of different agencies and guides 
coordination against them. The Manual covers institutional structure, key variables for 
monitoring drought, declaration of drought, drought response, relief and mitigation. 
 
To promote the use of modern technology, the Manual was revised / updated in 
2020. The revised Drought Manual provides for use of modern technology in 
monitoring/determination of drought. New scientific indices and parameters was 
incorporated for a more accurate assessment and monitoring of drought.  
 
District Agriculture Contingency plan (DACPs) is prepared by ICAR-CRIDA for 651 
districts in the Country which provides for contingency measures to cope with drought for 
rainfed and irrigated (ground water irrigated, tankfed and canal command areas), farming 
situations on account of delayed onset of monsoon ( 2/4/6/8 weeks delays) and (early/mid 
season/ terminal drought) for field and horticulture crops. The contingency measures 
include alternate crops/ crop varieties/agronomic practices/ other management options 
appropriate for drought scenarios. 

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) along with weather index based 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) provide a 
comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crop  to farmers suffering crop 
loss/damage arising out of unforeseen natural calamities. PMFBY covers risks from 
prevented sowing to post harvest losses.    
Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme improves water use efficiency through Micro 
Irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems.  
The focus of Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme is on Integrated Farming 
System (IFS) to enhance productivity and minimise risks associated with climatic 
variability. Under RAD, crops/ cropping system is integrated with activities like horticulture, 
livestock, fishery, agro-forestry, apiculture etc. to enable farmers, not only in maximize 
farm returns for sustainable livelihood but also to mitigate the impacts of drought, flood or 
other extreme weather events.  Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), 
Agroforestry & National Bamboo Mission also aim to increase climate resilience in 
agriculture. 
National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) project implemented 
by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed and promoted 
climate resilient technologies in agriculture for vulnerable areas of the country. The outputs 
of the project help the regions to cope with extreme weather conditions like droughts, 
floods, frost, heat waves, etc. For enhancing the resilience and adaptive capacity of 
farmers to climate variability, the Concept of “Climate Resilient Villages” (CRVs) was 
initiated under NICRA. Location-specific climate resilient technologies are demonstrated 
in climatically vulnerable districts for adoption by farmers. Capacity building programmes 
are conducted to educate the farmers on various aspects of climate change for wider

DRONE-BASED LAND SURVEYS AND DIGITISATION OF PROPERTY RECORDS 
  
395. DR. PRASHANT YADAORAO PADOLE:      
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Ministry has assessed the impact of drone-based land surveys and digital 
property records on dispute reduction and transparent land governance;  
(b) if so, the details thereof and the number of land disputes resolved before and after 
implementation along with coverage of drone surveys and digitized records; state and district 
wise; and  
(c) the details of time reduction in land record verification and registration. 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
  
(a), (b) and (c) The main objective of the SVAMITVA Scheme is to provide Record of Rights to 
property owners in rural inhabited areas. Under the Scheme, rural inhabited land is demarcated 
using drone survey and Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) technology to create 
high accuracy maps of abadi areas of villages. These highly accurate maps help reduce property-
related disputes by clearly demarcating property boundaries and creating Record of Rights. The 
Scheme provides for ground verification and resolution of objections/disputes by the competent 
State authorities before issuance of Property Cards, ensuring transparency and fair demarcation 
of properties.  
  
No such assessment has been undertaken on the reduction of property-related disputes, time 
taken for land record verification and registration, or improvement in land administration before 
and after implementation of the SVAMITVA Scheme. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj 
has conducted an impact evaluation of the Scheme through IIM Ahmedabad to assess the impact 
on bank loan uptake and Gram Panchayat’s own sources of revenue. The study found substantial 
increase in bank loan amounts availed against property cards and increase in Gram Panchayat’s 
property tax and other local taxes after implementation of SVAMITVA Scheme. The Ministry 
does not maintain data on the number of land disputes resolved before and after implementation 
of the Scheme. As on date, drone survey has been completed in 3.30 lakh villages, and 3.24 crore 
Property Cards have been prepared for 1.97 lakh villages. State and district-wise details are at 
Annexure.

entries.head:
O.I.H. 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE

TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st  JULY, 2026 
 
INCOME OF MUSTARD AND BAJRA PRODUCING FARMERS  
 
396. SHRI BHAJAN LAL JATAV: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण 
मंğी be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the schemes being implemented by the Union Government to 
increase the income of mustard and bajra producing farmers;  
(b) the extent to which the farmers of Rajasthan have benefited from these schemes;  
(c) the assistance made available for the development of value addition, storage and 
marketing infrastructure; and  
(d) whether any special scheme is under consideration to promote agro-processing in 
the Karauli-Dholpur region? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): The Government of India is implementing a comprehensive range of 
Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes across the country, including 
Rajasthan, aimed at increasing the income of farmers including those growing mustard 
and bajra. These interventions aim to improve production & productivity, reducing 
whole cultivation costs, mitigating production risks and enhancing farmers’ income. 
Details at Annexure 1. The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) 
aims at enhancing domestic edible oil production including mustard & rapeseed to 
achieve self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in edible oils.  Under the Mission in 
Rajasthan, an expenditure amounting to Rs. 74.90 crores has been incurred during 
FY 2025-26. 
  

 
       The Sub-Mission on Shree Anna under the National Food Security & Nutrition 
Mission (NFSNM) is being implemented to increase the production and productivity of 
millets, including Bajra, in the 28 States and 2 Union Territories, including Rajasthan. 
Under the programme, assistance is provided for demonstration of improved 
production and protection technologies, distribution of certified seeds, integrated 
nutrient and pest management, and other interventions aimed at enhancing 
productivity. Under the Mission in Rajasthan, an expenditure amounting to Rs. 127.53 
crores has been incurred during FY 2025-26. 
(c) & (d): The Government of India supports the development of agricultural value 
addition, post-harvest management, storage and marketing infrastructure through 
various schemes and programmes such as Agriculture Infrastructure Fund 
(AIF), Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (ISAM), Mission for Integrated 
Development of Horticulture (MIDH) etc.  In addition, under the Pradhan Mantri 
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY), financial assistance is available to States 
for undertaking State-specific projects aimed at strengthening agricultural value 
chains, post-harvest management, processing, storage and market linkages, based 
on local priorities and requirements. 
       Under AIF, loans worth ₹4,895.13 crore have been sanctioned for 6,544 projects 
with a total project cost of ₹8,123.67 crore. In Karauli district, loans worth ₹14.39 crore 
have been sanctioned for 20 projects with a total project cost of ₹25.19 crore. In 
Dholpur district, loans worth ₹25.11 crore have been sanctioned for 25 projects with a 
total project cost of ₹52.22 crore.  
      Under ISAM, 1,934 storage infrastructure projects of storage capacity of 39.53 lakh 
MT have been assisted with subsidy release of Rs. 151.49 crore up to 30.06.2026. In 
addition to storage infrastructure, 610 Marketing Infrastructure (other than storage) 
projects have also been assisted with subsidy release of ₹ 106.94 crore. Karauli and 
Dholpur district have 1 project each with a storage capacity of 5,000 MT each, for 
which a subsidy of ₹37.50 lakh and ₹25.00 lakh has been released respectively. 
     No special scheme is under consideration for promotion of agro-processing in the 
Karauli–Dholpur region.

entries.t: Benefits of Government Schemes for Delhi Farmers
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 397 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21ST  JULY, 2026 
 
BENEFITS OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES FOR DELHI FARMERS 
 
397. SHRI YOGENDER CHANDOLIA 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that farmers of National Capital Territory of Delhi 
are not getting the benefits of various Central Government Schemes meant for 
farmers, such as PMFBY, Kisan Credit Card and PM-KUSUM; 
(b) if so, the details of total number of farmers in NCT of Delhi identified under 
Agriculture Census and the number of farmers covered under each of the above 
schemes, district-wise, for the last three years and the current year; 
(c) the reasons for low coverage/pending applications under these schemes in Delhi, 
including issues related to land records, portal access and coordination with GNCTD; 
(d) whether the Government has taken or proposes to take any steps to ensure 100% 
saturation of eligible farmers in Delhi under Central Schemes; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and the timeline fixed for the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Agriculture is a State subject. Government of India supports State 
Governments/Union Territories through a range of Central Sector and Centrally 
Sponsored schemes. These schemes encompass entire spectrum of agriculture 
including credit, insurance, income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, 
seeds, mechanization, marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, 
irrigation, extension, procurement of crops and digital agriculture. 
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and weather index based 
Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) provide financial 
support to farmers at the time of losses due to natural calamities. The adoption of the 
schemes is voluntary for States/Union Territories as well as farmers. The UT of Delhi is 
not implementing the scheme. 
The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme is being implemented in Delhi. Till date, a 
total of 1,821 Kisan Credit Cards have been issued to farmers in Delhi. 
No proposal/demand has been received from the State Implementing Agency of 
the Government of NCT of Delhi for allocation under PM-KUSUM, being implemented 
by Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. 
Under Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) and Krishonnati 
Yojana (KY), financial assistance is released to States/UTs for implementation of 
approved projects and interventions under the respective scheme components. The 
Government of NCT of Delhi has been provided assistance under these schemes based 
on approved Annual Action Plans.  In the last three years,  action plans of ₹5.77 crore 

and ₹1.10 crore have been approved by Government of India for implementation of 
projects under PM-RKVY and KY respectively based on the proposal received from 
Government of Delhi. For the current Financial Year 2026–27, Annual Action Plan (AAP) 
for KY has been approved with an outlay of ₹10.00 lakh under the Digital Agriculture 
Mission, ₹130.43 lakh under Agriculture Extension, and ₹140.43 lakh under the Mission 
for Atmanirbharta in Pulses.  Further, an amount of ₹339.00 lakh has been approved 
under the Crop Residue Management (CRM) component of PM-RKVY, while ₹36.49 
lakh has been approved under the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF). 
(c) to (e): As per the Agriculture Census (2015–16), Delhi had a total of 20,842 
operational holdings, defined as land wholly or partly used for agricultural production. 
The low coverage is primarily attributable to the prevalence of marginal 
landholdings, relatively small number of farmers engaged in agriculture and allied 
activities, and the fact that a significant proportion of farmers cultivate leased agricultural 
land. 
Saturation of beneficiaries under various scheme is a continuous process and 
depends upon identification of eligible beneficiaries, participation of the State/UT 
Government and fulfillment of the prescribed eligibility conditions.

MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
 LOK SABHA

 ANSWERED ON 21st JULY, 2026 
 
                           Ajanur Fishing Harbour 
 
398.  Shri Rajmohan Unnithan:  
 
          Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)   whether any proposals have been received from the Government of Kerala for the 
modernisation and expansion of Ajanur  Fishing Harbour in Kasaragod under Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), if so, the current status of such proposals;  
 
(b)     the details of financial assistance sanctioned by the Government for fisheries infrastructure 
in Kerala during the last three years; and  
 
(c)    the time by which the pending projects will get approval and implemented? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH) 
(a) The proposal for c onstruction of Ajanur  Fishing Harbour in Kasargod District in Kerala 
was submitted by  the G overnment of Kerala for fi nancial assistance under Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The proposal was examined and found to be economically 
unviable due to its proximit y to existing fishing harbours, high construction costs, additional 
costs in environmental mitigation measures and limited number of mechanized fishing vessels 
belonging to Ajanur . These reasons  were communica ted to the Government of Kerala . No 
revised proposal for Ajanur Fishing Harbour has been received from the Government of Kerala. 
 
(b)  During the last three financial years from 2023-24 to 2025-26, funds to the t une of Rs 
192.94 Crore was  released under the Centrally Sponsored Component of PMMSY for fisheries 
development projects including fishing harbour infrastructure to the Government of Kerala. 
During 2026-27, a mother sanction of Rs 30 crore was issued to Government of Kerala. In 
addition, Rs 25 Crore was also released under central sector component of PMMSY for fishing 
harbour infrastructure.  
 
(c) The Department of Fisheries, Government of India has processed all proposals for 
fisheries infrastructure received from Kerala, and no proposal is pending for approval at present. 
*******

400.  SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH: 
      SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE: 
      SMT. SUPRIYA SULE: 
 
Will the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare/ कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the decline in sugarcane production 
in Maharashtra due to crop diseases such as red rot, erratic weather conditions 
including El Niño-induced drought and unseasonal rains, and the increasing shift of 
farmers towards alternative crops because of rising labour and cultivation costs; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed impact on sugar recovery, farmer 
incomes, and the functioning of cooperative sugar mills in Maharashtra, district-
wise; 
(c) whether any special financial assistance, disease-resistant sugarcane varieties, 
climate-resilient farming practices, and irrigation support are proposed for 
sugarcane-growing regions in the State; and 
(d) the steps being taken to strengthen research, disease surveillance and extension 
services to safeguard Maharashtra’s sugar economy and protect the livelihoods of 
sugarcane farmers? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE 
कृͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏयमंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  The production of Sugarcane has increased from 1,099.70 lakh tonnes during 
2024-25 to 1,316.49 lakh tonnes during 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimates) in the State 
of Maharashtra (Annexure I).  
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), through its 
Regional and Central Integrated Pest management Centers at Nagpur and Nashik 
regularly conducts pest surveillance and disseminates Integrated Pest Management 
(IPM) knowledge through training programmes like Farmers Field Schools, Season 
Long Training Programme and Orientation Programme.  

Surveys were conducted in various districts of Maharashtra and infestation of 
red rot disease in sugarcane above Economic Threshold Level (ETL) was observed in 
34 Ha only out of 4295 Ha surveyed during 2024-2025. Similarly, infestation above 
ETL was observed in 5 Ha only out 1450 Ha surveyed in 2025-2026. Accordingly, 
advisories were issued to farmers. Details of trainings conducted and advisories 
issues are at Annexure II. 
(b):  As per inputs received from Department of Food and Public Distribution, the 
State Government systematically assesses estimation of area and productivity of 
sugarcane. Sugar recovery depends closely on the specific crop variety, soil 
conditions, weather parameters, and several other regional agro-climatic factors. As 
per recent concluded crushing season, the average sugar recovery rate  was recorded 
at 11.26% across Maharashtra. There were a total of 210 operational sugar mills (of 
both cooperative and private crushing entities) during current sugar season across the 
state. In terms of impact on farmer incomes, the implementation of regulatory payout 
mechanisms remains highly effective, with approximately 99.6% of Fair and 
Remunerative Price (FRP) payments successfully disbursed to growers during current 
sugar season. 
 To build long-term economic resilience, the State Government continuously 
encourages mills to diversify their revenue streams, including the setting up and 
technical upgradation of co-generation power plants and ethanol distillation units 
under the National Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP), thereby enabling mills to 
optimize cash flows and become less dependent on sugar market price volatility alone.  
Further, the Central Government has increased the Fair and Remunerative 
Price (FRP) of sugarcane for the ensuing Sugar Season 2026–27 to Rs. 365 per 
quintal, up from Rs. 355 per quintal in the current Sugar Season 2025–26, based on 
a sugar recovery rate of 10.25% 
(c) & (d):   During 2014-25, a total of 341 Drought tolerant Varieties have been 
released by Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), out of which 36 are of 
Sugarcane.  
As informed by the State Government, the State of Maharashtra has been 
implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme National Food and Nutrition Security 
Mission (NFNSM) – Commercial crop: Sugarcane Development Programme since 
2014-15. Under NFNSM, emphasis has been given on transfer of technology through 
demonstrations and training in order to extend benefits to the farmers.  
  

Under the programme, the following components are being implemented: (a) 
demonstration on inter-cropping and single bud chip technology with sugarcane, (b) 
assistance for breeder seed production, (c) tissue culture plantlets, (d) State level 
training for 2 days, (e) Distribution of plant protection and bio agents; (f) Local 
initiatives Raton and Trash Management distribution and Supercane nursery.

SELECTION METHODOLOGY UNDER PM-DDKY 
404. SHRI G KUMAR NAIK: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has prepared district-wise scores and rankings based on the 
criteria of agricultural productivity, cropping intensity and credit disbursement for selection 
under Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY); 
(b) if so, the details and the criterion-wise scores and rankings of all districts considered for 
inclusion under the scheme; 
(c) whether the Government will place the methodology, weightage assigned to each 
parameter and cut-off values used for selection in the public domain; 
(d) whether any districts were excluded despite meeting one or more of the prescribed 
criteria and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government has undertaken any independent assessment or validation of 
the selection methodology and if so, the details and findings thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): The 100 districts under Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (DDKY) have 
been selected based on three indicators of low productivity, low cropping intensity and less 
agriculture credit disbursement.   
The number of districts for each State is based on net cropped area and number of 
operational holdings, ensuring balanced regional development and fostering agricultural 
growth where it is most needed. 
(c) & (d): The methodology used published data, which is already in public domain, of above 
mentioned three indicators. Each State was covered under DDKY, with at least 1 district, 
based on net cropped area and number of operational holdings, hence question of exclusion 
does not arise. Further, if States identify additional districts that require similar focused 
attention, they may adopt and replicate the same framework and approach in those districts 
using their existing administrative mechanisms and available scheme resources. 
(e): Since scheme is in 1st year, no independent assessment has been commissioned.

IMPACT OF GROUNDWATER CRISIS ON AGRICULTURE 
405.  SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study regarding the economic losses suffered 
by farmers in Bhiwani-Mahendergarh Lok Sabha Constituency due to declining groundwater 
availability and increasing irrigation costs, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any district-wise assessment has been made regarding the suitability of climate-
resilient and low-water-consuming crops for the region, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)whether the Government proposes to introduce a special pilot programme for millet, olive, 
medicinal plants and arid horticulture cultivation in the constituency, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether any proposal is under consideration for establishment of a Dryland Agriculture 
Research and Demonstration Centre in South Haryana; and 
(e)if so, the details thereof along with the expected benefits to farmers of Bhiwani and 
Mahendergarh districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a):  Government has not conducted any study regarding the economic losses to farmers 
in Bhiwani-Mahendergarh Lok Sabha Constituency due to declining groundwater. However, 
Central Ground Water Board jointly with the State Ground Water Departments, carries out 
annual assessment of dynamic groundwater resources at the block level. The assessment 
provides updated estimates of annual groundwater recharge, annual extractable groundwater 
resource, annual groundwater extraction and stage of groundwater extraction, and categorizes 
assessment units as Safe, Semi-Critical, Critical and Over-Exploited based on stage of 
groundwater extraction. Out of 19 groundwater assessment units in Bhiwani, Charkhi Dadri and 
Mahendragarh districts 14 units fall under over-exploited, critical and semi-critical units. 
 
(b): Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) - Central Research Institute for 
Dryland Agriculture has prepared District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) for all districts 
of the country, which identify district-specific climate-resilient and low-water-requiring crops and 
suitable varieties based on local agro-climatic conditions. For Bhiwani and Mahendragarh 
districts of Haryana, the recommended crops include pearl millet, greengram, mothbean, 
clusterbean, cowpea, castor, sesame, mustard, and chickpea. 
 
(c) to (e):  As per the information received from the Government of Haryana, the Centre 
of Excellence for Semi-Arid Horticulture Crops, Gignow, Bhiwani and the Integrated Horticulture 
Development Centre, Sundrah, Narnaul are operational in the constituency to promote semi-
arid horticulture cultivation. The Centres demonstrate improved varieties of semi-arid 
horticultural crops along with modern technologies such as micro-irrigation, automation and 
protected cultivation. They also serve as centres for production of quality planting material and 
hybrid vegetable seedlings and impart training to farmers on improved horticultural practices 

and efficient water management. Government assistance is also being provided for area 
expansion of horticultural crops through financial support for establishment of new orchards and 
cultivation of vegetables, spices, flowers and aromatic plants to promote crop diversification. To 
promote diversification towards horticulture, Government assistance is being provided to 
farmers for the area expansion of fruit crops such as ber, aonla, citrus (kinnow), guava, and 
strawberry, as well as for the cultivation of vegetables, spices, flowers and aromatic plants. 
During the year 2026–27, in District Bhiwani and Narnaul a target of approximately 2,360 acres 
with a total financial outlay of Rs. 3.18 crore has been earmarked for the area expansion of 
horticultural crops. Government assistance at the rate of 40% to 50% is being provided to 
farmers for establishment of new orchards and for the cultivation of vegetables, spices, flowers, 
and aromatic plants.

(a) to (c) The Union Cabinet approved the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on 12 
November 2025 with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for the period FY 2025–26 to FY 
2030–31. The Mission aims to enhance India's export competitiveness, with                    
a special focus on MSMEs, first-time exporters and labour-intensive sectors, through an 
integrated approach combining trade finance support with measures to improve market 
access and export readiness. 
 

 
2 
 
Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative provides the district-level framework for 
decentralised export promotion duly engaging all stakeholders and is aided by Export 
Promotion Mission at grassroots level. 
 
 
The institutional infrastructure under DEH comprises State Level Export Promotion 
Committees (SEPCs) and District Export Promotion Committees (DEPCs).

i. Support for Interest Subvention aims to bridge the interest-rate gap and ensure 
liquidity for MSME exporters at globally competitive rates against items notified. 
ii. Support for Collateral for Export Credit aims to bridge existing collateral gap 
and enable access to export credit for MSMEs. 
iii. Support for Alternative Trade Instruments provides alternate export financing 
mechanism by subventing export factoring interest rates for MSMEs. 
iv. Credit Guarantee Facility for E-Commerce Exporters supports MSME e-
commerce exporters selling via courier, postal or fulfilment warehouses through credit 
guarantee and interest subvention support on revolving working capital. 
v. Support for Emerging Export Opportunities enables MSMEs to expand into 
new/high-risk markets through access to shared-risk and credit-enhancement 
instruments. 
 
( e ) Available to all MSMEs, the Niryat Disha sub-scheme is focused on trade 
enablers such as export quality and compliance support, international branding and 
packaging, market access initiatives, logistics cost support to low export intensity

The National Database on Sexual Offenders (NDSO), is a centralized database 
established by NCRB in 2018 under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is designed to 
assist law enforcement agencies in the investigation, detection and prevention of 
sexual offences, including offences under the Protection of Chi ldren from Sexual 
Offences (POCSO) Act, by maintaining records of sexual offenders. The database 
serves as an investigative tool to facilitate the identification of accused and repeat 
offenders, verify criminal antecedents, during investigation of sexual o ffences. 
Access to NDSO is restricted to authorized law enforcement agencies, ensuring that  
information is used for official investigative purposes.  
 (c) to (e): National Crime Records Check (NCRC) portal developed by NCRB is used 
by government agencies for the preliminary verification of employees and 
personnel. It facilitates preliminary crime record check using CCTNS/ Inter-operable 
Criminal Justice System (ICJS) database.  
States/UTs have launched citizen portal over CCTNS application facilitating 
verification request by individuals/ organizations. Educational institutions, child 
care homes, and other establishments may request for verification of individuals 
through CCTNS citizen portals. States/UTs police can use NCRC for verifying crime 
records of an individual during the verification process.

Reporting Portal for reporting incidents of online child sexual exploitation and other 
cyber-crimes, and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline (1930) provides

entries.t: One District One Product for Karbi Anglong
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 408. 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 21ST JULY, 2026. 
 
ONE DISTRICT ONE PRODUCT FOR KARBI ANGLONG 
 
408.  SHRI AMARSING TISSO: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao districts of Assam have been identified 
under the  One District One Product (ODOP) initiative and, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  the products identified under the initiative in the said districts; 
 
(c)  the details of financial, technical and marketing assistance, including support 
for branding and exports, provided under the initiative in the said districts; and 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to establish dedicated ODOP export hubs 
or common facilitation centres in Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao and, if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d):  One District One Product (ODOP) is an initiative by the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) with the aim of selecting, 
branding, and promoting at least one product from each district of the country 
to enable holistic growth across all regions. The selection of ODOP products is 
undertaken by the respective State/UT Governments. The Government of 
Assam has identified Ginger as an ODOP product for Karbi Anglong and Dima 
Hasao districts. 
The implementation of ODOP is primarily throug h convergence with the 
schemes/programmes of the Central Ministries/Departments and the State 
Governments. No district-specific financial allocation is made under the ODOP 
initiative. 
Several steps have been undertaken to promote and enhance the visibility  of 
products identified under the ODOP initiative, including those identified from 
Assam. These steps include facilitating participation in domestic and 
international exhibitions; capacity -building initiatives in collaboration with 

various agencies; and e -commerce onboarding drives for the Government e -
Marketplace (GeM)-ODOP Bazaar, which showcases and stocks India’s best 
ODOP products. 
The ODOP initiative has previously collaborated with key institutions such as 
the Indian Institutes of Technology (IIT Bom bay, Roorkee, Kharagpur, and 
Bhubaneswar), and National Institute of Design (NID Ahmedabad), along with 
the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and Press Information Bureau 
(PIB), to undertake capacity-building initiatives focused on product innova tion, 
diversification, quality enhancement, and market readiness, thereby supporting 
local industries including agriculture-based products from Assam. 
For promoting ODOP at the international level, engagement with MEA and 
Indian Missions abroad, virtual buyer -seller meets, and participation in 
international exhibitions have been undertaken. Also, various ODOP Products 
have been included in gifting at mul tilateral and bilateral meetings in India to 
popularize them internationally. 
Further, the Government of Assam has informed that the PM Formalization of  
Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme provides financial 
assistance for setting up ODOP unit s, along with branding and marketing 
support for food processing units. Under the Scheme, financial assistance has 
been extended to 7 ODOP units in Karbi Anglong and 8 ODOP units in 
Dima Hasao. District Export Promotion Committees have been constituted in 
all districts to promote ODOP products. The State Government has constructed 
the Unity Mall in Guwahati, which has stalls showcasing ODOP products, 
including those from Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao.

entries.t: Agriculture Distress due to Extreme Climate
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS’ WELFARE  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 409 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21st JULY, 2026 
 
AGRICULTURE DISTRESS DUE TO EXTREME CLIMATE 
 
 409. ADV GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the increasing agricultural distress caused 
by unpredictable rainfall, extreme heatwaves, falling groundwater levels, and climate 
change-related crop losses, particularly in drought-prone and tribal regions of the 
country; 
(b) the details of the measures being taken to support farmers facing rising fertilizer, diesel 
and irrigation costs; 
(c) whether any district-specific assessment has been conducted regarding the impact of 
climate variability on crop productivity and farmer incomes in vulnerable regions; and 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to strengthen climate-resilient agriculture, 
improve water conservation and protect small and marginal farmers from recurring crop 
losses? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI  RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b) The Government is taking various measures to promote sustainable agricultural 
practices and effectively address the climate change-related challenges. The Government 
supports farmers by ensuring the availability of key fertilizers at affordable prices through 
price regulation and subsidy mechanisms. Government has also implemented Nutrient 
Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) 
Fertilizers. Under NBS policy, MRP of P&K fertilizers are decontrolled and companies are 
free to fix MRP as per their business dynamics at a reasonable level. Further, under Urea 
Subsidy Scheme, Govt ensures affordable urea availability to farmers by providing 
government subsidies covering production and freight costs, with urea sold at a fixed 
Maximum Retail Price (MRP). In addition, under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, 
assistance is provided to States for promoting Integrated Nutrient Management through the 
judicious use of fertilizers, thereby improving fertilizer use efficiency and promoting 
balanced nutrient application. Since the inception of the scheme (2014-15), 26.18 crore 
Soil Health Cards have been generated. Fertigation is being promoted through micro-
irrigation systems under the Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) Scheme. Fertigation enables the 
application of water-soluble fertilizers directly to the root zone through micro irrigation 
systems, ensuring precise and uniform nutrient delivery. This improves fertilizer use 
efficiency, reduces nutrient losses, and promotes judicious use of fertilizers. Since the 
inception of the scheme (2014-15), an area of 114.60 lakh hectares has been brought under 
micro-irrigation, benefitting about 100 lakh farmers. Further, as of the pre-monsoon 2026 
assessment, the groundwater situation remains largely stable across the country. Out of 
9,085 monitoring wells, 87.8% (7,977 wells) fall under the normal category.  Ministry of New 
and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is implementing Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha 

evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) under which financial assistance is provided for 
the installation of standalone solar agricultural pumps, including the replacement of existing 
diesel agricultural pumps in off-grid areas where grid supply is not available. Against the 
sanctioned capacity of 13.07 lakh solar pumps, around 11.5 lakh solar pumps have been 
installed, benefiting an equivalent number of farmers. These installations have resulted in 
annual savings of around 793 million litres of diesel and reducing the cost of irrigation. All 
these measures help in reducing the cost of production.      
 
(c) & (d): The Government, through Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is 
implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) that 
studies the impact of climate change on agriculture, conducts district level risk and 
vulnerability assessment of agriculture. Under the project, risk and vulnerability assessment 
of agriculture to climate change has been carried out at district-level for 651 predominantly 
agricultural districts as per Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) protocols. 
310 districts were identified as vulnerable out of which 109 districts have been categorized 
as ‘very high’ and 201 districts as ‘highly’ vulnerable. District Agriculture Contingency Plans 
(DACPs) for these 651 districts have also been prepared to address weather aberrations 
and recommending location specific climate resilient crops and varieties and management 
practices. To enhance resilience to climate variability, location-specific climate-resilient 
technologies, including the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), aerobic rice, direct-se

Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Sports 
 
LOK SABHA

Promotion of Traditional Indigenous Sports 
 
†41. Shri Anoop Pradhan Valmiki: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether some major sports receive greater attention and resources, 
while several nonmainstream  and traditional indigenous sports witness 
limited participation among the youth; 
 
(b) if so, the steps taken/being taken by  the Government to promote 
these sports at school,  college and community levels through 
infrastructure, financial assistance and talent identification; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to introduce any special schemes 
or incentives to boost participation of youth in sports; 
 
(d) the measures being taken by the Government to provide players of 
such traditional sports with international training, scientific support and 
appropriate guidance for global sport competitions; and 
 
(e) whether any long -term stra tegy has been formulated to enhance 
India's global competitiveness and performance in these sports and if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to ( c) 'Sports' being a State subject, the res ponsibility for 
development of sports, including promotion of traditional and indigenous 
sports at school, college and community level through infrastructure, 
provision of financial assistance, talent identification,  rests primarily 
with the respective Sta te/Union Territory Governments. The Union 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Government supplements these efforts by bridging  critical gaps.  The 
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports implements the following schemes 
for the promotion of sports in the country, including traditional and 
indigenous games, and to encourage greater participation of youth in 
sports: 
 
(i)     Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports; 
(ii)     Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs); 
(iii) Cash Incentives to Medal Winners in International Sports Events 
and their Coaches; 
(iv) National Sports Awards; 
(v)     Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons; 
(vi) Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Program for 
Sportspersons; 
(vii) National Sports Development Fund; 
(viii) Running Sports Training Centres through Sports Authority of 
India (SAI); and 
(ix) National Centre for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR). 
 
Details of the above schemes are available in the public domain on the 
websites of this Ministry and the Sports Authority of India. 
 
(d) The 'Promotion of Rural and Indigenous/Tribal Games' sub-
component of the Khelo India Scheme is specifically dedicated to the 
development and promotion o f rural and indigenous sports in the 
country. Financial assistance is provided for conduct of competitions, 
training programmes, awareness activities and ot her promotional 
initiatives to encourage wider participation at the school, college and 
community levels. 
 
(e) The Government’s long -term approach is to st rengthen the sports 
ecosystem from grassroots to elite level through the Khelo India 
Scheme, assistance to National Sports Federations, sports infrastructure 
development, talent identification, scientific training and competition 
exposure. The objective is to promote a wider sporting culture, preserve 
and popularise indigenous games, develop athletes in i dentified 
disciplines and improve India’s performance at national and international 
levels.

National Cooperative Policy 2025 
411. Dr. C M Ramesh: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
a) whether the National Cooperative Policy, 2025 envisages expansion of cooperatives into 
new sectors such as food processing, renewable energy, logistics, exports and digital 
commerce;  
b) whether the Government has identified sector -wise opportunities for promoting 
cooperative enterprises in Andhra Pradesh, particularly in fisheries, horticulture, dairy, 
tribal products, women-led enterprises and handloom sectors; 
c) whether any proposals have been received from the State Government of Andhra Pradesh 
for financial or technical assistance under the Policy; and 
d) if so, the details thereof, district -wise, including the likely employment generation and 
increase in farmers' income expected from such initiatives? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) Yes, Sir. The expansion of cooperatives into new sectors such as food processing, 
renewable energy, logistics, exports and digital commerce is enunciated in the National 
Cooperation Policy, 2025. Some of which are as follows: 
“4.2.5 Promote exports of cooperative sector products to international markets and 
enhance the share of the cooperative sector in the total export of the country;  
4.2.9. Promote the enhancement of existing processing capacities, including the 
manufacturing of value -added products through capital infusion, to increase 
members' incomes;  
5.1.3. Promote cooperatives to leverage e-commerce platforms, such as the Government e -
Marketplace (GeM) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), to access 
a large customer base and achieve better pricing;  
7.1.2. Promote the entry and strengthening of cooperatives in new and emerging sectors, in 
both urban and rural space, such as micro -insurance, renewable energy, water 

Page 2 of 3 
 
distribution, health, education, waste management, transportation, biogas production, 
mobile application -based aggregator services (for example – cooperative of taxi 
drivers, individuals providing household services (like plumber, electrician, etc.)), 
etc., to enhance diversification and increase member income.” 
(b) Yes, Sir. The Central Government has identified opportunities for promoting 
cooperative societies in Andhra Pradesh in the dairy sector under the White Revolution 2.0. 
Under the said initiative, it has been envisaged to set up 7042 new dairy cooperative societies 
(DCS) and to strengthen 2107 existing DCS. To date, 1078 new DCS have been formed, and 
807 existing DCS have been strengthened.  
Moreover, the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), a statutory 
organization under the Ministry of Cooperation, is implementing the “Yuva Sahakar” and 
“Swayam Shakti Sahakar” Schemes. Both the schemes are fully funded and supported by 
NCDC. Yuva Sahakar Scheme is implemented with the aim of encouraging newly formed 
cooperative societies with new and/or innovative ideas. The objective of the “Swayam Shakti 
Sahakar” Scheme is to facilitate access to affordable, cost -effective, and reliable financial 
services to the poor, including women ’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs), to undertake 
common/collective socio - economic activities to promote sustainable livelihoods. NCDC 
extends funding on a project basis. 
(c) & (d): No, Sir. No proposal has been received from the Government of Andhra Pradesh 
for financial or technical assistance under the National Cooperation Policy, 2025.  
However, NCDC has been mandated to promote economic development through cooperative 
institutions. The primary objective of this Corporation is to promote, strengthen, and develop 
farmer cooperatives with a view to enhancing production, productivity , and the creation of 
post-harvest infrastructure. To this end, NCDC extends financial assistance to cooperatives in 
diverse sectors such as agricultural marketing and inputs, processing, storage, marketing of 
agricultural produce, and supply of seeds, fertilizers , and other agricultural inputs. Since its 
inception, NCDC has been providing financial assistance under its Corporation -sponsored 
schemes as well as Central Sector Schemes of various Ministries, covering a wide spectrum 
of notified commodities and services. As of 30.06.2026, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed 
₹73,454.93 crore for the development of cooperative institutions in the state of Andhra

entries.head:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
 MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION 412

E-GRAM SWARAJ PORTAL IN SCHEDULED TRIBE-DOMINATED AREAS 
  
412. DR. FAGGAN SINGH KULASTE: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the utilization of e-Gram Swaraj and Audit Online 
portals by Gram Panchayats in Scheduled Areas and tribal-dominated areas is lower than the 
national average in these regions; 
  
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
  
(c)  the current status of the preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDP) in 
alignment with the provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 
1996, and the subsequent uploading of these plans on the e-Gram Swaraj portal in these areas; 
  
(d)  the major challenges identified regarding digital infrastructure, internet bumbling, 
connectivity, electricity supply, and technical capacity, along with the steps taken by the 
Government to mitigate them; and 
  
(e) whether the Government has conducted special training and capacity building programmes 
for elected representatives and panchayat officials in tribal areas formulated a specific action 
plan to strengthen digital governance in these regions of Panchayats, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a) to (b)  The Parliament enacted the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the 
Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) under Article 243M(4)(b) of the Constitution to extend the 
provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to the Fifth Schedule Areas with certain exceptions and 
modifications. Panchayats, being "Local Government", are a State subject and operate through 
the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. Accordingly, implementation of PESA, including the 
adoption and utilisation of digital governance applications such as eGramSwaraj and 
AuditOnline in Scheduled Areas, falls within the purview of the respective State Governments. 
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj facilitates digital governance through the e-Panchayat 
Mission Mode Project (MMP), including eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, and periodically 
reviews their implementation with the States through review meetings and other monitoring 

2 
 
mechanisms. The Ministry has also developed 10 PESA Indicators to facilitate assessment of 
PESA implementation by the States, one of which relates to the uploading of Gram Panchayat 
Development Plans (GPDPs) of PESA Gram Sabhas on the eGramSwaraj portal. 
The State-wise details of utilisation of eGramSwaraj/ status of GPDP uploads in PESA areas, are 
placed below.

(c)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has initiated Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) 
integration of PESA within the GPDP framework to enable the preparation of PESA-specific 
Village Development Plans. A dedicated PESA-GPDP Portal has been launched by the Ministry 
to facilitate the preparation, implementation, and monitoring of Gram Panchayat Development 
Plans (GPDPs) in Scheduled Areas under the provisions of the PESA Act. 
Further, in Plan Year 2026-27, PESA has been included as a separate theme in 
eGramSwaraj Portal with 42 activities. It has also been made mandatory for Gram Sabhas in 
Fifth Schedule Areas to take up at least one activity under PESA theme while preparing their 
GPDP plan. 
(d)  In certain rural and tribal areas, challenges such as inadequate digital infrastructure, 
intermittent internet connectivity, and limited technical capacity have been experienced, 
affecting the adoption of digital governance applications. To address these challenges, the 
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, in coordination with the State Governments, provides continuous 
technical support, undertakes periodic reviews of the implementation of the e-Panchayat 
applications, and upgrades the applications based on feedback received from the stakeholders. 
Further, internet connectivity to Gram Panchayats is being strengthened through the BharatNet 
project being implemented by the Department of Telecommunications to provide broadband

419. SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:   
(a)  the major progress made to empower Gram Panchayats and enhance transparency 
through the 'Gram Swaraj Abhiyan' and digital governance via the 'e-Gram Swaraj, portal in the 
country during the last two years; 
  
(b)  the specific budgetary assistance provided by the Government to strengthen the three-tier 
Panchayati Raj system and develop rural infrastructure in Madhya Pradesh; and 
  
(c)  whether the Government is providing any special financial package or technical 
assistance to address the lack of basic amenities such as modernization of Panchayat Bhawans 
and computer/internet connectivity in the remote and tribal-dominated Gram Panchayats of 
Chhindwara district, if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH)  
  
(a)  The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project 
(MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of strengthening 
transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions 
(PRIs) through digital enablement across all States. eGramSwaraj application developed under 
the e-Panchayat MMP is being implemented across Gram Panchayats throughout the country to 
strengthen transparency, accountability and digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions. 
eGramSwaraj facilitates planning, budgeting, accounting, progress reporting and asset 
management. 
As on date, during the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,730 Gram Panchayats and equivalent 
across the States/UTs, 2,55,251 Gram Panchayats and equivalent (98.65%), have uploaded their 
Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on e-Gram Swaraj and 2,45,839 Gram Panchayats 
and equivalents (95%) have made payments amounting to ₹57,337 crore through the e-
GramSwaraj–PFMS interface.  
The State-wise status of implementation of eGramSwaraj during last two years, is placed at 
Annexure.  

2 
 
(b)  Ministry of Panchayati Raj has been implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. The 
main objective of the scheme is to build the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by 
creating a learning ecosystem, especially through training for the Elected Representatives (ERs), 
functionaries, and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities to function 
effectively, and also by supporting exposure visits, development of training modules and 
materials, etc.  
Rural Local Bodies, including Gram Panchayats in Madhya Pradesh, receive Finance 
Commission Grants released by the Ministry of Finance for providing basic services and creation 
and maintenance of community assets and civic infrastructure in rural areas. The year wise 
details of funds released to the State of Madhya Pradesh under the Fifteenth Finance

(c)  No, Sir. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj does not provide any separate special financial 
package specifically for the Chhindwara district. 
Panchayat, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the Seventh 
Schedule of the Constitution of India. Thus, the primary responsibility of providing dedicated 
office infrastructure for Gram Panchayats and computer/internet connectivity in Panchayats lies 
with States/UTs. However, under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA), the Ministry supplements the efforts of States/UTs in building Panchayat 
infrastructure and Computers and peripherals, at a limited scale, with particular focus on the 
North Eastern States. Accordingly, since the inception of Revamped RGSA i.e. 2022-23, the 
Ministry has approved the procurement of 289 computers and the construction of 50 Panchayat 
Bhawans for the State of Madhya Pradesh. District-wise information is not maintained centrally.  
Further, the Ministry has developed digital applications such as eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline and 
mActionSoft to facilitate digital planning, accounting, audit and monitoring of Panchayat assets. 
The Ministry also extends technical support and capacity-building for effective adoption of these 
applications. Internet connectivity to Gram Panchayats is being improved through initiatives of 
the Department of Telecommunications, including the BharatNet project.

कृषि और ककसान कल्याण राज्य मंत्री (SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): No, there is no proposal to establish a National Soybean Research Centre in 
the Dharashiv and Parbhani districts of Maharashtra.  
 
 Dharashiv (4.54 lakh ha) and Parbhani (2.76 lakh ha) districts of Maharashtra account

2014–2025 along with matching crop management technologies for the Soybean farmers.  
 
 During 2023-24 to 2025-26, against the indents of 12202 quintals of soybean breeder 
seed, 36252 quintals breeder seed was supplied to the state by the AICRP on Seed centres. 
To augment the local availability of the quality seed of latest varieties of Soybe an, the

the National Mission on Edible Oil-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) during 2024-25. 
 
 To create awareness and demonstrate the new varieties and technologies, 1300 
frontline demonstrations were conducted at farmers’ fields during the last past five years.

Dharashiv and Parbhani districts of Maharashtra.

(a) to (d) The Government continuously monitors the availability, market arrivals, 
wholesale and retail prices, buffer stock position and export trends of onion across the 
country, including in Maharashtra and the Nashik region.  
Onion prices are influenced by several factors, including inter alia, crop area, weather 
conditions, seasonality, production and productivity, arrivals, storage losses, domestic 

2 
 
demand and international prices. Therefore, variations in mandi prices cannot be 
attributed solely to changes in the export policy. 
The existing policy framework provides for market intervention, buffer procurement 
and calibrated trade-policy measures. Whenever domestic supplies show stress, 
calibrated and temporary measures, such as minimum export price (MEP), export 
duties, or temporary restrictions, are imposed in the public interest to ensure food 
security, and withdrawn once the supply situation eases.  
The export policy of onion is accordingly calibrated from time to time, based on the 
prevailing domestic availability and price situation, with the objective of balancing the 
interests of farmers and domestic consumers. The flexible export regime based on the 
dynamics of domestic availability and prices gives Government the ability to respond 
promptly to exceptional supply and price situations.

MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 427 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
Implementation of National Cooperation Policy, 2025 
 
427. Shri E T Mohammed Basheer: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has prepared any roadmap and timeline for implementation the 
National Cooperation Policy, 2025 aimed at expanding the cooperative sector and 
connecting nearly 50 crore people, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the financial allocation made for the implementation of the policy, including support for 
proposed cooperatives in sectors such as taxi services, insurance, tourism and green 
energy; and 
(c) the steps taken and progress achieved so far in implementing the policy, particularly with 
regard to ensuring the participation and benefits for Dalits, Adivasis and women? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) Yes, sir. The National Cooperation Policy (NCP) 2025 was launched on 24th July 2025 by 
the Hon’ble Home & Cooperation Minister. The policy has been envisaged to fulfil the 
mandate of the Ministry of Cooperation - “Sahkar-se-Samriddhi.” It provides a roadmap 
for the systematic and holistic development of the cooperative sector. It has 6 strategic 
pillars, 16 objectives, and 83 recommendations to be achieved over the next 10 years. The 
policy further envisages creating an economic framework aimed at including 50 crore 
people within the ambit of cooperatives and enhancing the cooperative sector's 
contribution to the Indian economy by three times in the next 10 years. 
(b) Sir, no specific budgetary allocation is envisaged as part of the Policy document. 
(c) The policy contains provisions relating to the participation and benefits for Dalits, 
Adivasis, and women, some of which are as follows: 
“4.2.2. Promote dairy cooperatives to initiate ‘White Revolution 2.0’ for the holistic 
development of dairy cooperatives, employment generation, and women’ s empowerment. 

6.1.1. Encourage the participation of women, youth, small & marginal farmers, and 
weaker sections (SC/ST, specially -abled, etc.) to foster inclusivity and assign them 
significant roles in cooperatives. 
6.1.2. Strengthen and promote cooperatives for the weaker and marginalized sections 
in sectors like fisheries, dairy, handloom weaving, handicrafts, minor forest produce, etc.” 
The major steps taken and progress made under the policy for ensuring the participation and 
benefits for Dalits, Adivasis, and women are as follows: 
i) The Ministry of Cooperation has launched an initiative to usher Cooperative-led "White 
Revolution 2.0” aimed at expanding cooperative coverage, employment generation and 
women's empowerment with the target of increasing the milk procurement of dairy 
cooperatives by 50% from the present level (i.e., 660 LKgPD in Base Year 2023 -24) 
over next five years (i.e., 1007 LKgPD in 2028-29) by providing market access to dairy 
farmers in uncovered areas and increasing the share of dairy cooperatives in organised 
sector. The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for White Revolution 2.0 was 
launched on 19.09.2024 by the Hon’ble Home & Cooperation Minister in the presence 
of the Hon’ble Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. On 25.12.2024, 
the Hon’ble Home & Cooperation Minister, in the presence of the Hon’ble Minister of 
Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, inaugura ted 6,600 newly set up Dairy 
Cooperative Societies (DCSs). So far, 25,282 DCSs have been registered in 31 
states/UTs. 
ii) The Government of India has approved the plan to establish new multipurpose Primary 
Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS)/dairy/fisheries cooperatives, aiming to cover all 
panchayats and villages, including those falling in the Tribal/Dalits/Adivasis areas i n 
the country, over the next five years. The initiative to establish new multipurpose PACS, 
dairy, and fishery cooperatives is supported by NABARD, NDDB, and NFDB through 
the convergence of various existing Government of India (GoI) schemes, including the 
Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF), the National Programme for Dairy 
Development (NPDD), and the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). As per the 
National Cooperative Database, a total of 38,138 new PACS/Large Area Multi-Purpose 
Societies (LAMPS), Dairy and Fishery Cooperative Societies have been registered, and 
21,292 Dairy and Fisheries Primary Cooperative Societies have been strengthened as 
of 15.06.2026 across the country since the approval of the plan on 15.2.2023. Furthe r, 
the State-wise details of PACS, dairy, and fishery cooperative societies formed along 
with members associated with them, are placed as Annexure-I.

INNOVATIVE TEXTILE RECYCLING TECHNOLOGIES 
 
429.   SHRI KANWAR SINGH TANWAR: 
 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्रमंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
(a) the details of action plan formulated by the Government to incentivize technologies that 
convert discarded textiles into engineered stone, furniture, interior decor materials and other 
high-value products;  
(b) the details of collaborative initiatives launched with research institutions, industry, start -ups 
and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to accelerate the commercialisation of 
innovative textile recycling technologies;  
(c) the details of financial assistance, tax incentives, and incubation support provided for the 
development of sustainable textile-based composite materials;  
(d) the steps taken to incorporate recycled textile products into government procurement, public  
infrastructure and affordable housing projects; and  
(e) the details of targets set to strengthen the circular economy by reducing textile waste, 
improving resource efficiency and promoting the widespread adoption of advanced recycling 
technologies? 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्रराज्‍ यमंत्री(श्री‍पबित्र‍मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (e)  In the Union Budget 2026 –27, the Hon'ble Finance Minister announced the "Tex -Eco 
Initiative" to promote a globally competitive and sustainable textiles and apparel sector. The 
initiative aims to support innovative technologies for the circular economy, in cluding textile 
waste management, recycling, and value addition, as well as the development of recycled fibres, 
new materials, sustainable packaging, and other high -value products from discarded textiles, in 
collaboration with research institutions, Textil e Research Associations, Centres of Excellence, 
industry, start-ups, and other relevant stakeholders. 
 
      Further, the government in view of the growing global importance of environmentally 
sustainable production practices including green technology ado ption, recycling and waste 
reduction, and their anticipated benefits in terms of enhanced global competitiveness, improved 
market access, enhanced environmental & economic resilience, and strengthened investor 
confidence, a number of initiatives have been taken: 

  
i. The Government has been facilitating a series of pilot projects across the country to raise 
awareness and build capacity on global best practices of sustainable production & 
consumption with focus on subjects such as: 
 A project titled “Eliminating  Hazardous Chemicals from Textile Fashion Supply Chain” 
in partnership with UNIDO and supported by Global Environment Facility (GEF) to 
eliminate hazardous chemicals from the apparel fashion supply chain in India while 
promoting sustainable practices aimed  at reducing environmental impacts particularly in 
terms of energy and waste use, and greenhouse gas emissions. 
 „Accelerating the Transition of the Indian Textile Sector towards Circularity‟ (In -Tex 
India) being implemented in collaboration with UNEP, focuses on scaling circular 
business models by leveraging Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Product Environmental 
Footprint (PEF) methodologies.  
ii. Under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), several research and 
development (R&D) projects have been sanctioned with a focus on environmentally 
sustainable technologies and materials. 
iii. The PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel Parks are designed as a world -class 
industrial ecosystem to build resilient infrastructure, promote sustainable industrialization 
and foster innovation. 
iv. In order to mitigate effects of increasing textile waste, Government has undertaken 
number of activities including signing of an MoU among Textile Committee, Standing 
Conference of Public Enterprises (SCOPE) and the Government  e-Marketplace (GeM) to 
promote the use of upcycled products in Government procurement. 
v. Further, the Ministry has released the report "Mapping of Textile Waste Value Chain in 
India" which provides a comprehensive assessment of textile waste generation, rec overy 
pathways, recycling technologies and opportunities to strengthen circularity across 
India‟s textile value chain.  
The Government's approach combines support for technology development, research and 
innovation, to strengthen demand for sustainable and  recycled textile products. Together, 
these are aimed at improving resource efficiency and environmental performance across the 
textile value chain while enhancing the global competitiveness of Indian textiles and apparel.
