REVISION OF MPLADS FUNDS 
   
484. SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA: 
  
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME 
IMPLEMENTATION be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the reasons for continuing the annual allocation under the 
Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) 
at Rs. 5 crore per Member since 2011 –12, despite  inflation and 
increased cost of public works; 
  
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any review or 
assessment of the adequacy of the present MPLADS limit in view of 
current development needs; 
  
(c) whether the Government proposes to revise or enhance  the 
MPLADS annual allocation and if so, the details thereof; and  
  
(d) whether the Government has prepared any time -bound roadmap 
or framework for increasing the MPLADS limit and if so, the details 
thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION; MINISTER OF 
STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CULTURE (RAO 
INDERJIT SINGH) 
(a) The Union Cabine t, in its meeting held on 05.05.2026, approved 
the continuation of the Members of Parliament Local Area 
Development Scheme (MPLADS) for the period from FY 2026–27 to FY 

2030–31, coterminous with the 16th Finance Commission period, with 
an annual entitlement of ₹5.00 crore per Member of Parliament. 
(b) The primary objective of the Members of Parliament Local Area 
Development Scheme (MPLADS) is to enable each Member of 
Parliament to recommend developmental works based on the locally 
felt needs of the people, with emphasis on the creation of durable 
community assets for the larger public good. 
The works permissible under the Scheme span a wide range of 
sectors, including public and community infrastructure, public 
conveniences, safety and security, education, public health, drinking 
water, and sanitation. While various Central and State Governme nt 
Ministries and Departments implement sector -specific schemes in 
these areas, the MPLADS is intended to complement such initiatives 
by addressing locally identified development needs, providing last -
mile connectivity, and bridging viability gaps, rather than replacing 
or duplicating existing schemes. 
Further, to enhance the coverage and impact of works under the 
Scheme in line with emerging development needs, the Union Cabinet, 
while approving the continuation of the MPLADS, also approved 
convergence of M PLADS with more number of Central and State 
Government schemes as well as projects of local bodies. This 
decision, based on the recommendations of the Third -Party 
Evaluation of the Scheme conducted by the Ministry in 2025, is aimed 
at facilitating the exec ution of larger and more impactful projects 
through pooled funding, thereby enhancing the overall effectiveness 
of the Scheme and enabling Members of Parliament to recommend 
works of greater scale and wider public benefit without duplication. 
(c) and  (d) At present, there is no proposal under consideration to 
revise or enhance the MPLADS annual allocation. However, t he 
Ministry receives and examines, on a continuous basis, the new 
suggestions from stakeholders, including suggestions for revision 
of entitlem ent of funds under MPLAD Scheme, following due 
process.

indicating their district -wise installed capacity, power generation and present operational 
status, 
(c) the total solar power capacity generated through these solar parks during the last three years 
and the current year along with the quantum of power supplied to the State grid; 
(d) whether any constraints relating to land acquisition, transmission infrastructure, financing 
or grid integration have affected the timely implementation of solar parks in Maharashtra; and  
(e) if so, the measures being taken by the Government to expand solar park capacity, strengthen 
transmission infrastructure and accelerate renewable energy generation in Maharashtra? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK) 
 
(a) & (b) The Government has sanctioned three solar parks in Maharashtra, under the scheme 
for “Development of Solar Parks and Ultra Mega Solar Power Projects” for achieving the 
State's renewable energy targets and the country's clean energy goals. The details of these solar 
parks indicating their district-wise installed capacity and status are given at Annexure. 
 
(c) Out of these three solar parks, 225 MW of solar project has been commissioned in 
Dondaicha solar park, progressively since December 2025. Since then, 38.3 million units and 
66.85 million units of solar energy have been generated in FY 2025-26 and 2026-27 (till June 
2026) respectively.  
 
(d) & (e) The Solar Park scheme is implemented in coordination with the State Governments 
and other stakeholders to ensure its effective implementation. Further, the Government 
periodically reviews the progress of the scheme with all stakeholders and regularly 
communicates with the States to resolve issues, if any, relating to land acquisition, transmission 
infrastructure, financing, grid connectivity, and other implementation-related matters.

MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 489 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22/07/2026 
MODERNISATION OF HAJ INFRASTRUCTURE 
489.  SHRI RAJA A:  
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of projects undertaken by the Government for modernising and expanding Haj 
infrastructure;  
(b) the measures being taken to improve coordination between Government, Haj Committee of 
India and State authorities for Haj 2026 preparations in the country especially in Tamil Nadu;  
(c) whether Haj quota for the State of Tamil Nadu would be increased in view of large number of 
Muslim pilgrims aspiring to perform Haj and increase in the population of Muslims in the State 
and if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) the  details of initiatives adopted to ensure safety, comfort and logistical convenience of 
pilgrims especially senior citizens and first-time Haj travelers? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
SHRI KIREN RIJIJU 
(a): The Government, through the Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Haj Committee of 
India, in coordination with the concerned authorities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has 
undertaken various initiatives to modernise  and enhance the infrastructure and facilities for 
Indian Haj pilgrims. Some of the major initiatives are as follows: 
i. Improved Infrastructure at Mina Camps:  The traditional accommodation 
arrangements at Mina have been upgraded by providing sofa-cum-beds, ensuring greater 
comfort, better utilisation of available space and improved living conditions for pilgrims 
during their stay. 
ii. High-Speed Train Connectivity:  Indian Haj pilgrims are facilitated to travel between 
Makkah and Madinah  through the High-Speed Rail , which has significantly reduced 
travel time, improved safety, and enhanced overall travel convenience. 
iii. Haj Suvidha App:  The Ministry has developed the Haj Suvidha App , a comprehensive 
digital platform that enables pilgrims to access important Haj -related services such as 
travel details, accommodation information, baggage tracking, emergency contacts, 

grievance redressal , health -related information, and other essential services, thereby 
improving communication and service delivery throughout the pilgrimage. 
iv. Hotel-Style Accommodation in Makkah:  Hotel-style accommodation has been 
arranged for Indian Haj pilgrims in Makkah with improved amenities and services, 
ensuring enhanced comfort, better accessibility, and a more convenient stay during the 
Haj period. 
 (b): The Government has undertaken several measures to improve coordination between the 
Ministry, the Haj Committee of India, and State Haj Committees for the preparations for Haj -
2026. These include strengthened institutional coordination through periodic review meetings,  
issuance of detailed guidelines and timelines for all operational activities, and regular 
consultations to streamline accommodation, transport, training, and other logistical 
arrangements. 
(c): The allocation of Haj quota among States and Union Territories is made in proportion to 
their Muslim population as per the latest applicable Census data. Accordingly, there is no 
separate proposal under consideration for increasing the Haj quota of the State of Tamil Nadu. 
(d): The Government has taken several initiatives to ensure the safety, comfort and logistical 
convenience of Haj pilgrims, with special emphasis on senior citizens and first -time pilgrims. 
The major initiatives are as follows: 
i. Mandatory Companion for Elderly Pilgrims:  Pilgrims aged 65 years and above  are 
required to be accompanied by a companion to ensure adequate assistance and support 
throughout the pilgrimage. 
ii. Comprehensive Insurance Coverage:  Every Haj pilgrim is provided with insurance 
coverage of up to ₹6.25 lakh , offering financial protection in the event of unforeseen 
contingencies during the Haj journey. 
iii. SHI Ratio: For Haj 2026, the State Haj Inspector ratio  has been improved to 1:150, 
ensuring better accessibility and prompt services for pilgrims. 
iv. Pre-Departure Training:  All selected Haj pilgrims are imparted comprehensive 
orientation and training before their departure to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, covering 
pilgrimage rituals, travel procedures, health advisories, safety measures, and the use of 
digital services. 
v. Medical Infrastructure in Saudi Arabia:  Medical infrastructure comprising hospitals, 
medical centres  and dispensaries is established at key pilgrimage locations in the 
Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to provide timely and quality healthcare services during the 
Haj period.  The Government deputes qualified doctors, paramedics and other medical 
personnel to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to provide medical assistance and emergency 
healthcare services to Indian Haj pilgrims. 
These initiatives collectively aim to provide a safer, more comfortable and 
pilgrim-friendly Haj experience, particularly for senior citizens and fi

entries.t: Implementation of Skill Development Programmes in Perambalur
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 49 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMMES IN PERAMBALUR 
  
49.  THIRU ARUN NEHRU: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether skill development programmes are being implemented in Perambalur Lok Sabha 
Constituency to train youth in agriculture -allied sectors, agro -processing and emerging 
opportunities; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of training centres, courses and placement records under such 
programmes; and 
 
(c)  the special provisions made for women, SC/ST communities and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) 
under such Programmes? 
  
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) to (c): Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up- skill training through an 
extensive network of skill development centres/institutes under various sche mes, viz. Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan  (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including Perambalur Lok 
Sabha Constituency, covering agricultu re-allied sectors, agro -processing and emerging sectors. 
The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills. 
The details of training centres, candidates trained and courses under various schemes of MSDE 
in Perambalur Lok Sabha constituency (Karur, Perambalur & Tiruchirappalli districts)  are given at 
Annexure. 
 
Under PMKVY 1.0 to PMKVY 3.0 a total of 1.11 Crore candidates were certified, out of which 24.38 
lakhs were reported placed under STT component of the scheme. Under PMKVY 4.0, which is 
under implementation since FY 2022-23, the focus is to empower our trained candidates to choose 
their varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same. 
 
To encourage participation of women in skill development programs, special provisions have been 
made for meeting expenditure on conveyance and boarding & lodging, as well as enhanced post -
placement support under the common cost norms. 
 
PMKVY 4.0 is a demand -driven scheme designed to benefit all sections of society. However, the 
Scheme includes a dedicated provision for Special Projects aimed at enhancing the participation 
of under -represented social groups, including SC, ST, women, and p ersons with disabilities 
(PwDs). Special emphasis is placed on empowering women and marginalized communities by 
facilitating their access to skill development programs. 

Under the JSS Scheme, the focus is being given to women and other vulnerable sections. Women 
constitute more than 80% of beneficiaries under the JSS scheme. Additionally, livelihood cells have 
been created at each JSS, headed by the Programme Officer of th e JSS and supported by other 
staff members. This cell forms linkages of the trained JSS beneficiaries, especially women 
beneficiaries, with the Self -Help Groups (SHGs) / Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) to promote their 
entrepreneurship and livelihood. 
 
Government of India approved a 30% reservation of seats for women candidates in all ITIs (Govt. 
& Private) across all courses, and these seats could be filled in accordance with the general 
reservation policy of each respective State/UT. Further, 19 National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) 
and more than 300 ITIs are exclusively for women. 
 
Under the NAPS Scheme, the introduction of trades in the services sector (Optional Trade) has led 
to a significant improvement in women's participation in apprenticeships. The percentage of women 
apprentices has observed an increase from 22.79% in 2024-25 to 25.80% in 2025-26.

entries.t: Sanitation and Drinking Water Facilities in Trains
entries.head:
§  Page 1 of 3 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 490 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
SANITATION AND DRINKING WATER FACILITIES IN TRAINS 
 
†490. SHRI DHARMENDRA YADAV: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that the sanitation system 
in various trains of the country, especially cleanliness of toilets and 
availability of water is still not at a satisfactory level and if so, the 
details thereof;  
(b) the details of complaints received regarding cleanliness in trains and 
railway stations and their disposal during the last three years, year and 
zone-wise;  
(c) the details of steps, technology/monitoring system implemented by the 
Government to ensure regular availability of clean drinking water and 
clean toilet facilities to the passengers; and  
(d) the corrective measures taken/being taken by the Government to make 
the grievance redressal system of Railways more effective, transparent 
and time bound?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d) Cleanliness is a continuous process and Indian Railway (IR) 
makes every endeavour to keep the trains clean and maintain availability of 
water in toilets. However, due to heavy passenger usage, en-route 
depletion of water, complaints regarding cleanliness of toilets and 
availability of water are sometimes received. Such complaints are attended 
promptly through the established maintenance and grievance redressal 
mechanisms. 

Page 2 of 3 
RailMadad is Indian Railways grievance redressal mechanism that provides 
passengers an integrated platform for grievances, assistance and inquiry. 
Regular monitoring for cleanliness is done through checks/inspections and 
complaints/feedback received through Rail Madad/RailOne app and other 
passenger interfaces. In RailMadad, passengers can seek redressal 
through multiple channels such as Helpline number-139, RailMadad Web, 
App and SMS.  Details of grievances resolved during last three years is as 
under: - 
Year % of total grievances 
resolved 
2023-2024 99.98% 
2024-2025 99.99% 
2025-2026 99.98% 
Some of the major steps taken to ensure cleanliness and hygiene and to 
ensure regular availability of clean drinking water and clean toilet 
facilities, are as sunder: - 
 IR has adopted “Uniform Drinking Water Quality Monitoring Protocol” 
as standardized by department of Drinking Water and Sanitation in 
February 2013. Drinking water supplied to the passengers at railway 
stations through water taps is suitably treated, as per requirement. 
Regular tests are conducted to ensure its quality.  Further, 
instructions for implementation of the Indian Railway Water Policy, 
2017, have also been issued to ensure availability of water at station 
premises. The policy envisages modernization of railway water 
supply systems by upgrading water supply infrastructure, replacing 
manually operated valves with automatic valves, and adopting SCADA 
(Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition)-based control systems. 
 To cater the need of travelling passengers, Rail Neer being the 
exclusive brand of Indian Railways along with other approved brands 
of Packaged Drinking water is being sold on trains and stations. 
 Mechanized Coach Cleaning is being ensured during primary 
maintenance for better cleaning of the coach including interior, 
exterior and toilets. 
 On-Board Housekeeping Service is being provided to ensure 
cleanliness on run and to attend to any passenger grievance. As part 
of the ongoing effort to strengthen on-board services, a policy 

Page 3 of 3 
decision has been taken to engage professional, technology-enabled 
and financially sound service providers with the objective to ensure 
sustained improvement in cleanliness, hygiene, linen management 
and passenger interface. 
 Clean Train Station service has been introduced for mechanized 
cleaning in identified trains during their scheduled stoppage enroute. 
Dedicated team of staff equipped with high pressure jet machines 
and cleaning equipment carries out cleaning followed by drying of 
coach toilets. 
 All passenger coaches have been installed with bio-toilets so that no 
human waste is discharged from coaches directly on the tracks 
resulting clean tracks and railway premises. The details of provision 
of bio toilets are as under: 
 
 
 
 Regular water filling in overhead tanks for toilets before train 
departure at en-route nominated watering stations.

HOLDING OF ELECTIVE OFFICE BY GOVERNMENT SERVANTS 
 
491. SHRI BHAUSAHEB RAJARAM WAKCHAURE: 
 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether OM Nos. 11013/1/2016-Estt.A-III dated 27th February, 2020 and 5th August, 2019 
of DoPT limit a Government servant to a maximum of two terms or five years, whichever is 
earlier, when holding an elective office and is prior sanction required for such positions; 
(b) whether this restriction solely applicable to Government-affiliated sports 
associations/federations or it extend to other types of organisations such as Durga Puja Samities, 
Ram Leela Committees and Jagran Committees formed by the Government servants/retired 
Government servants and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether this rule also apply to private associations/federations where a Government servant is 
a member and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether this rule also applicable to religious organisations such as Puja Samities, Ram Leela 
Committees and Jagran Committees regardless of whether they are registered under the 
Trust/Societies Act or are unregistered; 
(e) if so, whether it similarly restrict Government servants from holding elective office in that 
organisation (Puja Samities, etc.) for more than two terms or five years, whichever is earlier and 
if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) whether any prior permission is being mandatory and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES 
AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
 
(a) to (f): The Government has issued instructions to all Ministries/ Department that a 
Government servant may hold elective office in any body, whether incorporated or not, for 
a period of two terms or for a period of 5 years, whichever is earlier, for which prior

per existing rules. It is necessary for the Competent Authority to keep in mind all the 
relevant factors while granting permission under Rule 15(1) (c) of Central Civil Service 
(Conduct) Rules 1964.

entries.t: Establishment of a New FM Radio Station at Pathanapuram in Kollam
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING 
LOK SABHA

(TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026) 
ESTABLISHMENT OF A NEW FM RADIO STATION AT PATHANAPURAM IN 
KOLLAM  
492. SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH: 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has received any proposal for establishing a new FM radio 
station at Pathanapuram in Kollam district, Kerala and if so, the details thereof;  
(b)  whether the Government has assessed the feasibility and requirement of setting up an 
FM radio station at Pathanapuram to improve radio coverage in the eastern and hilly 
regions of Kollam district and adjoining areas; 
(c) if so, whether any survey or technical study has been conducted regarding frequency 
availability, transmission infrastructure and coverage for such a station and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to establish a new FM radio station at Pathanapuram 
under Prasar Bharati or through the private FM broadcasting policy and if so, the details 
and timeline thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken or proposed by the Government to improve FM radio coverage and 
public broadcasting services in the eastern parts of Kollam district including 
Pathanapuram? 

 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(DR. L. MURUGAN) 
(a) to (e): Broadcasting Infrastructure and Network Development (BIND) scheme is a Central 
Sector Scheme for development, modernization and upgradation of broadcasting infrastructure 
of Doordarshan and Akashvani in the country. BIND scheme has been approved with a total 
outlay of ₹2539.61 crore for 2021-26. The scheme has been extended upto 31.03.2027. 
The scheme includes setting up and modernization of transmitters and studios of Akashvani, 
expansion of DD Free Dish DTH platform and DD TV channels. It also includes upgrading 
production & transmission facilities.  
Establishment of new transmitters is an ongoing process depending upon need assessment, 
available resources, inter-se priority and feasibility. 
Presently, 14 Akashvani broadcasting stations are operational in Kerala state having total 19 
transmitters (4 Medium Wave and 15 FM) of varying capacity. A 100W FM relay station at 
Punalur (in Kollam district) is operational which is about 12 km radial distance from 
Pathanapuram.

494. THIRU DR. S JAGATHRATCHAKAN: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the progress registered under modernisation programmes 
covering high-speed and semi-high-speed train systems including sleeper 
variants of advanced trainsets designed to improve long-distance rail 
travel and strengthen passenger mobility across the country;  
(b) the current status of implementation relating to manufacturing, testing, 
deployment and expansion of such train services along with the railway 
corridors identified for their introduction;  
(c) the details of the impact anticipated from these initiatives on travel 
time, network capacity, operational efficiency, regional connectivity 
and the overall passenger travel experience;  
(d) the details of the infrastructure and technological upgrades undertaken 
by the Government for supporting the operation of advanced train 
systems, including track improvements, signalling modernisation and 
safety enhancement measures; and  
(e) the initiatives proposed by the Government for accelerating railway 
modernisation while improving efficiency, safety, passenger comfort 
and the quality of long-distance rail services across the country?

MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND

(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (e) Modernisation of Indian Railways (IR) across country is a 
continuous & ongoing process subject to operational requirement, 
safety/security requirement, technical feasibility, commercial viability, 
resource availability, etc. and aims at improving safety/security, capacity, 

Page 2 of 25 
speed, operational efficiency, passenger comfort, environmental 
sustainability & adoption/development of advanced technologies. 
Semi-High Speed Train system: Indian Railways (IR) is focussed on 
providing affordable, good quality services to all sections of society. With a 
view to improve travel experience of the passengers, Indian Railways have 
introduced indigenously designed and manufactured Vande Bharat (Sleeper 
& Chair Car), Amrit Bharat, Namo Bharat Rapid Rail services with modern 
coaches, advanced safety features and passenger amenities. 
A. Vande Bharat train services (Chair Car): After the launch of 1st semi-
high speed train service on 15 February 2019 on the New Delhi–Kanpur–
Prayagraj–Varanasi corridor, Vande Bharat (VB) services have expanded 
rapidly across the national rail network and now, 162 VB train services are

 Improved fire safety – Aerosol based fire detection and suppression 
system in electrical cabinets and lavatories.  
 Higher acceleration with design/operating speed of 180/160 KMPH.  
 Driver-Guard communication with voice recording facility & Crash 
hardened memory.  
 Air conditioning units provided with indigenously developed UV-C 
lamp based disinfection system for deactivating 99% harmful bacteria 

Page 3 of 25 
from conditioned air to improve the hygiene standards inside the 
passenger area.  
 Better Ride Comfort.  
 CCTVs in all Coaches.  
 For Divyangjan passengers special lavatory in the driving coaches on 
each end.

monitoring.

(a) the progress made in deployment of Kavach 4.0 including the kilometers 
of routes covered and the number of locomotives equipped therewith as

(b) the railway zones and high-density corridors identified for 
implementation during the year 2025-2026 and 2026-2027, year and 
zone-wise;  
(c) whether any timeline has been fixed for the network-wide deployment of 
Kavach and if so, the details thereof; and

Kavach across Railway network?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
 
(a) to (d): 
1. Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP)  

Page 2 of 4 
system. Kavach is a highly technology intensive system, which 
requires safety certification of highest order (SIL-4). 
2. Kavach aids the Loco Pilot in running of trains within specified speed 
limits by automatic application of brakes in case Loco Pilot fails to do 
so and also helps the trains to run safely during inclement weather. 
3. The first field trials on the passenger trains were started in February 
2016. Based on the experience gained and Independent Safety 
Assessment of the system by Independent Safety Assessor (ISA), three 
firms were approved in 2018-19, for supply of Kavach Ver 3.2. 
4. Kavach was adopted as National ATP system in July, 2020. 
5. Implementation of Kavach System involves following Key Activities: 
a. Installation of Station Kavach at each and every station, block 
section. 
b. Installation of RFID Tags throughout the track length. 
c. Installation of telecom Towers throughout the section. 
d. Laying of Optical Fibre Cable along the track. 
e. Provision of Loco Kavach on each and every Locomotive running on 
Indian Railways.  
6. Based on deployment of Kavach version 3.2 on 1,465 RKm on South 
Central Railway and experience gained, further improvements were 
made. Finally, Kavach specification version 4.0 was approved by RDSO 
on 16.07.2024. 
7. Kavach version 4.0 covers all the major features required for the 
diverse railway network. This is a significant milestone in safety for 
Indian Railways. Within a short period, IR has developed, tested and 
started deploying Automatic Train Protection System. 
8. Major improvement in Version 4.0 includes increased Location 
Accuracy, Improved Information of Signal Aspects in bigger yards, 

Page 3 of 4 
Station to Station Kavach interface on OFC and Direct Interface to 
existing Electronic Interlocking System. With these improvements, 
Kavach Ver.4.0. is planned for large scale deployment over Indian 
Railways.

497.  SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the number of IndiaAI Data and AI Labs approved, established and operational in the country, 
State/UT-wise especially in Andhra Pradesh; 
(b) the number of persons enrolled, trained and certified through such Labs since inception, year 
and State/UT-wise especially in Andhra Pradesh; 
 (c) the details of courses, training programmes and capacity-building initiatives offered through 
such Labs and the institutions engaged in their implementation; 
(d) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised for establishment and operation of such 
Labs, year and State/UT-wise especially in Andhra Pradesh; 
(e) whether the Government has assessed training, placement, employment and entrepreneurship 
outcomes of persons trained through such Labs and if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) the details of steps taken or proposed by the Government to establish additional IndiaAI Data 
and AI Labs and strengthen their utilisation in Andhra Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (f): IndiaAI Mission: 
India’s AI policy is based on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of democratizing 
technology. It is aimed at creating economic opportunities and employment for youth, while 
addressing risks associated with it. 
 
India’s AI strategy builds on India’s vibrant IT sector with annual revenue of 300 billion dollars 
and 60 Lakh strong workforce. India AI Mission supports India’s AI ambitions under seven 
pillars including development of AI models, applications, datasets, talent development and 
affordable compute. 
 
AI models: 
The Government of India is supporting Indian startups and institutions to develop large 
language models.  
 
20 indigenous sovereign model proposals have been identified for support, comprising 12 
LLMs and 8 SLMs. Notable successes so far include: 
• Sarvam AI’s Sarvam 30 billion parameter and 105 billion parameter models 
• Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model 
• BharatGen’s multilingual foundation models 
• Avataar AI’s video generation model 
Domain-specific SLMs, include specialized models and AI frameworks addressing healthcare, 
language technologies and agentic AI systems are at various stages of development and 
deployment. 
 

 
 
Affordable compute:  
• Compute service providers empanelled: 15 
• Number of projects supported: 237  
• GPU hours sanctioned: 93.18 lakh GPU hours 
Application Development:  
• 12 National-level Hackathons/Innovation Challenges launched.  
• Supported the development of 62 AI prototypes and 20 AI solutions deployment 
Talent development: 
• 686 fellowships have been awarded across undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral 
programmes in 178 institutions. 
• YUVA AI for All programme has been completed by over 26.5 lakh individuals. 
 
IndiaAI Data and AI Labs  
Under the IndiaAI FutureSkills pillar, IndiaAI Data and AI Labs are being established to create 
AI-ready talent by providing hands -on training in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science and 
related emerging technologies, particularly in Tier -2 and Tier-3 cities. The primary objective 
of these Data and AI Labs is capacity building and skill development. Accordingly, the labs are 
focusing on training and certification activities. More details about these labs can be accessed 
from https://indiaai.gov.in/hub/indiaai-futureskills

entries.t: Limited Digital Infrastructure in Western Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 499   
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 22.07.2026 
 
LIMITED DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN WESTERN UTTAR PRADESH 
 
499.  SHRI ZIA UR REHMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of limited digital infrastructure, cyber awareness and IT- 
based employment opportunities in Western Uttar Pradesh;  
(b) if so, the details of steps taken by the Government to promote digital inclusion and IT skill 
development in the region;  
(c) whether similar challenges exist across the country; and  
(d) if so, the details of national measures undertaken to strengthen digital governance and the 
IT ecosystem?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d): In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister's vision to democratise technology and empower 
citizens, the Government of India had launched the Digital India programme in July, 2015. At 
its core, the programme promotes three interconnected goals: strengt hening digital 
infrastructure, delivering government services digitally, and empowering citizens through 
digital literacy and employment. 
 
The Government has implemented several initiatives and policy measures to strengthen digital 
infrastructure, create cyber awareness, generate IT -based employment opportunities, and 
expand digital inclusion across the country including Uttar Pradesh.  Details of some of the key 
initiatives are as follows: 
 
Digital Connectivity and Digital Infrastructure: Digital India has contributed to the rapid 
expansion of internet access, through initiatives such as BharatNet, which aims to provide high-
speed internet to rural and remote areas. As a result, there has been a substantial increase in 
internet accessibility and usage across the country, and internet penetration in India has grown 
in the last decade.  
 
• Telecom, Internet & Broadband Penetration: Total telephone connections in India grew 
from 93.3 crores in March 2014 to 133+ crores in March, 2026. In Uttar Pradesh, the total 
number of telephone subscribers has crossed 18.60 crore.  
• Internet subscribers jumped from 25.15 crore in March 2014 to 109.27 crore in March, 
2026. In Uttar Pradesh, the total number of Internet subscribers has crossed 14.64 crore.  
• The overall tele-density which was 75.23 % in March 2014 rose to 93.26% in March 2026. 

• BharatNet - Linking Villages to the Internet: The infrastructure created under 
BharatNet project is a national asset, accessible on a non -discriminatory basis to the 
Service Providers, and the same can be utilized to provide broadband services, such as Wi-
Fi Hotspots, Fibre to the Home (FTTH) connections, leased lines, etc. As of June 2026, a 
total of 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) have been made service -ready under the 
BharatNet Project across the country, including 49,299 GPs in Uttar Pradesh. 
• Aadhaar: Aadhaar is the world’s largest digital identity programme that provides 
biometric and demographic -based unique digital identity. Aadhaar  created a trusted 
biometric identity platform for secure and instant digital authentication. Aadhaar 
enrolments increased from 0.42 crore in 2010-11 to over 144+ crore by June 2026. In Uttar 
Pradesh, over 24.25 crore Aadhaar have been generated.  
• Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI has revolutionized digital transactions across the 
country. UPI has empowered millions of individuals and small businesses in rural and 
remote areas to make fast, secure and low -cost digital payments, significantly advancing 
financial inclusion. UPI is now live in over eight countries, including the UAE, Singapore, 
Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius and Qatar, making India a global trailblazer 
in digital payments. 
o UPI serves more than 49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks 
on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system.  
o UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real-time digital 
payments.  
• DigiLocker has provided anytime access to authentic digital documents from original 
issuer for the common citizen. More than 71.66 crore users are registered with DigiLocker 
to avail its services and more than 936.03 crore documents issued from 2822 issuers 
onboarded on the platform. More than 645 Lakh Aadhaar enabled registrations have taken 
place in the state of Uttar Pradesh to avail DigiLocker services. 
• Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance (UMANG) for accessing digital 
services through mobile App, one mobile application for all government services, is 
operational and offers 2585 services  for individuals. In the State of Uttar Pradesh, 92 
services from various departments are integrated/onboarded on the UMANG platform. 
• Common Services Centres – CSCs are offering government and business services

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 05 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Final Notification on the Western Ghats Panel Report 
 
05. ADV. ADOOR PRAKASH; 
ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE; 
 
Will the MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
 (a) whether the Government received suggestions/recommendations from the various State 
Governments including Kerala for the exclusion of villages demarcated as Eco-Sensitive Areas 
(ESA) on Western Ghats after the last iteration draft notification on the Western Ghats; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action taken by the Government on the said 
suggestions/recommendations; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to accept the specific recommendation of Kerala to limit 
the ESA boundaries to approximately 8,711.98 sq.km across 98 villages thereby excluding all 
human settlements, farmlands and plantations; 
(d) whether the Government has taken any decision about the final notification on the 
Kasturirangan panel report relating to the conservation of Western Ghats; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor and the time by which the final notification 
is likely to be issued? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) In order to protect the rich biodiversity of Western Ghats region, the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change has published the draft notification on Ecologically 
Sensitive Area of Western Ghats, vide S.O. 3060(E) dated 31.07.2024 with an area of 56,825.7 
square kilometer spread across six States namely, Goa, Gujarat, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra 
and Tamil Nadu. 
 
In order to address the issues raised by the respective State Governments, the Ministry has 
constituted a Committee to examine the suggestions of the six States in a holistic manner, keeping 
in view the conservation aspects of the ecosystem, and the rights, privileges, needs and 
developmental aspirations of the region. The concerns/suggestions of the State Governments, 
including Kerala are deliberated by the Committee with the respective State Governments on 
merit for finalizing its recommendations with respect to the draft notification. The 
recommendations are thereafter duly examined by the Ministry before finalizing the draft 
notification. Moreover, the Ministry has also received comments/objections/suggestions on the 
draft notification from various stakeholders and the same have been forwarded to the respective 
State Governments, including Kerala for providing comments/suggestions.

QUESTION 
50. Shri Arun Bharti: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has systematically monitored the utilization of 
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds toward improving rural civic 
infrastructure in Bihar; 
(b) if so, the total quantum of CSR expenditure successfully channelled by major 
corporate entities into public health and educational projects in the State during 
2025-26; 
(c) whether these systematic corporate contributions have measurably 
improved the condition of primary healthcare centers and Government schools 
in the State's aspirational districts, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the details of the digital monitoring frameworks established to ensure that 
these corporate welfare expenditures are executed with absolute transparency; 
and 
(e) the future initiatives planned to mandate third -party social audits for major 
CSR projects executed in Bihar to guarantee long -term infrastructural 
sustainability and direct community benefit? 
 
                                                     ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS    AND 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
  
(a) to (d). Under the Companies Act, 2013, CSR is a Board driven process and the 
Board of the company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR 
activities of the company based on the recommendation of its CSR Committee.  
The Board of the company is required to disclose the CSR Policy implemented by 
the company in its Board report and the Board of the company has to satisfy itself 
that the funds so disbursed have been utilised for the purposes and in the manner 
as approved by it, and the Chief Financial Officer or the person responsible for 
financial management shall certify to the effect.  In case any amount remains 
unspent then such amount shall be transferred in the designated fund(s) in 
Schedule VII in the prescribed time limit. Further, the first proviso to Section 135 
(5) of the Act provides that the company shall give preference to the local area 
and areas around it where it operates.  However, the emphasis on local area is 
only directory and not mandatory in nature and companies need to balance local 
area preference with national priorities. 
Contd…/- 

 
 
-2- 
 
The existing legal provisions regarding formation of CSR committee, formulation 
of CSR policy, Annual Action Plan on CSR, identification of the project and area 
in which project will be implemented, certification of CSR expenditure by Chief 
Financial Officer (CFO) and audit of CSR expenditure by statutory auditors, etc., 
provide adequate mechanisms to ensure transparency and accountability. 
 
Whenever any violation of CSR provisions is reported, action against such non -
compliant Companies is initiated as per provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 
and rules made thereunder after due examination of records and following due 
process of law.   
 
As per the section 137 of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) and Rules made 
thereunder, the companies are required to hold Annual General Meeting (AGM) 
within six months from the end of financial year. Thereafter, financial statements 
and board report containing disclosure about CSR are to be filed in MCA21 within 
30 days of the AGM. As th :e filing date for the current financial year i.e 2025 -26 
is not due as yet, the information on CSR data in Bihar for the Financial Year 
2025-26 is not available. 
(e): There is no such proposal to mandate third-party social audits for major CSR 
projects to guarantee long -term infrastructural sustainability and direct 
community benefit.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 501 
TO BE ANSWERED ON WEDNESDAY, 22ND JULY, 2026 
 
EARTHQUAKE RISK IN KANGRA-CHAMBA-DHARAMSALA BELT 
 
501.     SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR: 
 
Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of recent seismic activity in Kangra-Chamba 
region of Himachal where 18 tremors were recorded in month of June with magnitudes 
ranging from 2.1-5.0 and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) has identified Kangra-
Chamba-Dharamshala belt as one of the areas with high potential for future major 
earthquake exceeding magnitude 7.0 and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of steps taken to strengthen earthquake monitoring, early warning systems, 
disaster preparedness in this highly sensitive region; 
(d) whether the Government has issued any fresh/recent advisories to States regarding 
enforcement of earthquake-resistant building norms and if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the details of action plan prepared to minimise loss of life, property in event of major 
earthquake, status of retrofitting vulnerable buildings and public awareness campaigns; 
and 
(f) whether the Government proposes to conduct any fresh seismic micro-zonation study 
of Kangra-Chamba-Dharamshala belt, provide additional financial, technical assistance 
to State for disaster resilience? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR 
MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY 
AND EARTH SCIENCES 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
(a) Yes. The Government has taken note of the seismic activity in the Kangra–Chamba 
region. The National Center for Seismology (NCS) under Ministry of Earth Sciences 
(MoES) continuously monitors earthquakes across the country through the National 
Seismological Network.  During June 2026, a total of 16 earthquakes were detected and 
reported by NCS through its 24×7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre in the Kangra–
Chamba region of Himachal Pradesh, as against 18 mentioned in the question. 
Magnitude-wise details of these earthquakes are as follows: 
 
Magnitude Range 2.0 - 2.9 3.0 - 3.9 4.0 - 4.9 5.0 - 5.9 
No. of Earthquakes 12 3 NIL 1 
 
(b) The Kangra–Chamba–Dharamshala region lies in Seismic Zone V, the highest 
earthquake hazard zone in India. Scientific studies, including those by NGRI and other 
institutions, indicate that the region is capable of generating large earthquakes 
exceeding magnitude 7.0 due to active tectonic processes. 

 
 
(c) The Government has strengthened earthquake monitoring by expanding the National 
Seismological Network and ensuring round-the-clock monitoring by NCS. Presently, 
NCS maintains the National Seismological Network of 172 seismic stations across the 
country for 24×7 real time earthquake monitoring. Out of 172, 7 stations (Shimla, 
Dharamshala, Tissa, Sundernagar, Kalpa, Bhakra and Pong Dam) are in Himachal 
Pradesh. In addition, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), in 
coordination with State Governments, promotes earthquake preparedness through 
mock drills, training of officials and first responders, preparation of disaster 
management plans, and strengthening of emergency response mechanisms. 
 
(d)  Yes. The Government has issued advisories and guidelines for adoption and 
enforcement of earthquake-resistant construction through the National Building Code 
(NBC), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) seismic design codes and Model Building 
Bye-Laws. The implementation of these codes is the responsibility of the respective 
State Governments and Urban Local Bodies. 
 
(e)  The Government follows a strategy to minimize loss of life and property through risk 
assessment, preparedness, capacity building, strengthening of critical infrastructures 
and promotion of retrofitting of vulnerable lifeline buildings by the concerned 
authorities. NDMA regularly undertakes public awareness campaigns, conducts school 
and community awareness programmes, mock exercises and training programmes to 
promote earthquake safety and preparedness. 
 
(f)  Seismic microzonation studies are undertaken by scientific institutions and universities. 
The Government continues to provide financial and technical assistance to states, 
including Himachal Pradesh, under various disaster management and mitigation 
schemes to enhance disaster resilience and preparedness.

entries.t: Floating Solar PV Projects in Water Bodies of Delhi
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 504 
ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
FLOATING SOLAR PV PROJECTS IN WATER BODIES OF DELHI 
504. SHRI MANOJ TIWARI 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has identified suitable water bodies including reservoirs, lakes, 
ponds and drains in the National Capital Territory of Delhi for the development of Floating 
Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) projects under the draft Floating Solar PV Potential Assessment 
Report prepared by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE); 
(b) if so, the details of the water bodies identified in Delhi, their estimated floating solar 
generation potential and the present status of each proposed project including the pilot project 
at Bawana;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide a single-window clearance mechanism for 
floating solar projects in Delhi involving agencies such as the Delhi Government, Delhi Jal 
Board, Irrigation and Flood Control Department and other authorities and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the targets fixed for installation of floating solar capacity in Delhi by the year 2030 along 
with the financial assistance and implementation roadmap envisaged for the National Capital 
Territory?  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK) 
 
(a) & (b) As per the “Solar PV Potential of India – Floating Solar” report published by National 
Institute of Solar Energy in June 2026; India’s floating solar potential is estimated to be 102.18 
GWp. As per th is assessment, no Floating Solar Photovoltaic  (FSPV) potential has been 
identified in the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi.   
 
However, as per the inputs received from the Government of NCT of Delhi, Indraprastha Power 
Generation Co. Ltd (IPGCL), a power generating company of the Delhi government,  has 
initiated the tendering process for a proposed floating solar power plant of around 2.904 MW 
capacity on the raw water reservoir at Pragati Power Station–III, Bawana. 
(c) As per the inputs received from the Government of NCT of Delhi , there is currently n o 
specific proposal for single window clearance mechanism for floating solar projects in Delhi. 
(d) As per the inputs received from the Government of NCT of Delhi, no such target has been 
fixed at present.

ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
AGRIPHOTOVOLTAIC PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
507. SHRI TANGELLA UDAY SRINIV AS 
Will the minister of new and renewable energy be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam 
Utthaan Mahabhiyaan (PM-KUSUM) in Andhra Pradesh including the number of solar pumps 
installed, farmers benefitted and funds utilised, year and district-wise particularly in Kakinada; 
(b) the number of Agriphotovoltaic  projects sanctioned in coastal Andhra Pradesh, the 
agricultural land covered and the average income enhancement per acre reported in any 
assessment; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the potential of offshore wind energy in the Bay of 
Bengal coastal zone adjacent to Kakinada and if so, the details of findings and proposed action 
thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to promote rooftop solar adoption among small 
traders, fishermen households and youth entrepreneurs in Kakinada district under the Pradhan 
Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PM-SGMBY)? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK) 
(a) PM-KUSUM is a demand driven scheme. The capacities are allocated based on demand 
received from the States/UTs. Based on the demand received from the state, a total of 2,93,587 
pumps are allocated under Component C (Feeder Level Solarization). However, no progress 
has been reported by the state so far.  
 
There is no demand received from the State of Andhra Pradesh for standalone solar pumps 
under Component B of the PM KUSUM scheme. 
 
(b) Component A of the PM KUSUM scheme allows for setting up of decentralized ground 
mounted grid connected solar power plants in stilt fashion (also known as Agrivoltaics) by 
farmers on their land.  There is no demand received from the State of Andhra Pradesh for 
installation of decentralized plants under Component A of the scheme. 
 
(c) No specific assessment/study has been carried out in the Bay of Bengal coastal zone 
adjacent to Kakinada for offshore wind potential. 
 
(d) To promote rooftop solar adoption among all, including small traders, fishermen households 
and youth entrepreneurs, the Ministry has taken various steps, which inter-alia includes: 

• Creating awareness about the scheme, through awareness and outreach program such 
as print advertising in leading newspapers, TV commercials campaigns, Radio 
campaigns across FM stations, including regional channels, etc., in the country. 
• Online process from application to disbursal of subsidy directly into the bank account 
of the residential consumer through National Portal. 
• Availability of collateral free loan from nationalized banks at concessional interest rate 
of repo-rate plus 50 bps i.e. 5.75% per annum for the present, with tenure of 10 years. 
• Simplified the regulatory approval process by waiving technical feasibility requirement 
and introducing auto load enhancement upto 10 kW. 
• Net metering agreement has been made part of application in the National Portal. 
• Simplified process for registration of vendors to ensure sufficient and qualified vendors 
are available. 
• Capacity building and training programmes are being conducted for creating skilled 
manpower. 
• Established a grievance redressal mechanism for the timely resolution of grievances. A 
Call Centre with telephone number 15555 is operational in 12 languages.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
KISAN RAIL CIRCUITS FOR ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
508. SHRI KESINENI SIVANATH: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of consultations held by the Government during the last two 
years with State Governments to identify potential Kisan Rail circuits, 
particularly for Andhra Pradesh;  
(b) the number of potential Kisan Rail circuits identified through such 
consultations along with their route alignments and commodities 
proposed for transportation, State/UT-wise;  
(c) whether the Government has conducted any operational and financial 
feasibility studies for the identified circuits, if so, the details thereof 
and if not, the reasons therefor; and  
(d) whether any Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) are being prepared for the 
proposed Kisan Rail circuits, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor, State/UT-wise?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d):   Kisan Rail trains have been introduced by Indian Railways – to 
move perishables including fruits and vegetables from production or 
surplus regions to consumption or deficient regions. Since its launch in 
August 2020, a total of 2,364 Kisan Rail services have operated on 167 
routes across various states including 116 outward services from Andhra 
Pradesh.   
 

Page 2 of 2 
Potential circuits of Kisan Rail are identified in consultation with Ministry 
of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Agriculture/Animal 
Husbandry/Fisheries Departments of State Governments as well as local 
bodies and agencies, Mandis etc., and services at applicable tariff are 
planned on the basis of demands placed and the operational feasibility. 
 
Besides, Business Development Units functional at all Railway Divisions 
are engaging with various stakeholders to assess the business requirement 
including transportation of perishables which can also be seasonal and 
need based. In the recent past, consultations were held by Railway 
Authorities with Government of Andhra Pradesh, officials of CONCOR and 
with District Administration of Ananthapuram for transportation of bananas 
from Tadipatri to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT). 
 
Further, steps have been taken to promote transportation of agricultural 
produce, especially food grain in containers, which is a safe and efficient 
intermodal mean of transport. To facilitate transportation of food grain, 
flour and pulses in container, a per-kilometer based pricing system (instead 
of commodity class and distance slab based freight system) has been 
recently adopted.

UPGRADE POSTAL FACILITIES

Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has implemented systematic measures to modernize branch post 
offices and enhance digital banking access within the Rajahmundry Parliamentary Constituency; 
 
(b)  if so, the total number of rural post offices successfully equipped with micro -ATMs and

citizens in utilizing digital financial services securely? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
 
(a) Department of Posts has deployed mobile devices, equipped with DREAM (Digital Rural

Constituency have been equipped with micro-ATMs and biometric devices. 
 
(c)     Central welfare pensions received in bank accounts, are being paid to senior citizens residing 
in local villages by post offices, through Aadhaar Enabled Payment System at their door step through

Besides, Department of Posts incurs expenditure centrally for providing digital connectivity across 
all its post offices. 
 
(e) Department of Posts regularly provides structured training to equip the post offices in 
providing digital financial services. Details are as follows: - 
 
(i) Dedicated learning m odules on digital financial literacy, secure digital transactions, cyber 
security and IPPB services are made available on the Dak Karmayogi Portal and iGOT Karmayogi 
platforms. 
 
(ii) Training modules and User Manuals are shared with the post offices periodically to enhance

Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Sports 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 51 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Allocation of Sports Development Funds 
 
51.     SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised for sports 
development since 2014 -15, including the current financial year, 
State/UT-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government considers the present allocation adequate 
to meet the sports infrastructure and athlete development requirements 
of all States and Union Territories; 
 
(c) if so, the justification therefor and if not, the steps taken by the 
Government to ensure equitable distribution of sports funds among the 
States and UTs; 
 
(d) whether any special financial allocation or assistance provided to 
Haryana in view of its outstanding contribution to India's medal tally in 
the Olympic Games, Paralympic Games and Commonwealth Games; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
  

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
[DR MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
 
(a) to (e ):  Funds are allocated by this Ministry Scheme –wise, not 
State/UT wise. The details of the funds allocated, released and utilised 
for various schemes of the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth 
Affairs & Sports , since 2014 -15 is available on the website 
(https://yas.gov.in/en/sports/financial-reports) of the Department. For 
the current financial year, Rs. 3113.36 cr is allocated to the Department 
of Sports. 
‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility of development  of 
sports, including sports infrastructure and athlete development 
requirements in the country (including Haryana), rests primarily with the 
respective State/Union Territory Governments. The Union  Government 
only supplements their efforts by bridging critical gaps.  
Further, Khelo India Scheme is a demand driven Scheme. The proposals 
received from the State/UT Governments and other eligible entities are 
considered for financial support, subject to their completeness, 
technical feasibility and availability of funds under the Scheme . The 
Khelo India Scheme provides support for creation and upgradation  of 
sports infrastructure, establishment of Khelo India Centres (KIC),  
support to Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCE), Khelo India 
Accredited Academies (KIAA), and training and support to Khelo India

511.  SHRI CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed support for fabless and embedded -system start-ups 
and the programme coverage and participation from Karnataka including coastal Karnataka;

and

ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (d):  Semiconductor industry:  
Semiconductor is a foundational industry. Semiconductor chips are now integral part of the 
electronic goods such as mobile phones, computers, household appliances, vehicles, railway 
equipment, drones, aeroplanes, etc.  
 
India’s semiconductor policy: 
Successive Governments in India made multiple efforts since 1960s to set up semiconductor 
industry. However, these efforts did not materialise. 
 
Semicon India program:  
In 2022, Government launched Semicon India program. It was based on Prime Minister 
Narendra Modi’s vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India. Clear policy proposals and 
steadfast execution of the Semicon India program have given historic success. 
 
Chip design is one of the most important parts of the semiconductor value chain. Recognising 
the potential of Indian chip engineers, the Government has undertaken several initiatives to 
strengthen the fabless semiconductor and embedded -system start -up ecos ystem under the 
Semicon India Programme and other pan-India initiatives.  
 
These initiatives include following support extended to the State of Karnataka: 
(i) The Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme has been launched as part of Semicon India 
Programme to support domestic companies, startups and Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in fabless and embedded -system design activities to 
develop semiconductor chips. 

        24 projects have been approved for financial support to develop semiconductor chips. In 
addition, 105 fabless chip design companies have been provided centralized access to 
advanced Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. 
(ii) The Chips to Start-up (C2S) Programme has been initiated for capacity building across 
the country to address the talent and design infrastructure requirements in fabless and 
embedded system design. 
The Programme aims to generate 85,000 industry -ready manpower at B.Tech., M.Tech. and 
Ph.D. levels across the country. So far, access to advanced EDA tools has been provided 
to 320 academic institutions, resulting into 175 design tapeouts at SCL Mohali and  
generation of 68,000 number of trained manpower. 
 
In the State of Karnataka: 
(i) The ChipIN Centre has been established at C-DAC, Bengaluru as a centralized national 
facility to strengthen the fabless and embedded -system design ecosystem under C2S 
Programme and DLI Scheme. 
       The Centre provides pan -India access to design infrastructure such as advanced EDA 
tools, Intellectual Property (IP) cores, hardware emulation, Field Programmable Gate 
Array (FPGA) -based prototyping, PARAM Utkarsh Supercomputer and regular 
trainings.  
       The Centre also facilitates and provides financial support for post -design activities such 
as Multi -Project Wafer (MPW) fabrication, packaging, post -silicon validation and 
characterization through domestic and overseas foundry partners. The other details o f 
support at ChipIN Centre are available at https://c2s.gov.in/chipin.jsp 
(ii) 80 organizations,  comprising 51 startups  and 29 academic institutions, have been 
provided access to advanced EDA tools and regular design trainings. This has enabled 
training of more than 8,500 engineers & students and cumulative utilization of more than 
75 lakh EDA tool-hours. 
(iii) 24 organizations, comprising 16 startups and 8 academic institutions, have been 
supported for implementation of semiconductor design projects with more than ₹200 
crore of committed support from MeitY. These projects encompass fabless and 
embedded-system design activities. 
(iv) 39 chip designs from 6 academic institutions have been taped out through SCL, Mohali 
(180 nm), while 5 chip designs from startups have been taped out through various 
foundries, including advanced technology nodes such as 12 nm at TSMC. 
 
Continuous feedback from participating organizations is leveraged to further strengthen 
support for fabless and embedded -system design startups by improving access to design 
infrastructure, technical support and skill development.

MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 512 
TO BE ANSWERED ON WEDNESDAY, 22ND JULY, 2026 
 
INDIA'S RAINFALL DEFICIT 
 
512.  SHRI V K SREEKANDAN: 
   
Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that according to India Meteorological Department, India’s rainfall 
deficit at 35% as monsoon progress stalls and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the shortfall in rainfall is concentrated in the regions the 
monsoon has failed to cover and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that central India faces 63% deficit as monsoon’s first round 
loses momentum and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether it is a fact that forecasters globally have warned be a Super El Nino year and 
if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR 
MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY 
AND EARTH SCIENCES 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
(a) No. The India Meteorological Department (IMD), under the Ministry of Earth 
Sciences (MoES), has not reported a 35% rainfall deficit for the country as a whole. 
Rainfall across the country is monitored daily, weekly, monthly, and seasonally. Any 
rainfall deficit is assessed for the corresponding period and region based on the Long 
Period Average (LPA). The rainfall status varies spatially and temporally during the 
progress of the Southwest Monsoon season, and temporary deficits over certain 
regions or during specific periods may occur due to the intra-seasonal variability of 
the monsoon. Up to 30 June 2026, the cumulative All India Southwest Monsoon 
rainfall was 40% below the LPA. As of 14 July 2026, the cumulative All India 
Southwest Monsoon rainfall was 21% below the LPA. 
 
(b) No. The rainfall deficit is not confined to regions where the monsoon has not 
advanced; it has also been observed in areas where it has already advanced. During 
the period from 1 June to 14 July 2026, 19 out of the 36 meteorological subdivisions 
across the country received deficient rainfall. 
 
(c) No. By the end of June 2026, Central India recorded a rainfall deficiency of 50% of 
the LPA. Subsequently, the region received substantial rainfall from 30 June to 8 July 
2026, significantly reducing the rainfall deficiency. As of 14 July 2026, the 
cumulative rainfall deficiency over Central India has reduced and stands at 11% 
below the LPA. 
 
 

 
 
(d) No. IMD, along with other international climate prediction centers, has predicted the 
development of El Nino conditions during the 2026 southwest monsoon season. 
During June 2026, El Nino conditions remained weak. It is likely to be weak to 
moderate during July and moderate during August, and become moderate to strong by 
the end of September. There is no officially defined category known as a "Super El 
Nino". Operationally, El Nino events are generally classified as weak, moderate, or 
strong based on the magnitude of sea surface temperature anomalies over the 
equatorial central Pacific Ocean.

†516 SHRI AMAR SHARADRAO KALE: 
  
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to state? 
  
(a)  whether Government has taken steps to promote coal gasification and other clean coal 
technologies during the current year 2026; 
  
(b)  if so, the number of coal gasification projects approved or under implementation, and their 
current status;

 (a):  Yes. To promote coal gasification, the Government approved, on 13.05.2026, a

₹37,500 crore.

facilitates cleaner utilisation of coal by enabling improved process efficiency , easier removal

utilisation and reduce emissions from coal-based industrial applications.

entries.head:
§  Page 1 of 2 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 518 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
PROGRESS OF GATI SHAKTI MULTI-MODAL CARGO TERMINALS 
 
†518. SHRI BUNTY VIVEK SAHU: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of progress made so far under the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal 
Cargo Terminal for development of freight capacity and rail-based 
logistics across the country and the target set for financial year 2026-
27;  
(b) the details of special rail infrastructure facilities being provided through 
the said scheme for industrial development and smooth transportation 
of agro-products in Madhya Pradesh; and  
(c) whether the Government proposes to set up any new Gati Shakti Multi-
Modal Cargo Terminal/multi-modal logistics hub for connecting coal 
industry maize and orange producing farmers of Chhindwada district 
with the global market and if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (c) : In order to encourage setting up of cargo terminals through 
private investment, ‘Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT)’ policy has 
been launched. Location of the GCTs is decided on the basis of demand from 
industry, potential of Cargo traffic, availability of railway infrastructure and 
overall logistics potential of the area.   
  
So far, 142 Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals (GCTs) have been commissioned, 
including 5 GCTs in Madhya Pradesh. In addition, In-Principle Approvals 
(IPAs) have been granted for the development of GCTs at 310 more locations 

Page 2 of 2 
including 19 locations in Madhya Pradesh. The 142 commissioned GCTs have 
an estimated freight handling capacity of 224 million tonnes per annum 
(MTPA). The policy has mobilized private investment of approximately 
₹10,000 crore through these GCTs. 
 
At present, no proposal to set up Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal in Chhindwada 
district has been received from industry.   
 
The Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals cater to a wide range of commodities 
including cement, steel, foodgrains, fertilizers, coal, fly ash, minerals, 
containers, automobiles, agricultural produce and other bulk as well as non-
bulk commodities. The policy has benefited key sectors such as cement, 
steel, power, mining, agriculture, logistics and manufacturing by providing 
improved rail connectivity and modern cargo handling infrastructure.  
 
The Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal (GCT) Policy has facilitated the development 
of modern multimodal cargo terminals closer to production and consumption 
centres, thereby improving rail connectivity for local industries, agricultural 
produce and other commodities. The policy has enabled creation of 
warehousing, silos, cold storage and other value-added logistics facilities, 
reducing first-mile/last-mile logistics costs and transit time and facilitated 
modal shift of freight from road to rail, thereby improving the overall 
efficiency and competitiveness of rail-based logistics.

entries.t: Offshore Wind Projects in Tamil Nadu along  Tamil Nadu's Coast
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 519 
ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
OFFSHORE WIND PROJECTS IN TAMIL NADU ALONG TAMIL NADU’S COAST 
  519. SHRI THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether the Government has conducted a comprehensive cumulative environmental and 
socio-economic impact assessment of the proposed offshore wind projects along the Tamil 
Nadu coast particularly in Kanyakumari, Thoothukudi and Ramanathapuram and if so, the 
details of findings thereof; 
(b) whether free, prior and informed consultations and statutory public hearings have been 
conducted with affected fishing communities before identifying offshore wind sites and if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) the steps taken by the Government to ensure that offshore wind development does not 
adversely affect traditional fishing grounds, marine biodiversity, the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere 
Reserve, endangered species and other ecologically sensitive coastal areas in Tamil Nadu; 
(d) whether the Government has a rehabilitation, compensation and livelihood restoration 
framework for fishermen & coastal communities likely to be affected by these projects and if 
so, the details thereof; and  
(e) whether the Government would review project siting and adopt less ecologically sensitive 
alternatives ensuring that Tamil Nadu's renewable energy transition does not come at the cost 
of its coastal communities & marine ecosystems and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)  
(a) The identified offshore wind sites off Tamil Nadu coast are about 12 km from Kanyakumari 
district and 100-120 km from Thoothukudi district. A Rapid Environmental Impact Assessment 
(EIA) study was carried out for the identified sites and the preliminary findings indicate that 
Inter-Tidal Benthos, Phytoplankton and Zooplankton exist in identified sites which might have 
marginal impact during construction phase of offshore wind projects. However, recolonization 
of these species shall happen within 3 months post-construction.  
In addition, a 75 acres site identified for Offshore Wind Test Station in Rameswaram, 
Ramanathapuram district. The Rapid EIA study carried out for Offshore Wind Test Station 
indicate preliminary findings as follows: 
• The proposed offshore wind project site does not overlap with turtle nesting grounds, 
which are located along Dhanushkodi Beach. 
• The project is not expected to have significant impacts on coastal birds. Appropriate 
mitigation measures, including installation of bird diverters and painting of one turbine 
blade black, have been recommended to further minimize bird collisions. 
• Seagrass beds are located about 3.6 km from the proposed project area and are not 
expected to be affected. 

• Seahorse habitats are located about 20 km from the proposed project site and are not 
expected to be affected. 
• Coral reefs are located about 4.5 km from the proposed project area and are not expected 
to be affected. 
• Milkfish habitats are located about 25 km from the proposed project area and are not 
expected to be affected. 
(b) to (e) National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) in consultation with Danish Energy 
Agency (DEA) carried out Marine Spatial planning (MSP) for offshore wind farms off Tamil 
Nadu coast and demarcated offshore sites. The ecologically sensitive areas have been excluded 
during MSP. The first offshore wind energy project is yet to be awarded in the country. As per the 
notified Offshore Wind Energy Lease Rules, 2023, a ctivities such as fishing for the purpose of 
livelihood and other activities that may co -exist with the offshore wind energy farm in the interest of 
the common public shall be permissible, if they do not affect the normal working of the offshore wind 
energy farm. The offshore wind projects development requires applicable Coastal Regulation Zone 
(CRZ) clearance from Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) as per National 
Offshore Wind Energy Policy. The CRZ clearance process generally includes consultations and 
statutory public hearings.  
Presently, there is no separate framework for rehabilitation, compensation and livelihood restoration on 
account of development of offshore wind projects. In case required, rehabilitation, compensation and 
livelihood restoration shall be governed as per ex tant rules and regulations of Government of India or 
concerned State Government.

Conservation and Development of Gokul Reservoir in Buxar, Bihar 
 
52. SHRI SUDHAKAR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) whether the foundation stone of Rs. 64 crore project for the conservation and development of the 
Gokul Reservoir situated in the Buxar district of Bihar was laid around two years ago; 
(b) if so, the present status of the said project along with the details of the progress made therein; 
(c) the total amount of funds sanctioned and actually utilized under this project so far; and 
(d) whether any revised timeline has been fixed for the completion of the project and if not, the 
reasons for the delay along with the steps being taken to resolve the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
 (a) to (d):  MoEF&CC had sanctioned the Integrated Management Plan (IMP) for conservation and 
management of Gokul Jalashay in Buxar, Bihar on 17.10.2024 at a total cost of Rs. 32.483 crore for 
five years under the National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA) scheme on 60:40 
cost-sharing between the Central and State Governments.  
 
As per the information provided by the State Government of Bihar, the works undertaken include 
installation of geo-tagged pillars along the wetland boundary, installation of information boards 
highlighting the ecological significance of the wetland, organization of awareness workshops and 
festivals, including the annual Gokul Jalashay Bird Festival to promote waterbird conservation, 
celebration of important public events to enhance awareness regarding wetland conservation, 
production and dissemination of resource materials for awareness and capacity building, and 
identification of suitable locations for establishing water quality sampling stations. So far, an amount 
of Rs. 25.34 lakhs has been utilized for implementation of the IMP. Since the duration of the IMP is 
five years i.e. till the end of financial year 2028-29, revised timeline is not a requisite at present.
