6.  Shri Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy: 
Shri Putta Mahesh Kumar: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether the Government has conducted any evaluation of the infrastructure facilities available in 
Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) in the country; 
(b)  if so, the details of the major findings, including gaps in fa cilities and compliance with required 
norms; 
(c)  the total number of ICT labs and smart classrooms sanctioned and functional in KGBVs, 
State/UT-wise and district-wise particularly in Prakasam district of Andhra Pradesh; 
(d)  the number of teaching posts s anctioned and vacant in KGBVs, State/UT -wise and district -wise, 
particularly in Prakasam district of Andhra Pradesh; 
(e)  the details of programmes, agencies involved and outcomes achieved as per the evaluation of the 
Government; and 
(f)  the steps taken b y the Government to address identified infrastructure gaps, fill teaching 
vacancies and strengthen academic resources in KGBVs in the country, with specific focus on 
Andhra Pradesh? 
A N S W E R 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (f): The Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSE&L), Ministry of Education, 
commissioned an evaluation of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) through the National 
Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) during 2022–23 to assess the performance and 
implementation challenges of the scheme. The evaluation covered four key areas : infrastructure, 
academics, financial management, and administration ; and gathered feedback from students, parents, 
teachers, wardens, SMC m embers, and d istrict and State authorities. Based on the findings, NCERT 
submitted a comprehensive evaluation report with recommendations to strengthen the quality and 
effective implementation of KGBVs. 
 
The NCERT evaluation , inter-alia, observed that KGBVs have played a significant role in 
improving access, enrolment, retention, and learning outcomes of girls from disadvantaged 
communities by providing a safe and supportive residential environment  while recommending training, 
ICT facilities, upgradation of KGBVs etc. 

 
 
Since then, various measures have been undertaken including upgradation of existing KGBVs 
upto class XII, construction of additional dormitories, toilets, boundary walls, furniture and equipment, 
bedding replacement, teaching-learning materials, library books, sports facilities etc., in all States/ UTs, 
as per their requirement including Andhra Pradesh.  The DoSE&L has approved ICT Labs and Smart 
Classrooms in all functional KGBVs as per Samagra Shiksha norms to empower girl students, make 
them digitally savvy, and enhance their learning outcomes. 
 
 Further, a structured training programme is organized for KGBV wardens in collaboration with 
the National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration (NIEPA). This initiative aims to 
strengthen the wardens’ capacity to manage resources effectively and enhance their institutional and 
administrative skills, thereby fostering a safe and supportive environment that promotes and improves 
quality education for girls. 
 
Education is in the Concurren t List of the Constitution of India and KGBVs are under the 
administrative control of respective State Governments and UT administrations. The matters related to  
operationalization and functioning of KGBVs including the recruitment, and deployment of teach ing 
and non -teaching staff of KGBVs, come under the purview of concerned State/UT Governments.  
Teaching and non-teaching staff of KGBVs are recruited by States/UTs, as per the terms and conditions 
of the respective States and UTs for KGBVs. The recruitment of teachers is a continuous process. The 
Central Govern ment, through Samagra Shiksha, provides assistance to the States and UTs for  
deployment of teachers in KGBVs to maintain appropriate Pupil Teacher Ratio as per the prescribed  
norms for various levels of schooling. 
 
As per the information received from the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, 37 KGBVs are 
functional in Prakasam district. Of these, 33 KGBVs have ICT labs and smart classroom facilities , 
except for 4 KGBVs which are newly functional. In And hra Pradesh, all 497 approved ICT Labs & 
Smart Class rooms are functional.

and Smart Classrooms sanctioned and functional in KGBVs are at Annexure.

LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 600
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22ND JULY, 2026
SILO MODERNISATION SCHEME
600. SHRI RAHULGANDHI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a): the total number of silo contracts awarded under the Hub and Spoke Silo Modernisation Scheme of
the Food Corporation of India (FCI), the distinct entities to whom they were awarded, the number and value
of contracts secured by each entity, phase-wise;
(b): the number of silo projects bundled together in each tender and the location and capacity of silos
awarded under the said scheme, tender-wise and company-wise;
(c): whether FCI had originally proposed restricting the award of more than one silo project bundle to a
single bidder under the said scheme and if so, the reasons recorded by FCI for this restriction;
(d): whether the said restriction and the technical-experience eligibility criterion were removed
following the 108th Public Private Partnership Appraisal Committee meeting and if so, the reasons therefor;
and
(e): whether the Government undertook any independent or expert consultation on the risk of market
concentration before removing the said restriction and if so, the details thereoF
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS.
FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(SHRIMATI NIMUBEN JAYANTIBHAI BAMBHANIYA)
(a) & (b): The list of silos awarded under Hub & Spoke Phase-I (DBFOT & DBFOO) and
Hub & Spoke Phase-II (DBFOO) is attached as Annexure-l.
The number and value of contracts secured by each entity, phase-wise are attached as
Annexure-II(a) & Annexure-II(b).
(c): Yes, based on stakeholder’s conference held to gauge the market perception, internal
examination & views of consultant, FCI proposed for restriction on number of bundle to be
awarded to a bidder be kept at 01 (one) for DBFOT projects.
(d): Yes, during discussion on DBFOO Phase-I Project, in the 108th PPPAC meeting,
regarding removal of restriction on number of projects to be awarded to the single bidder, NITI
Aayog was of the view that against the storage gap of around 240 LMT in the country, the total
Silo storage capacity development envisaged was only around 1 11 LMT at 249 locations. Out of
these 249 locations, only 66 locations with 24.75 LMT capacity were envisaged in DBFOO
Phase-1 project. Hence, the presumption of concentrations and monopoly of storage capacity
didn't appear to be well founded. Therefore, in order to get financially sound bids (such, that
allow bidders to quote taking into consideration economies of scale) and in the interest of


competition and letting market forces prevail, no restriction on number of projects that can be
bidded/awarded to a single entity was kept.
Further, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) was of the view that Projects under
DBFOO mode are sizeable in terms of number of locations, storage capacity and the Total Project
Cost. And, as per the information available, there were not many players in this field, at that time.
Therefore, it was suggested by DEA that Minimum Eligibility Qualification/ shortlisting
of bidders should be only based on the Financial Capacity. This will widen the bidding universe
to include financial sector players also, who may not possess the necessary technical experience
but have the requisite financial strength for implementing the projects, thus improving the
biddability of the projects.
In view of the above mentioned suggestions and detailed brainstorming, the said restriction
and the technical-experience eligibility criterion were removed.
(e): No Sir.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 601 
(TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026) 
SETTING UP OF 10 KW FM STATIONS  
601.   SHRI KOTA SRINIVASA POOJARY: 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that large parts of Chikkamagaluru District especially 
the Malnad and hilly areas are not covered by mobile network and villagers lack access 
to information on weather, education, market rates and Government schemes; 
(b)  if so, whether the Government has received any proposal/request for setting up of 10 KW 
FM Stations at Chikkamagaluru Dattapeeta, Koppa Balgadi BSNL Tower and Mudigere 
Hand Post BSNL Tower in Chikkamagaluru District;  
(c)  if so, whether the Government proposes to sanction the said three 10 KW FM Stations to 
provide seamless information coverage to remote villages of Chikkamagaluru, Kadur, 
Tarikere, Belur, Koppa, Sringeri, N.R. Pura, Mudigere and Kalasa Taluks; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof and the time by which the FM Stations are likely to be sanctioned 
and made operational?  
 

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(DR. L. MURUGAN) 
 
(a) to (d): Broadcasting Infrastructure and Network Development (BIND) scheme is a Central 
Sector Scheme for development, modernization and upgradation of broadcasting infrastructure 
of Doordarshan and Akashvani in the country. BIND scheme has been approved with a total 
outlay of ₹2539.61 crore for 2021-26. The scheme has been extended upto 31.03.2027. 
The scheme includes setting up and modernization of transmitters and studios of Akashvani, 
expansion of DD Free Dish DTH platform and DD TV channels. It also includes upgrading 
production & transmission facilities. 
Chikkamagaluru district is presently served by a 100 W FM Relay Transmitter at Sringeri, a 
20 kW MW Transmitter (675 kHz) at Bhadravati covering the proposed locations and adjoining 
areas, and a 10 kW FM Transmitter at Hassan covering other parts of the district. Establishment 
of new transmitters is an ongoing process. Schemes for new FM stations are formulated and 
implemented from time to time, depending upon need assessment, available resources, inter-se 
priority, feasibility and Government approval. 
Residents of the district can access Doordarshan and Akashvani services through alternative 
platforms. DD Free Dish, Prasar Bharati's free-to-air DTH service, carries all Doordarshan 
channels and 48 Akashvani channels without any subscription fee. More than 260 Akashvani 
channels are available on the NewsOnAIR mobile app. Doordarshan and Akashvani channels 
are also available on WAVES OTT platform.

entries.t: New Regulations to Cover Social Media Users
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 603 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 22.07.2026 
  
NEW REGULATIONS TO COVER SOCIAL MEDIA USERS 
  
603. SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M.: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government is planning new regulation to cover social media 
users and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is also true that the Government is considering sending take down notices to 
individual users for their social media posts; 
(c) if so, whether it is a fact that the move has been criticized by many including the Internet 
Freedom Foundation calling it a massive expansion of unconstitutional censorship; 
(d) if so, whether it is also a fact that the Government has been increasingly issuing broad 
takedown orders in the last several weeks against posts and accounts that are anti -
establishment; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (e): The policies of Government are aimed at ensuring an Open, Safe and Trusted and 
Accountable Internet for its users, including women and children. Government is committed 
to ensure that the Internet in India is free from any form of unlawful content or information. 
 
The Information Technology Act, 2000 (“IT Act”) and Rules made thereunder have put in 
place a framework to deal with unlawful and harmful content in the digital space.  The IT Act 
and rules made thereunder provide for Government to issue lawful blocking or ders and 
reasoned intimations for removal of/disabling access to unlawful information. The Hon’ble 
Supreme Court, in its judgment dated 24 th March, 2015 in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India 
(Writ Petition (Civil) No. 167 of 2012), upheld the constitutional validity of these provisions. 
 
Any person aggrieved by the orders under the IT Act can challenge such orders before the 
Courts. The Hon’ble Karnataka High Court, in its judgment dated 30 th June 2023 in Writ 
Petition No. 13710 of 2022, upheld the Government’s exercise of its lawful powers under the 
IT Act. 
 
*****

In order to access the wind potential in the region, t he National Institute of Wind Energy has 
established two (2) Wind Monitoring Stations in the South 24 Parganas District under the 
Mathurapur Lok Sabha Constituency. The measured mean wind speeds at these two locations 
are 4.77-4.81 m/s at 25 m height. 
The wind resource measured indicates relatively low wind speeds, which are not considered 
economically viable for commercial wind power development. 
(c) & (d) As per the inputs received from Government of West Bengal, the Sundarbans region 
is one of the priority areas for deployment of Renewable Energy (RE) technologies, considering 
its ecological significance and the need for conservation of its unique biodiversity. Since 
Mathurapur is a part of the Sundarban  region, it also falls within this focus area for RE 
interventions

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 611 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
PUNCTUALITY AND CATERING SERVICES IN RAILWAYS 
 
611. SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government tracks the high rate of delays and poor 
punctuality in ordinary passenger and express trains that severely 
disrupt the daily schedules of small traders and common commuters, if 
so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(b) the average punctuality percentage recorded for non-premium express 
trains during the last two quarters of 2026;  
(c) whether IRCTC is strictly enforcing the mandatory display of 
standardised, fixed rate-cards to stop private catering vendors from 
illegally overcharging passengers for meals and water bottles in running 
trains, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(d) the number of financial fines levied/vendor catering contracts cancelled 
for overpricing/supplying unhygienic food items in 2025-26; and  
(e) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to install digital QR-
code payment stickers across all pantry carts?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) and (b) Punctuality is accorded high priority on Indian Railways (IR) and 
all possible efforts  are made to run trains on time. However, on Indian 
Railways, several factors affect punctuality which include foggy weather, 
path constraints, asset maintenance and other issues, alarm chain pulling, 
agitations, cattle run over and other unforeseen circumstances.  

Page 2 of 6 
The average punctuality of Mail/Express trains during the 1st quarter of 
2026  (i.e. January-March) was 75.05% and that during the 2nd quarter (i.e. 
April-June) was 75.76%.    
The overall punctuality of  trains (including all Mail/Express, Vande 
Bharat Express, Rajdhani Express, Shtabadi Express etc.) on Indian Railways 
during 2026-27 (April to June)  was 76.32%. 
 
The steps taken to improve punctuality of train services include: 
 Regular, continuous and real-time monitoring of punctuality of trains 
using technological tools and IT systems. 
 Use of an integrated digital platform for monitoring of train operations 
comprising Integrated Coaching Management System (ICMS) and 
Control Office Application (COA) which are integrated with National 
Train Enquiry System (NTES). 
 Progressive advancement for automatic uptake of timings by the train 
movement itself, is being achieved through GPS devices fitted 
locomotives {Real-Time Train Information System (RTIS) and Remote 
Monitoring and Management of Locomotives and Trains (REMMLOT)} 
and Data loggers integrated with the station signaling system.  
 Data loggers ensure real time and realistic reporting of arrival / 
departure of passenger trains at stations. 
 IR has been replacing conventional coaches (ICF coaches) by modern 
light weight LHB coaches having state-of-the art technology. The 
Production units of Indian Railways are producing only LHB coaches 
from April 2018 onwards. The production of LHB coaches has 
continually increased during the years and about 50,000 LHB coaches 
have been turned out since 2014. IR has also been proliferating Vande 
Bharat, Namo Bharat Rapid Rail and Amrit Bharat trains, for quick 
acceleration and deceleration. 

Page 3 of 6 
 To improve punctuality, IR also undertakes rationalisation of time 
tables. One such exercise, in a scientific manner, was undertaken  
with the assistance of IIT- Mumbai using their traffic simulator. The 
exercise also aimed at provisioning of fixed  Integrated Maintenance 
blocks on all sections to minimise detention and improve punctuality. 
 New generation High capacity Locomotives are being utilised for Right 
powering of trains. 
●  Further, with a view to minimise and mitigate the effect of fog and to 
assist the Loco Pilots run the train during foggy weather conditions the 
following steps have been taken by Indian Railways: 
(i)   GPS based FOG SAFE DEVICE – A Global Positioning System 
(GPS) based portable 'Fog Safe Device' (FSD) is being provided to 
Loco Pilots, which displays upcoming critical landmarks such as 
approaching signal, level crossing gates, permanent speed 
restrictions etc. in advance during poor visibility conditions like fog. 
This device is used for safe train operation especially during winter 
season and to help reduce stress on Loco Pilots while running in 
poor visibility conditions.  As on 30.04.2026, there are 32,748 Fog 
Safe devices available over Indian Railways. 
(ii)   Modified Semi-Automatic Stop Signal (MASS) System: MASS has 
been introduced on the Automatic Signalling territory during 
abnormal conditions like Fog & Bad Weather impairing visibility. The 
system helps minimise delay in train operation during foggy weather 
conditions.

entries.head:
Government of India 
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
Department of Consumer Affairs 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 613 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
 
 
SALE OF EXPIRED FOOD PRODUCTS WITH ALTERED LABELS 
 
613. SHRI MANICKAM TAGORE B: 
 
DIGITAL CONSUMER JUSTICE AND ENFORCEMENT OF CONSUMER COMMISSION 
ORDERS 
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken note of the recent case in Delhi involving sale of  expired 
food products with altered manufacturing and expiry dates and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether similar cases of relabeling and resale of expired food items have been reported  across 
the country and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government has taken any steps to identify and dismantle organised ne tworks 
involved in procurement and resale of expired or near-expired food products nationwide and if 
so, the details thereof; 
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the scale of such illegal practices both in Delhi and other 
parts of the country and if so, the data thereof; 
(e)  whether counterfeit and expired food items are being distributed through retail stores, wholesale 
markets and e-commerce platforms across the country and if so, the details of the  action taken 
by the Government in this regard; and 
(f)  whether the Government considers existing enforcement by Food Safety and Standards  
Authority of India (FSSAI) and State Food Safety Departments sufficient to tackle such rackets 
operating in multiple States and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE  
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI B.L.VERMA) 
 
 
(a) to (f): Food Safety & Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has informed that Food Safety 
Department of Delhi and FSSAI has taken cognizance of recent case in Delhi involving sale of expired 
food products with altered manufacturing and expiry dates. It was reported that four Delhi based firms 
were involved in deliberate removal and re -printing of expiry dates, batch numbers, and other 
mandatory label declarations on food products. 
 
 A joint team of Food Safety Officer from Food Safety Department of Delhi and Northern 
Regional Office of FSSAI have conducted immediate inspections in the above mentioned premises 
under the provisions of the Food Safety & Standards Act 2006. During the inspection, various food and 
non-food items of different brands were found stored at the premises. Several food products were 
allegedly found bearing forged manufacturing dates, expiry dates, batch numbers and altered label 
declarations. 

 
 Criminal proceedings have been initiated as per law and Licenses of these 04 firms have been 
suspended. 
 
 Food Safety Department of Delhi has issued an Order dated 09.07.2026 to all Designated 
Officers and Food Safety Officers in its jurisdiction to conduct regular special enforcement drive in this 
regard till further order or until specifically reviewed by the Commissioner. This enforcement drive 
will focus on: 
 
 Fraudulent re-labelling of expired food products; 
 Tampering with expiry dates, "Best Before" date s, batch numbers, manufacturing dates, QR 
codes, or other statutory declarations; 
 Counterfeit labels and packaging; 
 Storage of expired food products intended for re-entry into the market; 
 Unauthorised repacking or relabelling activities; 
 and any other practice amounting to food fraud, misbranding, or consumer deception. 
 
 Further, FSSAI has also issued directions to all Commissioners of Food Safety of States/UTs 
to undertake Nationwide surveillance and appropriate action under the provisions of the Food Saf ety 
and Standards Act, 2006 against instances of tampering of expiry dates, fraudulent re -labelling and 
sale/distribution of expired food products vide Order dated 09.07.2026. 
 
 More than 99% of the Food Business Operators (FBOs) fall within the jurisdiction of the 
State/UT Food Safety Authorities. Accordingly, the enforcement and implementation of the provisions 
of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act, 2006) primarily rests with the State/UT Food 
Safety Authorities within their respective jurisdictions. To ensure compliance with the standards, limits, 
and other statutory requirements prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the 
regulations made thereunder, the State Food Safety Authorities undertake regular surveil lance, 
monitoring, targeted enforcement drives, inspections, and sampling activities across the food sector. 
 
 Any deviation from the prescribed standards or violation of the provisions of the FSSR, when 
detected, results in stringent regulatory and puniti ve action against the non -compliant Food Business 
Operators (FBOs) in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the rules framed 
thereunder, including suspension & cancellation of licence, prohibition on sale, seizure & destruction 
of non -compliant food articles and judiciary act

entries.t: Misusing of AI-based Image Generation Platforms
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 614 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
  
MISUSING OF AI-BASED IMAGE GENERATION PLATFORMS 
  
†614.  DR. ANAND KUMAR: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that by misusing Artificial Intelligence (AI) based image 
generation platforms, photos of individuals especially women and children are being altered to 
create objectionable and obscene image thereby posing a serious threat to their privacy, dignity 
and safety; 
(b) the number of such cases registered during the last three years and the number of FIRs 
registered in such cases along with the number of cases in which action has been taken by the 
Government; 
(c) whether the Government has issued any specific guidelines/rules related to the IT Act, cyber 
laws or AI to prevent such misuse and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government is proposing to introduce more stringent regulatory mechanism to 
fix the accountability of AI platforms to provide immediate relief to victims and to ensure the 
prompt removal of such objectionable content? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
  
(a) to (d):   The policies of the Government are aimed at ensuring an open, safe and trusted and 
accountable internet for its users, including women and children. The Information Technology 
Act, 2000 and the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics 
Code) Rules, 2021, together, have put in place a stringent framework to deal with unlawful and 
harmful content in the digital space. 
 
Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 (“IT Act”) 
The IT Act provides punishment for various cyber offences such as identity theft (section 66C), 
impersonation (section 66D), privacy violations (section 66E), publishing or transmitting 
obscene or sexually explicit content (sections 67, 67A, 67B). It also empowers Police to 
investigate offences (Section 78 and 80). 
 
IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (“IT Rules”) 
The IT Rules cast specific obligations on intermediaries to observe due diligence while 
discharging their duties and shall inform the users of computer resources not to host, display, 
upload, modify, publish, transmit, update or share any information that is harmful to children, 
obscene, pornographic, invasive of another’s privacy, insulting or harassing on the basis of 
gender or violates any law for the time being in force. 
 

The intermediary, within two hours from the receipt of a complaint made by an individual or 
any person on behalf, in relation to any content which involves full / partial nudity, exposing 
the private area and artificially morphed images of an individual should take all reasonable and 
practicable measures to remove or disable access to such content which is hosted, stored, 
published or transmitted by it. 
 
 
Recent amendments: 
Recent amendments to IT Rules require social media platforms and other intermediaries to 
remove unlawful content within three hours of the receipt of an order of a court of competent 
jurisdiction or reasoned intimation by the Appropriate Government or its agency.  
 
Intermediaries, in cases where the violation involves the commission of an offence under any 
law currently in force —such as the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 read with the Bharatiya 
Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, or the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, 
which mandates reporting must report such offence to the appropriate authority in accordance 
with the provisions of the applicable law. 
 
On 10th February, 2026, the Government strengthened the regulatory framework by amending 
the IT Rules, 2021 to address harms arising from synthetically generated information (SGI), 
including deepfakes and AI-generated content. 
 
Key points related to the amendment are as follows:- 
•    Intermediaries are required to ensure clear labelling and traceable metadata for 
permissible AI -generated content, so that users can easily identify synthetically 
generated material and prevent deception or misuse. 
•    It further strengthens user accountability and platform due diligence, including 
mandatory user awareness regarding legal consequences of unlawful AI -generated 
content and stronger compliance obligations for social media intermediaries. 
•   Importantly, the guidelines explicitly cover child sexual exploitation material, non -
consensual intimate imagery, impersonation and other harmful AI -generated content, 
requiring platforms to prevent such content and take prompt action when detected. 
•   Strengthening of timelines for compliance, including reduced timelines for removal of 
unlawful information upon actual knowledge upon valid reasoned intimation from the

617.  SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA:

(a) whether the Government is aware of such cases in which Member 
of Parliament Local Area Development (MPLAD) works of the MPs 
belonging to the opposition party are delayed and their works are not 
approved on time; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to take punitive action against

(c) if so, the reaction of the Government thereto; 
(d) the number of such works in Gurdaspur district of Punjab which 
could not be  started or completed even after months of 
recommendations or are being repeatedly recommended; 
(e) whether the Government is likely to take cognizance in the matter 
in which the BDPO Dera Baba Nanak herself said in the DISHA 
committee in front of the entire administration that she would not get

MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, MINISTER OF 
STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CULTURE [RAO 
INDERJIT SINGH] 
 
(a) to (c) Under the MPLAD Scheme, Hon’ble Member of Parliament 
send their recommendati ons of development works directly to 

District Authorities through eSAKSHI portal and the same are 
sanctioned and implemented by the District Authorities in 
accordance with the administrative, financial and technical rules of 
the concerned State/UT Governme nts and in accordance with the 
Guidelines on MPLADS. 
As per the MPLADS Guidelines, the Implementing District Authority 
shall, before sanctioning any work, ensure that all requisite statutory 
and regulatory clearances have been obtained from the competent 
authorities, that the work conforms to the MPLADS Guidelines, and 
that a written undertaking has been obtained from the concerned 
User Agency confirming its willingness to bear the operation and 
maintenance costs of the proposed asset from its own resources. 
As per Para 4.3.4 of the MPLADS Guidelines 2023, in case of material 
breach of MPLADS Guidelines by any individual/authority concerned, 
he/she shall become liable for disciplinary/penal action. The 
government of the State/UT concerned shall fix responsi bility and 
take necessary disciplinary action against the erring/delinquent 
officials/implementing agencies/vendors etc. in all such cases of 
material breach and wilful non-compliance of MPLADS Guidelines. 
However, it has been observed that delays in the i ssuance of 
administrative and technical sanctions for works recommended 
under the MPLAD Scheme are generally attributable to factors such 
as submission of incomplete proposals, local disputes, constraints 
relating to land availability or site feasibility, requirements of 
statutory clearances, and technical issues at the district level. As per 
the MPLADS Guidelines, the responsibility for timely scrutiny, 
sanction, and execution of works rests with the District Authorities. 
Whenever instances of inordinate d elay are brought to the notice of 
the Ministry, the concerned State/UT Government and District 
Authority are requested to examine the matter and take appropriate 
administrative action against the responsible officials under the 
applicable service rules. They are also advised to strengthen internal 
monitoring and oversight mechanisms to ensure timely 
implementation of works recommended by Hon’ble Members of 
Parliament. 
(d) to (e) As per Para 3.2.4 of the MPLADS Guidelines, 2023, the 
sanction/rejection in res pect of all recommendations made by the 
Member of Parliament shall be issued by the Implementing District 
Authority within 45 days from the date of receipt of the 
recommendations to the Implementing District Authority. 

As per para 3.2.6 of the MPLADS Guide lines, 2023, the period of 
operation of model code of conduct notified by the Election 
Commission, as applicable to the jurisdiction of a particular 
Implementing District Authority, shall not be included in the 
reckoning of time limits as mentioned in para  3.2.4 of the MPLADS 
Guidelines, 2023. 
As per Para 3.2.12 of the MPLADS Guidelines, 2023, the sanction 
letter issued by the Implementing District Authority shall stipulate a

which should gen erally not exceed one year. In exceptional cases, 
for instance in difficult/ hilly terrain, etc., where the implementation 
time is likely to exceed one -year, specific justification for the same 
shall be incorporated in the sanction letter.

DIGITAL CONNECTIVITY IN REMOTE AND HILLY AREAS, KOLHAPUR 
 
619.  SHRI SHAHU SHAHAJI CHHATRAPATI: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether dedicated funding will be provided for 4G/5G Saturation Project and BharatNet 
implementation in backward blocks of Radhanag ari and Gaganbawda in Kolhapur, facing unstable 
mobile connectivity in remote rural and hilly areas; 
 
(b)  the current BSNL 4G tower installation status, PM -WANI Wi-Fi hotspots operational and 
optical fibre connectivity coverage block-wise; 
 
(c)  whether Kolhapur proposes to included in the next phase of Digital India Land Records 
Modernization Programme (DILRMP) for farmers' benefit; and 
 
(d)  the details of the funding allocation, implementation timeline and digital literacy centres 
planned by 2027? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
(a)  Scheme-wise, including 4G Saturation Project and BharatNet, dedicated funding is provided 
for telecom infrastructure connectivity in remote and hilly area s through Digital Bharat Nidhi 
(DBN). 
 
(b)  As on 30.06.2026, 14 Government funded 4G mobile towers have been commissioned in 
Radhanagari and Gaganbawda blocks of Kolhapur.  Further, 587 WiFi  Hotspots in Kolhapur are 
operational. 122 kilometers and 31 kilometers of optical fibre cable have been laid in Radhanagari 
and Gaganbawda blocks respectively under BharatNet project. 
 
(c)  Kolhapur has already been incorporated into the core modernizatio n phases of the Digital 
India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP). 
 
(d)  The Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) was initiated to reach 
digital literacy in 6 crore rural households (one person per household) nationwide. The Scheme was 
implemented by CSC e- Governance Services India Limited through 4.39 Lakh Common Service 
Centres (CSCs) spread across 2.5 Lakh Gram Panchayats in the country.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 620 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
REVIEW OF STATISTICAL FRAMEWORKS  
620. SHRI BAIJAYANT PANDA: 
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether any methodological review has been undertaken to assess 
adequacy of existing statistical frameworks and if so, the details thereof: 
(b) whether any expert groups or technical consultations have been 
constituted and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government proposes to update statistical standards or 
survey instruments and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMP LEMENTATION; MINISTER OF STATE 
(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING; AND 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CULTURE [RAO INDERJIT 
SINGH] 
(a) to (c) The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation 
(MoSPI) undertakes periodic methodological reviews of the statistical 
framework to ensure that o ﬃcial statistics remain representative of the 
current structure of the economy and continue to meet emerging data 
requirements. The major methodological reviews undertaken by the 
Ministry are outlined below. 
MoSPI has undertaken comprehensive base revision exercises for the 
Gross Domestic Product (GDP), All India Index of Industrial Production 
(IIP) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) to ensure that these 
macroeconomic indicators adequately reflect the evolving structure of 
the economy and align with international statistical standards. 
Accordingly, the base year of GDP has been revised from 2011 –12 to 
2022–23 based on the recommendations of the Advisory Committee on 
National Accounts Statist ics (ACNAS); the base year of IIP has been 
revised from 2011 –12 to 2022 –23 under the guidance of the Technical 
Advisory Committee on IIP; and the base year of CPI has been revised 
from 2012=100 to 2024=100 under the guidance of an Expert Group 
constituted for the purpose. These revisions incorporate updated data 
sources, expanded coverage, revised item baskets and weights, 

improved estimation methodologies, enhanced use of administrative data 
sources such as GST and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) 
database, improved estimation of the unincorporated sector using the 
Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) and the 
Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), adoption of internationally 
accepted statistical practices, and other methodological refinements. 
In addition, many technical consultations and brainstorming sessions 
were held with experts, academicians, State Governments and other 
stakeholders for seeking their inputs and feedback for base revision 
exercise of aforementioned macro economic indicators. Moreover, pre -
release consultative workshops were also held before the release of the 
revised series of these indicators. 
Further, MoSPI continuously reviews and updates the statistical 
standards, concepts, classiﬁcations, survey instrument s and 
methodologies adopted in National Sample Surveys (NSS) to meet 
emerging data requirements, align with national and international best 
practices, and improve the quality, relevance and timeliness of o ﬃcial 
statistics. Accordingly, survey schedules/que stionnaires, sampling 
design, concepts and de ﬁnitions, item classi ﬁcations, ﬁeld procedures, 
data collection methodology, validation protocols and tabulation plans 
are reviewed before each major survey based on recommendations of the 
Steering Committee for  National Sample Surveys (NSS), Technical 
Advisory Groups (TAGs), survey -speciﬁc Technical Expert Groups(TEGs), 
and consultations with Central Ministries/Departments, State 
Governments, subject matter experts and other stakeholders. The 
changes are ﬁnalized after pilot studies and ﬁeld testing, wherever 
required. 
As a result, modernization of National Sample Surveys has been done 
through various initiatives such as the adoption of digital platforms such 
as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) and the e -SIGMA 
system, incorporating in -built validation checks, real -time data 
monitoring, AI -enabled chatbots, and multilingual interfaces. These 
initiatives have substantially improved data quality and led to reduction 
in time lag in release of survey data from 8 -9 months to 45 -90 days. 
Annual Survey Results are now released within 90 -120 days; quarterly 
results within 45 -60 days and monthly results within 15 -30 days of 
completion of surveys. MoSPI has launched short duration surveys to 
cater the emergi ng need for high -frequency socio -economic indicators. 
Additionally, sampling design of major surveys have been modiﬁed by 
adopting district as the basic stratum enabling states to generate 
district level estimates of key indicators.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS. FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 621
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22ND JULY, 2026
ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF FPS DEALERS
621. SHRI SHAFI PARAMBIL:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased
to state:
(a): whether the Government has any proposal to include schemes such as Jan Poshan Kendra,
Pradhan iVlantri Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) through Fair Price Shops (FPSs) to enhance the
economic viability of FPS dealers;
(b): if so, the details thereof including the timeline for implementation;
(c): whether the Government has received any representations from Fair Price Shop Dealers
Associations in this regard and if so, the details thereof;
(d): whether the Government has any proposal to sell rice and wheat under the Open Market
Sale Scheme through Fair Price Shops to enable consumers to purchase grains at Government-
specified rates; and
(e): if so, the details thereoF
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS.
FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(SHRIMATI NIMUBEN JAYANTIBH Al BAMBHANIYA)
(a) to (c): Department of Food and Public Distribution has collaborated with the Ministry of Skill
Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) to enhance the capacity and confidence of Fair Price
Shop (FPS) dealers by equipping them with essential entrepreneurship and business management
skills. Under this collaboration, NIESBUD (an autonomous institute under MSDE) has developed
a specialized training programme for FPS dealers covering digital and financial literacy, e.-
commerce, retail management. and basic nutrition


To date, approximately 325 FPS dealers across nine States–Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh,
Gujarat, Telangana, Karnataka, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Bihar–have
undergone this training. As a result, 90 FPS outlets have been converted into Jan Poshan Kendras
(JPKs) across five cities: Hyderabad, Ghaziabad, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, and Indore, improving their
commercial viability and community outreach.
The Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana was launched by the Government of
India to make quality generic medicines available at affordable prices for all citizens. Under this
scheme, special outlets called Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) are opened across the country. These
Kendras provide medicines that are about 50% to 80% cheaper than branded medicines, helping
reduce healthcare expenses for patients.
The government has adopted a franchisee model for opening of JAKs by inviting online
applications from individual entrepreneurs, non-governmental organisations, societies, trusts, firITls,
private companies, etc. through the website www.janaushadhi.gov.in. Any individual having a D.
Pharma. or B. Pharma. qualification either herself/himself or any individual or organisation that has
employed a person with such a qualification as a pharmacist for obtaining a drug licence from the
State Licensing Authority concerned, is eligible to open a Jan Aushadhi Kendra.
There is no such proposal to include Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi
Pariyojana (PMBJP) through Fair Price Shops (FPSs).
(d) to (e): The surplus food grains (Wheat & Rice), beyond the Public Distribution System (PDS)
and Other Welfare Schemes (OWS) requirements are sold through open sale under the Open
Market Sales Scheme (Domestic) [OMMSS(D)]. Under OMSS (D), Bharat Atta and Bharat Rice
were launched on 6.11.2023 and 6.02.2024, respectively, with a view to providing atta (wheat
flour) and rice to general consumers at subsidized rates. These commodities are sold to the general
public through NAFED/ NCCF/ Kendriya Bhandar through own stores/ mobile vans and/ or E-
commerce/ big chain retailers only.

SHRI BENNY BEHANAN:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of beneficiaries covered under National Food Security Act (NFSA) and PM Garib
Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) as on 30.06.2026, State/UT-wise;
(b) whether free foodgrains under PMGKAY have been extended beyond the year 2024 and if so,
the financial implication thereof;
(c) whether any States have reported exclusion of eligible beneficiaries due to Aadhaar seeding
issues and if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of the steps taken by the Government to ensure portability under One Nation One
Ration Card (ONORC)?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(SHRIM ATI NIMUBEN JAYANTIBHAI BAMBHANIYA)
(a): The State/UT wise details of beneficiaries covered under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan
Anna Yojana (PIVIGKAY) are at Annexure.
(b): Yes, the period for distribution of free of cost foodgrains under PMGKAY has been
extended for five years from 1 st January, 2024, with an estimated financial outlay of Rs. 1 1.80 lakh
crore totally to be borne by Central Government.
(c): Under the joint responsibility of the Central and the State Governments, the responsibility
for identification of beneficiaries and issuance of ration cards within the coverage determined hr
the State/UT rest with the concerned States/UTs


The Central Government has issued advisories to all the States/Union Territories from time to time
to identify all eligible and poor persons/ households including vulnerable Sections of Society for
inclusion under the NFSA. States undertake updation of their beneficiary database so that ineligible
ration cards get deleted and better targeting of rightful beneficiaries is ensured. Thus, deletion of
ineligible beneficiaries and addition of eligible beneficiaries under the Act is a continuous process.
Further, all States/UTs have been advised that no genuine beneficiary or household shall be
denied from receiving entitled quota of subsidized foodgrains only for want of Aadhaar or due to
failure of biometric/Aadhaar authentication due to network/connectivity/linking related issues,
other technical reasons, or poor biometrics of the beneficiary.
(d): The nationwide portability of ration cards is popularly known as the One Nation One RatIon
Card (ONORC) feature. Through this technology driven reform, approximately 80 Crore
PMGKAY beneficiaries are empowered to lift their entitled foodgrains from any Fair Price Shop
(FPS) of their choice, anywhere in the country, by using their same existing ration card with
biometric authentication on an electronic Point of Sale (ePoS) device. Currently, ONORC feature is
enabled in all 36 States/UTs, across the country, covering almost 100% PMGKAY beneficiaries.
As on date, more than 221 Crore portability transactions (including migrant labourers) have been
recorded under ONORC

entries.head:

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS  
DEPARTMENT OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 623 
 ANSWERED ON 22ND JULY, 2026 
 
CALL DROP AND POOR MOBILE NETWORK CONNECTIVITY 
 
623. SHRI MANI A: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of the persistent call drop and poor mobile network 
connectivity issues reported from several rural and semi-urban areas of Dharmapuri district in Tamil 
Nadu, affecting students, farmers, small businesses and emergency communication, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  whether any district-wise assessment has been undertaken to identify the reasons for frequent 
call drops, including network congestion, inadequate telecom tower infrastructure, handover failures 
between cell towers and restrictions on installation of new t elecom sites in Dharmapuri, if so, the 
details thereof; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to direct telecom service providers to strengthen mobile 
infrastructure by installing additional towers and upgrading network capacity in the district, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
 
(d) the timeline and other measures proposed to ensure uninterrupted and reliable mobile 
connectivity for residents of Dharmapuri district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
(a) Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) monitors the performance of service 
providers against the benchmark of various Quality of Service parameters, as prescribed in Quality 
of Service (QoS) Regulation. As per Performance Monitoring Report published by TRAI for the 
month of May 2026 for mobile services, all the service providers are meeting the benchmark of all 
network related QoS parameters in Tamil Nadu License Service Area which includes Dharampuri 
District. 
 
(b)  TRAI conducts Independent Drive Tests (IDT) and Operator Assisted Drive Tests (OADT) 
regularly for assessment of mobile network performance and the results are published on TRAI 
website. 
 
(c)  Telecom Service Providers periodically assess their network coverage and impr ove 
connectivity by optimizing the existing network and by installing new Base Transceiver Stations 
(BTSs) as per techno-commercial feasibility. 
 
(d)  Government has undertaken several initiatives under Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) for 
provisioning of 4G mob ile services in identified uncovered villages/ locations across the country 
including Dharampuri District. So far, 11 mobile towers have been installed under 4G saturation 
schemes for providing mobile services in 19 villages of the Dharampuri District.

STATE AND DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSIONS IN LADAKH 
 
625. SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA: 
 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
 
 
(a)  whether the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission and District Consumer  Disputes 
Redressal Commissions have been established and are functional in the Union Territory of Ladakh 
as mandated under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; 
(b)  if not, the reasons for the non-establishment or non-functioning of these forums in Union Territory 
of Ladakh; 
(c)  whether the Government has formula ted a timeline for setting up these commissions and  making 
them fully operational in Ladkah; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and the steps taken by the Government to expedite their  establishment 
including recruitment and infrastructure development; and 
(e)  the details of measures being taken by the Government to ensure effective consumer  grievance 
redressal until these forums are functional? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE  
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(SHRI B.L. VERMA) 
 
(a) to (e) :  State and District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions have been established in the 
Union Territory of Ladakh. Further, one member is appointed in the Leh District Consumer Disputes 
Redressal Commission. 
 
Under the provisions of the Consumer Pr otection Act, 2019, it is the responsibility of the State 
Governments to fill up the vacancies of President and Members in the State Commissions and District 
Commissions. Further, as per Rule 6(4) of the Consumer Protection (Qualification for appointment, method 
of recruitment, procedure of appointment, term of office, resignation and removal of the President and 
members of the State Commission and District Commission) Rules, 2020, the process of appointments 
shall be initiated by the State Government atleast 6 months before the vacancy arises.  
 
As per Section 32 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, if, at any time, there is a vacancy in the 
office of the President or Member of the District Commission, the State Government may, by notification, 
direct - 
a) any other District Commission specified in that notification to exercise the jurisdiction in respect 
of that district also; or 
b) the President or a member of any other District Commission specified in that notification to 
exercise the powers and discharge the functions of the President or member of that District 
Commission also. 
 

 
 
The National Consumer Helpline (NCH) administered by the Department of Consumer Affairs has 
emerged as a single point of access to consumers across the country for their grievance redressal at a pre -
litigation stage. Consumers can register their grievances from all over the country in 17 languages including 
Hindi, English, Kashmiri, Punjabi, Nepali, Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, 
Maithili, Santhali, Bengali, Odia, Assamese and Manipuri through a toll -free number 1915. These 
grievances can be registered on Integrated Grievance Redressal Mechanism (INGRAM), an omni-channel 
IT enabled central portal, through various channels- WhatsApp (8800001915), SMS (8800001915), email 
(nch-ca@gov.in), the NCH app, the web portal (consumerhelpline.gov.in) and the Umang app, as per their 
convenience. 1,853 companies, who have voluntarily partnered with NCH as part of the ‘Convergence’ 
programme directly respond to these grievances according to their redressal process and revert by providing 
a feedback to the complainant on the portal.  
 
The Department  launched “e-Jagriti” portal on 1st January, 2025, which aims to enhance consumer 
grievance redressal through Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning integration and modern features like 
faceless onboardi ng and role -based dashboards. It unifies existing applications (OCMS, e -Daakhil, 
NCDRC CMS, CONFONET) into a single, scalable platform, allowing users to file complaints seamlessly 
from anywhere with multilingual support. The portal is designed to provide a convenient, transparent and 
efficient means for consumers to seek redressal by enabling online complaint filing, digital submission of 
documents, online payment of fees and also supports virtual courtrooms, enabling the hearing of cases 
remotely and ensuring faster disposal while reducing dependency on physical infrastructure. These features 
address bottlenecks like geographical barriers, scheduling conflicts and manual interventions and has 
reduced reliance on physical proceedings and has accelerated justice delivery.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS 
(DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL & TRAINING) 
 
LOK SABHA

(ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026) 
 
NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR CIVIL SERVICE TRAINING INSTITUTIONS 
 
626. SHRI VISHWESHWAR HEGDE KAGERI: 
 SHRI SURESH KUMAR KASHYAP: 
 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has introduced major changes under National Standards for Civil 
Service Training Institutions (NSCSTI)- 2.0 which has replaced NSCSTI-2.0 and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(b) the progress made in implementation of the NSCSTI-2.0; 
(c) the details of the number of training institutions assessed and accredited under NSCSTI-2.0 
along with their performance grading; and 
(d) the measures taken to strengthen the quality and standardisation of civil service training 
across Central Government institutions? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES 
AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
 
(a) to (d): The National Standards for Civil Service Training Institutions (NSCSTI) has been 
revised and launched as NSCSTI 2.0 on 18.07.2025. The revision of NSCSTI was undertaken 
to ensure alignment with the evolving objectives of Mission Karmayogi and the strategic role 
of Civil Service Training Institutions (CSTIs) in institutionalizing continuous learning and 
delivering competency- based training. 
 
A review of the implementation of NSCSTI was undertaken through a structured 
consultative process, wherein a national level workshop with accredited CSTIs was convened 
to obtain detailed feedback on the existing framework. The findings from the review formed 
the basis for restructuring the framework and rationalization of the assessment metrics from 
59 to 43 under NSCSTI 2.0. The assessment metrics focus on themes like course design, 
faculty development, resource and training targets, digitization and training delivery, training 
evaluation and quality assurance, governance and operation functions of the training 
institution.  
 
Measures taken to strengthen the quality and standardization of civil services training 
include the preparation of Quality Improvement Plans (QIPs) based on gap analysis, 
supported by mentoring from higher-rated institutions; faculty development through targeted 
training programmes; support for the digitisation of training content; strengthening of 
governance, procurement, and training management processes; and the establishment of a  

 
Page 2 of 2 
 
 
 
continuous benchmarking and collaborative ecosystem to facilitate resource sharing, real-
time data-driven decision-making, and long-term institutional development across Central 
and State training institutions. 
 
Training Institutes are awarded 1-Star to 5-Star ratings as per their performance in the 
assessment. So far 209 Institutes have been accredited, out of which 25 have received 4-star 
or above rating. The remaining institutions have ratings 3- star or below.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 629 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 22.07.2026 
 
CSCs IN THANJAVUR 
 
629. SHRI MURASOLI S: 
 
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the number of Common Service Centres (CSCs) functional in Thanjavur district; 
(b) the status of digital literacy programmes implemented in the said district under central 
schemes during the last three years; and 
(c) the details of cybercrime and/or data fraud complaints originating from Thanjavur district 
which have been reported to CERT-In and the number, nature and details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) to (c): As of 31 st May 2026, a total number of 685 CSCs were functional in Thanjavur 
district of Tamil Nadu out of which 486 CSCs were functional in rural areas. 
 
Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) was initiated to provide 
digital literacy in 6 crore rural households (one person per household) nationwide including 
the State of Tamil Nadu. A total of 6.39 crore individuals were trained across the country. 
Under the PMGDISHA Scheme in the State of Tamil Nadu, a total of 14.07 lakh+ beneficiaries 
were trained, out of which 52,646 beneficiaries trained in Thanjavur District of Tamil Nadu. 
The scheme has been concluded on 31.03.2024. 
 
National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT) is providing training on 
digital literacy through courses such as Course on Computer Concepts (CCC), Awareness in 
Computer Concept (ACC), Basic Computer Course (BCC), etc. through its wide  network of 
56 own centres and 9000+ partner institutions. NIELIT’s Digital Literacy (CCC) course 
includes a dedicated component on financial literacy and digital financial services. The module 
provides basic awareness of financial tools, services, and gov ernment schemes, enabling 
learners to make informed financial decisions and effectively use digital financial platforms. 
NIELIT has one (1) own Centre in Tamil Nadu at Chennai for skill development activities in 
the State. Further, NIELIT has more than 35 partner institutes in the State, including 6 in the 
district of Thanjavur. In the last 03 years, through this network, NIELIT has trained/skilled 
37,500+ candidates across the State of Tamil Nadu. 
 
A comprehensive initiative “PM eVidya” was initiated by Ministry of Education (MoE), 
Government of India as part of Atma Nirbhar  Bharat Abhiyaan on 17th May, 2020, which 
unifies all efforts related to digital/online/on -air education to enable multi -mode access to 
education across the country. States/UTs collaborate with NCERT to utilise, monitor and 

evaluate the effectiveness of these initiatives as per their requirements. NCERT also provides 
regular guidance/ feedback to States/UTs on the quality of these initiatives. 
The key components of PM eVidya  are also aligned towards enhancing digital literacy and 
include 200 DTH TV channels and 400 Radio channels to enable all States/UTs to provide 
supplementary education in various Indian languages for classes 1-12. 
 
Under the PM eVidya 200 DTH TV Channels initiative, the State of Tamil Nadu has been 
allotted five dedicated channels (TN PM eVidya 158-162). 
 
Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the Nation’s One Nation, One 
Digital platform for providing quality e-content for school education in States/UTs along with 
QR coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. As a participant in DIKSHA, States/UTs 
have generated and contributed over 3.67 lakh content in local/regional languages enabling 
multilingualism. 
 
Overall, 579.41 crore learning sessions for 2.29 crore users have been completed on DIKSHA 
by students, teachers and other stakeholders. The platform supports both online and offline 
access, enabling learners to download content and continue learning witho ut internet 
connectivity. 
 
The stakeholders have access to more than 836 Virtual Labs and 100 Virtual skill labs (50 each 
in Hindi and English) on DIKSHA that help students with simulation of real-world laboratory 
environment. 
 
Cybercrime or fraud complaints are not reported to Indian Computer Emergency Response 
Team (CERT-In). These are being reported through Cybercrime Helpline number 1930 and 
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal ( https://cybercrime.gov.in/) to Ministry of Home 
Affairs. 
 
*******

entries.t: Demand of General Class Coaches in Railways
entries.head:
§  Page 1 of 6 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 631 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
DEMAND OF GENERAL CLASS COACHES IN RAILWAYS 
 
631. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing demand for General 
Class coaches, particularly among short-distance passengers and 
economically weaker sections who depend on affordable rail travel, if 
so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(b) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of passenger 
demand, occupancy levels and overcrowding in General Class coaches 
across the railway network, if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to increase the number of General 
Class coaches in existing trains/introduce additional General Class 
services to meet the growing public demand, if so, the details thereof; 
and  
(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken to reduce overcrowding and 
enhance the availability of General Class accommodation across the 
Railways?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d) The number of unreserved passengers travelling on Indian 
Railways has gradually increased over the last three years. However, it is 
also a fact that occupancy pattern of trains is not uniform throughout the 
year and it varies over lean and peak periods. During peak rush periods, the 
occupancy of the trains especially on popular routes remains full whereas 
during lean period and on less popular routes, there is sub optimal 
utilization. 

Page 2 of 6 
With a view to meet the demand of passengers travelling in 
unreserved coaches, Indian Railways (IR) have significantly increased the 
facilities for passengers demanding general class travel. During the 
financial year 2024-25 alone, 1250 general coaches have been utilised in 
various long-distance trains to have at least 4 general class coaches. 
Similarly, during the year 2025-26 about 870 Coaches including 160 General 
Class and during the year 2026-27 (up to 30.06.2026)  about 190 coaches 
including 20 general class coaches  have been utilised for permanent 
augmentation. 
To cater to the travel demand of the low and middle income families, 
Indian Railways have taken up manufacturing of 17,000 non-AC coaches 
(general/sleeper). 
On IR, the percentage of non-AC coaches, is about 70% as indicated 
below: 
           
 
 
 
  Distribution of coaches:

entries.t: Expansion of Renewable Energy Projects in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 633 
ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
EXPANSION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECTS IN UTTAR PRADESH 
 
633. SHRI JITENDRA KUMAR DOHARE 
 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of the fact that the expected expansion of new and 
renewable energy schemes has not taken place in the Etawah Lok Sabha Constituency of Uttar 
Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details of projects sanctioned and installed and amount spent under the Pradhan 
Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PM -SGMBY), Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha 
evam Utthaan Mahabhiyaan (PM-KUSUM), solar rooftop installation, solar pumps and other 
renewable energy schemes in the Etawah Lok Sabha Constituency during the last three years, 
scheme wise; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to sanction additional solar high mast lights, solar street 
light and other community solar energy projects to increase energy availability in the rural and 
remote areas of the Etawah Lok Sabha Constituency; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK) 
(a) & (b) The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy ( MNRE) through state implementing 
agencies, is implementing various schemes/programmes across the country including in the 
Etawah Lok Sabha Constituency of Uttar Pradesh.  
 
The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) and PM Kisan Urja Suraksha evam 
Utthaan Mahabhiyaan (PM -KUSUM) scheme are demand driven scheme, wherein no state -
wise allocation is made. 
 
Under the PMSG: MBY, since its launch in February 2024, a total of 17,929 applications have 
been received and 11,364 RTS systems have been installed, benefitting 11,364 households, and 
an amount of Rs 78.27 crore has been disbursed as Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to the 
beneficiaries of the scheme as on 20.07.2026 , in the districts covering Etawah Lok Sabha 
Constituency.  
 
As reported by the S tate Implementing Agencies of the state of Uttar Pradesh, based on the 
demand received from the state and sanction issued by the MNRE , a total of 414 agriculture 
pumps have been solarised and an amount of Rs. 216.24 Cr has been released in Etawah Lok 
Sabha Constituency of Uttar Pradesh, under the PM KUSUM scheme during the last three 
years. 
 

 
 
In addition, the UPNEDA has reported solarisation of 19 Government buildings with 
installation of 1933 kW capacity solar PV and an expenditure of Rs. 8.20 Cr, and installation 
of 1320 solar street lights with expenditure of Rs. 2.72 Cr during the last three years in Etawah 
Lok Sabha Constituency of Uttar Pradesh. 
(c) & (d)  Presently, there is no specific scheme operational in the MNRE for providing support 
for installation of solar high mast lights, solar street light and other community solar energy 
projects to increase energy availability in the rural and remote areas of the Etawah Lok Sabha 
Constituency.

#634. SHRI RAJESH RANJAN: 
 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether most Central Ministries do not even send an acknowledgement of receipt of letters 
received from Members of Parliament relating to their Parliamentary Constituencies and matters 
of public interest and even in most cases no meaningful reply is received; 
(b) if so, whether the Government considers this to be against the dignity of Parliament and 
constitutional role of elected representatives; 
(c) the number of Ministries/Departments presently complying with the provisions of the 
guidelines issued by the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions on 12 January, 
2026 providing for sending an acknowledgement within 15 days and a reply within the next 15 
days and the mechanism put in place to monitor such compliance; and 
(d) the details of concrete steps proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure accountability 
of the Ministries/Departments for violating the prescribed timelines for responding to the letters 
of Members of Parliament? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES 
AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
 
 (a) to (d): The Government has issued detailed guidelines for observance of proper procedure 
and protocol in official dealings between Administration and Members of Parliament(MP) 
and State Legislatures(SL) including that of acknowledgement letter to MPs, to all Ministries/ 
Department and State Governments/ Union Territories . Para 4(vii) of DoPT’s OM dated 
12.1.2026 states “Each communication received from the Member of Parliament, a member 
of the public, a recognized association or a public body will be acknowledged within 15 days, 
followed by a reply within the next 15 days of acknowledgement sent.” 
 
These guidelines have been reiterated from time to time to sensitize all State 
Government officials at the State/Division/District levels, with regard to their duties and 
obligations in relation to dealing with Hon’ble Members.

However, any complaints received from Members of Parliament regarding non-
compliance of protocol through Lok Sabha Secretariat and Rajya Sabha Secretariat are 
examined and factual reports are sought from concerned authorities/ State Governments.

entries.t: Minority concentrated Area Development in Raichur :
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 636 
ANSWERED ON- 22/07/2026 
    
 
MINORITY CONCENTRATED AREA DEVELOPMENT IN RAICHUR 
 
 
636. SHRI G KUMAR NAIK 
   
  
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:- 
 
(a)  the details of minority-concentrated blocks, towns and wards identified in Raichur district 
under PMJVK and the socio-economic and basic amenity indicators on the basis of which they 
were selected;  
 
(b) the status of access to secondary schools, PHCs, piped drinking water, household toilets, 
pucca roads and street lighting in such minority-concentrated areas of Raichur ward/taluk-wise; 
 
(c) the details of the number of PMJVK projects sanctioned for Raichur since 2018 and those 
remaining incomplete, non-operational or abandoned along with the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) the comparative position of minority -concentrated areas in Raichur vis -à-vis district 
averages on literacy, female literacy, school dropout rates, unemployment and housing 
deprivation; and 
 
(e) the details of specific interventions proposed during the next three years to bridge these 
deficits in minority -concentrated areas of Raichur along with the timelines and budgetary 
allocations? 
 
 
ANSWER 
  
 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU) 
 
(a) to (c)  Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme 
and one of the flagship programmes of the Ministry of Minority Affairs for creation of 
community infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas in sectors such as Health, Skill 
Development, Education, Women -centric Projects, Drinking Water and Sanitation, Sports, 
Renewable Energy, Tourism, Animal Husbandry and other community infrastructure. 
 
As per the revised PMJVK Guidelines, the scheme is being implemented in all districts 
across the country. Under the revised guidelines, the States/UTs may propose infrastructure 
projects in identified areas where the concentration of minority population is more than 25% 
within a catchment area of a 15 km radius. 
 
 
 

 
 
PMJVK is a demand -driven scheme. Projects under the Scheme are considered and 
approved based on proposals received from the respective State Governments/UT 
Administrations. The identification of project locations, including minority -concentrated 
blocks, towns, wards and villages, as well as assessment of local infrastructure gaps and socio-
economic needs, is undertaken by the concerned State Government/UT Administration while 
formulating project proposals in accordance with the Scheme guidelines. 
 
Accordingly, no separate list of minority -concentrated blocks, towns or wards in 
Raichur district, or ward/taluk-wise data on socio-economic and basic amenity indicators such 
as access to secondary schools, Primary Health Centres (PHCs), piped drinking wat er, 
household toilets, pucca roads and street lighting, is maintained centrally by the Ministry under 
PMJVK. The details of PMJVK projects approved for Raichur district, Karnataka since 2018, 
including their implementation status, are given at Annexure-I. 
 
(d) & (e) The implementation, execution, operation, and maintenance of projects 
approved under the scheme are the responsibility of the respective State Governments/ Union 
Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the Ministry does not maintain or capture district -
specific data regarding the comparative position of minority-concentrated areas in Raichur vis-
à-vis district averages on literacy, female literacy, school dropout rates, unemployment, and 
housing deprivation. Further, the Ministry does not maintain information o n State -specific 
interventions proposed during the next three years, including timelines and budgetary 
allocations, for bridging such deficits in minority-concentrated areas of Raichur. 
 
As the execution, operation and maintenance of approved projects are the responsibility 
of the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. No such data is captured 
by the Ministry. 
 
*****

PM-KUSUM IN BIHAR 
639. SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY 
 
WILL THE MINISTER OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY BE PLEASED TO 
STATE: 
 
(a) the current status of implementation of Pradhan Mantri-Kisan Urja Suraksha evam 
Utthaan Mahabhiyaan (PM-KUSUM) under the three distinct operational components to 
achieve comprehensive agricultural de-dieselisation across the country; 
(b) the total number of decentralized solar plants set up, off-grid solar pumps deployed and 
grid-connected pumps solarised across the country, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the specific progress achieved, number of solar pumps commissioned and aggregate clean 
energy generated under these frameworks in the State of Bihar particularly in Saran; 
(d) the structural specifications of the digital tools deployed including the centralized 
integration portal and Remote Monitoring Systems (RMS) to track real-time generation 
parameters; and 
(e)    the measures taken by the Government to streamline central financial assistance releases 
and fast-track power purchase agreement executions between farmers and local power 
distribution companies? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK) 
 
(a) to (b) The PM-KUSUM scheme has been implemented with the objective to provide energy 
security, d e-dieselisation of the agriculture sector and enhancing income of farmers. The 
installation of solar pumps under Component B of the scheme, has contributed towards 
replacement of diesel pumps and de-dieselization of the farm sector. 
 
The implementation timeline of PM KUSUM scheme is extended till 31.03.2027 for all 
components of the scheme. The State/UT wise progress, including Bihar, under PM KUSUM 
is placed at Annexure-I.  
 
(c) Based on the demand received from the State , total of 1,40,300 pumps are allocated for 
solarization under Component C (Feeder Level Solarization) to the state of Bihar. As reported 
by state implementing agencies (SIAs), total of 4570 pumps are solarized till 30.06.2026, out 
of which 702 pumps are solarized in Saran. 
 
 
(d) To monitor solar assets under all different components of PM -KUSUM scheme , the 
Ministry has developed Centralized Solar Energy Data Management (SEDM) Platform 
supported by State-level Remote Monitoring Systems (RMS).  The structural specifications of 
the digital tools include: 
• Three-tier Digital Architecture  
• Remote Monitoring System (RMS) 

• Communication Architecture  
• Cyber Security Features 
• Real-time Generation Parameters 
• Centralized Integration Portal 
 
(e)The Ministry has taken several proactive steps for accelerating the implementation of the 
scheme and release of CFA, which inter-alia includes:  
 
•  Simplification of scheme guidelines in January 2024 
•  Inclusion of all Components under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund for easy access to low 
cost financing to farmers 
•  Addressing land and other technical bottlenecks through, online portal development, 
creation of land bank, land lease rent etc. 
• Regular reviews with SIAs to expedite the installation of sanctioned capacities and pumps 
across the country. 
• Simplifications of formats for release of CFA 
• Extending implementation timelines till March 2027.
