entries.t: Status of Employment in Etah and Kasganj
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 64 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
STATUS OF EMPLOYMENT IN ETAH AND KASGANJ 
 
†64. SHRI DEVESH SHAKYA:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of the number of agricultural workers and construction 
workers registered on the e -shram portal in the districts of Etah 
and Kasganj at present;  
(b)whether the Government is aware of the fact that due to the lack 
of employment opportunities at the local level, migration of the 
youth to Delhi and Noida is increasing, and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government proposes to formulate any policy or rules 
to ensure mandatory employment of 75 per cent local youth in the 
Jawahar Thermal power project and railway construction works in 
the region and if so, the details thereof; and  
(d)whether the Government has any proposal to establish an 
Employees' State Insurance (ES I) hospital or a special medical 
facility centre for the workers of unorganised sector in Etah Lok 
Sabha Constituency and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26 th August, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW). 
The eShram portal registers the unorganised workers and provides 
them a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis.  
 
  As on 14 th July 2026, over  31.78 crore unorganised 
workers have already been registered on the eShram portal. 
 
  Details of the agriculture workers and construction 
workers registered on the eShram  portal in the districts of Etah and 
Kasganj is annexed. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  Employment generation coupled with improving 
employability is a priority of the Government. Accordingly, 
Government is implementing various employment generation 
schemes across t he country including Bundelkhand Region. The 
details of various employment generation schemes/programmes 
being implemented by the Government may be seen at 
https://dge.gov.in/schemes programmes . 
 
  ‘Employment’ being a subject under the Concurrent List, 
the Employment Service in India is the Joint concern of the Central 
and State Government. Directorate General of Employment, Ministry 
of Labour and Employment is responsible for laying down policies, 
standards and procedures for coordination of the National 
Employment Service at all India level. The Employment Exchanges 
function under the direct administrat ive and financial control of the 
respective State Government /UT Administration. 
 
  The occurrence and filling up of vacancies in Central 
Government, State Governments, PSUs, Public Sector Banks and 
other Government aided institutions is a continuous proce ss and 
efforts are made to fill up the vacancies as per the provisions of their 
respective recruitment rules. 
 
  Employees State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) accords 
approval for establishing an ESIC Hospital in consultation of 
respective State Governments as the operation and management of 
Hospital is done by the concerned State Government as per the 
provision of Section 58 of the erstwhile Employees State Insurance 
Act 1948 (now subsumed under Section 40 of the Code on Social 
Security, 2020). 
  
  At present no proposal to establish an Employees' State 
Insurance (ESI) hospital or a special medical facility centre for 
worker in the unorganised sector in Etah Lok Sabha constituency has 
been received from Government of Uttar Pradesh.

entries.t: Promotion Schemes for Independent and Regional Film Makers
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 640 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
PROMOTION SCHEMES FOR INDEPENDENT AND REGIONAL FILM MAKERS 
640. DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE: 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
a) whether the Government has taken note that many film makers producing quality and 
content-driven films face difficulties relating to financing, high production costs, limited 
access to modern studios, post-production facilities and inadequate international marketing 
support; 
b) if so, whether these challenges have affected India's ability to secure greater recognition and 
awards at major international film festivals; 
c) if so, the details of film production, post-production and film city infrastructure available in 
Maharashtra particularly in Mumbai, Nashik and Pune; 
d) whether the Government proposes to provide financial assistance, incentives, co-production 
facilities and dedicated promotion schemes for independent and regional film makers in 
Maharashtra; and 
e) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen Maharashtra's film ecosystem and enhance 
the global competitiveness of Indian films at international film festivals and markets? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(DR. L. MURUGAN) 
 
(a) to (e):  
Under the Development, Communication and Dissemination of Filmic Content (DCDFC) 
Scheme, the Government provides financial assistance for the production of regional films. 
These initiatives benefit filmmakers across the country, including those from Maharashtra, and 
contribute to strengthening India's film ecosystem and enhancing its global competitiveness. 
  

The Government has also undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the Indian film ecosystem 
and enhance the global outreach of Indian cinema. Through the National Film Development 
Corporation (NFDC), financial assistance is provided to such filmmakers. 
To facilitate international promotion and market access, the Government supports the 
participation of Indian filmmakers at major international film festivals and film markets. The 
Ministry also collaborates with industry bodies such as The Federation of Indian Chambers of 
Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) to promote 
Indian cinema and create opportunities for international partnerships. 
In addition, financial assistance is provided to Indian Missions abroad for organising activities 
aimed at promoting Indian cinema and facilitating engagement between Indian and 
international film industries. Such initiatives include the WAVES Bazaar, Work -in-Progress 
Labs, Viewing Rooms, film markets, and programmes for facilitating international co -
productions. These platforms provide project development support, networking opportunities, 
and international market access to Indian Filmmakers. 
Maharashtra continues to be one of the country's leading film production hubs, with world -
class infrastructure and facilities. Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari (Film City), Goregaon is 
located in Mumbai.  Institutes like the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, and 
Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), Mumbai support capacity building of the 
sector. Apart from these, a wide network of production and post-production facilities by private 
sector is also functioning across Mumbai, Pune and Nashik. 
To further examine the issues related to film sector, the Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting has recently constituted a High -Level Study Group. Based on the report of this 
Group, further policy interventions will be formulated.

entries.t: UMEED Portal for Registration of Waqf Properties
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 642 
ANSWERED ON 22/07/2026 
  
UMEED PORTAL FOR REGISTRATION OF WAQF PROPERTIES 
 
642. SMT. SAJDA AHMED 
 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:-  
   
(a) whether the registration of Waqf properties on the UMEED portal has been completed across 
the country; 
(b) if so, the details of total Waqf properties registered and those left out due to technical or other 
reasons, State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether legal ownership, protection and administrative rights of Waqf properties registered on 
the portal have been formally recognized; 
(d) if so, the details of legal framework or notifications issued in this regard; and 
 
(e) the steps taken to resolve pending/left -out registrations and ensure complete digitization and 
transparency of Waqf records? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU) 
 
(a) to (b): As per Section 3B(1) of the UMEED Act, 1995, every waqf registered under this Act, 
prior to the commencement of the Act, shall file the details of the waqf and the property dedicated 
to the waqf on the portal and database, within a period of six months, with a provision for further 
extension of up to six months by the Waqf Tribunal on sufficient cause being shown by the 
mutawalli. 
 
As on 1 7.07.2026, total 7,99,978 waqf properties have been initiated for uploading on 
the UMEED Central Portal–2025. Out of these, 6,17,102 waqf properties have been validated and 
approved by the approver , 91,623 number of waqf properties pending at various stages of 
uploading, while 91,253 properties have been rejected during verification. The number of waqf 
properties, state-wise available at various stages of Maker, Checker and Approver are available in 
public domain on the UMEED Central Portal- 2025, i.e., umeed.minorityaffairs.gov.in.   

 
(c) & (d): The UMEED Central Portal -2025 is a statutory portal developed in accordance with 
Section 3(ka) the UMEED Act, 1995, for uploading and managing entire lifecycle of waqf 
properties including registration, verification, survey by the Collector, mutation, annual account 
audit etc.   
 
(e)   As the statutory remedy available under the Act, further extensions were granted to the State/UT 
Waqf Boards by the concerned Hon’ble Waqf Tribunals/Courts  after expiry of initial six months . 
Ministry has facilitat ed by reopening the UMEED Central Portal -2025 for those State/UT Waqf 
Boards who have been granted further extension by the concerned Hon’ble Waqf Tribunals or Courts 
for the purpose of uploading details of existing waqf and properties dedicated to waqf. 
 
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 643 
(TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026) 
CONVERSION OF NARKATIAGANJ AKASHVANI KENDRA  
643. SHRI SUNIL KUMAR: 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has received any proposal to convert the Narkatiaganj Akashvani 
Kendra in West Champaran district of Bihar which is very small and has very low 
broadcasting capacity at present into a modern long range Akashvani Kendra; and 
(b)  if so, the details thereof along with the time by which it is likely to be approved? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(DR. L. MURUGAN) 
(a) and (b): Broadcasting Infrastructure and Network Development (BIND) scheme is a Central 
Sector Scheme for development, modernization and upgradation of broadcasting infrastructure of 
Doordarshan and Akashvani in the country. BIND scheme has been approved with a total outlay 
of ₹2539.61 crore for 2021-26. The scheme has been extended upto 31.03.2027. 

The scheme includes setting up and modernization of transmitters and studios of Akashvani, 
expansion of DD Free Dish DTH platform and DD TV channels. It also includes upgrading 
production & transmission facilities. 
A 10 KW FM relay station at Narkatiaganj was commissioned in 2021. A 100 meter tower has

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 648 
ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
  
WELFARE OF MINING AFFECTED COMMUNITIES 
 
648: SMT. PRATIMA MONDAL: 
 
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the manner in which the Government  is monitoring compliance with District 
Mineral Foundation (DMF) obligations to ensure that mining -affected communities 
receive the intended benefits in healthcare, education and local infrastructure; and 
(b) the details of the action taken by the Governme nt to curb illegal mining and 
improve real -time monitoring of mineral extraction, transportation and royalty 
collection across the country? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES  
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
  
(a)  As per the Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana (PMKKKY) 
Guidelines, 2024, the power to approve expenditure of DMF funds lies with the 
Governing Council of DMF headed by District Magistrate having elected 
representatives such as MPs, MLAs, and MLCs as members. Further, the Guidelines 
provide for the constitution of a State Level Monitoring Committee under the 
Chairpersonship of the Chief Secretary to monitor the performance of DMFs, 
compliance with transparency norms, audit requirements, and annual reporting 
obligations. 
  
Further, to strengthen accountability and transparency in the utilization of DMF 
funds, the Guidelines stipulate audit of DMF accounts by the Comptroller and Auditor 
General (CAG) as per the schedule decided by CAG. Additionally, the Ministry of 
Mines in December 2 025 directed all DMFs to conduct annual audits of DMF 
accounts through Chartered Accountants empaneled by CAG. 
  
(b)  Section 23C of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) 
(MMDR) Act, 1957 empowers the State Government to frame rules to preven t illegal 
mining and improve real time monitoring of mineral extraction, transportation and 
storage of minerals and for purposes connected therewith. Section 9 of the MMDR 

Act, 1957 mandates holder of mining lease to pay royalty for minerals as per rates 
notified in Schedule -II of the Act. Hence, these matters fall primarily under the 
purview of the State Government. However, the Central Government has taken 
various measures for curbing illegal mining across the country. Some of these steps 
are as under: 
 
(i) The MMDR Act, 1957 was amended through the MMDR (Amendment) Act, 2015, 
wherein Sections 30B and 30C read with Section 21 and 23C, inter -alia, provide 
stringent punitive provisions for illegal mining, transportation and storage. These are 
punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine 
which may extend to five lakh rupees per hectare of the area. Provisions have also 
been made for setting up of Special Courts for the purpose of providing speedy trial 
of offences relating to illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals.  
 
(ii) The Ministry of Mines has launched the Mining Surveillance System (MSS) 
through Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) in collaboration with Ministry of Electronics 
and Information Technology (Meit Y) and Bhaskaracharya Institute for Space 
Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG), Gandhinagar for detection of incidence of 
illegal mining by use of space technology and surveillance of area up to 500m 
outside the lease boundary to check incidences of illegal mining.

entries.t: Use of Domestic Coal in Thermal Power Plants
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COAL 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 649 
ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
USE OF DOMESTIC COAL IN THERMAL POWER PLANTS 
  
†649. SHRI KANWAR SINGH TANWAR: 
  
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to state: 
(a) the strategy formulated to increase the use of domestic coal in thermal power plants based 
on imported coal with a view to strengthen energy security, reduce import dependence and 
better utilisation of indigenous coal resources; 
(b) the policy measures adopted in coordination with the Ministry of Power, Ministry of 
Railways, Coal India Limited and other agencies to ensure timely supply of quality domestic 
coal, strengthen coal evacuation infrastructure and facilitate necessary technical modifications 
for increased use of domestic coal; 
(c) the progress made in increasing the share of domestic coal in thermal power plants based 
on imported coal and reducing thermal coal imports; 
(d) the measures taken by the Government to improve coal washing, quality management and 
logistics efficiency; and 
(e) the long term action plan prepared to achieve self-sufficiency in thermal coal while ensuring 
reliable, economical and sustainable power generation? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
(a): The Government has  taken various policy initiatives as under to increase use of 
domestically produced coal and to reduce coal import dependency: 
i. The Annual Contracted Quantity (ACQ) has been increased upto  100% of the 
normative requirement, in the cases where the ACQ was either reduced to 90% of 
normative requirement (non -coastal power plants) or where the ACQ was reduced to 
70% of normative requirement (coastal power plants). Increase in the ACQ would result 
in more domestic coal supplies, thereby, reducing the import dependency. 
ii. Vide amendment to the Non-Regulated Sector (NRS) linkage auction policy introduced 
in 2020, the tenure of coking coal linkages in the NRS linkage auction has been revised 
for a period upto 30 years. Increase in tenure of coking coal linkages in the NRS linkage 
auction for a period upto 30 years shall have a positive impact towards coal imports 
substitution. 
iii. Government has decided in 2022 that coal to meet the full Power Purchase Agreement 
(PPA) requirement of all the existing linkage holders of Power Sector shall be made 

available by the coal companies irrespective of the trigger level and ACQ levels. This 
decision of the Government of meeting the full PPA requirement of the linkage holders 
of the Power Sector shall reduce dependence on imports. 
iv. A new sub -sector ‘Steel using Coking coal through WDO route’ has been created in 
March, 2024 under the NRS linkage auctions which will lead to increase in the domestic 
coking coal consumption and also increase availability of washed coking coal in the 
country, thereby, reducing coking coal imports. 
v. Coking Coal Mission has been launched to enhance coking coal supply to the Steel 
Sector to reduce imports of coking coal. Initiatives have been taken to enhance coking 
coal production.  
vi. Imported Coal Based (ICB) Plants have been allowed to secure coal under the Revised 
SHAKTI Policy, 2025. The coal availability for ICB Plants under this Policy shall 
reduce dependence of these ICB plants on imported coal. 
vii. Existing Fuel Supply Agreement (FSA) holders have been allowed to secure coal under 
the Revised SHAKTI Policy, 2025 after procuring 100% of the ACQ coal under 
existing FSA. Coal availability beyond the ACQ to existing FSA holders will benefit 
the power producers to meet the full requirement of the power plants. 
viii. Coal linkages under the recently created CoalSETU window under the Non-Regulated 
Sector linkage auctions shall increase the availability of washed coal in the country and 
consequently lead to reduction in coal imports.  
(b): The Ministry of Coal launched a Coal Logistics Plan in coordination with concerned 
Ministries and stakeholders to assess and address issues in the coal logistics chain, including 
constraints related to availability of railway rakes and transportation. The plan covers the entire 
coal supply chain from mines to end -use plants and identifies measures to improve coal 
evacuation efficiency. Various key measures strengthen coal evacuation infrastructure 
undertaken by the Government are as under:- 
i. 33 critical railway infrastructure projects have been identified to address gaps in rail 
connectivity and strength coal evacuation from the coal bearing States by FY 2030.  
ii. To enhance the rail evacuation with the objective of increasing the share of rail transport 
in coal movement to around 75% by FY 2030. 
iii. 139 first -mile connectivity (FMCs) projects having 1319 MTY (million tons per 
annum) capacity are planned to set up by FY 2029-30.  
iv. Development of alternative evacuation modes, including Rail-Sea-Rail (RSR) logistics, 
to optimize long-distance coal transportation.

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE

Single-Window Clearance Mechanisms 
 
65. SHRI ANIL YESHWANT DESAI: 
SHRI ARVIND GANPAT SAWANT: 
 
Will the MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased
 to state:  
 
(a) the details of railway, mining, dam/irrigation and new/existing National Highway projects pending 
for environmental clearance during the last five years along with the project-wise cost and expected 
timelines for completion of the said projects; 
(b) the reasons for delays in granting clearance and the average time taken for clearance in each sector; 
(c) the impact of such delay on project execution and economic growth; 
(d) the steps being taken by the  Government to expedite the clearance process, including any 
proposed policy reforms or single-window clearance mechanisms; and 
(e) whether any sector-specific measures have been introduced to ensure timely approvals while 
maintaining environmental sustainability, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
 
(a) to (e): The Government of India has issued Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) 
Notification, 2006 under the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section (2) of 
section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per the provisions laid down in the EIA 
Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, the proposals specified in its Schedule are 
appraised by the Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) at Central Level and State Expert Appraisal 
Committee (SEAC) at the State/UT Level, considering all the environmental implications associated 
with the project, including issues raised during the Public Consultation. Based on the 
recommendations of the EAC/SEAC, the proposals are considered by the Ministry or the State 
Environmental Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) respectively for approval for grant of 
Environmental Clearance (EC) or otherwise. As per the provisions stated above, ECs are granted after 
due consideration of environmental issues and incorporation of appropriate environmental 
safeguards, including mitigation measures prescribed in the Environmental Management Plan (EMP). 
 
As per the extant provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, 
Environmental Clearance is required for project activities falling under the 38 categories specified in 
its Schedule. Railway projects are not covered under the provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006, as 
amended. The details of proposals related to mining, dam/irrigation and new/existing National 

Highway are available on the PARIVESH portal. For the FY 2025-26, the average time taken for 
grant of Environmental Clearance to various projects of various sectors was 57 days against statutory 
timelines of 105 days prescribed in the EIA Notification, 2006. 
 
To expedite the process of granting Environmental Clearances, the Ministry has, in the recent past, 
undertaken many systemic reforms both through the technological intervention by upgrading the 
PARIVESH portal (a Single Window Portal providing end-to-end online solution), amendments in 
the EIA Notification 2006 and Clarifications/Guidelines issued through different Office 
Memorandums (OMs).  These reforms include increasing the validity of Terms of Reference 
(ToR)/Environmental Clearnce (EC), allowing flexibility in baseline data collection before ToR 
approval, and reforms in the Public Hearing process. Further, the process for granting Environmental 
Clearance to Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) has been rationalised. PSPs that do not require Forest 
Clearance or Wildlife Clearance, do not involve the creation of new reservoirs, and do not result in 
any increase in the submergence area or storage capacity of the existing reservoir are now treated as 
Category B2 projects. The Ministry has also amended Item 6 of Appendix IX of the EIA Notification, 
2006 stipulating environmental safeguards in order to exempt prior EC for the extraction of ordinary 
earth in respect of linear projects.  
 
Further, to facilitate the expeditious appraisal of mining projects, out-of-turn appraisal has been 
introduced for critical, strategic, and atomic mineral mining projects through the PARIVESH portal. 
Public Hearing requirements have also been exempted for specified critical, strategic, and atomic 
mineral mining projects, and these projects will be appraised at the Central level irrespective of the 
lease area involved in the proposals. In addition, Standard Terms of Reference and out-of-turn 
appraisal have been introduced for underground coal mining projects.  
 
The aforementioned reforms, especially paperless governance in clearance management through 
PARIVESH portal ( https://parivesh.nic.in ),  have ensured that development proceeds with robust 
environ

(i) PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM (PMJVK) 
 
Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram" (PMJVK), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, is 
one of the flagship program of the Ministry of Minority Affairs for creation of community 
infrastructure in the Minority Concentration Areas of the country in the sectors viz. He alth, 
Skill Development, Education, Women Centric Projects, Drinking Water and Supply, 
Sanitation, Sports, Renewable energy and Other Community Infrastructure.  
 

PMJVK is a demand driven scheme and State/UT-wise allocation of funds is not made 
under the Scheme. Projects are considered and approved on the basis of proposal received from 
respective State Governments/ UT Administrations. The projects are drafted/ form ulated by 
the respective State Governments/ UT Administrations. No such project proposal has been 
received from the UT of Lakshadweep under PMJVK. 
 
 
(ii)  PRADHAN MANTRI VIRASAT KA SAMVARDHAN (PM VIKAS) 
 
The Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) is a flagship Scheme of the 
Ministry which converges five erstwhile schemes viz. ‘Seekho Aur Kamao’, ‘Nai Manzil’, ‘Nai 
Roshni’, ‘Hamari Dharohar’ and ‘USTTAD’; and focuses on socio -economic empowerment 
of six notified minorities through skill development; entrepreneurship and leadership of 
minority women; and education support for school dropouts across the country, including 
Lakshadweep. 
 
Under the scheme, projects are allocated to eligible Project Implementing Agencies 
(PIAs) at the national level and are not allocated on a State/UT -wise basis. Consequently, 
State/UT-wise details of funds sanctioned and utilized under PM VIKAS are not main tained. 
Further, no PIA is presently imparting training under PM VIKAS in the Union Territory of 
Lakshadweep. 
 
At present, no proposal has been received under PM VIKAS Scheme for Lakshadweep. 
 
 
(iii)  SCHOLARSHIP 
The Ministry has implemented the following three Scholarship schemes alongwith the 
Maulana Azad National Fellowship Scheme for the educational empowerment of the six 
centrally notified minority communities viz. Buddhist, Christian, Jain, Muslim, Parsi and Sikh: 
i) Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme; 
ii) Post Matric Scholarship Scheme; and 
iii) Merit-cum-Means based Scholarship Scheme. 
Number of beneficiaries and funds released under scholarship schemes in Lakshadweep 
since 2023, is Nil, However, fund released under Maulana Azad National Fellowship (MANF)

(iv)   JIYO PARSI 
Release of financial assistance under Jiyo Parsi is a unique Central Sector Scheme 
launched in 2013 -14 with the objective to reverse the declining trend of Parsi population by 
adopting a scientific protocol and structured interventions, stabilize their population and 
increase the population of Parsis in India. 
 

Release of financial assistance under Jiyo Parsi Scheme is demand -driven and is 
available to eligible members of the Parsi community across the country. Currently there are 
no beneficiaries of the scheme in Union Territory of Lakshadweep. Thus, no funds have been 
allocated, released or utilised under the Scheme for the Union Territory of Lakshadweep during 
the last three years and the current year.

Occurrence and filling up of vacancies are continuous processes on Indian 
Railways considering its size, spatial distribution and criticality of 
operation. Adequate and suitable manpower is provided to cater to the 
regular operations, changes in technology, mechanisations and innovative 
practices. The vacancies are filled up primarily by placement of indents by 
Railways with Recruitment agencies as per operational and technological 
requirements. 
 
The RRB examinations are quite technical in nature entailing large scale 
mobilization of men and resources and training of manpower. Railway 
overcame all these challenges and successfully conducted the recruitment 
in a transparent manner following all laid down guidelines. No instance of 
paper leakage or similar malpractice has occurred during the entire 
process.

system of publishing the Annual Calendar from 2024 for recruitment to 
various categories of Group ‘C’ posts. The introduction of the Annual 
Calendar is benefitting the aspirants in the following manner:  
 More opportunities for candidates;  
 Opportunities to those becoming eligible every year;  
 Certainty of exams;  
 Faster Recruitment process, Training and Appointments

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
REDEVELOPMENT OF RAILWAY STATION AT TIRUVALLUR AND 
GUMMIDIPOONDI UNDER ABSS 
 
656. SHRI SASIKANTH SENTHIL: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to augment frequency 
and capacity on the Chennai–Tiruvallur–Arakkonam suburban section;  
(b) the status of station redevelopment at Tiruvallur and Gummidipoondi 
under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme (ABSS);  
(c) whether new sub-urban lines, halt stations or foot-over-bridges in 
Tiruvallur district are under consideration and if so, the details thereof; 
and  
(d) whether the level crossings in Tiruvallur district approved for 
conversion to Road Over-Bridges and if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d) Presently, there are 4 existing lines in Chennai – Tiruvallur – 
Arakkonam section. Further, to improve the connectivity and capacity of 
Rail network in Chennai Suburban Area, Final Location Survey for 5th and 6th 
line Chennai – Tiruvallur – Arakkonam (68 km) has been sanctioned. 
 
Sanctioning of projects requires consultation with various stakeholders 
including State Governments and necessary approvals viz. appraisal of NITI 
Aayog, Ministry of Finance etc. As sanctioning of projects is a continuous 
and dynamic process. 
 

Page 2 of 15 
Station Redevelopment 
 
Tiruvallur and Gummidipundi stations, located in Tamil Nadu, have been 
identified for development under Amrit Bharat Station Scheme. 
Development works at this station have been taken up at a good pace.   
 
At Tiruvallur station, the works for extension and improvement of existing 
station building, booking office, parking, improvement of platform surface 
of platform no. 1 & 6, platform shelter and the structural works of new 
concourse and entrance porch have been completed. The works of 12m 
wide foot over bridge, lifts, improvement of circulating area and signages 
have been taken up. 
 
At Gummidipundi station, the works of improvement of parking, second 
entry booking office, improvement of platform surface of platforms 1 & 2 
and 3 & 4 and installation of lifts have been completed. The works of new 
station building, improvement of pedestrian plaza, drainage and approach 
road at first entry, integrated Passenger Information System and 12 m wide 
foot over bridge have been taken up. 
 
Further, development / redevelopment / upgradation / modernisation of 
stations on Indian Railways is a continuous and ongoing process and works 
in this regard are undertaken as per requirement, subject to inter-se 
priority and availability of funds. Development / redevelopment / 
upgradation / modernisation of a station is carried out based on category 
of station/condition/traffic handled etc. 
 
Ministry of Railways has launched Amrit Bharat Station Scheme for 
redevelopment of stations with a long-term approach. 
 

Page 3 of 15 
The scheme involves preparation of master plans and their implementation 
in phases to improve the stations of Indian Railways. The master planning, 
keeping in view the necessity of each station, includes: 
 
 Improvement of access to station and circulating areas 
 Integration of station with both sides of city 
 Improvement of station building 
 Improvement of waiting halls, toilets, sitting arrangement, water 
booths  
 Provision of wider foot over bridge/subway to commensurate with 
passenger traffic 
 Provision of lifts/escalators/ramps 
 Improvement of platform surface/ provision of platform shelter 
 Provision of kiosks for local products through schemes like ‘One 
Station One Product’ 
 Parking development 
 Amenities for Divyangjans 
 Better passenger information systems 
 Provision of air concourse, executive lounges, Multimodal integration, 
landscaping, etc. 
 
The scheme also envisages sustainable and environment friendly solutions 
etc. as per necessity, phasing and feasibility and creation of city centre at 
the station in the long term. 
 
So far, 1340 stations have been identified for development under Amrit 
Bharat Station Scheme, out of which 77 stations, including Tiruvallur and 
Gummidipundi stations, are located in Tamil Nadu. The names of stations

entries.t: Misuse of Mobile Applications to Remotely Disable e-Rickshaws
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 657 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 22.07.2026 
  
MISUSE OF MOBILE APPLICATIONS TO REMOTELY DISABLE E-RICKSHAWS 
  
†657. SHRI CHANDAN CHAUHAN: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the instances of misuse of mobile applications 
associated with battery management systems to remotely disable e -rickshaws and other electric 
vehicles and extort money from drivers particularly economically  weaker e-rickshaw drivers, on 
the pretext of restoring the vehicles to operational condition; 
(b) if so, whether the Government, in coordination with the State Governments, proposes to identify 
the individuals and entities responsible for such incidents, initiate penal action against them and 
provide appropriate relief to the affected drivers; 
(c) if so, whether the Government proposes to implement mandatory cyber security and 
authentication standards for mobile applications and battery management systems associated with 
electric vehicles; and 
(d) the details of other measures being taken by the Government to prevent the recurrence of such 
incidents and to ensure consumer protection in view of the increasing use of electric vehicles in the 
country? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
  
(a) to (d):  Government has taken cognizance of reports regarding the misuse of certain Battery 
Management System (BMS) mobile applications that enabled unauthorised remote control of e -
rickshaw batteries. On 3rd July 2026, Government issued orders for removal of such applications on 
app stores. 
 
Further, Government has institutionalised a nationwide integrated and coordinated framework to 
strengthen cybersecurity and digital resilience across digital ecosystems, which, inter alia, includes: 
i. National Cyber Security Coordinator (NCSC) under the National Security Council Secretariat 
(NSCS) to ensure coordination related to cyber security amongst different agencies. 
ii. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT -In) is designated as the national 
agency for responding to cyber security incidents under the provisions of section 70B of the 
Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. 
iii. National Cyber Coordination Centre (NCCC), implemented by CERT -In, examines the 
cyberspace to detect cyber security threats. It shares the information with concerned 
organizations, state governments and stakeholder agencies for taking action. 
iv. The Government has established National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre 
(NCIIPC) for protection of critical information infrastructure in the country under the 
provisions of section 70A of the IT Act, 2000. 
v. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, administered by the Department of Consumer Affairs, 
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, was enacted to modernize the 

framework governing consumer protection in the era of globalization, technologies, e -
commerce markets, etc. 
vi. ‘Information Security Education and Awareness (ISEA)’ project is implemented by MeitY for 
strengthening human resources in the area of Information Security and creating general 
awareness. Awareness material on various aspects of cyber hygiene & cyber secur ity is 
disseminated through portals such as www.staysafeonline.in,www.infosecawareness.in and 
www.csk.gov.in.

RAJPURA - MOHALI RAILWAY PROJECT 
 
659. SHRI GURMEET SINGH MEET HAYER: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the current status, financial outlay and completion 
timeline of the approved Rajpura-Mohali railway line project;  
(b) the details of the section-wise maximum permissible speed limit from 
Bathinda to Chandigarh via new track and plans to upgrade the tracks 
to increase train speeds on this route;  
(c) whether trains coming from the Malwa region require an engine reversal 
at Rajpura Junction to reach Mohali and if so, the details thereof;  
(d) whether the feasibility of a crossing with the Ambala-Sirhind via grade-
separated crossing track was studied and if so, the details thereof;  
(e) whether new trains are planned from Delhi to Chandigarh via this new 
route with a stop at Mohali and if so, the details thereof; and  
(f) whether any new stations, logistics hubs or dry ports are planned along 
this new track to boost local trade and if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (f) : Rajpura – Mohali new line project (18 Km) has been sanctioned 
recently at a cost of Rs. 443 crore. This project will directly connect 
Southern Punjab (Bathinda area), between Sirhind – Gobindgarh and 
Rajpura area to Chandigarh avoiding Ambala. Land acquisition has been 
taken up. The project has been declared as special Railway Project. Total 
73 Ha of land is required for the project. Preliminary notification for land 

Page 2 of 11 
acquisition has been issued. An outlay of Rs. 100 crore has been allocated 
for this project in FY 2026-27. 
 
This new Railway line connecting Rajpura to Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar 
(Mohali) is set to transform regional connectivity by seamlessly linking 
major hubs like Rajpura Junction, Sarai Banjara and Sahibzada Ajit Singh 
Nagar (Mohali). This project addresses a long-standing demand of the 
people of Punjab’s Malwa region for shorter and more direct rail 
connectivity to the state capital. This project will provide a boost to local 
economy. 
 
The speed potential of Bathinda - Rajpura route has been upgraded to 110 
kmph.  
 
Further, strengthening, upgradation, modernisation and improvement of 
track infrastructure is a continuous and ongoing process over Indian 
Railways. The following measures are being taken by Indian Railways to 
upgrade railway tracks:  
 
i. Modern track structure consisting of 60kg, 90 Ultimate Tensile 
Strength (UTS) rails, Wider and heavier Pre-stressed Concrete Sleepers 
(PSC) with elastic fastening, fan-shaped layout turnout on PSC 
sleepers and H-beam Sleepers on girder bridges are being used while 
carrying out primary track renewals.  
ii. The Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossings are being used 
in turnout renewal works.  
iii. Supply of 260m long rail panels have been increased to avoid welding 
of joints, thereby improving safety and riding quality  
iv. Thick Web Switch Expansion Joints are being used in place of earlier 
Conventional/Improved SEJs. 
v. Adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e. Flash Butt Welding.  

Page 3 of 11 
vi. Adoption of mechanized system for track maintenance using high 
output plain tampers and points & crossing tampers for improved 
maintainability & reliability of track.   
vii. Deployment of state-of-the-art modern machines including Rail 
Grinding Machines to further improve asset reliability. 
viii. Mechanisation of track laying activities through use of track machines 
like PQRS, TRT , T-28 etc. 
ix. Interlocking of Level Crossing (LC) Gates for enhancing safety at LC 
gates. 
x. Use of advanced Phased Array technology of testing of rail and welds. 
xi. Deployment of Integrated Track Monitoring Systems (ITMS) and 
Oscillation Monitoring System (OMS) for comprehensive health 
assessment to ascertain optimal maintenance requirements. 
xii. Adoption of portable Track Measuring Trolley for continuous recording 
of track parameters in yards. 
xiii. Using web enabled Track Management System (TMS) for integration 
and data analytics of the track inspection records received through 
various sources to enable precise maintenance inputs. 
 
As a result of above measures, there has been significant increase in 
speed potential of the tracks. The details of speed potential of railway

SKILL INDIA MISSION 
 
66. SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  the major achievements of the Skill India Mission during the last twelve years and the 
current year including the number of youth trained, certified and employed under various skill 
development programmes, State/UT-wise; 
 
(b)  the details of the progress made in vocational education, apprenticeships, 
entrepreneurship development and digital skilling under the said Mission; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the impact of Skill India 
initiatives on employability, job creation and industry readiness of the workforce, and if so, the 
details thereof; 
 
(d) the details of beneficiaries and skill development infrastructure created in Madhya 
Pradesh, particularly in Satna district; and 
 
(e)  the steps taken/being taken by the Government to align skill development programmes 
with emerging sectors such as Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, green jobs, advanced 
manufacturing to achieve the objectives of Viksit Bharat 2047? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) & (b)  Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re -skill and up -skill training through 
an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country. The SIM aims at enabling 
the youth of India to get future -ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills. State-wise details 
of the candidates trained/enrolled under various schemes of MSDE are at Annexure-I. 
 
Amongst the schemes of MSDE, placements were tracked under the Short -Term Training 
component of PMKVY only in the first three versions (PMKVY1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0) 
implemented from 2015-16 to 2021-22. State-wise details of candidates placed under first three 
versions of PMKVY (1.0 to 3.0) are at Annexure-II. Out of 56.89 lakh candidates that have been 
certified under Short -Term Training, 24.3 lakh candidates have been reported placed with a 
placement rate at 42.8%. Under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to 
choose their varied career pa th with orientation through industry relevant skill courses that 
include the On-the-Job Training (OJT). 
 

Apart from vocational training and apprenticeship, National Institute for Entrepreneurship and 
Small Business Development (NIESBUD) and the Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) 
under the aegis of MSDE conduct Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme (EAP ) and 
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) nationwide to foster an entrepreneurial 
mindset focus on training, credit access, and market access. PM Vishwakarma  scheme, 
launched in September 2023, provides holistic support (upskilling, toolkits, and collateral -free 
credit) to artisans in 18 traditional trades. MSDE launched Swavalambini programme in February 
2025 in the North Eastern States of Assam, Meghalaya, M izoram and in Uttar Pradesh and 
Telangana to cultivate entrepreneurial mindsets among female candidates. Thus far, total of 
1200 female candidates have been trained under EAP and 602 candidates have been trained 
under EDP. 
 
Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) is the unified digital public infrastructure platform that facilitates 
course discovery, enrolment, and certification. MSDE has introduced job roles in emerging 
sectors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, Drone Te chnology, Mechatronics, and 
Internet of Things under schemes like PMKVY and CTS.   DGT has signed MoUs  with global 
tech leaders including IBM, Microsoft, Autodesk, AWS, Shell, etc. to facilitate the provision of 
technical and professional skills training in modern technologies. The Skilling for AI Readiness 
(SOAR) programme offers structured foundational a nd applied AI skill development for both 
students and educators.

(b): Minimum Support Price (MSP) payments for procured foodgrains are made to farmers for
the quantity procured, thereby facilitating the sale of their produce at the notified MSP.
(c): To ensure timely payment of MSP of foodgrains to farmers, including small and marginal
farmers, extensive awareness campaigns are conducted prior to the commencement of the
procurement season to disseminate information regarding the MSP procurement process,
registration procedure and payment. Further, payment of MSP of foodgrain is made through Direct
Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the farmers' registered bank accounts within 48 hours of the procurement
of their produce, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines,
(d) & (e): No specific independent audit is being conducted to confirm the compliance of MSP
in Rajasthan.

MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
DEPARTMENT OF FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 662
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22ND JULY, 2026
SMART GRAIN ATMS
662. SHRI HARENDRA SINGH MALIK:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a): whether the Government is making any special budgetary provision for installation of smart
Grain ATMs at fair price Shops under One Nation One Ration Card Scheme for migrant workers
in the Muzzaffarnagar Lok Sabha Constituency;
(b): whether there is any time-bound plan to achieve zero storage losses offoodgrains by
adopting modern silo technology in the warehouse of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and the
State Warehousing Corporation in Muzaffarnagar;
(c): whether the Government proposes to provide pulses and edible oils at subsidised rates, in
addition to fortified rice to Below Poverty Line (BPL) ration card holder in IVluzaffarnagar through
the Public Distribution system;
(d): whether any new guidelines have been issued to further strengthen the Mobile Ration Van
Service in remote villages oflV[uzaffarnagar for the effective implementation of the Pradhan-
Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PM-GKAY); and
(e): if so, the details thereoF
ANSWER
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
(SHRIMATI NIMUBEN JAYANTIBHAI BAMBHANIYA)
(a) & (b): The Grain ATM, branded as Annapurti, is a design, conceptualized and developed
by World Food Programme (WFP) India. This automated grain dispensing machine aims to
provide an enhanced experience to beneficiaries by offering 24/7 access to food grains with speed,
precision and transparency using the existing biometric authentication system. It also aims to
enhance access of migrant National Food Security Act / One Nation One Ration Card beneficiaries
to their TPDS (Targeted Public Distribution System) entitlements and to ensure exact weighment.
The role of the Government of India is limited upto facilitation of willing States and the
United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) in the said initiative by acting as coordinator. The
Government of India has not made any budgetary provision for installation of smart Grain ATMs
at fair price shops (FPS) under One Nation One Ration Card Scheme for migrant workers in the
country.


Silo storage is mechanized and automated, which aids in curtailing losses. Further Silos are
being constructed on Public Private Partnership (PPP) basis and Concessionaire is liable for any
abnormal loss. Maximum loss to the extent of 0.05% of intake quantity only is permissible in
storage of wheat in Silos in case the storage period is more than 1 (one) year.
At present, no Steel Silo project is planned in the IViuzaffarnagar Lok Sabha Constituency
by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) or the State Warehousing Corporation (SWC).
(c): The Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) is now governed as per the provisions of
the National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFS A). Under the Act, the term “foodgrains'’ is defined as
rice, wheat or coarse grains or any combination thereof conforming to such quality norms as may
be determined, by order, by the Central Government from time to time.
At present, no proposal for inclusion of more commodities like pulses and edible oils under
the scheme is under consideration of the Government.
(d) & (e): Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) under National Food Security Act
(NFSA), 2013 is operated under the joint responsibility of the Central and the State/Union Territory
(UT) Governments. The operational responsibilities for allocation of foodgrains within the States/
UTs, identification of eligible beneficiaries, issuance of ration cards to them, distribution of
foodgrains to eligible beneficiaries under TPDS, issuance of license to Fair Price Shop dealers,
supervision over and monitoring of functioning of FPSs etc. rest with the concerned State/UT
Governments.
The State Government of Uttar Pradesh has reported that Fair Price Shop (FPS) is
operational at each Gram Panchyat level to ensure the convenient distribution of foodgrains to
beneficiaries and foodgrains are being distributed through ePoS machines integrated with electronic
wejghing machines

ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
  
LANDSLIDE EARLY WARNING SYSTEM 
  
664.   SMT. PRIYANKA GANDHI VADRA: 
  
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government proposes to implement a pan -India Landslide Early 
Warning System (LEWS) in land -slide vulnerable regions and if so, the details 
thereof;  
(b) whether prototype of the regional LEWS for the country being developed by 
Geological Survey of India (GSI) has proven effective in timely prediction of landslides 
and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the details of experimental landslide forecast bulletins issued by GSI during the 
last two years and its accuracy, district-wise;  
(d) whether the Government has evaluated the gap s in existing Landslide Early 
Warning Systems and if so, the details thereof along with the action taken to address 
the same;  
(e) whether the Government proposes to establish a Landslide Early Warning System 
in Wayanad Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the details thereof; and  
(f) whether the Government has taken initiatives to involve local communities & NGOs 
in data collection for landslide/landslip prediction and evaluated the increased efficacy 
of such systems wherever in use and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL AND MINES 
(SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY) 
  
(a) and (b):  Geological Survey of India (GSI) has developed a prototype model and 
has implemented Regional Landslide Forecasting System (RLFS) based on empirical 
rainfall thresholds, for the landslide-prone States in a phased manner since 2020. GSI 
has extended the RLFS coverage to 28 districts (4 operational stage and 24 
experimental stage) in 10 landslide prone States viz. Assam, Himachal Pradesh, 
Karnataka, Kerala, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu and West 
Bengal. 
  
GSI’s landslide forecast model is mainly based on rainfall thresholds derived from past 
rainfall and landslide occurrence data, in conjunction with the rainfall forecast model 

data r eceived from different national agencies. This model forecasts the landslide 
probability of the area with four forecast levels viz. Low, Moderate, High and Very High 
with 24hrs and 48hrs lead time and has demonstrated fairly high reliability, with 
forecast showing strong correlation with ground realities during critical weather events. 
The landslide forecast accuracy evaluation shows the critical success index (CSI) 
more than 70% across the forecasting zones of operational districts viz. Darjeeling, 
Kalimpong, the Nilgiris and Rudraprayag. 
  
(c) & (d): GSI has provided operational/experimental landslide forecast bulletins to 16 
districts since the 2024 monsoon, and also extended the same to a total of 21 districts 
in eight landslide -prone States during the 2025 monsoon. The district -wise varied 
accuracy parameters, that is, the Critical Success Index (CSI) is given at Annexure-I. 
GSI has taken measures to address  a few constraints in the RLFS which warranted 
further improvement in accuracy, granularity, and  robustness with additional site -
specific high-resolution inputs. 
  
(e): GSI initiated ground work for the regional landslide forecasting for rainfall induced 
landslides in Kerala since 2021 and started sharing the experimental landslide forecast 
bulletin for Wayanad district, from 25/06/2024 with the respective State Disaster 
Management Authority (SDMA) and District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) 
for ground testing, feedback and validation during the monsoon period. The 
experimental forecast bulletin s have been issued for 204 and 241 days during 
monsoon of 2024 and 2025 respectively. 
  
(f): GSI engages with local communities in landslide -prone areas. The Community -
based volunteers and Gram Panchayat representatives are involved through 
coordination with SDMA/DDMA.  At district and sub-divisional levels, GSI partners with 
DDMA, involving Tehsil and Block -level officials to cascade knowledge to grassroot 
communities. In 2025 -26, landslide awareness programmes and use of the 
Bhooskhalan mobile app, develo ped by GSI for crowd -sourcing landslide data and 
visualizing forecast bulletins, were carried out in various landslide prone districts.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
GAP IN CONSUMPTION CAPACITY BETWEEN STATES 
 
666.   SHRI T R BAALU:  
  
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME 
IMPLEMENTATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has carried out studies on Consumer 
Prices recently and if so, the details thereof along with the findings; 
(b) the details of average Monthly Per Capita Consumption 
Expenditure during the last three years, according to official surveys; 
(c) whether it is a fact that there is big difference in Consumption 
Expenditure and purchasing power amongst States and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the deta ils of the actions being taken by Union Government 
including policy interventions to reduce the gap in Consumption 
capacity between States?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF 
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION; MINISTER OF 
STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CULTURE (RAO INDERJIT 
SINGH) 
(a): No specific study on consumer prices has been undertaken by the 
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) recently. 
However, MoSPI has strengthened the Consumer Price Index (CPI) 
compilation framework through a comprehensive base revision from 
2012 to 2024, using the latest Household Consumption Expenditure 

Survey (HCES) 2023–24. CPI is a measure of movement of  prices in the 
items consumed by the Households.  
(b) & (c) : MoSPI conducts survey on Household Consumption 
Expenditure at regular intervals wherein information on consumption of 
food and non -food items by the household are collected. The latest 
surveys on  Household Consumption Expenditure (HCES) were 
conducted during August , 2022 – July, 2023 and Augus t, 2023 – July, 
2024. Prior to this, the survey on the said subject was conducted in NSS 
68th round d uring July, 2011 - June, 2012. Information on Average 
Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE) for each State/UT 
across rural and urban sectors from the last two surveys of HCES 
conducted during 2022 -23 & 2023 -24 is given at  Annexure. MoSPI, 
however, has not conducted any study/survey on the difference in 
Consumption Expenditure and purchasing power amongst States. 
(d): The Government has undertaken various policy measures to 
enhance household consumption, strengthen purchasing power and 
promote inclusive economic growth across States. It has sustained 
public investment in infrastructure and continued support for 
employment generation and skill development. Access to affordable 
credit has been expanded through schemes such as PM MUDRA Yojana 
and PM SVANidhi.  
Financial inclusion has been strengthened through the Pradhan Mantri 
Jan Dhan Yojana with over 95 per cent of house holds having access to 
a bank account. The Government has also promoted digital financial 
services through the continued zero Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) 
regime for UPI transactions. Direct Benefit Transfer, enabled through 
the JAM (Jan Dhan -Aadhaar-Mobile) trinity, has ensured the efficient 
and transparent transfer of welfare benefits directly into beneficiaries' 
bank accounts. In addition, income tax relief measures, GST rate 
rationalisation, reduction in customs duties on selected inputs and 
intermediate goods, and targeted welfare interventions have supported 
disposable incomes and domestic demand.

†667. SHRI BHUMARE SANDIPANRAO ASARAM: 
          SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the status of Vande Bharat Express and high-speed train 
projects across the country and the proposed routes and timelines for 
the expansion of these services particularly in Maharashtra and 
Madhya Pradesh;  
(b) whether the Government proposes to introduce Vande Bharat Express 
or other high-speed trains connecting major cities of Maharashtra and 
Madhya Pradesh;  
(c) if so, the proposed routes and the time by which the said routes are 
likely to be operational; and

train services for rural and economically backward communities in

(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d) As the railway network straddles across State boundaries, trains 
are introduced across such boundaries as per network requirement. 
However, with a view to improve travel experience of the passengers, 
Indian Railways have introduced indigenously designed and manufactured 
Vande Bharat (Sleeper & Chair Car) with modern coaches, advanced safety 
features and passenger amenities.  
 

Page 2 of 13 
Vande Bharat services (Chair Car) 
Presently, 81 Pairs of Vande Bharat Express Chair Car services are 
operational on the Indian Railways network which have the following 
features: 
 Jerk Free Semi-Permanent couplers. 
 Fitted with KAVACH. 
 Centrally controlled Automatic Plug Doors and Fully Sealed wider 
gangways. 
 Emergency Alarm Push buttons and Talk Back Units on all 
Coaches. 
 Improved fire safety - Aerosol based fire detection and suppression 
system in electrical cabinets and lavatories. 
 Higher acceleration with design/operating speed of 180/160 KMPH. 
 Driver-Guard communication with voice recording facility & Crash 
hardened memory. 
 Air conditioning units provided with indigenously developed UV-C 
lamp based disinfection system for deactivating 99% harmful 
bacteria from conditioned air to improve the hygiene standards 
inside the passenger area. 
 Better Ride Comfort. 
 CCTVs in all Coaches. 
 For Divyangjan passengers special lavatory in the driving coaches 
on each end. 
 Coach condition monitoring System (CCMS) display with remote 
monitoring

MOBILE TOWERS IN PVTG VILLAGES IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
 
668. DR. C M RAMESH: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether it is true that the Ministry of Communications, Department of Telecom has 
sanctioned mobile towers in 1010 habitations in (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group) PVTG tribal 
villages in Andhra Pradesh under PM JANMAN with an estimated cost of Rs. 95 crores; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of habitations covered in Anakapalli district of Andhra Pradesh where there 
are more than 8,500 PVTG tribal population; and 
 
(c)  the details of the status of implementation of the above project? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
(a) to (c) As on 30.06.2026, 3,231 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) 
villages/habitations have got 4G mobile coverage, out of 4,543 PVTG villages/ habitations identified 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) prog ram. These 
villages/ habitations were covered under 4G mobile projects funded by Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), 
and no specific fund was allocated for providing mobile coverage to PVTG habitations/ villages.  In 
the State of Andhra Pradesh, of the identified villages/ habitations, 1,409 PVTG habitations/ villages 
have got 4G mobile coverage, of which 9 are in Anakapalli District.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 669 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 22.07.2026 
  
PAX SILICA ALLIANCE 
  
669. SHRI E T MOHAMMED BASHEER: 
  
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has prepared a roadmap to leverage the Pax Silica alliance for 
attracting investment, securing advanced technology and strengthening domestic semi -conductor 
manufacturing and Artificial Intelligence infrastructure; 
(b) if so, the details of measures proposed to address India’ s limited capacity for extraction, 
processing and refining of critical minerals required for semi-conductor and AI supply chains; and  
(c) whether the Government has assessed the potential impact of stricter security audits, export 
restrictions and supply -chain compliance requirements on Indian companies particularly Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises seeking to participate in global tec hnology value chains and if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
                                                                                                                 
(a)  to (c):  India joined the Pax Silica Alliance on February 20, 2026, on the sidelines of the India 
AI Impact Summit, reaffirming its commitment to strengthening trusted, resilient and diversified 
global semiconductor value chains.  
Government is leveraging the Alliance as a strategic platform to deepen partnerships with partner 
countries for facilitating access to advanced technologies, and promoting collaboration in 
semiconductors, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, researc h, innovation and talent 
development.  
 
Government also participated in the 3 rd Pax Silica Summit held in Washington DC, on 25 –26 June 
2026, with aforesaid vision.  
 
Government has approved the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) in 2025 with a proposed 
expenditure of Rs.16,300 crore and an expected investment of Rs.18,000 crore by Public Sector 
Undertakings (PSUs) and other stakeholders to secure a long -term sustainable supply of critical 
minerals and strengthen India’s critical mineral value chains encompassing all stages from mineral 
exploration and mining to beneficiation, processing, and recovery from end-of-life products.  
 
The Government has successfully auctioned 56 critical mineral blocks and 11 Exploration Licence 
blocks, which include 6 blocks of critical minerals to secure critical mineral supply chain.    
 
Government has taken cognizance of the evolving global regulatory landscape, including stricter 
security audits, export control measures and supply -chain compliance requirements, and their 
potential implications for Indian companies. These issues have been  consistently raised through 
bilateral and multilateral forums, including the Pax Silica Summit, the India –EU Trade and 
Technology Council (TTC), and other strategic dialogues, with a view to promote transparent, trusted 
and conducive ecosystems.  
 

Government has also been implementing measures to strengthen the competitiveness of domestic 
enterprises through the India Semiconductor Mission, the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme, 
the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), the IndiaAI Mission, and capacity -
building initiatives to enable Indian companies, including MSMEs, to meet global quality and 
enhance their participation in global technology value chains.

67. SHRI B Y RAGHAVENDRA:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the salient features of the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar 
Yojana (PM -VBRY) and the progress made in its implementation 
since its launch;  
(b)the details of the establishments regist ered and first -time 
employees enrolled under the said Scheme in the country, 
State/UT-wise and district-wise in Karnataka;  
(c)the total financial assistance sanctioned and disbursed to eligible 
first-time employees and establishments in the country, State /UT-
wise especially Shivamogga district in Karnataka;  
(d)the number of establishments and beneficiaries covered in the 
manufacturing sector along with the facilitation and awareness 
measures undertaken through the Employees' Provident Fund 
Organisation (E PFO) to encourage sustained additional 
employment; and  
(e)the steps taken by the Government to promote formalisation of 
employment and improve employability and the measures proposed 
to accelerate registration and coverage under the Scheme, 
particularly in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The Union Cabinet, on 1 July 2025, approved the 
Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled the Pradhan 
Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote 
employment generation, enhance employability, and strengthen 
social security across all sec tors including MSMEs and rural 
enterprises, with a particular focus on the manufacturing sector.  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  The scheme aims to incentivise creation of more than 3.5 
Crore jobs all across the country, over a period of 2 years including 
the state of Karnataka.  
  The scheme comprises of two parts i.e. Part A and Part B 
and focuses on providing support to both employees and employers 
by way of incentives. The scheme provides for incentives for 1.92 
crore eligible First time employees under Part A. I ncentive for 
creation of approximately 2.59 crore additional jobs to employers is 
provided for under Part B of the scheme. The Employees’ Provident 
Fund Organisation (EPFO) is the implementing agency for the 
scheme. 
  The state-wise details of the registra tions and incentive 
disbursed since the start of implementation till June, 2026 under the 
scheme in the country including the state of Karnataka, are provided 
at Annexure-I. 
  The district -wise details of the incentive disbursement 
under Part A and Part B of the scheme, since the start of 
implementation till June, 2026, for the State of Karnataka, are 
provided at Annexure-II. 
  The scheme and its provisions have been widely 
disseminated through extensive outreach efforts across the country. 
EPFO has underta ken awareness and stakeholder outreach 
programmes, including monthly Nidhi Aapke Nikat (NAN) 
programmes, SMS/email and digital communication campaigns etc. 
to facilitate timely registration and seamless transfer of benefits.  
  A dedicated portal (pmvbry.e pfindia.gov.in) has been 
developed to facilitate all scheme-related processes and for real-time 
monitoring. Detailed Scheme Guidelines, Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs), and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) have 
been made available on this portal for ease of understanding.

(a) to (d):  The policies of Government of India are aimed at ensuring open, safe, trusted and 
accountable cyberspace for users in the country. The Government is cognizant of the risks and 
harms arising from the misuse of digital technologies including Cyb er Frauds. The Barathiya 
Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, The Information 
Technology Act, 2000, The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital 
Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 and other related laws together  established a framework to 
address cyber frauds. 
 
The Information Technology Act, 2000 (“IT Act”): 
•    Section 66C prescribes an imprisonment of up -to three years and fine which may 
extend to rupees one lakh for identity theft; 
•    Section 66D prescribes an imprisonment of up -to three years and fine which may 
extend to rupees one lakh for cheating by personation by using computer resource; 
•     Section 66 prescribes a punishment of upto three years or with fine which may 
extend to five lakh rupees or with both for computer related offences; 
•       Section 43 prescribes penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer 
system etc. 
The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) 
Rules, 2021: 
•      The IT Rules cast specific obligations on intermediaries to make reasonable efforts 
to ensure that users of their computer resources do not host, display, upload, modify, 
publish, transmit, store, update or share any information that deceives or mis leads, 
impersonates another person or that violates any law for the time being in force. 

•        Intermediaries are required to remove any unlawful content within three hours of 
the receipt of an order of a court of competent jurisdiction or on receipt of a reasoned 
intimation by the Appropriate Government or its authorized agency. 
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 
•   The BNS, 2023 addresses the offences involving Organized Crime (Section 111), 
Cheating by Personation (Section 319), Forgery (Section 336 / 337), etc., and other 
cyber-enabled frauds. 
  
To monitor and to strengthen the mechanism to deal with cybercrimes in a comprehensive and 
coordinated manner, the Central Government has taken steps which, inter -alia, include the 
following: 
•      The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime Coordination 
Centre’ (“I4C”) as an attached office to deal with all types of cybercrimes in the 
country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner. 
•    The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (“NCRP”) has been launched, as a 
part of the I4C, to enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of 
cybercrimes, with special focus on cybercrimes against women and children. The 
portal is accessible at https://cybercrime.gov.in. Cybercrime incidents reported on 
this portal, their conversion into FIRs and subsequent action thereon are handled by 
the State/UT Law Enforcement Agencies concerned as per the provisions of the 
law. 
•      The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ 
(CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting 
of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. A toll -free 
Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online 
cyber complaints. 
•      A State of the Art, Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre (CFMC) has been established 
at I4C where representatives of major banks, Financial Intermediaries, Payment 
Aggregators, Telecom Service Providers, IT Intermediaries and representatives of 
States/UTs Law Enforcement Agency are working together for immediate action 
and seamless cooperation to tackle cybercrime. 
•    Samanvaya Platform has been made operational to serve as an  Management 
Information System (MIS) platform, data repository and a coordination platform 
for LEAs for cybercrime data sharing and analytics. It provides analytics -based 
interstate linkages of crimes and criminals, involved in cybercrime complaints in 
various States/UTs. The module ‘Pratibimb’ maps locations of criminals and crime

ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
PM-KUSUM IN ODISHA 
676. SMT. APARAJITA SARANGI:  
 
WILL THE MINISTER OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY BE PLEASED TO 
STATE: 
(a) whether the target set under the Pradhan Mantri-Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan 
Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) to install 34,800 MW of solar capacity with the financial support 
of Rs. 34,422 crore by March 2026 has been achieved; 
(b) if so, the details of the solar capacity sanctioned, installed and commissioned under each 
component of the PM-KUSUM as on 31 March, 2026, State and component-wise; 
(c) whether there exists an implementation gap of 8,562 MW under Component A between 
the sanctioned capacity and the capacity installed/commissioned and if so, the details thereof; 
and 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the reasons for Odisha being India's leading producer 
of essential minerals for solar value chain and having ports which facilitate imports of raw 
materials and exports of modules, Odisha has only two approved Production Linked Incentive 
(PLI) Scheme manufacturing units in the Solar PV sector under the PLI and has not yet emerged 
as an high energy solar PV manufacturing and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK) 
(a) & (b) The Government has launched PM-KUSUM scheme in March 2019, which has been 
scaled-up in January 2024 and aims to add capacity of 34.8 GW. As reported by state 
implementing agencies (SIAs), a total of 13.11 GW of solar capacity has been installed u nder 
the scheme till 31.03.2026. 
The implementation timeline is extended till March 2027 for those projects where Power 
Purchase Agreement (PPA) has been signed by 31.12.2025. 
The State/UT-wise and Component wise details of progress under PM -KUSUM scheme till 
30.06.2026 is placed at Annexure I. 
 
(c) PM-KUSUM is a demand driven scheme. As per the demand raised by the state, the 
Ministry has allocated total of 10,000 MW under Component A of the scheme. As reported by 
SIAs, total of 9,871 MW of PPAs has been signed till cut off date, i.e. 31.12.2025 and 1,726.92 
MW has been installed till 30.06.2026. 
 
(d) The manufacturers who have been issued letters of award under Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) Scheme for High Efficiency Solar PV Modules, can set-up their manufacturing 
plants anywhere in India, including Odisha. The location of manufacturing facilities is decided 
by the manufacturers based on their commercial and business considerations. Various factors 
may be taken into consideration by them, including availability of land, industrial 
infrastructure, reliable and cost -competitive power supply, log istics, availability of skilled 
workforce, proximity to suppliers and markets, and overall ease of doing business.

PMJVK SCHEME IN TAMIL NADU 
 
 
677. SHRI SACHITHANANTHAM R 
   
 Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) the details of the amount of fund allocated to the States during the last five years under the 
Pradhan Mantri Jan VIkas Karyakaram (PMJVK), State-wise particularly in Tamil Nadu; and  
 
(b) the details of the amount allocated and works done during the last five years for Dindigul 
district of Tamil Nadu under the PMJVK scheme?   
 
 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU) 
 
(a) & (b):  The Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) is a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of the Ministry of Minority Affairs aimed at creating community infrastructure in 
identified Minority Concentration Areas across the Country. The Scheme supports projects in 
sectors such as health, education, skill development, women-centric initiatives, drinking water 
and sanitation, sports, renewable energy, tourism, animal husbandry, and other community 
infrastructure. 
PMJVK is a demand -driven scheme, and no State -wise allocation of funds is made 
under the Scheme. Funds are released against eligible projects approved under the Scheme. 
The State-wise details of funds released during the last five years, including for the State of 
Tamil Nadu, are provided at Annexure-I. 
No project has been sanctioned in Dindigul district of Tamil Nadu under PMJVK during 
the last five years. Accordingly, no funds have been allocated or released, and no works have 
been undertaken in the district under the Scheme during this period.
