entries.t: Effect of Severe Heat Wave Conditions
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 678 
TO BE ANSWERED ON WEDNESDAY, 22ND JULY, 2026 
 
EFFECT OF SEVERE HEAT WAVE CONDITIONS 
 
678.  ADV GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI:    
Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the unusually severe heatwave conditions 
witnessed across several parts of the country during the year 2026 with temperatures 
crossing 45°C in many regions and reports indicating that heatwaves are arriving earlier 
and lasting longer due to climate change and possible El Niño conditions; 
(b) the details of heatwave-related deaths, water shortages and power demand recorded during 
the current year, State/UT-wise particularly in Maharashtra including tribal districts like 
Nandurbar; 
(c) whether the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and other agencies have 
issued revised heat action guidelines for protection of outdoor workers, children, elderly 
citizens and economically weaker sections and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the details of the funds allocated for climate adaptation, urban cooling and heat mitigation 
measures, State/UT-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR 
MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY 
AND EARTH SCIENCES 
(DR. JITENDRA SINGH) 
 
(a)-(b) No. The data indicate that unusually severe heatwave conditions were not witnessed across 
several parts of the country during the year 2026 relative to historical extremes. The India 
Meteorological Department (IMD) continuously monitors heatwave conditions across the 
country through its extensive observational network and issues routine forecasts and 
warnings. During the hot weather season of 2026, certain regions, particularly Vidarbha in 
Maharashtra, southern Uttar Pradesh, and northern Madhya Pradesh, recorded air 
temperatures exceeding 45°C. Climatological data confirms that these regions historically 
experience similar temperatures during the peak heatwave months of April and May. 
 
(c)-(d) The IMD, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, supports nationwide heat-resilient 
planning by generating and issuing daily special heatwave warning bulletins and localized 
Impact-Based Forecasts (IBF) at the meteorological sub-division and district levels. These 
forecasts contain risk-based advisories designed to safeguard vulnerable groups. These 
operational alerts are transmitted in real-time to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the National 
Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), State Disaster Management Authorities 
(SDMAs), District Magistrates, health departments, and public utility sectors. To enable 
institutional preparedness well in advance, the IMD regularly issues monthly and seasonal 
heatwave outlooks. The department provides foundational climate information, real-time 
weather observations, and risk analytics that empower the NDMA and state agencies to 
implement localized Heat Action Plans (HAPs) across various States. Most of these public-
centric heatwave information products and risk-mapping tools are deployed on an open-
access, web-GIS platform accessible to the general public at the designated URL 
(https://dss.imd.gov.in/dwr_img/GIS/heatwave.html).        
 
******

DEPARTMENT OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS

DIGITAL BHARAT NIDHI 
 
679. DR. MALLU RAVI: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed the utilisation of the Digital Bharat Nidhi for 
supporting State-led broadband infrastructure projects to achieve universal digital connectivity and 
if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  whether proposals have been received from State Governments seeking financial assistance 
from the Digital Bharat Nidhi and if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has received a proposal from the Government of Telangana for 
financial support to the T-Fiber project and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to evolve a transparent framework for extending Digital 
Bharat Nidhi assistance to State broadband networks in order to accelerate rural connectivity and 
digital inclusion; and 
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
(a)  BharatNet project has been approved for provision of broadband connectivity in a phased 
manner to all Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the country. The Government has reviewed the BharatNet 
project and approved the Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) to upgrade and co nnect all the GPs 
across the country.  
 
(b) to (e) The Government of India has communicated in-principle approval to the Government 
of Telangana for implementation of ABP. The Government of Telangana has informed that a new 
special purpose vehicle (SPV), namely, Telangana Rural Internet Infrastructure Corporation Limited 
(TRIICL) has been formed for implementation of ABP. Under ABP, the Government of India has 
provisioned ₹3,189 crore to upgrade and connect 12,769 GPs in Telangana state. Further, a 
transparent framework has been provisioned through which the assets created under the BharatNet 
Project are available to the service providers on non-discriminatory basis to provide services such as 
Fiber-to-the-Home (FTTH), leased lines, dark fiber etc. for accelerating rural connectivity and digital 
inclusion.

entries.t: Expansion of Higher Education Ecosystem under NEP, 2020
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 68 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Expansion of Higher Education Ecosystem under NEP, 2020 
 
68. Thiru Dr. S Jagathratchakan: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the progress made in expansion of the higher education ecosystem in the country in line 
with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 particularly with regard to 
higher enrolment, improved access and enhanced educational opportunities, with specific 
reference to the State of Tamil Nadu; 
 
(b) the details of the key findings emerging from the current distribution of universities and  
colleges, including regional disparities, infrastruc ture deficiencies and gaps in access to 
higher education facilities across different parts of the country; 
 
(c) the developments observed in efforts to improve availability of higher education 
institutions and strengthen educational infrastructure in underserved regions; and 
 
(d) the course of action proposed by the Government for ensuring balanced expansion and  
equitable access to higher education institutions across all regions of the country? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d) : Education is in Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of the Higher 
Education Institutions are in the domain of the respective States. The Centre and States 
together endeavor to uplift the educational status of the  students of the country, especially in 
the under-served areas and the disadvantaged communities.   
 
As per All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE), enrolment in higher education 
has increased to 4.5 crore in 2023 -24 from 3.42 crore in 2014 -15 (an increase of 31.5%) . 
Overall GER has reached to 30 in 2023-24 from 23.7 in 2014-15. 
 
In the State of Tamil  Nadu, enrolment has increased to 35.77 lakh in 2023-24 from 
33.53 lakh in 2014-15. Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) has increased to 52.3 in 2023 -24 from 
44.6 in 2014-15. 

 
To cater to needs of educationally unserved/ underserved areas , the Ministry of 
Education has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -
USHA) scheme, which  envisages improvement in access, equity and excellence in State 
Higher Education system through support under various components viz., Multi- Disciplinary 
Education and Research Universities (MERU), Grants to Strengthen Universities (Accredited 
& Unaccred ited Universities), Grants to Strengthen Colleges (Accredited & Unaccredited 
Colleges), New Model Degree Colleges and Gender Inclusion and Equity Initiatives . The 
government has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in 
June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA) with an 
outlay of Rs. 12926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phase of 
RUSA, for the period 2023 -24 to 2025 -26, to cater to the needs of educationally unserv ed/ 
underserved areas. Under the scheme, 613 units have been approved with a total amount of 
Rs.8,168.51 crore. 
 
Union Cabinet in its meeting held in May, 2025 has approved expansion of academic 
and infrastructure capacity including creation of Research Park of five new IITs which had 
been established in the State/UT of Andhra Pradesh (IIT Tirupati), Kerala (IIT Pala kkad), 
Chhattisgarh (IIT Bhilai), Jammu & Kashmir (IIT Jammu) and Karnataka (IIT Dharwad) 
with a total outlay of Rs. 11,828.79 crore. The government has also approved a total of Rs. 
1,942 Crore for expansion of academic & hostel infrastructure, and develop ment of Research 
Park for IIT Jodhpur, IIT Patna and IIT Indore through Higher Education Financing Agency 
(HEFA). 
 
As per AISHE, the total number of registered Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) 
has increased to 64,756 in 2023-24 from 51,534 in 2014-15. 
 
Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU), also strive towards enhancing 
access and equity to higher education through distance mode. It pays special attention to 
disadvantaged sections of the society and regions by establishing study centres in th e 
backward areas and districts.  
 
Union Budget 2026 -27 has announced setting up of 5 University Townships in the 
vicinity of major industrial and logistic corridors and 1 girls’ hostel in every district through 
Viability Gap Funding /capital support to enc ourage enrolment of girls in STEM institutes/ 
courses. 
 
  Setting up of higher education institutions is an ongoing process. Depending on the 
need, educational institutions are opened from time to time. The Central Higher Education 
Institutions/Universities are envisaged as pace setting institutions to provide academic 
leadership to other institutions in the region.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 680 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
OBSCENE CONTENT ON OTT PLATFORMS 
680 SHRI RAJABHAU PARAG PRAKASH WAJE: 
 
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state; 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the increasing availability of 
obscene, vulgar, sexually explicit and culturally insen sitive content on OTT 
platforms, social media channels and digital entertainment platforms, as well as use 
of abusive and derogatory language in certain stand-up comedy programmes;  
(b) if so, whether the Government has received complaints from citizens, p arents, 
educational institutions and social organizations regarding the adverse impact of 
such content on children, youth and Indian cultural values;  
(c) the details of action taken by the Government during the last three years against 
OTT platforms, digi tal content creators and online programmes found violating 
existing laws, guidelines or codes of ethics; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to introduce stricter regulations, stronger content 
monitoring mechanisms, age -verification systems and penal p rovisions to curb the 
spread of objectionable content and protect societal and cultural values and if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
  

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(DR. L. MURUGAN) 
 
(a) to (d):  
Government has  notified the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and 
Digital Media, Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 on 25.02.2021 under IT Act, 2000 to put in 
place an institutional mechanism for publishers of news &  current affairs on digital 
media and publishers of online curated content (OTT Platforms). 
Part-III of the rules provides for a Code of Ethics for digital news publishers and 
publishers of online curated content (OTT platforms).  Complaints are addressed u nder 
the provisions of the IT Rules, 2021. 
Section 79(3)(b) of IT Act, 2000 provides for notification to the intermediaries for 
removing/disabling access to unlawful content.  
Based on complaints, the Government regularly takes actio n against such 
intermediaries and OTT platforms. The Government has disabled 50 OTT platforms for 
public access in India in last two years for displaying obscene content  and for violation 
of Section 67 and 67A of the IT Act, Section 294 of the BNS, and Section 4 of the 
Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986.

CONSTRUCTION OF ROB/RUB AT LEVEL CROSSING NO. 285 
 
†682. SHRI BRIJENDRA SINGH OLA: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any study on the traffic jams 
occuring at railway level crossings in Rajasthan particularly in the 
Jhunjhunu Lok Sabha Constituency;  
(b) if so, the railway level crossing identified by the Government in the said 
constituency where there is a need to construct ROB/RUB;  
(c) the time by which the ROB/RUB are likely to be constructed at railway 
level crossing number 285 located in Bhamarwasi village of Jhunjhunu 
district; and  
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (d): As on 01.04.2026, Indian Railways has 15,689 Nos. manned Level 
Crossings (MLCs) on Broad Gauge (BG). Of these, 764 Nos. MLCs are 
situated in the State of Rajasthan, including 16 Nos. MLCs falling within the 
Jhunjhunu Lok Sabha Constituency. 
Sanctioning of works of Road over Bridge (ROB)/Road under Bridge 
(RUB) in lieu of Level crossings (LCs) is a continuous and dynamic process 
of Indian Railway. Such works are prioritised and taken up on the basis of 
their impact on safety in train operations, mobility of trains & impact for 
road users and feasibility etc. 

Page 2 of 2 
No. of ROBs/ RUBs constructed on Indian Railways during the period 
2004-14 viz-a-viz 2014-26 (Upto May’26) is as under: 
 
 
 
 
  
 As on 01.06.2026, 4,993 Nos. ROBs/ RUBs works are sanctioned at a 
cost of approx.₹ 1,17,492 Cr on Indian Railways including 618 Nos. ROBs/ 
RUBs works at a cost of approx. ₹ 6,137 Cr in the state of Rajasthan and 17  
Nos. ROBs/ RUBs works at a cost of approx. ₹ 114 Cr in Jhunjhunu Lok 
Sabha Constituency which are at various stages of planning and execution. 
 LC No. 285 at km 321/3-4 on Sikar-Loharu section was closed during 
gauge conversion in the year 2015 by constructing RUBs on either side 
considering the population centre of the village and to facilitate public 
movement. (RUB No. 176A on Loharu side & RUB No 176B on Sikar side) 
 Completion & commissioning of ROB/RUB works depends on various 
factors like cooperation of  State Governments in giving  consent for 
closure of LC,  fixing of approach alignment, approval of General 
Arrangement Drawing (GAD), land acquisition, removal of encroachment, 
shifting of infringing utilities, statutory clearances from various 
authorities,  law and order situation in the area of project / work sites,  
duration of working season in a year for the particular project / area  due to 
climatic conditions etc.  All these factors affect the completion time of the 
projects / works.

3. Interlocking of Level Crossing (LC) Gates has been provided at 10,395 
Level Crossing Gates up to 30.06.2026 for enhancing safety at LC 
Gates. 
4. Complete Track Circuiting of stations to enhance safety by verification 
of track occupancy by electrical means has been provided at 6,671 
stations up to 30.06.2026.

foggy weather.

affected areas which enables loco pilots to know the distance of the 
approaching landmarks like signals, level crossing gates, etc.

Strength (UTS) rails, Prestressed Concrete Sleeper (PSC) Normal/Wide 
base sleepers with elastic fastening, fan shaped layout turnout on PSC 
sleepers, Steel Channel/H-beam Sleepers on girder bridges is used 
while carrying out primary track renewals. 
11. Mechanisation of track laying activity through use of track machines 
like PQRS, TRT , T-28 etc. to reduce human errors. 
12. Maximizing supply of 130m/260m long rail panels for increasing 
progress of rail renewal and avoiding welding of joints, thereby 
improving safety. 
13. Ultrasonic Flaw Detection (USFD) testing of rails to detect flaws and 
timely removal of defective rails. 
14. Laying of longer rails, minimizing the use of Alumino Thermic Welding 
and adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e., Flash Butt 
Welding. 
15. Monitoring of track geometry by OMS (Oscillation Monitoring System) 
and TRC (Track Recording Cars). 
16. Patrolling of railway tracks to look out for weld/rail fractures. 
17. The use of Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossing in turnout 
renewal   works. 
18. Inspections at regular intervals are carried out to monitor and educate 
staff for observance of safe practices.

entries.t: Modernisation of Railway Bridges in Gujarat
entries.head:
§  Page 1 of 2 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 684 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.07.2026 
 
MODERNISATION OF RAILWAY BRIDGES IN GUJARAT 
 
†684. SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has launched any new scheme for the 
modernisation of railway bridges in the country;  
(b) if so, the details thereof; and  
(c) the amount of funds allocated for the said scheme in the Gujarat?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RAILWAYS, INFORMATION & BROADCASTING AND 
ELECTRONICS & INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
(a) to (c) Safety of Bridges across the country is accorded high priority by 
Indian Railways (IR). There is an established system of inspection of 
railway bridges on Indian Railways. All the railway bridges are inspected 
twice a year, one before the onset of monsoon and one detailed inspection 
after the monsoon. Annual Inspection of all the bridges is conducted to 
ascertain the physical condition of the bridge and repairs/ 
rehabilitation/regirdering/rebuilding measures are taken up wherever 
required. In addition, certain railway bridges are also inspected more 
frequently depending upon their condition. Comprehensive Technical 
inspection of important & major bridges is done in a way that 20% of such 
bridges are inspected annually. 
 
 Repair/strengthening/rehabilitation/rebuilding of railway bridges is a 
continuous process and is undertaken whenever so warranted by their 
physical condition as ascertained during these inspections.  During 2014-

Page 2 of 2 
2026 (upto June’ 2026), 18835 nos of railway bridges were 
repaired/rehabilitated/strengthened/rebuild in Indian Railway.  
 
 IR has developed the Bridge Management System (BMS) which is a 
comprehensive digital repository and decision-support tool developed for 
effective management of the entire bridge inventory of Indian Railways. It 
maintains extensive data related to maintenance history, inspection 
records etc. of each bridge. 
 
 For inspection and maintenance, IR is also using new technology like 
automatic water level monitoring integrated with BMS, Scour monitoring 
system, under water inspection through the use of Remote Operated 
Vehicle and 3D river bed scanning.  
 
 Railway projects are sanctioned/executed Zonal Railway wise and not 
State-wise as Railway projects may span across State boundaries.  Gujarat 
state is covered under North Western Railway & Western Railway. During 
2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27(up to June’26) about Rs. 7,216.11 crores 
have been allocated on repair/rehabilitation/strengthening/ rebuilding in 
Indian Railway which includes Rs. 896.21 crores for railway bridges in 
North Western Railway & Western Railway.

UTILISATION OF BUDGET 
 
685. SHRI AZAD KIRTI JHA: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the reasons for the low utilization of budget allocations during FY 2024-25, with only 6% of 
funds allocated to the BSNL/MTNL Revival Plan, 23% for Bharat Net and 8% for the Connectivity 
for Indian Railways (CIOR) scheme spent; 
 
(b) the details of project deadlines and measurable output milestones introduced following 
repeated Standing Committee observations regarding underutilization; and 
 
(c)  whether the Department has operationalised any risk -based or performance -linked budget 
monitoring mechanism since the said observations and if so, the details of these mechanisms? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. PEMMASANI CHANDRA SEKHAR) 
 
 
(a) In FY 2024 -25, the utilization of funds against Revised Estimates (RE) was  99.87% in 
BSNL/MTNL Revival Plan, 61.46% in Bharat Net and 72.06% in Prevention of Spoofed Incoming 
International Calls System (CIOR).  
 
The reasons  for 61.46% utilization of funds in FY 2024 -25  in respect of Bharat Net is due 
to delay in finalization of bids for implementation of Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) by BSNL, 
which is Project Management Agency for ABP. 
 
(b)  BharatNet programm e has been approved for provision for broadband connectivity in a 
phased manner to all Gram Panchayats (GPs) in the country. Further, the Government has approved 
the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) to upgrade the existing network created under Phases I 
and II of BharatNet and to create incremental network for connectivity to the remaining GPs, and to 
the remaining non-GP villages on an on -demand basis with minimum demand for five home fibre 
internet connections, operation and maintenance for 10 years and provision of 1.5 crore home fibre 
internet connections.  During June 2026, BharatNet Point of Presence (PoPs) at 80,472 GPs are 
operational. 
 
(c) The Department is utilising online digital platforms, viz., Public Financial Management 
System (PFMS) and eLekh a for monitoring expenditure and fund utilisation. The physical and 
financial progress in respect of Projects/Schemes is regularly monitored at highest level to ensure 
optimal  utilization of funds.

69.  Shri Pushpendra Saroj:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION  be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the current student -to-computer ratio in Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar  
Navodaya Vidyalayas in the country, classified State/UT -wise and district -
wise for Uttar Pradesh;  
(b)  the number of schools w here computer laboratories are either non -
functional or operating  below prescribed digital infrastructure norms under 
Central guidelines, State/UT -wise and district -wise for Uttar Pradesh;  
(c)  the total Central funds sanctioned, released and utilised duri ng the last five 
years for ICT  infrastructure and computer laboratory upgrades in these 
schools, State/UT -wise particularly for  Uttar Pradesh;  
(d)  the findings of any monitoring or audit conducted by the Ministry regarding 
gaps in digital  access affecting  computer-based learning and examinations; 
and 
(e)  the time -bound plan adopted by the Central Government to reduce the digital 
infrastructure  deficit in centrally administered schools in Uttar Pradesh?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
 
(a)  As per information received from Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS ) and 
Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), t he current student -to-computer ratio at the 
national level is 15:1 in Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) and 10.8:1 in Navodaya 
Vidyalayas (NVs). The State/UT -wise student -to-computer ratio in KVs and NVs is 
at Annexure -I, while the district -wise student -to-computer ratio for the State of 
Uttar Pradesh in respect of KVs and NVs is at Annexure-II & III, respectively . 

 
 
(b) The details of KVs , State/UT-wise and district -wise in the State of Uttar 
Pradesh that are operating below the prescribed digital infrastructure norms are at 
Annexure-IV and Annexure-V, respectively. 
The State/UT-wise details of NVs that are operating below the prescribed 
digital infrastructure norms are at Annexure -VI. There are 09 NVs in the districts of 
Uttar Pradesh namely Agra, Azamgarh, Banda, Jhansi, JP Nagar, Jaunpur, 
Faizabad, Deoria, Etawah and Hapur  of that are operating below the prescribed 
digital infrastructure norms .  
(c) As per information received from KVS , ICT infrastructure is developed 
through the Vidyalaya Vikas Nidhi (VVN) in KVs. Additionally, funds from Central 
Government have also been sanctioned under the PM SHRI Scheme  for KVs  for 
ICT infrastructure/computer laboratories. The State/UT -wise details (including the 
State of  Uttar Pradesh ) of Central funds sanctioned  / utilized in last five years , in 
respect of KVs and NVs are at Annexure -VII. 
(d) & (e) Setting up of ICT / digital infrastructure in KVs and NVs is a continuous 
process which depends upon various factors such as opening of new schools, 
addition of higher classes, availability of funds, availability of Internet connectivity 
etc. ICT infrastructure is monitored by KVS and NVS on a regular basis through 
periodic reviews and reports received from their Regional Offices, and the 
respective schools. The identified gaps, wherever reported, are addressed, subject 
to availability of resources and operational requirement s. KVS and NVS are 
continuously strengthening ICT infrastructure through the provision of computer 
laboratories, computers and furniture in computer labs, smart classrooms, internet 
connectivity, and other digital resources. ICT infrastructure in newly ope ned KVs 
and NVs is also being established. This also includes the schools located in the 
State of Uttar Pradesh.

(a) & (b)   Dynamic Groundwater Resources of the country incl uding Balasore district of Odisha, are 
assessed jointly by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) and the State Governments. The assessment 
provides updated estimates of annual groundwater re charge, extractable groundwater resources, groundwa ter 
extraction and stage of groundwater extraction alon g with categorization of assessment units as Safe, Semi-
Critical, Critical and Over-Exploited. 
As per the Dynamic Groundwater Resources Assessment , 2025, the total Annual Groundwater 
Recharge of Balasore district has been assessed as 143080 Hectare Metres (HAM), the Annual Extractable  
Groundwater Resource as 132164 HAM and the Annual Groundwater Extraction for all uses as 78812 HAM. 
Accordingly, the Stage of Groundwater Extraction ha s been assessed as 59.63 per cent. Out of the total  12 
assessment units (Blocks) in the district, 11 asses sment units have been categorized as 'Safe' and one  
assessment unit as 'Semi-Critical'. Groundwater Res ource Assessment was conducted in 2017 and 2020, an d 
annually from 2022 onwards. No assessment was carri ed out in 2015, 2016, 2018, and 2019. The details a re 
given in the Annexure.

is primarily the responsibility of the State Governments. However, the Central Government supplements the 
efforts of the State Governments by providing technical and financial assistance through its various schemes 
and programmes. The major steps taken in this direction including those relating to Balasore district are as 
under: 
i. Groundwater conservation and augmentation efforts a re being undertaken through the flagship Jal 
Shakti Abhiyan (JSA), an annual mission-mode campai gn for water conservation and artificial 
recharge. More than 2 crore water conservation and artificial recharge works have been taken up 
across the country through convergence including 12,027 works in Balasore district. 
ii. To further strengthen these efforts, the Hon'ble Pr ime Minister launched the Jal Sanchay Jan 
Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative in 2024 to make rainwat er harvesting a mass movement through 
community participation. More than 1.55 crore artif icial groundwater recharge and water storage 
works have been created across the country includin g 19,221 works in Balasore district under the 
initiative. Subsequently, the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagi dari–Catch the Rain (JSJB-CTR) campaign was 
launched nationwide on 1 st  June, 2026 to further promote water conservation and artificial recharge. 
iii. Mission Amrit Sarovar was launched by the Governmen t of India with the objective of developing 
and rejuvenating at least 75 water bodies in each district of the country. As an outcome, nearly 69,000 
Amrit Sarovars have been constructed/rejuvenated ac ross the country including 80 water bodies in 
Balasore district, contributing to enhance water st orage and groundwater recharge.VB-G RAM G 
(Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin) (earlier MGNREGS) works 
related to water conservation and water harvesting including large scale desiltation projects for wate r

exploited and Critical rural blocks.

Mapping and Management Programme (NAQUIM 1.0) cover ing about 3,806 sq. km of Balasore 
district. Aquifer maps and groundwater management p lans have been prepared and shared with the 
Government of Odisha for scientific planning and sustainable groundwater management.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

†696. SHRI AMRA RAM: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the construction of new high-capacity 
power transmission lines and towers are causing damage to farmers' agricultural 
land, crops and irrigation systems and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) th e number of farmers affected by these projects and the details of the 
compensation provided to them during the last five years, State-wise;  
 
(c) whether there is a wide disparity in the rates and procedure of providing 
compensation to farmers affected by such power transmission lines in various 
States;  
 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;  
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to formulate a uniform and fair 
compensation policy nationwide, and provide appropriate annual or one -time 
compensation to farmers for  land-use restrictions under towers and power line 
corridors; and  
 
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) to (f):  (i)  During the construction of transmission lines and towers, 
temporary damage on agricultural land, standing crops and, in some cases, 
irrigation facilities may occur depending upon the terrain, route alignment and 
site conditions. However, Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) make efforts to 
minimise such impacts through optimisation of transmission line alignment, 
adoption of suitable tower designs, and use of appropriate construction 
methodologies. 
 
……….2. 

 
 
- 2 - 
 
(ii)  The Right of Way (RoW) for transmission lines is acquired in accordance 
with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003. Compensation towards damage 
to crops, trees, other losses during construction, and for diminution in land value 
under the RoW corridor, is provided to landowners in accordanc e with the 
applicable policies of the respective State Governments. In this regard, Ministry 
of Power, Government of India issued guidelines dated 14.06.2024 regarding 
payment of compensation for ROW for transmission lines. Supplementary 
guidelines were is sued on 21.03.2025, which were further amended on 
15.12.2025. State Governments may adopt these guidelines in their entirety or 
issue their own modified guidelines. In the absence of State Government 
guidelines, these guidelines issued by the Central Gover nment shall apply for 
determining compensation.  
 
(iii) The transmission projects/ schemes are implemented across the country 
by various agencies including Public Sector Undertakings, State Transmission 
Utilities and Private Transmission Service Providers (TSP).  State-wise details of 
the number of farmers affected or the details of compensation provided to them 
under transmission projects, is not maintained by this Ministry.

(a) the progress made so far in the implementation of the Viability Gap Funding 
(VGF) Scheme for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), includ ing the energy 
storage capacity approved and commissioned thereunder;  
 
(b) the policy, financial and technical measures taken by the Government to 
promote standalone and co -located Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) 
projects for strengthening the integration of renewable energy;  
 
(c) the manner in which Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) have been 
envisaged to meet peak power demand, ensure grid reliability and stability and 
facilitate the effective integration of renewable energy;  
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to provide any additional policy, financial 
or incentive support to promote rapid expansion of energy storage technologies, 
domestic manufacturing, attract investment and encourage their wider adoption 
across the States and if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(e) whether any Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects have been

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) Ministry of Power is administering two Viability Gap Funding (VGF) schemes 
for the development of total 43.8 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). 
The details, including the implementation status of the two schemes, are as 
under:  
 

 
 
 
(i) Viability Gap  Funding (VGF) Scheme through Budgetary Support:  The 
Central Government approved the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme for the 
development of 4 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity with a 
budgetary outlay of ₹3,760 crore. Subsequently, owi ng to the decline in BESS 
prices, the capacity supported under the Scheme has been enhanced to 13.8 GWh 
within the approved budgetary outlay. As on date, Battery Energy Storage 
Purchase Agreements (BESPAs) have been executed for 12.7 GWh, financial 
closure has been achieved for 6.54 GWh, 0.5 GWh capacity has been 
commissioned and VGF amounting to ₹168.04 crore has been disbursed. 
 
(ii) Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for development of 30 GWh of BESS 
supported through Power System Development Fund (PSDF):  Ministry of Power, 
vide order dated 09.06.2025, initiated VGF scheme for development of 30 GWh of 
BESS with financial support of ₹5,400 crore from the Power System Development 
Fund. Under this scheme, 25 GWh has been allocated to 15 States for meeting 
their storage requirements, while 5 GWh has been allocated to NTPC Ltd. to 
support electricity demand during non-solar hours and optimize the utilization of 
existing thermal and transmission infrastructure. As on date, Letters of Award 
(LoAs) have been issued  for 22.43 GWh, Battery Energy Storage Purchase 
Agreements (BESPAs) have been executed for 19.65 GWh, and financial closure 
has been achieved for 5 GWh capacity. Further, sanction for the disbursement of 
₹180 crore towards VGF, consequent upon the achievement of financial closure, 
has been issued.

a series of coordinated policy, regulatory, demand -side, and supply -side 
measures to promote the development and deployment of Energy Storage 
Systems (ESS), including Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The details of 
these measures are provided in the Annexure-I. 
 
(c) : Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) can play a vital role in meeting 
peak electricity demand and ensuring grid reliability by storing electricity during 
periods of low dem and or high renewable energy generation and supplying it 
during periods of peak demand.  BESS enables time-shifting of energy, enhances 
grid flexibility, facilitates the integration of renewable energy, and reduces 
dependence on expensive peak power. Gener ating companies can use BESS to 
maximize the value of their generation by shifting off-peak energy to peak periods, 
while grid operators and distribution licensees can utilize BESS for peak load and 
congestion management, demand -supply balancing and ensuri ng reliable and 
quality power supply to consumers.  BESS with Grid Forming Inverters may also 
help in stable grid operation.

entries.head:
1 
 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

698.  Shri MANICKAM TAGORE B: 
Shri VIJAYAKUMAR ALIAS VIJAY VASANTH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the extent of water scarcity across States due to declining 
groundwater levels, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether the groundwater depletion has reached c ritical levels in certain regions, if so, the detai ls thereof, 
State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has implemented any programmes for groundwater recharge and conservation, if 
so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether the rainwater harvesting has been effec tively promoted nationwide, if so, the details ther eof 
including the targets set and achievements made and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(e) whether the watershed development programmes ha ve improved water availability in rural areas, if s o, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(f) whether adequate funds have been allocated for water conservation schemes, if so, the details ther eof 
including their utilisation status and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a) & (b)  Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country are assessed annually by the Central Ground 
Water Board (CGWB) in collaboration with the State Governments. As per the Dynamic Ground Water 
Resources Assessment, 2025, the total Annual Ground  Water Recharge has been assessed at 448.52 Billion  
Cubic Metres (BCM), the Annual Extractable Ground W ater Resource at 407.75 BCM and the total Annual 
Ground Water Extraction at 247.22 BCM. The Stage of  Ground Water Extraction for the country has been 
assessed at 60.63 per cent.  
Out of 6,762 assessment units (Blocks/Taluks/Mandal s), 730 (10.80%) have been categorised as 
Over-exploited, 201 (2.97%) as Critical, 758 (11.21 %) as Semi-Critical, 4,946 (73.14%) as Safe and 127  
(1.88%) as Saline. The State/UT-wise details of gro undwater resources are provided through link given 
below. 
https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/711d8d476bbf498cd90f8038e7371227.pdf 

2 
 
 
The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) monitors grou ndwater levels throughout the country. As 
per the post-monsoon 2025 monitoring, about 90 per cent of the analysed wells recorded groundwater lev els 
between 0 and 10 metres below ground level. The Sta te-wise depth-to-water level distribution is given at 
Annexure.  
Comparison of the Dynamic Ground Water Resources As sessments of 2017 and 2025 indicates an 
increase in annual groundwater recharge from 431.86  BCM to 448.52 BCM, a reduction in annual 
groundwater extraction and a decline in the Stage o f Ground Water Extraction from 63.33 per cent to 60 .63 
per cent. During the same period, the proportion of  assessment units categorised as Safe increased fro m 63 
per cent to 73.14 per cent, while the proportion of  Over-exploited assessment units declined from 17 per cent 
to 10.80 per cent. These trends reflect the sustain ed efforts of the Central and State Governments tow ards 
scientific groundwater management and conservation. 
(c) & (d)  Water being a State subject, sustainable developme nt and management of groundwater resources is 
primarily the responsibility of the State Governmen ts. However, the Central Government supplements the  
efforts of the State Governments by providing techn ical guidance, policy support and financial assista nce 
through various schemes and programmes. The major i nitiatives taken to promote groundwater recharge, 
conservation and rainwater harvesting are as follows: 
i. The Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) regulates  groundwater extraction in the country 
through the Guidelines dated 24.09.2020 and amendme nts thereto. The Guidelines mandate 
implementation of rainwater harvesting and artifici al recharge measures by industries, infrastructure 
and mining projects for obtaining No Objection Cert ificates (NOCs) for groundwater withdrawal and

(b) & (c) : For the Ethanol Supply Year 2024-25, the average procurement cost of ethanol stands at Rs. 
71.55 per litre (inclusive of transportation and GST), which was higher than the cost of refined petrol.  
 

The OMCs purchase ethanol under the EBP Programme at remunerative prices so that farmers are 
fairly compensated. For instance, Maize based ethanol prices have increased progressively and its 
current procurement price is Rs 71.86/litre (exclusive Transportation and GST). Therefore, if 
international crude price remains at around US $70 per barrel, ethanol becomes costlier than pure 
petrol. India has managed to protect consumers from full impact of volatile global crude oil prices, as 
nearly 20% of every litre of petrol sold consists of domestically produced ethanol.  
 
This is one of the principal reasons that, despite unprecedented global disruptions, India witnessed one 
of the most moderated increases in retail fuel prices among major economies and its neighbouring 
countries over the years:

MODIFIED UDAN SCHEME FOR NORTH-EASTERN STATES  
703.    SHRI GAURAV GOGOI                        
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the total number of routes sanctioned under UDAN Scheme for Assam and 
other North Eastern States across all phases along with the number of routes 
currently operational and the number of routes discontinued after the Viability Gap 
Funding period ended; 
(b) whether the Government has examined the CAG's finding that only 7 -10 per 
cent of UDAN routes remained financially viable after the subsidy period, and if 
so, the details thereof along with the specific mechanism provided  under the 
Modified UDAN Scheme 2026-2036 to prevent recurrence of such failures; 
(c) the amount earmarked specifically for North -Eastern routes, airport 
development and helipad connectivity out of the Rupees 28,840 crore allocated 
under the Modified UDAN Scheme; and 
(d) the action taken against airlines that surrendered North -Eastern routes before 
the end of their contracted subsidy period? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) Under the UDAN Scheme, a total of 90 routes have been operationalised across 
all phases for the North Eastern States, including Assam. Out of these, 38 routes 
are currently operational. Further, 28 routes in the North Eastern States have 
completed their three -year Viability Gap Fun ding (VGF) tenure and  are presently 
non-operational. 
 

(b) More than 50% of the routes under UDAN are currently operational and more 
than 25% routes are operational commercially. Further, the next phase of the 
Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)-UDAN has been launched on 04.07.2026.  
The modified scheme incorporates a tapered VGF mechanism extending up to five 
years, wherein financial support is for a longer time in a tapered manner to enable 
airlines to transition towards commercially sustainable operations.   
 
(c) Modified UDAN is being implemented from FY 2026 -27 to FY 2035 -36 with 
an outlay of Rs. 28,840 crores including Rs 12,159 crore for development of 
Aerodromes, Rs 10,043 crore for VGF to support airline operators, Rs 2577 crore 
for O&M support, Rs.3,661 crore for developing 200 heliports in the North Eastern 
Region, Himalayan and Islands States/UTs and Aspirational districts. The scheme 
aims to connect 120 new destinations, serve 4 crore passengers over the next 10 
years, across the country including the North East.

tenure due to a variety of factors such as the COVID -19 pandemic, aircraft

707.  SHRI SUBBARAYAN K:  
COM. SELVARAJ V:  
 
Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has brought out a roadmap 
on Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) revealing that the progress in translating the 
pumped storage potential into commissioned capacity has been uneven and slow; 
and  
 
(b)  if so, the details of the bottlenecks identified in the execution of such 
projects and the remedial measures proposed to be taken in this regard? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) : The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has prepared a roadmap to achieve 
100 GW of Pumped Storage Project (PSPs) capacity addition by 2035 -36. The 
roadmap presents a comprehensive assessment of the current status of pumped 
storage development in the country, State -wise assessed potential, and the 
projected capacity addition trajectory up to 2035 -36, keeping in view the 
increasing penetration of Variable Renewable Energies (V REs) and the 
corresponding need for long duration storage. The report also outlines key policy, 
regulatory and institutional measures required for expeditious development and 
improved viability of PSPs, including aspects related to project clearances, 
transmission planning, and manufacturing preparedness. 
 
(b) : The development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) is impacted by various 
challenges including difficulties in carrying out survey and investigation activities 
in forest areas, issues related to land acquisition, Re habilitation and 
Resettlement (R&R), Eco-Sensitive Zones, high initial capital costs, and delays in 
the creation of essential infrastructure.  To address these challenges and 
facilitate accelerated development of PSPs, the follo wing measures have been 
taken: 
 
(i) Ministry of Power (MoP) has notified Guidelines to promote development of 
Pumped Storage Projects in the country on 10.04.2023. 
…….2.

(ii) Budgetary Support towards Co st of Enabling Infrastructure, i.e., 
roads/bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication infrastructure and 
transmission line from power house to nearest pooling point. 
 
(iii) To provide a transparent, fair, standardized procurement framework based on 
open c ompetitive bidding with appropriate risk -sharing between various 
stakeholders, MoP vide Gazette notification dated 06.02.2025, has notified 
tariff based competitive bidding (TBCB) guidelines for procurement of storage 
capacity/stored energy from pumped storage plants.  
 
(iv) The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), vide its notification 
dated 26.06.2025, has provided for 100% waiver of Inter -State Transmission 
System (ISTS) charges for Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) for a period of 25 
years from the  Commercial Operation Date (COD), in respect of projects for 
which the construction work is awarded on or before 30.06.2028. 
 
(v) The Government of India, vide Gazette notification dated 01.08.2025, has 
revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to setting up hydro 
generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the CEA. 
Further, the Government has exempted off -stream closed -loop pumped 
storage schemes, irrespective of the quantum of capital expenditure, from the 
requirement of concurrence by the CEA. 
 
(vi) Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has revised Guidelines for formulation and 
concurrence of Detailed Project Report (DPR) of PSPs. Under the revised 
guidelines, the timeline for concurrence of DPR has been reduced from 90 
days to 50 days for PSPs. Further, the clearance of Inter-State Aspects is not 
required for PSPs. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), vide its 
notification dated 18.05.2023, has enabled appraisal of PSPs under B2

(viii) The MoEF&CC on 14.08.2023, has issued specific Terms of Reference (TOR) 
for the proposals involving off stream PSPs wherein collection of baseline 
data for one season (other than monsoon) is prescribed for off stream closed 
loop PSPs and collection of baseline data for two seasons (pre -monsoon & 
post-monsoon) is prescribed for off stream open loop PSPs. 
 
(ix) The MOEF&CC on 20.08.2024, has extended the provisions relating to survey

VAN Yojana 2019, amended in 2024, Government provides financial assistance 
for setting up Advanced Biofuels projects including SAF

entries.t: Threat to the Existence of Geruwa River in Bahraich District
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 709 
ANSWERED ON 23.07.2026 
THREAT TO THE EXISTENCE OF GERUWA RIVER IN BAHRAICH DISTRICT 
†709.  Dr. ANAND KUMAR: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasi ng silt deposition, reducing depth and the conseque nt 
threat to the very existence of the Geruwa river in Bahraich district and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government is also aware that prote cted aquatic species such as the Ganges river dolph ins, 
crocodiles and gharials are found in the Geruwa riv er and are being adversely affected by the degradat ion of 
the river and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any study/survey has been conducted reg arding the causes of silt deposition in the river, 
particularly deforestation in the upper catchment areas and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the concrete steps being taken by the Governmen t for the conservation of the Geruwa river, desilta tion, 
forest conservation and protection of aquatic biodiversity? 
ANSWER  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY ) 
(a)    Erosion, movement and deposition of sediment are  natural geo-morphic processes in rivers. Rivers te nd 
to maintain a balance between the silt load carried  and the silt load deposited, thereby maintaining a  river 
regime. The entire Geruwa River, located upstream o f the Girija Barrage, falls under the Katarnia Ghat  
Wildlife Sanctuary. The Government of Uttar Pradesh  has informed that due to reduced flow in the Geruw a 
River, the water velocity decreases, leading to the accumulation of silt in the river bed.  
(b) to (d)    Under the Namami Gange Programme, the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun conducted a 
biodiversity survey of the Geruwa River in January 2023, during which the presence of the Gangetic Dol phin 
(Platanista gangetica ) and Gharial ( Gavialis gangeticus ) was recorded. Gharials of different size classes,  
including nesting females, were observed, indicatin g the presence of a breeding population in the Kata rnia 
Ghat Wildlife Sanctuary stretch. WII has identified  and trained 26 Ganga Praharis from Bahraich distri ct to 
support aquatic biodiversity conservation along the Geruwa (Girwa) and Ghaghra rivers.  
Dredging/de-silting of rivers is not considered tec hno-economically feasible, as the benefits are 
generally marginal and effective only for a short d uration. De-silting measures, including dredging in  specific 
reaches of rivers for the removal of drainage conge stion, channel capacity improvement and navigation 
purposes, are formulated and implemented by the con cerned States/agencies, as required, based on prope r 
scientific model studies. For the comprehensive and  holistic management of sediments, the Department o f 
Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuve nation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, in extensive 
consultations with Central Ministries/Departments a nd State Governments/UTs, has prepared the “Nationa l 
Framework for Sediment Management ”.  The Framework emphasizes reducing silt generation rather than silt 
removal and promotes technological innovations and best practices. It also lays emphasis on sediment 
management through integrated river basin managemen t plans, giving due consideration to the environmen t 
and ecology. 
 *****

11,671 claims have been rejected and a total of 6,04,969 claims are pending for decision. 

Further, the details of number of claims (individual and community) received, the number of 
claims approved (Title distributed), Claims rejected, Claims disposed off during the last three 
years, month- wise and State/UT-wise are available at this Ministry’s website- on FRA- 
MPR-  https://tribal.nic.in/FRA.aspx. 
  
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, being the Nodal Ministry for administering the 
legislative matters of FRA, exhorts all State Governments to abide by the provisions contained 
in FRA and ensure that all eligible claimants are provided the rights which are due to them.   
  
(d) & (e): As stipulated in Rule 16 of FRA, the State Government has to ensure through its 
departments that all government schemes, including those relating to land improvement, land 
productivity, basic amenities and other livelihood measures, are provided to such claimants 
and communities whose rights have been recognized and vested under the FRA. Further, the 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial support to State Governments under the Dharti 
Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA) for strengthening Gram Sabhas and 
Community Forest Resource Management Committees. Additionally, FRA patta holders are 
supported through convergence with schemes of the Department of Agriculture, Animal 
Husbandry and Fisheries, wherein beneficiary contribution has been limited to 10%, wherever 
required, to facilitate greater uptake. Further, eligible FRA title holders are covered under the 
PM-KISAN scheme implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.  
  
    The Ministry of Tribal Affairs continues to work with other Ministries / Departments for 
effective implementation and to ensure that benefits of these schemes reach forest right holders 
in full measure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 712 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
INCREASE IN AIRFARE  
712.      SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH   
             DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE                  
             PROF VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD               
             SMT SUPRIYA SULE                        
             SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE           
             SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL                   
             SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE  
           
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the significant increase in 
domestic and international airfares following the ongoing geopolitical tensions 
and conflict involving Iran and the United States which have led to higher 
aviation fuel costs and flight disruptions and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of the increase in average air ticket prices on major routes 
connecting Maharashtra particularly Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur during the last 
six months; 
 
(c) whether the airlines have imposed fuel surcharge or revised fare structures 
due to rising Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices and longer flight routes and if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to  monitor increases in airfare and 
protect passengers from excessive fare hikes; 
 
(e) whether any consultations have been held with airlines regarding fare 
rationalisation and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(f) the measures proposed to ensure affordable air connectivity for passengers 
travelling from Maharashtra? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 

(a) to (f): The ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia have significantly 
impacted ATF prices which has resulted in introduction of fuel surcharge in 
mid-March, 2026 by Indian carriers. 
 
The Fuel surcharge was introduced by the airlines in March, 2026 and was 
revised in the month of April 2026 based on flight distance. 
 
In order to ensure that airlines d o not charge airfares outside the range declared 
by them, Tariff Monitoring Unit (TMU) has been set up in Directorate General 
of Civil Aviation (DGCA) which monitors airfares on selected 78 routes (72 
domestic & 06 international) on random basis, including  three routes from 
Mumbai. 
 
The Government has taken several measures to support the aviation sector and 
help keep air travel affordable, which include, one -time budgetary support not 
exceeding Rs. 10,000 crores for Oil Markreting Companies (OMCs) to pro vide 
Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) price stablisation support to the Scheduled Indian 
Airlines due to exceptional fuel price volatality arising from the West Asia 
crisis and for domestic operations, ATF prices were capped at a maximum 
increase of 25% over th e 1st March, 2026 base price, effective from 1st April 
2026 for the months of April and May, 2026. 
 
The issue of high VAT on ATF has been taken up with the States/ UTs by the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation. As a result, 23 States/ UTs have reduced VAT on 
ATF since September 2021. More recently, in May, 2026, the State of 
Maharashtra has reduced the VAT on ATF from 18% to 7% for a period of 6 
months. 
 
Various factors influenced by combination of market forces like market 
competition, passenger demand, seat oc cupancy and seasonal variati ons, etc. 
also affect airfares. 
 
With the repeal of Air Corporation Act in March, 1994, airlines are free to 
establish airfare based on their operational & economic viability while adhering 
to Rule 135 of the Aircraft Rules, 1937. 
 
The Government generally refrains from regulating airfares to maintain market 
competitiveness, however, it retains vigilant oversight role, intervening in 
exceptional circumstances by redistributing capacity across various sectors and 
imposing temporary fare caps, such as during the Covid Pandemic, festivals like 
Maha kumb or other extraordinary instances like Pahalgam incident &  the 
Indigo flight disruptions. 
 

Regular consultations are being carried out by DGCA with airlines from time to 
time, in order to sensitize to exercise moderation/ self - regulation while fixing 
the airfares and increasing capacity.

entries.t: International Air Cargo Facilities in Punjab
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 715 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
INTERNATIONAL AIR CARGO FACILITIES IN PUNJAB  
715.    DR. AMAR  SINGH             
             
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the inadequate international air cargo 
facilities in Punjab despite the State's significant contribution to agricultural and 
industrial exports and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the present status of the proposals for establishing dedicated cargo terminals, 
cold-chain facilities, customs clearance and warehousing at Sri Guru Ram Dass 
Jee International Airport, Amritsar and Shaheed Bhagat Singh International 
Airport, Chandigarh; 
(c) whether representations have been received from trade and industry bodies 
seeking direct international cargo connectivity from Punjab and if so, the details 
thereof, including the action taken thereon; 
(d) the reasons for the non -availability of dedicated int ernational freighter 
services from Punjab; and 
(e) the steps taken to strengthen air cargo infrastructure, reduce export logistics 
costs and improve export competitiveness for farmers, Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and industries in Punjab? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e) The development of cargo facilities is a continuous process and 
depends on various factors such as airport development progress, increase in 
scheduled operations, handling capacity, growth in domestic cargo volumes and 
demand from airlines. The Government's approach is to provide suitable policy 
and congenial regulatory regime, for the encouragement of infrastructure 
development, simplification of procedures, te chnological upgradation, and 
deployment of skilled manpower, all aimed at efficient and cost -effective air 
cargo services delivery. 
 

The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has established an International Air 
Cargo Facility, including a Centre for Perishable Cargo (CPC), at Sri Guru Ram 
Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar. The facility is presently being operated 
by AAI Cargo Logistics and Allied Services Company Limited. Further, at 
Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh, which is oper ated by 
Chandigarh International Airport Limited, an Integrated Cargo Complex is 
available for cargo operations. 
 
The airlines initiate cargo operations based on their internal assessment of cargo 
potential, handling capabilities and overall commercial vi ability of operating 
from any airport. Further, the exporters, based on their commercial viability, 
requirements, utilize available air cargo facilities in accordance with various 
determining factors, including the destination country, airline operations, and 
the availability of direct or connecting services to the intended destinations. 
******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 716 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  23rd July 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE  
716.    DR. PRABHA MALLIKARJUN                  
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the adequacy of airport infrastructure 
to meet the growing passenger and cargo traffic demand across the country and 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of airports operating beyond their d esigned capacity and the 
measures proposed to address congestion and operational bottlenecks; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of infrastructure 
gaps relating to terminals, runways, cargo handling and air traffic management 
systems and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the investments proposed for modernisation and expansion of airport 
infrastructure in the next five years; and 
(e) whether any airport expansion, modernisation or greenfield airport projects 
are under consideration in Ka rnataka that would improve connectivity to 
districts such as Davanagere and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (d): Airport infrastructure, including passenger terminals , runways, 
aprons, cargo facilities and other airside infrastructure, is developed by the 
Airports Authority of India (AAI) and other airport operators based on traffic 
growth, operational requirements, airline demand, financial viability and 
techno-economic considerations. 
 
Expansion and modernisation projects undertaken at airports across the country 
have enhanced the total passenger -handling capacity to over 580 million 
passengers per annum (MPPA), while passenger traffic handled during 2025 -26 
was about 420 million. 
 

Passenger traffic varies across airports depending on factors such as seasonal 
demand, festivals, holidays and airline schedules, which may lead to temporary 
congestion during peak periods. Airport operators continuously monitor traffic 
and take necessary operational measures to ensure smooth passenger 
facilitation. 
 
In line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, airport development is being 
undertaken through Greenfield airports, revival of unserved and underserved 
airports under RCS -UDAN, e xpansion of existing airports, and promotion of 
private investment under the PPP mode. So far, 25 Greenfield airports have 
been accorded In -Principle Approval, of which 14 are operational, while 6 
proposals have been granted Site Clearance. Further, 95 aer odromes have been 
operationalised under RCS -UDAN (as on 10.07.2026). The modified UDAN 
Scheme envisages connectivity to 120 new destinations and serving 4 crore 
passengers over the next ten years. 
 
(e): Under the Greenfield Airports Policy, 2008, a develop er, including a State 
Government, is required to identify a suitable site, undertake a pre -feasibility 
study and submit a proposal to the Central Government for grant of Site 
Clearance followed by In-Principle Approval. No proposal for development of a 
Greenfield airport at Davanagere has been received from the Government of 
Karnataka. 
******

entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †719 
ANSWERED ON 23/07/2026 
  
TAP WATER CONNECTIONS IN UT OF DADRA AND NAGAR HAVELI AND 
DAMAN AND DIU 
  
†719. SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI: 
Will the Minister of Jal Shakti be pleased to state: 
(a) whether more than eighty per cent of rural households have been provided with tap water 
connections under the Har Ghar Jal component of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) in the country 
as of July, 2026; 
(b) if so, the details thereof in respect of the Union Territory (UT) of Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
and Daman and Diu; 
(c) the details of rural households provided with tap water connections during the last two years 
till date, State-wise; and 
(d) the details of the funds allocated, released and utilised under the said Mission in respect of 
the UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu during the last two years till date? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) & (b) Drinking water is a State subject. The power to plan, design, approve and implement 
drinking water supply schemes/projects lies with State/UT Government. Government of India, 
in partnership with States/UTs is implementing Jal Jeevan Mission, since August , 2019, to 
make provision of tap water supply of prescribed quality on a regular and long -term basis to 
every rural household. 
Significant progress has been made in the country since the launch of Jal Jeevan Mission, 
towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the start of Jal Jeevan Mission 
in August 2019, only 3.23 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections. As on 20.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural households in the country, more than 
15.89 crore (82.10%) households are reported to have tap water connections in their homes. 
Dadra Nagar Haveli & Daman Diu had reported in 2022 that they had provided tap water 
connection to all rural households in the UT. (Source: JJM-IMIS). 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(c) The details of rural househo lds provided with tap water connections during the last two 
years till date, State-wise under the Jal Jeevan Mission in rural areas is in public domain and 
available on JJM dashboard at: https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx 
(d) No funds have b een released to the UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 
during the last two years till date under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM). The details are available 
on JJM Dashboard (https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/jjmindia.aspx).

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 720 
ANSWERED ON 23RD JULY, 2026 
PLI SCHEME IN MADHYA PRADESH 
  
720. SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of projects approved and the investment realised under Production Linked 
Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) in Madhya Pradesh along 
with the employment generated therefrom; 
(b) whether the Ministry has identified the Satna-Vindhya region as a potential agri-food 
processing cluster considering its production of tomato, onion and other horticultural 
crops and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether proposals for integrated processing, value-addition, cold-chain and food 
preservation infrastructure in the region are under consideration and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) the steps being taken to promote Farmer-Producer Organisations (FPOs), food 
processing Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and export-oriented value 
chains in Madhya Pradesh under the vision of Viksit Bharat, 2047? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
(a): Under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), 
10 manufacturing units of approved applicants have been established in Madhya Pradesh. 
Approved applicants have reported actual investment of ₹657.69 crore against committed 
investment of ₹468.15 crore and generation of 21,281 direct and indirect employment 
opportunities in the State. The investments have also resulted in creation of additional food 
processing capacity of 1.42 lakh metric ton per annum (LMTPA). 
(b): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries is implementing Operation Greens, a 
component of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY). Under the Operation 
Greens Scheme, Satna has been identified as one of the production clusters for Carrot. Further, 
various regions of Madhya Pradesh have been identified as production clusters for fruits such 
as Kinnow, Amla and Guava and vegetables such as Tomato, Onion, Potato, Beans, Gourds, 
Carrot, Cauliflower, Okra, Green Peas, Ginger and Garlic. 
(c): Under the Operation Greens Scheme, the Ministry has approved one Integrated Value 
Chain Development Project in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, which is operational and has 
benefited about 2,000 farmers. Dhar district has been identified as a production cluster for 
Guava, Gourds, Ginger and Garlic. Further, under the Scheme for Creation of Infrastructure 
for Agro Processing Clusters (APC), a component scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 

Sampada Yojana (PMKSY), three projects have been approved in Madhya Pradesh, namely 
M/s Nimar Agro Park (Barwani), M/s Bharti Agro Cluster (Betul) and M/s Prashun Foods Pvt. 
Ltd. (Dhar), for creation of modern food processing infrastructure based on the cluster 
approach. 
(d): Under the Operation Greens Scheme, one Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) has been 
linked to the processing hub established in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh. 
Further, under the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) 
Scheme, 35% credit-linked capital subsidy (maximum ₹10 lakh per unit) is provided for setting 
up new micro food processing enterprises and upgradation of existing units, including Farmer 
Producer Organisations (FPOs), thereby providing financial, technical and business support. 
The Scheme also provides 35% credit-linked assistance up to ₹3 crore for creation of Common 
Infrastructure by FPOs, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Cooperatives and Government agencies, 
enabling establishment of common processing, storage, packaging, testing and value addition 
facilities. To strengthen market access and exports, the Scheme provides Branding & 
Marketing support of up to 50% of the eligible project cost to groups of FPOs, SHGs and 
Cooperatives for development of common brands, packaging, labelling and quality 
standardisation. The Scheme is being implemented through the State Government under a 
demand-driven framework, strengthening FPO-led value chains, promoting entrepreneurship, 
technology upgradation and value addition, thereby contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 
2047 by enhancing farmers' income, generating employment and improving the 
competitiveness of the food processing sector. In Madhya Pradesh, loans for 15,946 micro food 
processing enterprises, including 18 FPOs, have been sanctioned as on 30th June, 2026. 
In addition, under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing 
Industry (PLISFPI), eligible applicants are supported through performance-linked incentives 
on achievement of eligible incremental sales. The Scheme includes a dedicated category for 
MSMEs engaged in innovative and organic food products and provides financial incentives for 
Branding and Marketing Abroad, thereby promoting value addition and enhancing the global

entries.t: 'Cities as Growth Hubs' Initiative under the Urban Challenge Fund
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 721 
TO BE ANSWERED ON JULY 23, 2026 
 
'CITIES AS GROWTH HUBS' INITIATIVE UNDER THE URBAN CHALLENGE 
FUND 
 
NO. 721 SHRI TEJASVI SURYA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether implementation of the "Cities as Growth Hubs" initiative under 
the Urban Challenge Fund has commenced and if so, the details thereof 
including its implementation framework, funding pattern and the 
categories of projects proposed to be supported; 
(b) the criteria for selection of cities and projects along with the details of 
proposals received, shortlisted and approved, State/UT -wise including 
those from Karnataka; 
(c) whether urban governance, municipal finance and planning reforms 
have been prescribed as preconditions for availing assistance under the 
Fund and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether measurable outcome indicators and targets relating to private 
investment mobilisation, infrastructure creation, municipal reforms and 
economic development have been prescribed under the initiative and if 
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
(a) to (d): The Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) scheme has been 
operationalized with the launch of Operational Guidelines for UCF on 15th 
April, 2026. UCF supports the development and strengthening of urban 
infrastructure through implementation of transformativ e and impactful 
projects under three verticals namely ‘Cities as Growth Hubs’, ‘Creative 
Redevelopment of Cities’ and ‘Water and Sanitation’.   
All Cities are eligible to participate under UCF. Chapter 7 of the operational 
guidelines includes details regarding the Project Appraisal and Challenge 
Framework including mandatory eligibility requirements, overall project 
flow/ implementation framework, and project evaluation process for 
…2/- 

-2- 
appraisal and selection of projects. The list of admissible projects under 
UCF are given under Chapter 5 of the operational guidelines. The scheme 
guidelines are in public domain and may be accessed at 
https://www.mohua.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/04/7950afb9b2d5cb773ba3d
6c64bde9726.pdf 
Under UCF, Central Assistance is limited to 25 per cent of the cost of 
bankable projects, with the stipulation that at least 50 per cent of the 
project cost shall be financed through market -based sources, including 
municipal bonds, bank loans and Public- Private Partnerships (PPPs). The 
remaining project cost is to be met by the concerned State/UT/ULB. 
So far, 33 projects have been approved/ accorded in -principle approval 
including 3 projects from State of Karnataka.  The approved projects in 
Karnataka include sewerage infrastructure aimed at enhancing sewage 
treatment capacity and improving environmental outcomes, as well as 
major urban transport infrastructure such as flyovers and a section of the 
Peripheral Ring Road in Bengaluru to help decongest traffic and improve 
urban mobility.  The State-wise details are given in Annexure.  
Further, reforms implementation is an integral feature of the UCF. The 
reform provisions under the Scheme are contained in Chapter 8 of the 
Operational Guidelines. States/UTs are required to submit a reform 
roadmap and report progress to the Ministry. The reforms broadly cover 
Market & Financial Reforms, Governance & Digital Reforms, Operational & 
Capacity Reforms, Urban Planning & Spatial Reforms, Project -Specific 
Reforms (UCF -linked) to strengthen municipal governance, financial 
sustainability & service delivery which will in turn aid implementation of 
projects under UCF. 
The Guidelines also provide for monitoring of project outcomes through 
measurable indicators, including mobilisation of market -based finance, 
infrastructure creation and implementation of project-linked reforms.

EXPANSION OF NATURAL GAS INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
722. SMT. RACHNA BANERJEE: 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of the Government's target to increase the share of natural gas in India's energy 
mix; 
(b) the details of the progress made in expanding the National Gas Grid and City Gas Distribution 
(CGD) network during the last three years, year-wise and State/UT-wise; and 
(c) the challenges being faced in achieving universal access to piped natural gas (PNG) and 
compressed natural gas (CNG)? 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी) 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (c): As per Energy Statistics 2026 released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, the share of natural gas in India's total primary 
energy supply was 7.12% (provisional) during Financial Year 2024–25. For increasing the share of 
natural gas in the energy basket, Government has taken various steps which inter-alia, include 
expansion of National Gas Grid Pipeline, expansion of City Gas Distribution (CGD) network, setting 
up of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Terminals, allocation of domestic gas to Compressed Natural 
Gas (Transport)/ Piped Natural Gas (Domestic) CNG (T)/PNG(D) on priority, allowing marketing 
and pricing freedom with a ceiling price to gas produced from high pressure/high temperature areas, 
deep water & ultra-deep water and from coal seams, Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable 
Transportation (SATAT) initiative to promote Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) etc. 
The National Gas Grid expansion is a continuous process. PNGRB authorizes entities to lay, build, 
operate and expand Natural Gas Pipelines (NGPL) across the country. The progress made in 
expansion of the National Gas Grid during the last three years is at Annexure-I. 
Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed Natural Gas 
(CNG) stations is part of the development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia 

include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, 
commercial and industrial units and CNG to transport sector is being carried out by the entities 
authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). The details of State/UT-wise 
CNG stations & DPNG connections progress for last three years is at Annexure-II. 
As informed by authorized CGD entities, challenges in achieving universal access to PNG and CNG, 
inter-alia, include: 
(i) High capital investment requirements for development of CGD infrastructure, particularly 
in sparsely populated and remote areas. 
(ii) Delay in obtaining statutory permissions/Right of Use (RoU)/Right of Way (RoW) and 
other approvals from various Central, State and local authorities for laying pipelines and 
establishing CNG stations. 
(iii) Land availability for installation of CNG stations, City Gate Stations (CGS) and other 
associated infrastructure. 
(iv) Availability and timely connectivity to the Natural Gas pipeline network, especially in 
areas where trunk pipeline infrastructure is under development. 
(v) Geographical and terrain-related constraints, including hilly, forest, coastal and difficult-
to-access areas, which increase project complexity and cost.

(a) the details of applications received, approved and rejected under
